metadata.topic: Retake Prep — Workflow, Tools and Administration deep dive (Design and Reference Guide 9.0 PDF)
metadata.note: Section-by-section coverage of every Workflow, Tools and Administration chapter of the guide: Workflow profiles, names, data units, member expansions, substitution variables, import methods, channels, confirmation/certification, OnePlace workflow, journals (pp. 638–778, 892–927, 1790–1813); Application Security Roles, Application Properties, Business Rules admin, dimension/project/application/system load-extract, File Explorer (pp. 437–452, 1475–1550, 1642–1646, 1769–1789); Data Management, Task Scheduler, PowerShell/Web API (pp. 429–436, 1460–1474, 1551–1613); Spreadsheet and Excel Add-in (pp. 1573–1585, 1860–1970); users, groups, system roles, system configuration (pp. 416–428, 1647–1700); logging, system tools, environment, servers (pp. 1701–1768). Deduplicated against the other retake files; a sample was independently fact-checked. Guide is 9.0; exam is based on 8.x.

questions.question: Houston is assigned South Houston and Houston Heights. Its Calculation Definitions list the parent Houston plus (Assigned Entities). With the Workflow POV on Houston, what do E#Root.WFProfileEntities and E#Root.WFCalculationEntities return?

options.A: Both return Houston, South Houston, Houston Heights
options.B: Both return South Houston and Houston Heights
options.C: WFProfileEntities: Houston only. WFCalculationEntities: South Houston, Houston Heights
options.D: WFProfileEntities: South Houston, Houston Heights. WFCalculationEntities: Houston, South Houston, Houston Heights

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says WFProfileEntities returns the entities assigned to the profile, while WFCalculationEntities returns all entities in the Calculation Definitions — Houston, South Houston and Houston Heights in this example (pp. 639–640). A is incorrect — WFProfileEntities returns only assigned entities, and Houston isn't assigned. B is incorrect — WFCalculationEntities includes Houston because it's in the Calculation Definitions. C is incorrect — this reverses the two expressions.

questions.question: Budget_Quarterly has a Workflow Tracking Frequency of Quarterly in a monthly application. With the Workflow POV on 2024Q2, what does T#Root.WFTimePeriods return?

options.C: 2024M6 only
options.D: 2024M1 through 2024M12

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says for non-Standard tracking frequencies WFTimePeriods returns the range of periods for the Workflow Unit; its Quarterly example returns 2024M4, 2024M5 and 2024M6. A is incorrect — for Quarterly tracking it returns the months in the quarter. C is incorrect — returning the last period of each year is WFCalculationTimePeriods' pattern, for range units. D is incorrect — that's the Range example with WFStartTime 2024M1 and WFEndTime 2024M12.

questions.question: UD1 holds cost centers, and three UD1 members are tied to the Engineering Workflow Channel. The Workflow Profile in the Workflow View uses Engineering. Which expression returns those three members?

options.A: E#Root.WFProfileEntities
options.B: UD1#Root.WFChannelMembers
options.C: UD1#Root.WFProfileEntities
options.D: A#Root.WFChannelMembers

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says WFChannelMembers (UD dimensions only) returns the UD members tied to the Workflow Profile's Workflow Channel. A is incorrect — this returns entities assigned to the profile. C is incorrect — WFProfileEntities is for the Entity dimension only. D is incorrect — WFChannelMembers is for user-defined dimensions only.

questions.question: A Cube View must show only the Income Statement accounts in the Account dimension of the current Workflow's cube. Which filter does this?

options.A: A#[Income Statement].Where(MemberDim = |WFCube|)
options.B: A#[Income Statement].Where(MemberDim = |WFAccountDim|)
options.C: A#[Income Statement].Where(InUse = |WFAccountDim|)
options.D: A#[Income Statement].WFProfileEntities

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide gives this example to filter the member list to accounts in the workflow's Account dimension, using the WFAccountDim substitution variable. A is incorrect — WFCube returns the cube name, not the Account dimension. C is incorrect — InUse is a True/False filter. D is incorrect — WFProfileEntities is an Entity-only expansion.

questions.question: What does E#[Total GolfStream].Member.Children.Where((Name Contains Balls) OR (Name = Clubs)).Children return that the same expression without .Member does not?

options.A: All other children of Total GolfStream, such as Corporate
options.B: Only the base entities, without Clubs and Golf Balls
options.C: Nothing extra; .Member is ignored when followed by an expansion
options.D: Total GolfStream itself

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says this expression 'returns Total GolfStream due to E#[Total GolfStream].Member', plus the filtered children and their children. A is incorrect — the Where clause still filters the children to Clubs and Golf Balls. B is incorrect — Clubs and Golf Balls are returned with their children. C is incorrect — .Member adds the starting member.

questions.question: The Formula Where clause (for example, F#Root.TreeDescendants(Formula <> '')) filters members that have Member Formulas. For which dimension is this filter NOT listed?

options.A: Scenario
options.B: Flow
options.C: Entity
options.D: Account

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide lists the Formula filter for Scenario, Account, Flow and UD1–UD8 members, not Entity. A is incorrect — Scenario is listed. B is incorrect — Flow is listed. D is incorrect — Account is listed.

questions.subtopic: Where Clause — User In Security Group
questions.question: Which is NOT one of the User In Security Group Where Clause choices?

options.A: UserInDisplayMemberGroup
options.B: UserInReadDataGroup2
options.C: UserInAnyDataSecurityGroup
options.D: UserInReadWriteDataGroup

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists UserInReadDataGroup, UserInReadDataGroup2, UserInReadWriteDataGroup, UserInReadWriteDataGroup2 and UserInAnyDataSecurityGroup; there's no display-group option. B is incorrect — it's a listed choice. C is incorrect — it's a listed choice. D is incorrect — it's a listed choice.

questions.subtopic: Substitution Variables — Profile Keys vs Index
questions.question: A Business Rule needs the numeric internal ID of the current Workflow Profile, not its position in the hierarchy. Which substitution variable returns it?

options.A: WFProfileKey
options.B: WFProfileIndex
options.C: WFProfileLastDescendantIndex
options.D: WFProfile

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the Workflow Profile Keys (WFProfileKey, WFReviewProfileKeys, etc.) 'return a numeric internal ID for Workflow Profiles'. B is incorrect — this gives the profile's numeric position in the hierarchy. C is incorrect — this gives an index of bottom descendants in the tree. D is incorrect — this gives the profile name.

questions.question: A report should show the prior Workflow period, but return it only if that period is still in the current year. Which variable fits?

options.A: WFTimePriorN
options.B: WFTimePriorInYearN
options.C: WFYearPriorN
options.D: WFSubPeriodPriorN

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says WFTimePriorInYearN returns the prior Workflow time period(s) only if still in the current year. A is incorrect — this returns the prior period even across a year boundary. C is incorrect — this returns the prior year's year portion. D is incorrect — this returns the previous sub-period portion, without the in-year limit.

questions.question: The Workflow is set to 2026M3. Which substitution variable returns the number 3?

options.A: WFSubPeriodNum
options.B: WFSubPeriod
options.C: WFTimeID
options.D: WFYear

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says WFSubPeriodNum returns the period's number; if the Workflow is set to M3, 3 is returned. B is incorrect — this returns the sub-period portion (for example, M3), not the number. C is incorrect — this returns the internal numeric ID of the time period. D is incorrect — this returns the year portion.

questions.question: How many optional WFText fields can be filled on a Workflow Profile and referenced as substitution variables?

options.A: Eight — WFText1 through WFText8
options.B: Four — WFText1 through WFText4
options.C: Two — WFText1 and WFText2
options.D: Six — WFText1 through WFText6

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says 'WFText1, WFText2, WFText3 and WFText4 … provides four optional text fields that can be populated and referenced from a Workflow Profile'. A is incorrect — eight Text properties exist on dimension members (Text1–Text8), not on Workflow Profiles. C is incorrect — there are four. D is incorrect — there are four.

questions.question: Which substitution variable returns the Time Dimension Profile name for the user's current Workflow POV?

options.A: WFTimeDimProfile
options.B: WFCubeRoot
options.C: WFTimeDesc
options.D: WFScenarioDim

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says WFTimeDimProfile 'returns the Time Dimension Profile name associated with the user's current Workflow POV'. B is incorrect — this returns the top level of the Workflow Profile hierarchy. C is incorrect — this returns the Workflow time description (for example, Feb 2011). D is incorrect — this returns the cube's Scenario dimension.

questions.question: An administrator wants a Workflow Name that starts with a Pre-Process task before input. Which input type offers Workflow Names that begin with Pre-Process?

options.A: Import
options.B: Form
options.C: Journal
options.D: Review

questions.explanation: B is correct: only the Form origin list includes Pre-Process options, such as (Pre-Process, Form Input) and (Pre-Process, Form Input, Process, Confirm, Certify). A is incorrect — Import names start with Import, Workspace or Central Import — none with Pre-Process. C is incorrect — Journal names start with Journal Input, Central Journal Input or Workspace. D is incorrect — Review profiles only have (Process, Certify) and (Process, Confirm, Certify).

questions.question: Which Workflow Names are available to a Review Workflow Profile?

options.A: (Process, Certify) and (Process, Confirm, Certify)
options.B: (Workspace) and (Workspace, Certify)
options.C: (Import, Validate, Process, & Certify) and (Process, Certify)
options.D: (Central Form Input) and (Process, Confirm, Certify)

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says that since Review profiles can't load data, their only tasks are (Process, Certify) and (Process, Confirm, Certify). B is incorrect — these are input-type options (Import, Form, Journal), not Review options. C is incorrect — Review profiles can't import. D is incorrect — Central Form Input is a Form-channel option.

questions.question: A range-based Forecast Workflow Unit spans 2024M1–2025M12. A Data Management step must calculate every period. Which expression returns the minimum periods needed, and what does it return?

options.A: T#Root.WFTimePeriods — all 24 months, 2024M1 through 2025M12
options.B: T#Root.WFCalculationTimePeriods — all 24 months
options.C: T#Root.WFCalculationTimePeriods — 2024M12 and 2025M12, since calculating the last period of each year also calculates the prior periods in that year
options.D: T#WFYear.Base — all 24 months

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says WFCalculationTimePeriods returns the last period of each year in the range; the engine calculates all prior periods in a year, so all 24 are covered. It's meant for DM steps and Business Rules. A is incorrect — WFTimePeriods returns every period in the range, not the minimum needed for calculation. B is incorrect — it returns only each year's last period. D is incorrect — this isn't the guide's documented Workflow calculation-period expansion.

questions.question: Certifiers must answer a set of questions during the Certify step. Which Workflow Profile property assigns them, and where are they built?

options.A: Confirmation Profile Name; built under Application > Workflow > Confirmation Rules
options.B: Certification Profile Name; built under Application > Workflow > Certification Questions
options.C: Certification Dashboard Profile Name; built under Presentation > Dashboards
options.D: Certification SignOff Group; built under System > Security

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the certification questions shown in the Certify step are managed in Certification Profile Name and configured under Application Tab/Workflow/Certification Questions. A is incorrect — that's for Confirmation Rules in the Confirm step. C is incorrect — that controls the dashboards in the Certify analysis pane. D is incorrect — that controls who can certify, not the questions.

questions.question: A Review profile has a Named Dependent on a shared services Input Parent that loads Entities for several regions. Process Cube on the Review profile should calculate only the Entities that belong to that region. What should be used?

options.A: Assigned Entities
options.B: Named Dependent Filter
options.C: Dependent Entities
options.D: User Cell Input Entities

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the Named Dependent Filter specifies the Entities that are valid dependents, because Named Dependents are usually shared services whose Entities span multiple Review profiles. A is incorrect — this placeholder is for Input Parent and Input Child types, and Review profiles have no assigned Entities. C is incorrect — this includes all Entities of Named Dependents, which may return Entities not relevant to the Review profile. D is incorrect — this placeholder is for Input Parent and Input Child types and covers the executing user's data entry.

questions.question: On a Base Input profile, Process Cube should calculate only the Entities that were adjusted by the profile's journal children. Which placeholder fits?

options.A: Loaded Entities
options.B: Assigned Entities
options.C: Journal Input Entities
options.D: User Cell Input Entities

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says this calculates all Entities adjusted with journal entries by the Adjustment Child profiles that are dependents of the Input Parent. A is incorrect — this covers Entities imported by Import Children. B is incorrect — this covers every Entity directly assigned to the profile. D is incorrect — this covers Entities affected by data entry by the user executing the Workflow.

questions.question: A Workflow Profile has five assigned Entities. How are its Confirmation Rules evaluated?

options.A: Once, against the Workflow Profile's parent Entity
options.B: Once, against the total of all assigned Entities
options.C: Only against Entities where the Confirmed switch is False
options.D: Individually for each Entity associated with the Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'The rules will process individually for each Entity associated with the Workflow Profile.' A is incorrect — they are not run only at a parent. B is incorrect — they are not run against a combined total. C is incorrect — the guide makes no such exception in this section.

questions.question: A weekly application has a Confirmation Rule with Frequency = Monthly. When does it run?

options.A: Every week
options.B: The last week of each month
options.C: The first week of each month
options.D: Only in December

questions.explanation: B is correct: Monthly 'runs the rules every month. If this is for a weekly application, they will run the last week of each month.' A is incorrect — that would be All Time Periods. C is incorrect — it is the last week, not the first. D is incorrect — that is Yearly.

questions.question: A Confirmation Rule uses Frequency = Half Yearly. In which periods does it run?

options.A: March and September
options.B: January and July
options.C: June and December
options.D: Every quarter-end

questions.explanation: C is correct: Half Yearly runs 'two times a year; once in June and December.' A is incorrect — those are not the documented periods. B is incorrect — those are not the documented periods. D is incorrect — that is Quarterly.

questions.question: Why is the Frequency Member Filter field grayed out on a Confirmation Rule?

options.A: The Frequency is not set to Member Filter
options.B: The rule's Action is No Action
options.C: The Scenario Type Name is set to All
options.D: The user is not in the Maintenance Group

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Frequency Member Filter 'only becomes available when Member Filter is chosen' as the Frequency; otherwise it is gray. B is incorrect — Action does not control this field. C is incorrect — Scenario Type does not control it. D is incorrect — security does not gray out this field.

questions.question: A Confirmation Rule fails. Its Action is Warning (Pass). No other rules fail. What can the user do?

options.A: Nothing until the rule is resolved
options.B: Proceed and Certify — a warning displays but does not stop the process
options.C: Certify only after an administrator overrides the rule
options.D: Proceed, but the Certify step is skipped

questions.explanation: B is correct: with Warning, 'a warning message will display to alert the user, but the process will not stop, and you will be allowed to Certify if there were no errors in other rules.' A is incorrect — that is Error (Fail). C is incorrect — no override is needed. D is incorrect — Certify still runs normally.

questions.question: A Confirmation Rule is set up with no Action. What happens when it runs?

options.A: It is treated as Error (Fail) by default
options.B: It is skipped during Confirm
options.C: Its value is displayed during confirmation for information only
options.D: It runs only if the Frequency is Member Filter

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'If No Action is associated with the rule, the value for the given rule will just be displayed during confirmation,' for information. A is incorrect — Error must be chosen explicitly. B is incorrect — it runs and displays its value. D is incorrect — Frequency does not depend on the Action.

questions.question: When is a Confirmation Rule's Failure Message shown?

options.A: Only when the rule's Action is Error
options.B: When the Action is Warning or Error
options.C: Whenever the rule runs, as the rule description
options.D: Only when the Rule Formula fails to compile

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Failure Message 'will only be used if the rule is associated with the Error Action.' B is incorrect — Warning rules use the separate Warning Message. C is incorrect — the description shown in the Workflow is the Rule Text. D is incorrect — compile results come from the check icon in the Rule Formula Editor.

questions.question: What happens to a Confirmation Rule Failure or Warning Message longer than 2,000 characters?

options.A: The rule will not save
options.B: It is split across two messages
options.C: It is moved to the Rule Text
options.D: It is truncated with an ellipsis (…) in the last three characters

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Messages longer than 2000 characters will be truncated with an ellipsis (…) placed in the last three characters.' A is incorrect — saving is not blocked. B is incorrect — there is no splitting. C is incorrect — Rule Text is a separate field.

questions.question: How does an administrator open the Rule Formula Editor for a Confirmation Rule?

options.A: Double-click the Rule Text
options.B: Right-click the rule line item and select Edit Rule Formulas
options.C: Open Business Rules and create a Finance rule named after the group
options.D: Select the rule group and click the Compile icon

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'To edit the Rule Formula, right click on the line item that needs to be edited and select Edit Rule Formulas.' A is incorrect — Rule Text is only a description. C is incorrect — formulas are kept with the rule, not in a separate Business Rule. D is incorrect — the check icon in the editor checks compiling; it does not open the editor.

questions.question: Where is a Confirmation Rule Profile assigned to a Workflow Profile, and which Rule Profile settings control where it can be picked?

options.A: Application Properties; Time Dimension Profile
options.B: Cube Properties; Workflow Channel
options.C: Workflow Profiles, Integration Settings; Entity and Account
options.D: Workflow Profiles, Data Quality Settings; Cube Name and Scenario Type

questions.explanation: D is correct: Rule Profile Settings set the Cube Name and Scenario Type where the profile can be used, and assignment is 'done in the Application Tab| Workflow Profiles| Data Quality Settings section.' A is incorrect — Application Properties is not where it is assigned. B is incorrect — Cube Properties is not where it is assigned. C is incorrect — Integration Settings are for import settings, and Entity/Account are not the Rule Profile settings.

questions.question: Which property exists on Certification Questions but NOT on Confirmation Rules?

options.A: Order
options.B: Frequency
options.C: Risk Level
options.D: Scenario Type Name

questions.explanation: C is correct: Certification Questions have Category and Risk Level ('dictate the importance of the question'); Confirmation Rules have Action, Failure Message and Warning Message instead. A is incorrect — both have Order. B is incorrect — both have Frequency. D is incorrect — both groups have Scenario Type Name.

questions.question: A certification question no longer applies, but auditors need its past answers. What should the administrator do?

options.A: Mark it Deactivated (and set a Deactivated Date) rather than deleting it
options.B: Delete it — responses are archived automatically
options.C: Set Response Optional to True
options.D: Change its Frequency to Yearly

questions.explanation: A is correct: Deactivated makes the question inactive so it no longer appears, and 'all historical responses will be preserved if the question is not deleted.' B is incorrect — preservation depends on not deleting. C is incorrect — the question still appears; answering just becomes optional. D is incorrect — it would still appear once a year.

questions.subtopic: Certification Questions — Question Text and Response
questions.question: How should Certification Question Text be written, and how can a question be made non-mandatory?

options.A: As a numeric threshold; set Action to Warning
options.B: To get a Yes or No response (with a free-text explanation field); check Response Optional
options.C: As a multiple-choice list; set Risk Level to Low
options.D: As a Rule Formula; set Frequency to Member Filter

questions.explanation: B is correct: the question 'should be phrased to illicit a Yes or No response,' with a free-text explanation field, and 'Check this box [Response Optional] in order to make the question optional.' A is incorrect — Action and thresholds belong to Confirmation Rules. C is incorrect — Risk Level shows importance; it does not make a question optional. D is incorrect — Rule Formulas belong to Confirmation Rules.

questions.subtopic: Top Level Cube for Workflow — One Structure per Cube
questions.question: The 'Sales' cube is referenced as a child cube by the 'TotalCorp' cube. An administrator tries to set Is Top Level Cube For Workflow = True on Sales so it can get its own Workflow hierarchy. What does the guide say?

options.A: It works, and Sales gets a second Cube Root Workflow Profile alongside TotalCorp's
options.B: It works only after suffix values are entered for Varying Workflow by Scenario Type on Sales
options.C: It cannot be done: each cube can participate in only one Workflow Management Structure, so a cube referenced by a higher-level cube cannot be a Top-Level Cube for Workflow
options.D: It works only if Sales is first marked as the Default Input cube in Application Properties

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide states each Cube can only participate in one Workflow Management Structure, so if a Cube is referenced by another higher-level Cube it cannot be set as a Top-Level Cube for Workflow. A is incorrect — a referenced cube cannot also be top-level, so no separate Cube Root is possible. B is incorrect — suffix values vary hierarchies within an eligible top-level cube; they do not make a referenced cube eligible. D is incorrect — there is no such property; eligibility is governed by the one-structure-per-cube rule.

questions.question: A new top-level cube has had no Suffix for Varying Workflow by Scenario Type values entered. How many Workflow hierarchies can its Workflow Management Structure have?

options.A: One — by default no suffix values exist, so the cube can only have one hierarchy
options.B: Ten — one per Scenario Type
options.C: Two — one for Actual and one for all planning Scenario Types
options.D: Unlimited — any number of Cube Root profiles can be created for the cube

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says 'By default, no suffix values are created which means the Cube can only have one hierarchy in its Workflow Management Structure'. B is incorrect — ten is the number of Scenario Types that variation can align to, but variation only happens when suffixes are assigned. C is incorrect — there is no built-in Actual/planning split; without suffixes there is one hierarchy. D is incorrect — Cube Root options come from the suffix groups; with none defined there is only one.

questions.subtopic: Creating Cube Root Hierarchies from Suffix Groups
questions.question: The FinancialReporting cube has suffix values Sys, Ent and Oth assigned to different Scenario Types. How does the administrator create the three Workflow hierarchies?

options.A: Click Create Child Under Current Workflow Profile and choose Review
options.B: Click Work with Templates and apply the (Default) template three times
options.C: On the Workflow Profiles screen, click Create a Cube Root Workflow Profile; the engine presents the three hierarchy options for the cube
options.D: Create three Default Input profiles manually, one per suffix

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says clicking Create a Cube Root Workflow Profile automatically presents the three Workflow hierarchy options for the FinancialReporting cube. A is incorrect — that creates a Review/Base Input/Parent Input child, not a new hierarchy. B is incorrect — templates set up Base Input profiles; they don't create hierarchies. D is incorrect — Default Input profiles cannot be created directly; they are generated with each Cube Root.

questions.question: Actual data has been loaded through Workflow for several months. The team now wants to change the cube's suffix values so Actual and Forecast use different Workflow hierarchies. What does the guide say?

options.A: Change the suffix, then close the Cube Root Workflow for prior periods to preserve history
options.B: Change the suffix on the Scenario member's Workflow Tracking Frequency instead
options.C: Change the suffix and use Update Input Children Using Template to rebuild the hierarchy
options.D: The Workflow Management Structure (suffix definitions) cannot be changed after Workflow processing has begun and data is being actively collected

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide states that after Workflow processing has begun and data is being actively collected for the Cube, the suffix definitions cannot be changed. A is incorrect — closing preserves historical hierarchy relationships, but it does not unlock suffix changes. B is incorrect — Workflow Tracking Frequency controls Workflow time periods, not suffix groups. C is incorrect — that button applies template input types; it does not change cube suffix definitions.

questions.question: An audit-driven design requires that data loading and data certification each have their own separate Workflow structures. Which best-practice layout from the guide is this?

options.A: Fully Integrated
options.B: Shared Services
options.C: Separation of Duties
options.D: Central Input

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide describes Separation of Duties as 'Data load and certification each have their own structures'. A is incorrect — this is the complete flow from loading to certification in the same structure. B is incorrect — here loading and certification are integrated, with shared services separated from certification. D is incorrect — Central Input is a channel option for corporate adjustments, not one of the three structure layouts.

questions.subtopic: Create Child Under Current Workflow Profile — Types
questions.question: Which profile type is NOT offered when an administrator uses Create Child Under Current Workflow Profile?

options.A: Default Input
options.B: Review
options.C: Base Input
options.D: Parent Input

questions.explanation: A is correct: the toolbar offers only Review, Base Input and Parent Input; Default Input profiles 'cannot be created directly' and are created automatically with a Cube Root (pp. 699, 706). B is incorrect — Review (reviewer or certification) is one of the three offered types. C is incorrect — Base Input (data load) is one of the three offered types. D is incorrect — Parent Input (parent adjustments) is one of the three offered types.

questions.question: According to the guide, how many different types of Workflow Profiles are available within a Workflow hierarchy?

options.A: Three
options.B: Eight
options.C: Five
options.D: Ten

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide states 'Eight different types of Workflow Profiles are available for use within a Workflow hierarchy' (Cube Root, Review, Default/Parent/Base Input, and the Import/Form/Adjustment children). A is incorrect — three is the number of types offered by Create Child (Review, Base Input, Parent Input). C is incorrect — this undercounts; the input child types are profile types too. D is incorrect — ten is the number of Scenario Types, not Workflow Profile types.

questions.question: An administrator tries to delete the Corporate_Default profile to tidy up a new Workflow hierarchy. What happens?

options.A: It is deleted and recreated the next time the Cube Root is saved
options.B: It is deleted, and all unassigned entities move to the Cube Root profile
options.C: It cannot be deleted — a Default Input profile is required for each Workflow hierarchy
options.D: It can be deleted only after Profile Active is set to False

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says a Default Input profile, prefixed with the Cube Root name (e.g., Corporate_Default), is required for each Workflow hierarchy and cannot be deleted. A is incorrect — the guide says it cannot be deleted at all. B is incorrect — it cannot be deleted; unassigned entities belong to the Default Input. D is incorrect — Profile Active toggles input channels; it doesn't allow deleting the Default Input.

questions.question: Which statement about Review Workflow Profiles is true?

options.A: They are where entities are bound to the Workflow for data loading
options.B: They have no direct relationship to an Entity or Origin member but can have Calculation Definitions assigned
options.C: They must have at least one Import, Form and Adjustment child
options.D: They cannot run calculations because they take no input

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Review Profiles have no direct relationship to an Entity or Origin Member, but can have Calculation Definitions so Cube calculations run in a controlled way during sign-off. A is incorrect — that is the role of Input Parent profiles. C is incorrect — that requirement applies to Input Parent profiles. D is incorrect — they can't take input, but they can have Calculation Definitions.

questions.question: Why must every Input Parent profile have at least one Input Child of each type (Import, Form and Adjustment)?

options.A: Because Calculation Definitions run only on Import children
options.B: Because Workflow Channels must be assigned once per child type
options.C: Because of the relationship between Input Child profiles and the Origin dimension members
options.D: Because the Cube Root needs one child per type to show its Open/Closed state

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the requirement 'exists because of the relationship between Input Child Profiles and the Origin Dimension Members'. A is incorrect — Calculation Definitions aren't limited to Import children, and this isn't the stated reason. B is incorrect — Workflow Channels are optional security layers, not the reason. D is incorrect — Cube Root state is unrelated to child types.

questions.question: An administrator wants to explicitly assign the entity 'Corp HQ' to the Corporate_Default profile on the Entity Assignment tab. What does the guide say?

options.A: Entities cannot be explicitly assigned to a Default Input profile; they belong to it implicitly when not assigned anywhere else
options.B: It works like any Base Input assignment
options.C: It works only for parent entities
options.D: It works only after the entity is unassigned from its Review profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says 'Entities cannot be explicitly assigned to a Default Input Profile'; any entity not explicitly assigned to a Parent Input or Base Input profile is implicitly assigned to the Default. B is incorrect — Default Input profiles don't accept explicit assignments. C is incorrect — no entity can be explicitly assigned to the Default Input. D is incorrect — Review profiles don't hold entity assignments in the first place.

questions.question: An administrator creates a Parent Input profile and finds an Import child under it. What is true about that Import child?

options.A: It is active and loads to O#Import for the parent entity
options.B: It is created automatically but forced to be inactive (Profile Active = False), because parent entities can only be adjusted through Forms or AdjInput
options.C: It must be deleted before the profile can be saved
options.D: It loads to O#AdjInput instead of O#Import

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the engine automatically creates an Import Child for each Parent Input profile, but forces it inactive, since parent adjustments are only allowed via Forms or AdjInput. A is incorrect — imports aren't allowed for Parent Input profiles. C is incorrect — it's kept but forced inactive. D is incorrect — Import children are tied to the Import origin member; on a Parent Input the child is simply inactive.

questions.subtopic: Parent Input — Which Parents to Assign
questions.question: In a 500-entity application, which parent entities need to be explicitly assigned to a Parent Input Workflow Profile?

options.A: All parent entities, so the Workflow can consolidate them
options.B: All parent entities that have IC activity
options.C: None; parent entities can only be adjusted from a Review profile
options.D: Only parent entities that must accept adjustments; the rest stay unassigned and are controlled by the Default Input profile

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says parent entities don't need explicit assignment unless they need to be adjusted, and most remain unassigned under the Default Input. A is incorrect — consolidation doesn't require parent assignment. B is incorrect — IC activity isn't the criterion. C is incorrect — Review profiles take no input; parent adjustments use Parent Input profiles.

questions.question: An Input Child profile (Import, Form or Adjustment) can be a child of which profile types?

options.A: Review, Parent Input or Base Input
options.B: Cube Root or Base Input
options.C: Any profile type, including another Input Child
options.D: Default Input, Parent Input or Base Input only

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Input Child types are always base members and 'can only be children of one of the three types of Input Profiles: Default, Parent or Base'. A is incorrect — Review profiles take no input and can't hold input children. B is incorrect — Cube Root is the top of the hierarchy; input children sit under input profiles. C is incorrect — input children are always base members, so they can't have children.

questions.question: An administrator selects a Base Input profile and looks for the Entity Assignment tab, but it isn't there. Where is it available?

options.A: Only on Review profiles
options.B: Only on the Default Input profile
options.C: Only in the Workflow Profile Grid View
options.D: Only when the Cube Root Workflow Profile is selected

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the Entity Assignment tab 'is only available when clicking on the Cube Root Workflow Profile'; from there the admin picks a profile and uses Unassigned Entities. A is incorrect — Review profiles have no entity relationship. B is incorrect — entities can't be explicitly assigned to the Default Input. C is incorrect — the Grid View is for bulk property changes, not the Entity Assignment tab.

questions.question: Which statement about the Unassigned Entities search on the Entity Assignment tab is true?

options.A: It uses 'contains' matching, and an entity disappears from the search once it is attached to a profile
options.B: It uses 'starts with' matching only
options.C: It is enabled for Review profiles too
options.D: Attached entities stay in the list, shown in grey

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the search uses 'contains' technology (whole or partial word), is only enabled for data loading profiles, and attached entities no longer appear. B is incorrect — it matches anywhere in the name. C is incorrect — it's only enabled for data loading profiles. D is incorrect — attached entities no longer appear.

questions.question: An administrator needs to change a property on 60 Workflow Profiles at once and group them by a column. What does the guide say about the Workflow Profile Grid View?

options.A: It is only available when the Cube Root Profile is selected
options.B: It is only available from the Workflow Templates screen
options.C: It is read-only and used only to export settings
options.D: It is only available on Base Input profiles

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the Grid View lets admins change many profiles at once, supports dragging a column label to the top to group data, and 'is only available when the Cube Root Profile is selected'. B is incorrect — it's on the Workflow Profiles screen with a Cube Root selected. C is incorrect — it's for making changes in bulk. D is incorrect — it requires the Cube Root profile.

questions.question: A template was applied to 40 Base Input profiles. The administrator then (1) changes the Forms input type's settings in the template and (2) adds a new 'Stats' input type. What can be pushed to the existing profiles?

options.A: Both changes, by reapplying the template
options.B: Only the Forms change; new input types must be added by hand
options.C: Neither; templates only apply when a profile is first created
options.D: Only the new Stats input type, using Update Input Children Using Template

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says changes to existing input types (Import, Forms, Journals) can't be applied after a template is applied, but a new input type can, via the Update Input Children Using Template button. A is incorrect — changes to existing input types can't be applied. B is incorrect — this is the opposite of what the guide says. C is incorrect — new input types can be applied to existing profiles.

questions.question: Which dimension is NOT a member of the Level 1 Cube Data Unit?

options.A: Parent
options.B: Account
options.C: Consolidation
options.D: Time

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists Cube, Entity, Parent, Consolidation, Scenario and Time as Cube data unit members; Account is added at Level 2, the Workflow data unit. A is incorrect — Parent is a Cube data unit member. C is incorrect — Consolidation is a Cube data unit member. D is incorrect — Time is a Cube data unit member.

questions.question: When is the Cube data unit locked by Workflow?

options.A: When any Review profile above the entity is opened
options.B: When the Import child completes the Validate step
options.C: When an Input Parent Workflow Profile is locked or certified, provided the entity is assigned to that profile
options.D: Only when the Cube Root Workflow is closed

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says 'The Cube data unit is locked when an input parent workflow profile is locked or certified, provided an entity is assigned to this parent workflow step'. A is incorrect — opening doesn't lock; Review profiles have no entity assignments. B is incorrect — validation doesn't lock the Cube data unit. D is incorrect — the Input Parent lock or certification is what's documented.

questions.question: At what level does the Workflow Engine control loading, clearing and locking by default when processing Stage data into the cube, if no Workflow Channels are in use?

options.A: The Workflow data unit (Level 2), which includes the Account dimension
options.B: The Cube data unit (Level 1)
options.C: The Workflow Channel data unit (Level 3)
options.D: The individual Stage row (Source ID)

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the workflow data unit is the default level used to control, load, clear and lock data during Stage processing, and its granularity includes the account dimension by default. B is incorrect — Stage loads are more granular than entity/scenario/time; they include Account. C is incorrect — Level 3 is used only when Workflow Channels are active. D is incorrect — the guide describes data-unit levels, not row-level control.

questions.question: Which analytic work item applies to the Cube data unit but NOT to the Workflow data unit or Workflow Channel data unit?

options.A: Clear data
options.B: Lock data
options.C: Translate
options.D: Load data

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide lists Clear, Load, Lock, Copy, Calculate, Translate and Consolidate for the Cube data unit, but only Clear, Load and Lock for the Workflow and Workflow Channel data units. A is incorrect — clearing applies at all three levels. B is incorrect — locking applies at all three levels. D is incorrect — loading applies at all three levels.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Channel Data Unit — Budget Contention
questions.question: In a cost center budget, many users submit data for different cost centers to the same entity and accounts, causing data contention. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Create a separate cube for each cost center
options.B: Set Load Overlapped Siblings to False
options.C: Assign every cost center to the NoDataLock channel
options.D: Assign the user-defined dimension holding cost centers as the Workflow Channel UD dimension, so each entity/cost center loads, clears and locks independently

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide's Workflow Channel budget example says assigning the cost center UD as the Workflow Channel dimension makes each entity/cost center act as an autonomous cell collection. A is incorrect — the guide solves this with the Level 3 data unit, not more cubes. B is incorrect — that skips overlap checks among sibling imports; it doesn't split by cost center. C is incorrect — NoDataLock removes channel control, the opposite of what's needed.

questions.question: When the Workflow Engine loads imported data from Stage to the cube, which Consolidation dimension member is the data forced to?

options.A: Translated
options.B: Top
options.C: OwnerPreAdj
options.D: Local

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says 'The workflow engine also forces imported data to use the local member of the consolidation dimension'. A is incorrect — Translated holds currency-translated values from the engine. B is incorrect — Top is the full consolidated result, not a load target. C is incorrect — OwnerPreAdj is a consolidation-calculated member.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the Workflow Engine's Clear and Replace data load steps?

options.A: Analyze prior loads → check workflow state → execute clear → check switches → execute load
options.B: Check workflow state → check data load switches → analyze prior data loads → execute clear → execute load
options.C: Check data load switches → execute clear → check workflow state → execute load
options.D: Execute clear → execute load → check workflow state → analyze prior loads

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists: 1) check workflow state (implicit/explicit lock), 2) check profile data load switches, 3) analyze prior data loads, 4) execute clear, then execute load (pp. 738–739). A is incorrect — workflow state is checked first, and switches are checked before clearing. C is incorrect — lock state is checked first, before any clearing. D is incorrect — clearing and loading are the last steps.

questions.question: How does the Workflow Engine run the load-data step of a Workflow load?

options.A: Sequentially by account in Account dimension order
options.B: In parallel by time period across the year
options.C: One Workflow Channel at a time
options.D: In parallel by entity — multiple entities process at the same time

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says 'Data loads using parallel processing by entity. Multiple entities process at the same time'. A is incorrect — the guide describes parallel processing by entity. B is incorrect — parallelism is by entity, not period. C is incorrect — parallelism is by entity.

questions.question: Under the San Diego Input Parent, 'Import GL Data' and 'Import Sales Detail' both load entity SD01, account 4000. GL loads 100 and Sales Detail loads 50. Load Overlapped Siblings is at its default. What lands in the cell?

options.A: 50 — the last sibling loaded replaces the first
options.B: 150 — overlapping siblings are cleared and reloaded with an accumulate load in hierarchy order, so values in the same cell are added
options.C: 100 — the first sibling in the hierarchy takes priority
options.D: The load fails with an overlapping data unit error

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says if siblings have overlapped data units, the engine clears both and reloads them using an accumulate load method in hierarchy order, and same-cell values 'are added together'. A is incorrect — last-in-wins only applies when Load Overlapped Siblings is False. C is incorrect — there's no priority rule; values accumulate. D is incorrect — the engine handles the overlap by accumulating; it doesn't fail.

questions.question: Central HR Load has Can Load Unrelated Entities = True and loads payroll to entities owned by Houston. Houston is certified. What happens when Central HR Load runs its load?

options.A: The load succeeds because Can Load Unrelated Entities overrides locks
options.B: The load succeeds and Houston is automatically un-certified
options.C: The data is accumulated with Houston's data in the same cells
options.D: Updates to Houston's entities are disallowed — Central HR Load follows the workflow and lock status of the profiles that own the entities

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Central HR Load doesn't control any entities, so it checks the lock/certification status of the owning profiles, and the engine disallows updates if Houston is certified or locked. A is incorrect — that setting allows loading unassigned entities but still respects their owners' status. B is incorrect — certification isn't reversed automatically. C is incorrect — accumulation applies to overlapping import siblings, not a locked owner.

questions.question: To boost parallel performance, Load Overlapped Siblings is set to False on a parent whose sibling import channels might overlap. If an overlap does occur, what happens?

options.A: The overlapping values are added together
options.B: The load fails and asks the user to re-run it in sequence
options.C: Sibling overlap checks are skipped, so the last processed channel overwrites the prior one
options.D: The first processed channel's values are kept

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says False means 'Do not check sibling channels for overlapping data units. If an overlapping condition occurs, the last processed channel overwrites the prior.' True is the default. A is incorrect — accumulation happens with the default True. B is incorrect — the guide says the last channel overwrites, not fails. D is incorrect — the last processed channel wins.

questions.subtopic: Stage Import Methods — Standard and Drill-Down
questions.question: A consolidation application is the book-of-record. Auditors must be able to drill down from a Cube value to the source and target Stage records for any current or historical period. Which Workflow Stage Import method meets this?

options.A: Direct
options.B: Blend
options.C: Direct with Blob storage
options.D: Standard

questions.explanation: D is correct: Standard stores each import's source and target records in Stage tables, so every period can be audited and Drill-Down from Finance to Stage works. A is incorrect — Direct is in-memory and does not store record details, so Drill-Down does not function. B is incorrect — Blend writes to external relational BI Blend tables, not a Finance Engine Cube. C is incorrect — Blob only changes how Direct stores summarized rows; Direct still keeps no source/target record detail.

questions.subtopic: Import Volumes — Row Limit vs Best Practice
questions.question: A team is sizing one Workflow import. What are the guide's row limit per Workflow and its best-practice recommendation, both measured in summarized records?

options.A: Limit 24 million; best practice 10 million
options.B: Limit 1 million; best practice 100,000
options.C: Limit 50,000; best practice 1,000
options.D: Limit 24 million; best practice 1 million

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide lists Row Limit Per Workflow = 24 million summarized records and Best-Practice Recommendation = 1 million summarized records. B is incorrect — 1 million is the best practice, not the hard limit. C is incorrect — 50,000 and 1,000 are the Direct Load error storage and error presentation limits. A is incorrect — the best practice is 1 million, not 10 million.

questions.question: In which Stage table are transformed source records summarized (the table whose row count drives the Workflow volume guidelines)?

options.A: StageDirectLoadInformation
options.B: StageAttributeData
options.C: StageSourceData
options.D: StageSummaryTargetData

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'The transformed source records are summarized in the StageSummaryTargetData table.' A is incorrect — StageDirectLoadInformation holds the serialized byte array only when a Direct Load uses Blob storage. C is incorrect — source data is not where the summarized target rows are counted. B is incorrect — attribute data is not the summarized target table the guide names.

questions.question: A single Workflow produces 24 million summarized records. The guide's best-practice solution is to parse the file across 24 partitioned Workflows. Which is NOT a benefit the guide lists for this partitioning?

options.A: Performance gains through parallel processing
options.B: Faster mapping and error correction
options.C: More transparent data validation
options.D: Drill-Down from Finance to Stage becomes available

questions.explanation: D is correct: Drill-Down depends on the import method (Standard stores records), not on partitioning; it is not in the list of benefits. A is incorrect — parallel processing gains are listed. B is incorrect — faster mapping and error correction is listed. C is incorrect — more transparent data validation is listed (along with shorter processing times).

questions.subtopic: Import Record Analysis — Where to Find Counts
questions.question: An administrator wants the total number of summary records produced by a Standard Workflow load. Where does the guide say to look?

options.A: Direct Load Status / Execution Status, Summary Row Count
options.B: BI Blend Processing Logs, Live Row Count
options.C: Task Activity / Load Cube, the SelectStageSummaryTargetRows entry
options.D: Audit Workflow Process, Lock History

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'OneStream Task Activity / Load Cube presents the details of the total number of summary records in the SelectStageSummaryTargetRows entry' for Standard Workflows. A is incorrect — that screen is for Direct Workflows. B is incorrect — those statistics are for Blend record analysis. D is incorrect — Audit Workflow Process shows task history and lock/unlock history, not summary row counts.

questions.question: How does the Blend import process differ from Standard and Direct in terms of record counts?

options.A: It summarizes source rows exactly like Standard
options.B: It loads one-to-one with no summarization or additional rows
options.C: It discards rows that do not map to a Cube intersection
options.D: It generates additional rows because Analytic Blend designs need aggregation points

questions.explanation: D is correct: Blend 'differs from other Stage Import processes by generating additional data records, or rows, rather than one-to-one or summarizations' because of aggregation points. A is incorrect — summarization is the Standard/Direct behavior. B is incorrect — the guide says Blend adds rows rather than loading one-to-one. C is incorrect — Blend writes to relational tables, not Cube intersections.

questions.question: Which functionality is still available in a Direct Load Workflow?

options.A: Drill-Down from the Finance Engine Cube to Stage source records
options.B: Import and Transformation Rule history
options.C: Appending to prior Imports
options.D: Business Rules, Transformation Rules and Derivative Rules

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says all other Workflow functionality remains in the Direct type, such as all Business Rules, Transformation Rules and Derivative Rules. A is incorrect — Drill-Down does not function with Direct Load. B is incorrect — Direct does not support historical audit of Import and Transformation Rule history. C is incorrect — Direct is inappropriate where loads must Append to prior Imports.

questions.question: A user fixes several Transformation Rules after a Direct Load import fails validation. How does the user apply the corrected rules?

options.A: Click Retransform on the Validate step
options.B: Run Load Cube again
options.C: Re-load the data
options.D: Use Clear All 'Import' Data From Cube and then Validate

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Direct Load Type does not support Re-Transform as Import records are not stored data. Data must be re-loaded.' A is incorrect — Retransform needs stored Stage records, which Direct does not keep. B is incorrect — Direct has no separate Load Cube step; it is a single Load And Transform. D is incorrect — clearing Cube data does not re-run transformations.

questions.question: Which scenario does the guide list as a common use for the Direct Load Workflow?

options.A: Extended Application moves from a detailed app to a summarized target app
options.B: Monthly trial balance loads that serve as book-of-record data for statutory consolidation
options.C: Loads where auditors must drill down from Cube cells to the underlying Stage source records
options.D: Loads that must keep source file and Transformation Rule history for historical reference

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists Extended Application data moves from a detailed application to a summarized target as a common Direct Load use, along with disposable data and high-volume nightly loads. B is incorrect — consolidations need durable, auditable book-of-record data (Standard). C is incorrect — Drill-Down is not supported by Direct. D is incorrect — Direct is not appropriate where source file import history is required.

questions.question: A Direct Load Workflow combines Parse/Transform, Validate Transformations and Intersections, and Load Cube. What is the single Workflow step called?

options.A: Load And Transform
options.B: Import, Validate, Load
options.C: Load Cube
options.D: Process Cube

questions.explanation: A is correct: Direct is an in-memory Workflow 'with only a single step for the data integration process, Load And Transform.' B is incorrect — that is the standard multi-step Import sequence the Direct type collapses. C is incorrect — Load Cube is the separate Load step in a Standard Workflow. D is incorrect — Process Cube runs calculations in the Process step, not the data integration.

questions.question: On the Direct Load Execution Status screen, which statistic should always equal the Summary Row Count?

options.A: Detailed Row Count
options.B: Error Row Count
options.C: Live Row Count
options.D: Loaded Row Count

questions.explanation: D is correct: Loaded Row Count is 'the recorded number of records loaded to the Finance Engine target Cube, which should always equal the Summary Row Count.' A is incorrect — Detailed Row Count is the total of Data Source and Derivative Rule records, before summarization. B is incorrect — no such equality is described for errors. C is incorrect — Live Row Count is a BI Blend statistic.

questions.question: A Direct Load import has 3,500 transformation errors. What happens, per the guide?

options.A: All 3,500 errors are shown on pageable Validation screens
options.B: Errors beyond 1,000 are written to StageSummaryTargetData for later review
options.C: The load is rejected because Direct Loads allow at most 1,000 errors in total
options.D: Up to 1,000 errors are presented per load; the data must be re-loaded to see the next batch

questions.explanation: D is correct: the error presentation limit is 1,000 records per Import load; if errors exceed 1,000, 'the data must be re-loaded' to generate the next batch (total Direct Load error storage limit is 50,000). A is incorrect — pageable Validation is a Standard Workflow feature. C is incorrect — the total storage limit is 50,000, not 1,000. B is incorrect — Direct Load errors are not stored in a table.

questions.question: An integration has complex mapping, and the team wants to use a Direct Load in production. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Use a Standard Workflow as 'development' to finalize core Transformation Rules, then a Direct Load as 'production'
options.B: Use a Blend Workflow as development, then convert it to Direct
options.C: Use Blob storage during development and switch to Row for production
options.D: Raise the 1,000-record error presentation limit in Application Properties during development

questions.explanation: A is correct: complex integrations 'may benefit by having a development, Standard Workflow, to finalize the core Transformation Rules'; once done, a production Direct Load manages only the Validation exceptions. B is incorrect — Blend targets relational tables, not Cubes, and is not the recommended development path. C is incorrect — Row/Blob only controls storage of summarized rows. D is incorrect — the guide states no such setting; the limit is fixed per load.

questions.question: How is a Direct Load Type Workflow configured?

options.A: As an Import channel Workflow using one of the 'Direct' Workflow Names
options.B: As a Forms channel Workflow with the Direct setting turned on
options.C: By setting the Cube's Data Storage property to Direct
options.D: By selecting Direct as the Load Method in the Load and Transform dialog

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'The Direct Load Type Workflow is an Import channel Workflow configured using various combinations of the Direct Workflow Name.' B is incorrect — Direct is an Import channel type, not Forms. C is incorrect — it is a Workflow Name choice, not a Cube property. D is incorrect — the Load Methods are Replace, Replace (All Time), Replace Background and Append.

questions.question: Which statement about Direct Load summarized data storage is correct?

options.A: Blob is the default and stores rows in StageSummaryTargetData
options.B: Row is the default; Blob stores summarized records as a serialized byte array in StageDirectLoadInformation
options.C: Row stores records in StageDirectLoadInformation; Blob stores them in StageSummaryTargetData
options.D: Both options store source and target detail so Drill-Down works

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'the default being Row' — Row stores transformed summary records in StageSummaryTargetData; Blob stores them 'as a serialized Byte array stored in the StageDirectLoadInformation.' A is incorrect — Row, not Blob, is the default. C is incorrect — it swaps the two tables. D is incorrect — neither stores source/target record detail; Drill-Down does not work for Direct.

questions.question: A monthly Direct Load Workflow is run for M1, but the source file also contains records for M2. What happens?

options.A: M2 records load to M2 because Direct supports multi-period files
options.B: M2 records are appended to M1
options.C: M2 records cannot load — a Direct Load cannot load data beyond the current Workflow Scenario and Time
options.D: M2 records load only if Allow Loads After Workflow View Year is True

questions.explanation: C is correct: Direct Load source file Data Keys must match the Workflow Data Keys; 'an Import to M1 cannot contain records for M2 in a Monthly Workflow.' A is incorrect — that is a Standard Workflow capability, not Direct. B is incorrect — Direct cannot append to prior imports either. D is incorrect — that property governs loads outside the Workflow year, not the Direct restriction.

questions.question: Which API function must an Extender Business Rule call to run batch file processing through the Workflow?

options.A: BRApi.Utilities.ExecuteDataMgmtSequence
options.B: BRApi.Journals.Data.ImportAndProcessJournals
options.C: BRApi.Utilities.ExecuteFileHarvestBatch
options.D: BRApi.Finance.Data.SetDataCell

questions.explanation: C is correct: batch processing uses an Extender Business Rule that calls BRAPi.Utilities.ExecuteFileHarvestBatch, which also accepts switches controlling how far Workflow processing goes. A is incorrect — that runs a DM sequence, not the file harvest batch. B is incorrect — that loads journal files. D is incorrect — that writes individual data cells.

questions.question: How is the batch file processing Extender Business Rule executed in the documented setup?

options.A: It runs automatically when a file is dropped in the Batch\Harvest folder
options.B: From the Import step of an Import Workflow Profile
options.C: From a Business Rule Data Management Step in a Data Management Sequence
options.D: From the Task Scheduler only, with no Data Management object

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says to create a Business Rule Data Management Step that calls the Extender Business Rule, and to run the Data Management Sequence after copying files to the Harvest folder. A is incorrect — files are processed when the sequence is executed, not automatically on drop. B is incorrect — batch processing is run through Data Management, not a manual Import click. D is incorrect — scheduling still runs the Data Management Sequence (via PowerShell or another scheduler).

questions.question: Where does OneStream automatically create the folder that batch files must be copied into?

options.A: File Share|Applications|Application Name|Batch|Harvest
options.B: File Share|Applications|Application Name|Incoming
options.C: File Share|Content|Batch|Harvest
options.D: Application Database|Batch|Harvest

questions.explanation: A is correct: OneStream creates a Batch\Harvest folder in each application's file share: System Tab|File Explorer|File Share|Applications|Application Name|Batch|Harvest. B is incorrect — Incoming is not the batch harvest folder. C is incorrect — the folder is under the application's folder. D is incorrect — the guide describes a File Share path.

questions.question: After a batch runs, which TWO sources of results does the guide describe?

options.A: A Task Activity entry for the batch, and a results object returned to the Extender Business Rule
options.B: An email to the administrator, and an Error Log entry
options.C: A Workflow Audit entry, and a new file in the Harvest folder
options.D: The Direct Load Execution Status screen, and the BI Blend Processing Log

questions.explanation: A is correct: each batch 'creates a detailed Task Activity entry', and the function 'returns a detailed results object to the Extender Business Rule' that can drive custom reporting and notification. B is incorrect — email is not described; notifications must be built from the results object. C is incorrect — these are not the described outputs. D is incorrect — those screens are for Direct and Blend imports.

questions.subtopic: Batch File Name — C and G Substitutions
questions.question: In a batch file name, what does the letter G mean in the Scenario or Time segment (for example, A-Houston;Import-G-2011M1-R.txt)?

options.A: The Scenario passed in the HarvestAndProcessFiles function call
options.B: The Workflow's Current DataKey from the Data Source
options.C: Generic — the batch engine picks the latest open period
options.D: The Global Scenario (or Global Time) set for the application

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'G can be passed as a substitution variable to reference the Global Scenario name set for the application' (and likewise Global Time). A is incorrect — that is C (current), which references the name passed in HarvestAndProcessFiles. B is incorrect — the Current DataKey dimension type is how the name reaches Data Sources, not what G means. C is incorrect — there is no 'Generic' option.

questions.question: A parameter list must show only base entities the current user can read or write. Which Where clause fits?

options.A: E#[Total GolfStream].Base.Where((IsIC = True) or (Currency = EUR))
options.B: E#[Total GolfStream].Base.Where((UserInReadDataGroup = True) or (UserInReadWriteDataGroup = True))
options.C: E#[Total GolfStream].Base.Where((Text1 = 'ReadData') or (Text2 = 'ReadWriteData'))
options.D: E#Root.WFProfileEntities

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says User In Security Group Where clauses restrict the list to members the user can read and write, with this exact OR example. A is incorrect — IsIC and Currency filter on intercompany and currency properties, not security. C is incorrect — TextN properties are free-form, not security. D is incorrect — it returns the profile's entities, regardless of user security.

questions.question: Which substitution variable returns the Scenario selected in the user's Workflow View?

options.A: GlobalScenario
options.B: WFScenarioDim
options.C: WFScenario
options.D: WFProfile

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says WFScenario returns the Scenario in the Workflow View. A is incorrect — GlobalScenario is the Global POV Scenario from Application Properties. B is incorrect — WFScenarioDim returns the Scenario Dimension for the profile's Cube. D is incorrect — WFProfile returns the profile name.

questions.question: What determines the period returned by |WFTimeFirstInYear|?

options.A: The Workflow Start Time entry for the Scenario
options.B: The Scenario's Input Frequency (W1, M1, Q1 or H1)
options.C: The Global Time in Application Properties
options.D: The Time Dimension Profile's fiscal year start only

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says WFTimeFirstInYear is the same as T#WFFirstInYear, T#W1, T#M1, T#Q1 or T#H1 based on the Scenario's Input Frequency. A is incorrect — that is WFStartTime. C is incorrect — that is GlobalTime. D is incorrect — the guide ties it to Input Frequency.

questions.question: A Cube Root Workflow is in the Open state for Actual, 2026M6. Which statement is true?

options.A: A high-level lock applies and individual profile lock statuses are ignored
options.B: Locking is controlled at the individual Workflow Profile level, and the hierarchy is read from memory (cache)
options.C: The hierarchy is read from a historical audit table
options.D: Input children are locked but Review profiles remain open

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says that in the Open state locking is controlled at the individual profile level and the hierarchy is accessed from memory (cache), giving very fast read performance. A is incorrect — this describes the Closed state. C is incorrect — reading from the historical table happens for a Closed Workflow. D is incorrect — the guide doesn't describe this split; in the Open state locking is per profile.

questions.question: After an administrator closes the Cube Root Workflow for Actual, 2025M12, users say opening that period's full Workflow hierarchy is slower. Why?

options.A: Closing recalculates every Calculation Definition in the hierarchy on first access
options.B: Closing forces every entity's data to be re-locked cell by cell on read
options.C: A closed Workflow is a point-in-time snapshot stored in a historical audit table and must be read from the database rather than cache
options.D: Closing moves the period's Stage data to an archive database

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says closing takes a snapshot into a historical audit table, so the hierarchy is read from the database instead of memory — a known performance penalty. A is incorrect — closing doesn't trigger calculations. B is incorrect — the closed state places one high-level lock; it doesn't re-lock cells on read. D is incorrect — the snapshot is of the hierarchy structure, not Stage data.

questions.question: When does the guide recommend closing a Workflow hierarchy?

options.A: At every month-end after all profiles are certified, to lock the period
options.B: Whenever a user needs to reload data to a certified profile
options.C: Only when major changes are being made to the Workflow hierarchy and cube structure and historical hierarchy relationships need to be preserved
options.D: Before every Consolidate, to improve calculation performance

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Workflow hierarchies 'should only be closed if major changes are being made to the Workflow hierarchy and the structure of a Cube and historical hierarchy relationships need to be preserved'. A is incorrect — certification and locking handle period control; closing is reserved for preserving history before major changes. B is incorrect — closing places a higher lock and would block, not enable, loading. D is incorrect — closing actually costs read performance and is unrelated to consolidation.

questions.question: On the Houston Base Input profile, the only Forms child has Profile Active = False. A user tries to send values to a Houston entity through an Excel Cube View. What happens?

options.A: The values save to O#AdjInput instead of O#Forms
options.B: The values save because Excel bypasses Workflow
options.C: The values can't be saved — with no active Form child, forms and Excel (SetCells or Cube Views) can't set data for Houston's entities
options.D: The values save but are flagged for the Confirm step

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says if a Forms child has Profile Active = False and no other active Form siblings exist, data entry forms and Excel cannot set cell values for the Input Parent's entities. A is incorrect — disabling the Form channel doesn't reroute data to another origin. B is incorrect — Excel data entry is controlled by the Form channel too. D is incorrect — the channel is disabled, so nothing is saved.

questions.question: A new data entry Cube View for a Forms channel shows every cell as read-only, although the user has write access. The Cube View's POV uses O#Import. What is the fix?

options.A: Set the Origin member to Forms — Form children require it or cells appear read-only
options.B: Set the Origin member to Top
options.C: Set the Origin member to AdjInput
options.D: Set Can Load Unrelated Entities to True

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says that for data entry forms 'the Origin Member must be set to Forms or the data cell will appear as read only'. B is incorrect — Top is a calculated aggregate, not an input member. C is incorrect — AdjInput is for journals unless the account's Adjustment Type is Data Entry; the Forms channel requires Forms. D is incorrect — that setting governs loading to unassigned entities, not the origin of a form.

questions.subtopic: Form Entry to AdjInput — Adjustment Type
questions.question: A team wants to use a data entry form to update the AdjInput origin member for a specific account. What must be true of that account?

options.A: Its Adjustment Type must remain Journal, the default
options.B: Its Adjustment Type must be Data Entry instead of the default Journal
options.C: Its Workflow Channel must be AllChannelInput
options.D: Its Is IC Account property must be True

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says forms can update AdjInput 'but this requires the account being updated to have its Adjustment Type set to Data Entry rather than the default value of Journal'. A is incorrect — Journal is the default that blocks form entry to AdjInput. C is incorrect — Workflow Channel is a separate security layer, not the requirement. D is incorrect — the IC flag is unrelated to form entry into AdjInput.

questions.question: Which pairing of Input Child type to the Origin member the Workflow Engine enforces is correct?

options.A: Import → Import; Form → Forms; Adjustment → AdjInput
options.B: Import → Import; Form → AdjInput; Adjustment → Forms
options.C: Import → Top; Form → Forms; Adjustment → AdjConsolidated
options.D: Import → BeforeAdj; Form → Forms; Adjustment → AdjInput

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says Import children force Origin to Import, Form children require Forms, and Adjustment children force AdjInput. B is incorrect — Forms and AdjInput are swapped. C is incorrect — Import children are forced to Import, and journals go to AdjInput, not AdjConsolidated. D is incorrect — BeforeAdj is an aggregate member; imports are forced to Import.

questions.subtopic: Load YTD and MTD — Where to Configure
questions.question: The Actual Scenario's Default View is YTD. In the Houston profile, Houston.Import submits YTD, but Houston.Sales Detail submits periodic data. Where is Sales Detail configured to behave as periodic?

options.A: Change the Actual Scenario member's Default View to Periodic
options.B: Select the Houston.Sales Detail input child, pick the Scenario Type (or (Default) for all), and change its Integration Settings
options.C: On the Houston Cube Root profile's Entity Assignment tab
options.D: In the Sales Detail Data Source's Amount field properties

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says to expand the Workflow Profile, select the Origin (input child) to configure, choose the Scenario Type (or (Default)), then change Integration Settings. A is incorrect — that changes the whole Scenario, including Houston.Import, which must stay YTD. C is incorrect — Entity Assignment binds entities; it doesn't set view behavior. D is incorrect — the guide places this on the Workflow Profile's Integration Settings, not the Data Source.

questions.question: After an input child is configured to submit MTD/periodic data in a Scenario whose Default View is YTD, how are accounts processed?

options.A: Both Flow and Balance accounts process as Periodic
options.B: Flow accounts stay YTD; Balance accounts become Periodic
options.C: All accounts follow the View member in each file row
options.D: Flow-type accounts process as Periodic; Balance accounts are still forced to YTD

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Flow Type accounts are processed as Periodic rather than YTD, while Balance accounts are forced to YTD on submission. A is incorrect — Balance accounts are forced to YTD. B is incorrect — this is backwards. C is incorrect — the configuration overrides file views for Flow accounts, and Balance accounts are forced to YTD.

questions.question: A top-side adjustment must be made to a Parent Entity through a Parent Input Workflow Profile using a form. Which Origin member is updated?

options.A: AdjInput
options.B: Forms
options.C: Import
options.D: AdjConsolidated

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says top-side adjustments through a Parent Input profile, by journal or form, both update the AdjInput member of the Origin dimension. B is incorrect — Base Input form entry uses Forms, but Parent adjustments by form or journal update AdjInput. C is incorrect — Import Children are not allowed for Parent Input profiles. D is incorrect — the guide names AdjInput for Parent Input adjustments.

questions.question: An administrator adds a description to a Workflow Profile so users see it when choosing a Workflow in OnePlace. Where must the description be entered for it to show in the Workflow Profile POV dialog?

options.A: In the Actual Scenario Type configuration
options.B: In the (Default) Scenario configuration of the profile
options.C: In the WFText1 field of the profile
options.D: In the Cube Root profile's Entity Assignment tab

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide notes that a description added in the Default Scenario will display in the Workflow Profile POV dialog in OnePlace. A is incorrect — the note specifies the Default Scenario. C is incorrect — WFText1–4 are optional text fields used as substitution variables, not the POV dialog description. D is incorrect — that tab is for binding entities.

questions.question: A controller can create and approve journals in the Houston Adjustment channel but the Post button never becomes available for her. She is not an administrator. Which group is she most likely missing?

options.A: Journal Post Group
options.B: Journal Process Group
options.C: Journal Approval Group
options.D: Certification SignOff Group

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says access to the Journal Post Group 'allows users to post a journal'. B is incorrect — that allows processing (creating/submitting) journals, which she can already do. C is incorrect — that allows approving, which she can already do. D is incorrect — that's for signing off on the Workflow, not posting journals.

questions.question: A senior accountant must be able to approve journals in a Workflow Profile but should not create or post them. Which group should she be in?

options.A: Certification SignOff Group
options.B: Journal Approval Group
options.C: Journal Process Group
options.D: Journal Post Group

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says access to the Journal Approval Group allows users to approve a journal. A is incorrect — Certification SignOff is for signing off the Workflow, not journal approval. C is incorrect — Journal Process allows users to process (create) journals. D is incorrect — Journal Post allows users to post journals.

questions.question: Prevent Self-Post is set to True (not 'True (includes Admins)'). An application administrator creates a journal in this Workflow Profile. What can the administrator do?

options.A: Only Submit; Approve and Post are disabled
options.B: Nothing — the journal must be posted by another administrator
options.C: Still use Quick Post
options.D: Post only after removing themselves from the Journal Post Group

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says with True, members of the Journal Post group can't post their own journals, but 'Administrators still have access to the Quick Post action'.
