A is incorrect — those limits apply to non-admin members of all three journal groups; admins keep Quick Post under True. B is incorrect — that applies only with True (includes Admins). D is incorrect — admins get journal rights automatically; group membership isn't the issue.

questions.question: Prevent Self-Approval = True. Which journals are excluded from the self-approval restriction?

options.A: Journals created by administrators
options.B: Journals created from any journal template
options.C: Auto Approved and Auto Reversing journals
options.D: Journals posted to entities in a Central Input Workflow

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Auto Approved and Auto Reversing journals are excluded; a journal from an Auto Approved template is auto-approved on submit, and the reversal created when an Auto Reversed journal is posted is also auto-approved. A is incorrect — with True (includes Admins), administrators are restricted too. B is incorrect — only the Auto Approved template type is excluded. D is incorrect — Central Input isn't an exclusion.

questions.question: A user is in the group assigned to the AdministerApplication role but isn't in any of the Workflow Profile's Journal Process, Approval or Post groups. What can they do with journals in that profile?

options.A: View journals only
options.B: Process journals only; approval and posting need group membership
options.C: Nothing until the Workflow Execution Group is assigned
options.D: Process, approve and post journals — administrators get these rights automatically

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says administrators (Administrators group or the AdministerApplication role's group) 'are automatically granted rights to process, approve, and post journals without being members of Journal Security groups'. A is incorrect — administrators get full journal rights automatically. B is incorrect — all three rights come automatically for administrators. C is incorrect — admin journal rights don't depend on the Workflow Execution Group.

questions.question: What is the default value of Prevent Self-Post and Prevent Self-Approval on a Workflow Profile?

options.A: False — administrators and members of the relevant journal group can post or approve their own journals
options.B: True
options.C: True (includes Admins)
options.D: Inherited from the parent Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says False is the default for both, letting administrators and Journal Post/Approval group members post or approve their own journals. B is incorrect — True must be set on purpose. C is incorrect — this is the strictest option and is not the default. D is incorrect — these are per-profile settings with False as the default.

questions.question: Require Journal Template = True on a Workflow Profile. Which statement is true?

options.A: Create Journals is disabled and journal files without a template can't be loaded, but System and Application administrators can still create free-form journals
options.B: Every user, including administrators, is blocked from free-form journals
options.C: Free-form journals can still be loaded from files; only the Create button is disabled
options.D: It also hides the Journal Process Group property

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the setting disables Create Journals, blocks loading journal files that don't contain a template, and that 'System and Application administrators can still create free-form journals'. B is incorrect — administrators are exempt. C is incorrect — file loads without a template are blocked too. D is incorrect — it works together with the Journal Process Group, which defines who can create journals.

questions.question: When an administrator looks at the Workflow Channel property on a new input child's Workflow Settings, what is it set to by default?

options.A: Standard
options.B: NoDataLock
options.C: AllChannelInput
options.D: (Unassigned)

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says 'By default, this is set to Standard' and that it is an option on each load channel (Import, Forms, Adjustments). B is incorrect — NoDataLock is a built-in channel, but not the input child's default. C is incorrect — AllChannelInput is assigned on purpose to control all channels; it isn't the default. D is incorrect — the property defaults to Standard, not unassigned.

questions.question: An administrator fills in Workspace Dashboard Name (Custom Workflow) on an Import child, but no dashboard appears for users. The Workflow Name is Import, Validate, Load. Why?

options.A: The dashboard must be in the Import Dashboard Profile Name instead
options.B: The dashboard must be a Cube View, not a dashboard
options.C: The property only works when the Workflow Name is Workspace or contains Workspace (for example, Workspace, Certify)
options.D: Workspace Dashboard Name is used only on Review profiles

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says this property 'only works with a workflow name of Workspace or any selected containing workspace'. A is incorrect — Import Dashboard Profile Name controls dashboards for the Import phase, not a custom Workspace workflow. B is incorrect — the property takes any dashboard from the Application Dashboards page. D is incorrect — it applies to input types with a Workspace Workflow Name.

questions.question: Users want a specific dashboard to show during the Validate phase of the Houston Import Workflow. Which Workflow Profile property sets this?

options.A: Import Dashboard Profile Name
options.B: Process Cube Dashboard Profile Name
options.C: Confirmation Dashboard Profile Name
options.D: Validate Dashboard Profile Name

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the dashboards wanted for the Validate phase are managed in Validate Dashboard Profile Name. A is incorrect — that controls the Import phase. B is incorrect — that's under Data Quality Settings for the Process step. C is incorrect — that's for the Confirmation step.

questions.subtopic: Can Load Unrelated Entities = False — Journals
questions.question: Can Load Unrelated Entities is False on an Adjustment child. A user creates a journal with a line for an entity not assigned to the Input Parent. What happens?

options.A: The journal can't be saved at all
options.B: The journal posts, and the unassigned entity's line goes to the Default Input
options.C: The journal can be saved but can't be submitted, approved or posted
options.D: The journal posts after an administrator approves it

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says 'A journal can be saved with unassigned entities, but cannot be submitted, approved, or posted'. A is incorrect — saving is allowed. B is incorrect — lines for unassigned entities block submission and posting. D is incorrect — it can't be submitted or posted, regardless of who approves.

questions.question: A user creates a new blank journal in a Workflow. What is its Entity Member Filter set to, and what changes when the journal is created from a template?

options.A: E#Root.WFCalculationEntities in both cases
options.B: E#Root.WfProfileEntities for a blank journal; a journal from a template uses the template's value
options.C: E#Root.Base for blank journals; templates also use E#Root.Base
options.D: E#Root.WfProfileEntities in both cases; template filters are ignored

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says new blank journals get E#Root.WfProfileEntities so only assigned entities appear, but journals created from a template use the template's Entity Member Filter. A is incorrect — the default is WfProfileEntities, and templates use their own filter. C is incorrect — the guide gives WfProfileEntities as the blank default. D is incorrect — templates override the default.

questions.subtopic: No Data Zero View Overrides — Consistency
questions.question: An administrator plans to use Flow Type and Balance Type No Data Zero View Override for a profile that loads MTD. What does the guide warn?

options.A: The Workflow must be loaded the same way for the entire year for Zero No Data
options.B: They only work when Force Balance Accounts to YTD View is False
options.C: They can only be set on the (Default) Scenario Type
options.D: They apply only to Forms channels

questions.explanation: A is correct: the tip says 'The entire Workflow for the year must be loaded consistently the same way for Zero No Data'. B is incorrect — the guide doesn't give this dependency. C is incorrect — these settings can vary by Scenario Type like other profile properties. D is incorrect — they're Integration Settings for loading data from Stage.

questions.question: An administrator enters 0 in Cache Page Size and in Cache Pages In-Memory Limit, then saves. What values do they default to?

options.A: Cache Page Size 200; Cache Pages In-Memory Limit 20000
options.B: Both default to 0, which means unlimited
options.C: Cache Page Size 50000; Cache Pages In-Memory Limit 100
options.D: Cache Page Size 20000 records; Cache Pages In-Memory Limit 200

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says both must be integers greater than 0, and invalid values default to 20000 records and 200 respectively on save. A is incorrect — the values are reversed. B is incorrect — 0 is invalid for both. C is incorrect — these aren't the documented defaults.

questions.question: What does Cache Page Rule Breakout Interval do?

options.A: It sets how many Cache Pages stay in memory before writing to disk
options.B: It sets how many records go in each Cache Page
options.C: After the entered number of Transformation Rules, processing pauses to check if the current Cache Page is fully mapped; if so, the remaining rules are skipped
options.D: It sets how many entities load in parallel

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the value is a count of Transformation Rules that marks where processing pauses to check if the Cache Page is fully mapped; if it is, the remaining rules aren't processed (invalid entries default to 0). A is incorrect — that's Cache Pages In-Memory Limit. B is incorrect — that's Cache Page Size. D is incorrect — parallel loading by entity isn't controlled by this setting.

questions.subtopic: Form and Journal Settings — Source Lists
questions.question: Which property controls the form templates displayed in a Forms channel, and where are those templates configured?

options.A: Journal Template Profile Name; configured under Data Collection > Journal Templates
options.B: Cube View Profile Name; configured under Presentation > Cube Views
options.C: Workspace Dashboard Name; configured under Application Dashboards
options.D: Input Forms Profile Name; configured under Application > Data Collection > Form Templates

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says form templates for the Forms channel are managed in Input Forms Profile Name and configured under Application Tab|Data Collection|Form Templates. A is incorrect — that's the Adjustments channel. B is incorrect — that controls analysis-pane Cube Views under Data Quality Settings. C is incorrect — that's for Workspace workflows.

questions.question: During which Workflow steps does the Cube View Profile Name content appear in the analysis pane when the user clicks the period level?

options.A: Process, Confirm and Certify
options.B: Import, Validate and Load
options.C: Certify only
options.D: Form Input and Journal Input only

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the Cube View Profile section 'is displayed when clicking on the period level during the Process, Confirm, and Certify steps'. B is incorrect — those steps use the Import and Validate Dashboard Profile settings. C is incorrect — that describes Certification Dashboard Profile Name. D is incorrect — those steps use the Forms and Journal Template profiles.

questions.question: An administrator opens Matching Parameters with the ellipsis, but the Currency, View and Plug Account fields can't be edited. What's the likely cause?

options.A: Matching Enabled is set to True
options.B: The profile is a Forms channel; matching is only for Import
options.C: The (Unassigned) box is still checked
options.D: The Entity Filter is not E#Root.WFProfileEntities

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide's tip says 'Make sure the (Unassigned) box is unchecked, otherwise the fields will not be available to update'. A is incorrect — True is required to configure Matching Parameters, not what blocks the fields. B is incorrect — matching can be configured on all channels of the profile. D is incorrect — the Entity Filter value doesn't lock the other fields.

questions.question: Intercompany matching for a profile must be exact to the penny. How should Matching Tolerance be set?

options.A: Set it to 0.01
options.B: Set Suppress Matches to True
options.C: Leave it at 0.0
options.D: Set the Plug Account Filter to the rounding account

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says 'If the matching tolerance must be on the penny, leave this at 0.0, otherwise add a tolerance threshold'. A is incorrect — that would allow a one-cent difference. B is incorrect — that suppresses matched items; it doesn't set tolerance. D is incorrect — the plug account filter names the IC plug account, not a tolerance.

questions.question: In Intercompany Matching Parameters, which field takes account-level dimension members (Flow, Origin, UD1–UD8) so users see the right data in the Workflow?

options.A: Detail Dims Filter
options.B: Partner Filter
options.C: View Filter
options.D: Entity Filter

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the Detail Dims Filter takes 'the Account-Level Dimension Members (Flow, Origin, UD1…UD8)'. B is incorrect — that's a member filter for partner entities. C is incorrect — that sets V#YTD or V#Periodic. D is incorrect — that sets the Workflow entities, usually E#Root.WFProfileEntities.

questions.question: A Base Input profile shows locked although nobody locked it, because its parent Workflow was certified. How is this lock cleared?

options.A: Unlock the Base Input profile
options.B: Reopen the Cube Root Workflow
options.C: Set Profile Active = False and back to True on the input child
options.D: Un-certify the parent Workflow Unit

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says an implicit lock is created when a Workflow Unit's parent has been certified, and 'Implicit locks can be cleared by un-certifying the Parent Workflow Unit'. A is incorrect — the lock comes from the parent's certification, not an explicit lock on the profile. B is incorrect — Open/Closed state isn't how implicit locks are cleared. C is incorrect — Profile Active enables or disables channels; it doesn't clear locks.

questions.question: A Workflow Unit with no assigned entities (such as a Central Input profile) is locked. What is the effect?

options.A: All entities in the cube are locked for that Scenario and Time
options.B: All Workflow processing for that unit is blocked, but no entity data locks are placed
options.C: Entities in its Calculation Definitions are explicitly locked
options.D: Nothing happens until the parent Review profile is certified

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide describes a Workflow Only Lock: if a locked Workflow Profile has no assigned entities, Workflow processing is blocked but no entity locks are placed. A is incorrect — there are no assigned entities, so no entity locks are placed. C is incorrect — explicit locks apply to assigned entities only. D is incorrect — the lock takes effect on its own and blocks processing.

questions.question: All Workflow processing is complete and the Workflow Unit is locked. A user tries to change a cell through Excel. How does OneStream decide whether the update is allowed?

options.A: The Analytic Engine checks with the Workflow Engine, which resolves the cell's Workflow status through the entity assignment relationship
options.B: Excel updates bypass Workflow and save if the user has cube write access
options.C: The cell is checked only against the Entity's Read and Write Data Group
options.D: The update is queued until the next Process Cube

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says any direct update (data entry form, Excel, etc.) triggers the Workflow Engine to validate the cell's Workflow state through the entity assignment relationship — a bidirectional control. B is incorrect — every input cell is tied to a Workflow Unit, so Excel is checked too. C is incorrect — security is checked, but Workflow state is also validated. D is incorrect — the update is validated immediately, not queued.

questions.question: An administrator locks an Input Parent Workflow Profile. What is locked?

options.A: Only the Import origin for its entities
options.B: Only cells tied to its Workflow Channel
options.C: Nothing until each input child is locked
options.D: All data cells for its assigned entities — the Input Parent and all Input Children, regardless of Origin binding or Workflow Channel (a Level One Data Unit Lock)

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says locking an Input Parent is a Level One Data Unit Lock that locks the parent and its input children regardless of Origin Member binding or Workflow Channel. A is incorrect — that would be an Origin lock on one Import child. B is incorrect — that's a Workflow Channel lock on an input child. C is incorrect — the parent lock covers all input children.

questions.question: Several Form input children under one parent each collect a different group of UD1 cost centers. Each group must be locked separately, even though all use O#Forms. What makes this possible?

options.A: Lock the Input Parent profile
options.B: Assign Workflow Channels to the Form input children and the related UD1 members so each channel locks independently within the Forms origin
options.C: Give each Form child a different Origin member
options.D: Use Named Dependents on a Review profile

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Workflow Channels on input children, tied to Accounts or UD members, give detailed locking within one Origin member — each Form child and the UD1 cells in the same channel lock independently. A is incorrect — that locks everything for its entities. C is incorrect — Form children are always bound to the Forms origin. D is incorrect — Named Dependents affect review dependencies, not lock granularity.

questions.question: A user is in the Workflow Execution Group of the North America Review profile but has no group membership on a descendant Base Input profile. Can the user lock that descendant?

options.A: No — they need the descendant's own Workflow Execution Group
options.B: No — they need the descendant's Access Group too
options.C: Only if they also have the UnlockWorkflowUnit role
options.D: Yes — the Execution Group right to lock applies to all descendant profiles, whatever their Access or Workflow Execution groups

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says locking requires Workflow Execution Group membership or inherited membership from an ancestor, and this right applies to all descendants regardless of their Access Group or Workflow Execution Group. A is incorrect — the right is inherited from the ancestor. B is incorrect — the guide says descendants' Access Groups don't matter. C is incorrect — that role is needed to unlock, not to lock.

questions.question: What does a non-administrator need to unlock a Workflow Profile?

options.A: Certification SignOff Group membership only
options.B: The UnlockWorkflowUnit role only
options.C: Maintenance Group membership plus the ManageWorkflowProfiles role
options.D: Workflow Execution Group membership plus the UnlockWorkflowUnit Application Security Role

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says unlocking as a non-administrator requires membership in the Workflow Execution Group and the UnlockWorkflowUnit role. A is incorrect — that group is for certifying, not unlocking. B is incorrect — Workflow Execution Group membership is also needed. C is incorrect — neither is the documented unlock requirement.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three predefined default Workflow Channels in a new application?

options.A: Standard
options.B: AdjInput
options.C: NoDataLock
options.D: AllChannelInput

questions.explanation: B is correct: the three predefined Workflow Channels are Standard, NoDataLock and AllChannelInput. AdjInput is an Origin dimension member (where journals are written), not a Workflow Channel. A is incorrect — Standard is predefined (the default for Accounts and Input Children). C is incorrect — NoDataLock is predefined. D is incorrect — AllChannelInput is predefined.

questions.question: Workflow Channels increase the granularity of which standard structure, letting designers clear, load and lock data at the intersection of Accounts and a User Defined dimension?

options.A: The Data Unit
options.B: The Workflow Unit
options.C: The Cube View
options.D: The Calculation Definition

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Workflow Channels are a mechanism used to increase the granularity of the standard Data Unit,' allowing clear, load and lock at Account/UD intersections. B is incorrect — a Workflow Unit is a single period for a Workflow Profile/Scenario. C is incorrect — Cube Views are reporting objects. D is incorrect — Calculation Definitions control which entities process/confirm.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Channels — Varying by Scenario Type
questions.question: Which statement about Workflow Channel configuration is correct?

options.A: The UD dimension for Workflow Channels can differ by Cube
options.B: Channel tags on Accounts are fixed for all Scenario Types
options.C: The UD dimension for Workflow Channels can be set per Scenario Type
options.D: Channel tags can vary by Scenario Type for both metadata members and Workflow Profiles, but the UD dimension type choice applies to all Scenario Types and Cubes

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'The Workflow Channel settings can vary by Scenario Type for both Metadata Members and Workflow Profile Members,' while the User Defined Dimension Type for Workflow Channel is set once at the application level and 'will apply to all Scenario Types and all Cubes.' A is incorrect — the UD choice is application-wide. B is incorrect — channel tags can vary by Scenario Type. C is incorrect — the UD dimension cannot vary by Scenario Type.

questions.question: What is the final step when setting up Workflow Channel Account phasing?

options.A: Select the User Defined Dimension Type for Workflow Channel under Application Properties
options.B: Assign NoDataLock to every Workflow Profile so locking follows each Account's channel
options.C: Create a Data Management Sequence that clears, loads and locks each Workflow Channel's Accounts
options.D: Tag each Input Profile with the channel it controls, wiring its clearing, loading and locking

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide's three steps are create Workflow Channels, tag each Account with its channel, then tag each Workflow Profile Input Profile with the channel it controls, which hard-wires data clearing, loading and locking for those members. A is incorrect — that is needed for UD phasing. B is incorrect — NoDataLock should be assigned only to metadata members, never Workflow Profiles. C is incorrect — locking is controlled through the profile's channel, not a Data Management Sequence.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Channels — Combined Account and UD Phasing
questions.question: A design uses Workflow Channel tags on both Accounts and UD3. Some Workflow Profiles are now incompatible with one of the tags. What does the guide say is required to combine Account and UD phasing?

options.A: Standard on metadata members and NoDataLock on Workflow Profiles
options.B: AllChannelInput on metadata members and Standard on Workflow Profiles
options.C: NoDataLock on metadata members and AllChannelInput on Workflow Profiles
options.D: A second UD dimension type designated in Application Properties

questions.explanation: C is correct: combining Account and UD phasing 'requires the use of the NoDataLock Workflow Channel on Metadata Members and the use of the AllChannelInput Workflow Channel on Workflow Profiles.' A is incorrect — NoDataLock belongs on metadata, not Workflow Profiles. B is incorrect — AllChannelInput belongs on Workflow Profiles, not metadata. D is incorrect — only a single UD type (UD1–UD8) can be designated.

questions.question: To fix an incompatibility, a designer assigns AllChannelInput to a Workflow Profile. What is the one negative consequence the guide notes?

options.A: Workflow locking for that profile reverts to the Origin Member level, which is less granular than the Workflow Channel level
options.B: The profile can no longer load data to Accounts tagged NoDataLock
options.C: The profile can no longer be certified
options.D: All metadata members revert to the Standard channel

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'The only negative consequence of this approach is the Workflow locking for Workflow Profiles using this setting reverts to the Origin Member level which is less granular than the Workflow Channel level.' B is incorrect — NoDataLock members work with any Workflow Profile. C is incorrect — certification is not affected. D is incorrect — metadata tags are not changed.

questions.question: A Trial Balance import child and a Supplemental import child each use their own Workflow Channel. A Trial Balance file contains an account tagged to the Supplemental channel. When does the user find out?

options.A: At Load Cube, when the sibling overlap check runs
options.B: At the intersection validation step, which checks that each intersection belongs to the correct Workflow Channel
options.C: At Certify, when the Dependent Status shows an error
options.D: Never — the record is silently loaded to the Supplemental channel

questions.explanation: B is correct: during Stage Load, 'at the intersection validation step, [OneStream] will make sure that all intersections being processed belong to the correct Workflow Channel... If not, the users will receive validation errors.' A is incorrect — the overlap check at Load Cube is about sibling Data Units. C is incorrect — the error appears at Validate, earlier. D is incorrect — it raises a validation error.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Channels — Load Cube with Separate Channels
questions.question: The Trial Balance and Supplemental import siblings use different Workflow Channels, and the Trial Balance profile is locked. A user clicks Load Cube on Supplemental. What happens?

options.A: Load fails because a sibling is locked
options.B: OneStream clears the Import Origin for all assigned entities and reloads both siblings
options.C: Only the Supplemental data is written to the Cube, because separate channels guarantee no overlap
options.D: Supplemental data is appended to the Trial Balance Data Unit

questions.explanation: C is correct: with separate channels, 'only the data for the selected Workflow Profile will be written to the Cube... regardless if it is locked or not. Trial Balance and Supplemental can never overlap, the Workflow Channel guarantees it.' A is incorrect — the lock on the sibling does not matter here. B is incorrect — that clear-and-reload happens only when channels are not used (or shared) and the data overlaps. D is incorrect — each channel is its own Data Unit.

questions.question: Two Import siblings share the same Workflow Channel and their data overlaps the same Data Unit. What does the Workflow Engine do at Load Cube?

options.A: Loads only the profile being processed and skips overlapping intersections
options.B: Clears all data for all assigned Entities for the Import Origin, reloads the first Import Child with Replace, then reloads the others in order so overlapped values are cumulative
options.C: Raises an intersection validation error and stops the load
options.D: Loads the most recently imported sibling and ignores the others

questions.explanation: B is correct: on overlap the engine will 'Clear all data for all assigned Entities for the Import Origin Member. Next, reload the first Import Child Workflow using Replace. Then, reload the second, third, etc.' so the result is cumulative. A is incorrect — that is the No Overlap behavior. C is incorrect — overlap is handled, not treated as an error. D is incorrect — all siblings contribute.

questions.question: Into which Origin dimension member are posted journals written?

options.A: BeforeAdj
options.B: AdjInput
options.C: Forms
options.D: AdjConsolidated

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'In the OneStream app, journals are written to the AdjInput member of the origin dimension.' A is incorrect — BeforeAdj is a parent of Import and Forms. C is incorrect — Forms holds form input. D is incorrect — AdjConsolidated holds adjustments that came up through consolidation, not direct journal input.

questions.question: A user copies three Posted journals from Actual into a Forecast scenario. Which is correct?

options.A: The copies keep Posted status and the original names
options.B: Only journals in Working status can be copied
options.C: Each journal can go to a different Target Scenario in one batch
options.D: The copies are set to Working status, and WfProfile_WfUnit_Scenario_TimePeriod_Index is appended to the name

questions.explanation: D is correct: journals in any status can be copied, but 'when copied, they will be set to Working status,' and 'WfProfile_WfUnit_Scenario_TimePeriod_Index is appended to the journal name.' A is incorrect — status resets to Working and the name changes. B is incorrect — any status can be selected. C is incorrect — the Target Scenario 'applies to all journals in that single-batch copy.'

questions.subtopic: Journals — Copy Into Another Adjustment Profile
questions.question: Who can copy journals into a specified Adjustment Workflow Profile?

options.A: Administrators and members of the Journal Process Group
options.B: Only members of the Approve Journals group
options.C: Any user with Workflow Execution access
options.D: Only the original journal creator

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Administrators and members of the Journal Process Group can copy journals into a specified Adjustment Workflow Profile.' B is incorrect — approval rights are not the stated requirement. C is incorrect — general Workflow access is not stated. D is incorrect — no creator restriction is described.

questions.question: A user selects four journals and clicks Delete Selected Item. Which journal statuses can be deleted?

options.A: Any status except Posted
options.B: Working, Submitted or Rejected
options.C: Working or Rejected only
options.D: Approved or Rejected only

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Journals in Working or Rejected status can be deleted.' A is incorrect — Submitted and Approved cannot be deleted either. B is incorrect — Submitted is not deletable. D is incorrect — Approved is not deletable.

questions.question: What does Reapply Template Settings to Journal do?

options.A: Clears the data from the selected journal and returns it to the original template
options.B: Updates the template from the journal's current values
options.C: Applies the template's Frequency to all periods
options.D: Reposts the journal using the template's POV

questions.explanation: A is correct: it 'will clear the data from the selected Journal and return it to the original template.' B is incorrect — the template is not changed. C is incorrect — it does not change frequency. D is incorrect — it does not post.

questions.question: A user checks Show UD Descriptions on the Journals page. Where do the UD descriptions come from, and what else changes?

options.A: From each member's description; Excel/CSV journal templates also change
options.B: From Application Properties; only the Journal page changes — reports, BRApis and Excel/CSV templates do not
options.C: From Cube Properties; journal reports also change
options.D: From the Dimension Library; BRApi exports also include them

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Descriptions are defined in the Application Properties' and 'This feature applies to the Journal page only. Reports, BRApis and Excel/CSV templates related to journals remain unchanged.' A is incorrect — templates do not change. C is incorrect — not Cube Properties, and reports do not change. D is incorrect — BRApis do not change.

questions.question: A user exports journals from the Journals page. Which is correct?

options.A: Workflow profile and scenario can be changed in the dialog
options.B: Output is a CSV file
options.C: Several statuses can be entered as a comma-separated list
options.D: Time uses T# syntax, and the output is an XLSX file

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Time Filter uses T# syntax (e.g. T#2023M1,T#2023M2), and 'Click OK to generate an XLSX file.' A is incorrect — 'Workflow profile and scenario are locked.' B is incorrect — the page export produces XLSX. C is incorrect — you select a single status or All.

questions.question: A user clicks Validate on a journal but cannot use the feature. Which TWO requirements does the guide state?

options.A: The Journal Processing security role, and member constraints configured in the Dimension Library
options.B: The Approve Journals role, and the journal in Submitted status
options.C: Administrator role, and Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year = True
options.D: Journal Template Type = Auto Approved, and a Confirmation Rule Profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'You must have the Journal Processing security role to use this feature and dimension member constraints must first be configured in the dimension library' (and the journal should be in Working status). B is incorrect — the journal must be in Working status, not Submitted. C is incorrect — neither is required. D is incorrect — neither is required.

questions.question: A user selects an existing journal line and clicks Add. What happens?

options.A: A blank line is added at the bottom
options.B: The selected line is copied
options.C: The selected line is moved up
options.D: The journal is validated

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Add: Creates a new journal line item. If an existing line is already selected, Add copies the selection. If no line is selected, the new line item is blank.' A is incorrect — that happens only when nothing is selected. C is incorrect — that is Up. D is incorrect — Validate is a separate toolbar button.

questions.question: Which Journal Type cannot be loaded from an Excel or CSV journal template?

options.A: Standard
options.B: Auto-reversing
options.C: Allocation
options.D: Auto Approved

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Standard or Auto-reversing. Allocation is not supported for Excel or CSV import.' A is incorrect — Standard is supported. B is incorrect — Auto-reversing is supported. D is incorrect — Auto Approved is a Journal Template Type, not a Journal Type.

questions.question: The Workflow Profile is Houston and its Adj input type is named Journals. What goes in the Workflow Name token of a journal Excel template?

options.A: Houston;Journals
options.B: Houston.Journals
options.C: Journals.Houston
options.D: Houston

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'if the name of the Workflow Profile is Houston, and the Adj input type is named Journals, enter Houston.Journals.' A is incorrect — the semicolon form is for batch file names. C is incorrect — the order is reversed. D is incorrect — the input type must be included.

questions.question: When is the optional CubeTimeName cell (to the right of Workflow Time) needed in a journal Excel template?

options.A: When the Scenario's Workflow Tracking Frequency is Yearly and Input Frequency is Monthly
options.B: When the journal is Auto-reversing
options.C: When Is Single Entity is False
options.D: When the template uses |WFTime|

questions.explanation: A is correct: CubeTimeName 'can be used when the Scenario's Workflow Tracking Frequency is Yearly, and the Input Frequency is Monthly' — e.g. Workflow Time 2019, CubeTimeName 2019M7. B is incorrect — auto-reversal is not related. C is incorrect — that affects line-level Entity columns. D is incorrect — |WFTime| just makes Workflow Time dynamic.

questions.question: In a journal Excel template, which tokens hold debit and credit amounts, and how is one Flow member applied to every row?

options.A: DR# and CR#; F#=None
options.B: AMTDR# and AMTCR#; F#:[None]
options.C: A#Debit and A#Credit; F#[None]
options.D: AMT# with sign; F#:None:

questions.explanation: B is correct: AMTDR# 'indicates the debited amount' and AMTCR# the credited amount; 'F#:[None] imports the None Flow Member for every Flow row' (the :[] static value syntax). A is incorrect — not the documented tokens or syntax. C is incorrect — not the documented tokens or syntax. D is incorrect — not the documented tokens or syntax.

questions.question: When loading a journal template, when must the Parent (P#) column be filled?

options.A: Always, for every line
options.B: Only when the Journal Balance Type is Balanced by Entity
options.C: Only when the target Consolidation member is OwnerPreAdj or OwnerPostAdj
options.D: Only for Allocation journals

questions.explanation: C is correct: P# 'only requires a Parent (P#) column value to be populated if the target Consolidation dimension member being updated is OwnerPreAdj or OwnerPostAdj. Otherwise, this entry can be left blank.' A is incorrect — it can usually be blank. B is incorrect — the balance type has no bearing on whether P# is needed. D is incorrect — Allocation is not supported for file import.

questions.question: How does a journal CSV template tell header rows from detail rows?

options.A: With an XFJ named range
options.B: With a row type in Column A: H for Header and D for Detail (!RowType)
options.C: With AMTDR# and AMTCR# in row one
options.D: Header rows are bold

questions.explanation: B is correct: '!RowType (H=Header) and !RowType (D=Detail) are used to tag the corresponding rows,' and 'Any rows tagged with H load as the Headers and any row tagged with D load as the details.' A is incorrect — XFJ named ranges are for Excel templates. C is incorrect — CSV uses DebitAmount/CreditAmount headers. D is incorrect — formatting is not used.

questions.question: In the ExportJournalsToXslx BRApi, which parameter CANNOT take a comma-separated list?

options.A: wfTimeMemberFilter
options.B: serverFilePath
options.C: wfScenarioName
options.D: journalStatus

questions.explanation: D is correct: journalStatus — 'You can search by status or use All to return all statuses. You cannot type a comma separated list.' A is incorrect — wfTimeMemberFilter accepts a comma-separated list such as T#2022H1, T#2022H2. B is incorrect — it is a single path; the restriction is stated for status. C is incorrect — it is a single scenario name; the restriction is stated for status.

questions.question: A rule must load journals from a file and take them through save, submit, approve and post in one call. Which BRApi?

options.A: BRApi.Journals.Data.ImportAndProcessJournals
options.B: BRApi.Journals.Data.ExportJournalsToCsv
options.C: BRApi.Utilities.ExecuteFileHarvestBatch
options.D: BRApi.Journals.Data.ExportJournalsToXslx

questions.explanation: A is correct: ImportAndProcessJournals(si, filePath, save, submit, approve, post, unpostAndOverwrite, throwOnError) defines the journal tasks to complete on load. B is incorrect — it exports. C is incorrect — it processes Harvest import files through the Workflow. D is incorrect — it exports.

questions.question: When can a journal be rejected, and what is the resulting status?

options.A: Any time; status becomes Working
options.B: After posting; status becomes Unposted
options.C: After it has been submitted for approval; status becomes Rejected
options.D: Only before submission; it is deleted

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'You can reject a journal after it has been submitted for approval... The journal status changes to Rejected.' A is incorrect — it must first be submitted. B is incorrect — removing posted data is Unpost. D is incorrect — reject does not delete.

questions.question: In what order are Journal Templates organized and attached to a Workflow?

options.A: Templates → Journal Template Profiles → Groups → Workflow Profiles
options.B: Templates are assigned directly to Workflow Profiles
options.C: Templates in Journal Template Groups → Journal Template Profiles → assigned to Workflow Profiles
options.D: Templates → Cube → Scenario Type

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Create pre-set Journal Templates in Journal Template Groups. After the Journal Template Groups are created, they are organized into Journal Template Profiles and then assigned to Workflow Profiles.' A is incorrect — Groups come before Profiles. B is incorrect — Profiles sit in between. D is incorrect — not the documented structure.

questions.question: A user creates a journal from an Auto Approved template and clicks Save. Which is correct?

options.A: The user must be in Approve Journals for the journal to be approved
options.B: The journal goes to Submitted and waits for approval
options.C: The user can edit the amounts freely after approval
options.D: Line items are validated and the journal becomes approved; the user only needs ProcessJournals

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'After pressing Save, the line items are validated, and the journal skips the approval process and becomes approved,' and the user 'only need[s] to be in the ProcessJournals security group.' A is incorrect — Approve Journals is not needed. B is incorrect — approval is skipped. C is incorrect — to edit it, someone in Approve Journals must reject it, then normal Submit/Approve steps follow.

questions.question: Which options are available for a Journal Template's Journal Requirement Level?

options.A: Not Used, Optional, Required
options.B: Required, Recommended, Optional
options.C: Standard, Auto Approved
options.D: Warning, Error, No Action

questions.explanation: A is correct: Journal Requirement Level works with Frequency and has 'Not Used (anymore), Optional, or Required.' B is incorrect — Recommended is not an option. C is incorrect — those are Journal Template Types. D is incorrect — those are Confirmation Rule actions.

questions.question: A journal template must appear only in September each year. Which configuration does the guide give?

options.A: Frequency = Yearly
options.B: Frequency = Quarterly with Is Single Entity True
options.C: Frequency = Member Filter with Frequency Member Filter T#WFYearM9
options.D: Frequency = All Time Periods with Requirement Level Optional

questions.explanation: C is correct: Member Filter turns on the Frequency Member Filter; 'if this journal only needs to be completed in September, use the filter T#WFYearM9.' A is incorrect — Yearly is December. B is incorrect — Quarterly shows four times a year. D is incorrect — that shows every period.

questions.question: An Auto Reversing journal posted in M3 must be unposted, and its reversal in M4 is not yet posted. What does the guide say?

options.A: Unpost M3; the M4 reversal is removed automatically
options.B: Delete the auto reversal journal from M4, then unpost M3
options.C: Reject the M4 reversal; it returns to Working
options.D: Unpost is not allowed for Auto Reversing journals

questions.explanation: B is correct: when un-posting, check the reversal is not posted; if not, 'delete the Auto Reversal journal from the next time period and un-post.' (On posting, the reversal is created in the next period in Approved state.) A is incorrect — the guide says to delete it yourself. C is incorrect — rejecting is not the documented step. D is incorrect — unposting is allowed.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the True/False template settings that control what a user can change when creating a journal?

options.A: Can Change Journal POV
options.B: Can Change Journal Balance Type
options.C: Can change Journal Line Items
options.D: Can change Journal Amounts

questions.explanation: B is correct: the settings are Can Change Journal Settings, Can Change Journal POV, Can change Journal Line Items and Can change Journal Amounts; there is no separate Balance Type setting. A is incorrect — it is listed. C is incorrect — it is listed. D is incorrect — it is listed.

questions.question: A multi-entity journal must have debits equal credits for each entity, not just in total. Which Journal Balance Type?

options.A: Balanced
options.B: Unbalanced
options.C: Is Single Entity = True
options.D: Balanced by Entity

questions.explanation: D is correct: Balance by Entity — 'Debits and credits in a multi-Entity journal must balance for each entity.' A is incorrect — Balanced checks the journal as a whole. B is incorrect — Unbalanced does no check (for one-sided journals). C is incorrect — Is Single Entity limits the journal to one entity; it is not a balance type.

questions.question: A template has Is Single Entity = False. What must users fill in?

options.A: Only the Entity in the Journal POV
options.B: The Cube, Entity and Parent columns on every journal line
options.C: An Entity Member Filter on every line
options.D: Nothing — Entity comes from the Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'If False, the Cube, Entity and Parent columns must be filled out for every line in the journal instance.' A is incorrect — that is the True behavior. C is incorrect — the Entity Member Filter only limits the entities shown. D is incorrect — Entity is not inherited this way.

questions.question: Which security groups are set on a Journal Template Group, and what does each control?

options.A: Access Group (access to the template group) and Maintenance Group (authority to maintain it)
options.B: Approve Group and Post Group
options.C: Read Data Group and Read and Write Data Group
options.D: Execution Group and Certification SignOff Group

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Access Group — Members of this group have access to the Journal Template group' and 'Maintenance Group — Members of this group have the authority to maintain the Journal Template group.' B is incorrect — those are journal process roles, not template group properties. C is incorrect — those are Entity data security groups. D is incorrect — those are Workflow Profile security groups.

questions.question: In OnePlace Workflow, how many Workflow Units are shown for a selected Workflow Profile, Scenario and Year, and how many can be active?

options.A: Twelve shown; only one active at a time
options.B: Twelve shown; any number active
options.C: Only open periods shown; one active
options.D: Four quarters shown; one active

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Twelve Workflow Units or periods are always displayed for selection, but only one can be selected and active at a given time.' B is incorrect — only one can be active. C is incorrect — twelve are always shown. D is incorrect — the guide describes twelve periods.

questions.question: A user right-clicks a Workflow and selects Clear All 'Import' Data From Cube. What happens to the Stage data?

options.A: It is deleted along with the Cube data
options.B: It is archived to the Harvest folder
options.C: It is converted to Forms data
options.D: It remains in Stage — only the Cube data is cleared

questions.explanation: D is correct: this option 'will clear all imported data from the Cube, but the data still remains in the Stage.' A is incorrect — Stage is not cleared. B is incorrect — the Harvest folder is for batch input files. C is incorrect — Origin members are not converted.

questions.question: An auditor wants to know who unlocked a Workflow period and when. Where is that history?

options.A: Audit Workflow Process, under Lock History > Workflow Lock/Unlock
options.B: View Processing Log on the Import step
options.C: Task Activity for the Load Cube step
options.D: Dependent Status on the Certify step

questions.explanation: A is correct: Audit Workflow Process gives date/time, user, duration and errors for each task, and 'audit history through Lock History > Workflow Lock/Unlock.' B is incorrect — the Processing Log covers how a source file was imported. C is incorrect — Task Activity covers processing jobs, not this lock audit view. D is incorrect — Dependent Status shows current task status, not lock history.

questions.question: A designer wants a different Workflow Profile description to show for the Budget Scenario Type than for Actual. Is this possible?

options.A: Yes — descriptions can be entered per Scenario Type
options.B: Yes — but only for Review profiles
options.C: No — descriptions can only be added using the Default Scenario Type
options.D: No — Workflow Profiles cannot have descriptions

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Descriptions can only be added to Workflow Profiles using the Default Scenario Type. Scenario Type specific descriptions cannot be used.' A is incorrect — Scenario Type descriptions are not supported. B is incorrect — no profile type is an exception. D is incorrect — descriptions are supported on the Default Scenario Type.

questions.question: A controller must reopen a parent Workflow by unlocking and uncertifying its ancestors in one action. Which right-click option is used?

options.A: Corporate Data Control
options.B: Corporate Certification Management
options.C: Unlock Descendants
options.D: Status and Assigned Entities

questions.explanation: B is correct: Corporate Certification Management 'allows a user to unlock and uncertify ancestors, or lock and certify descendants.' A is incorrect — Corporate Data Control preserves and restores data. C is incorrect — Unlock Descendants unlocks but does not uncertify ancestors. D is incorrect — that only shows Origin status.

questions.question: Before a late restatement, a controller wants to save the current Cube data so it can be put back if the changes need to be undone. Which right-click option fits?

options.A: Corporate Certification Management
options.B: Lock Descendants
options.C: Audit Workflow Process
options.D: Corporate Data Control

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Corporate Data Control lets a user preserve data if changes need to be made and restore the preserved data if necessary. A is incorrect — Corporate Certification Management unlocks/uncertifies ancestors or locks/certifies descendants. B is incorrect — locking prevents changes; it does not save a copy. C is incorrect — Audit Workflow Process shows task history.

questions.question: In a multi-period Workflow View, a user must replace every Workflow Unit for the current Source ID, but other Source IDs must stay. Which Load Method?

options.A: Replace
options.B: Append
options.C: Replace (All Time)
options.D: Replace Background (All Time, All Source IDs)

questions.explanation: C is correct: Replace (All Time) 'Replaces all Workflow Units in the selected Workflow View (if multi-period).' A is incorrect — Replace clears only the current Workflow Unit for that Source ID. B is incorrect — Append only adds new rows. D is incorrect — it deletes all Source IDs, which the requirement forbids.

questions.question: What is distinctive about how Replace Background (All Time, All Source IDs) works?

options.A: It runs the delete in a background thread while the new file parse or connector run is happening
options.B: It runs the load as a scheduled Data Management job
options.C: It replaces only Workflow Units that already have errors
options.D: It replaces Cube data but leaves Stage untouched

questions.explanation: A is correct: it replaces all Workflow Units and all Source IDs 'in a background thread while the new file parse or connector execution is running. The delete is being performed while parse is being performed.' B is incorrect — it is not a DM job. C is incorrect — it replaces all Workflow Units. D is incorrect — it replaces Stage data.

questions.subtopic: Load Method — Replace after Cube Load
questions.question: Data from a file was already loaded to the Cube, and a corrected file arrives. The user re-imports with Replace. What is true?

options.A: Replace is blocked once data is in the Cube; the user must Clear All 'Import' Data first
options.B: The Cube is updated automatically with the new file's data as soon as Validate completes successfully
options.C: Replace clears every Source ID in the Workflow, not only the one in the new file
options.D: Allowed; the user then completes the Workflow tasks again and loads the new data to the Cube

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Replace clears data for the previous file with the same Source ID and can be done even if it was already loaded to the Cube; the user then completes the Workflow tasks and loads the new data. A is incorrect — Replace is explicitly allowed. B is incorrect — the Cube is only updated after Load Cube is run again. C is incorrect — Replace targets the specific Source ID; clearing all Source IDs is Replace Background.

questions.question: An icon on the Import step shows that data cannot be imported to periods before the current Workflow year. Where is the setting behind this icon?

options.A: Workflow Profile, Integration Settings
options.B: Scenario properties, Workflow Tracking Frequency
options.C: Application Properties, Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year
options.D: Data Source properties, Time dimension

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'The Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year setting is controlled under Application|Tools|Application Properties' (as are Allow Loads After Workflow View Year and Enforce Global POV). A is incorrect — not a Workflow Profile setting. B is incorrect — Tracking Frequency controls Workflow periods, not this restriction. D is incorrect — not a Data Source setting.

questions.question: A user right-clicks an imported row, but Drill Back is not available. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The Workflow used the Append load method
options.B: The data was loaded from a file, not a Connector Data Source
options.C: The Workflow is locked
options.D: The user lacks the Journal Processing role

questions.explanation: B is correct: Drill Back 'is only available if data was loaded using a Connector Data Source.' A is incorrect — the load method is not the condition. C is incorrect — locking is not the stated condition. D is incorrect — that role relates to journal validation.

questions.question: During Validate, in what order does OneStream run its two checks?

options.A: Intersection check first, then mapping check
options.B: Confirmation Rules first, then mapping check
options.C: Only the mapping check; intersections are checked at Load Cube
options.D: Mapping check first (every piece of data has a map), then the intersection check against Cube constraints

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'First, OneStream will check to make sure each piece of data has a map. Next, OneStream will check to make sure the combination of Dimensions can be loaded into the Cube.' A is incorrect — the order is reversed. B is incorrect — Confirmation Rules run at Confirm. C is incorrect — intersections are checked during Validate.

questions.question: A new GL account fails Validate as unmapped. The user picks a target on the Transformation Errors screen. What type of Transformation Rule is created by default?

options.A: One-To-One
options.B: Mask
options.C: Range
options.D: Composite

questions.explanation: A is correct: on the Transformation Errors screen 'The default will be a One-To-One Transformation Rule.' B is incorrect — Mask is not the default. C is incorrect — Range is not the default. D is incorrect — Composite is not the default.

questions.question: Validate reports an intersection error. What does the guide describe as the way to fix it from the Validate step?

options.A: Click Retransform without changing any rule, since intersection errors clear on retransform
options.B: Clear All 'Import' Data From Cube, re-import the file, then run Validate again
options.C: Open View Transformation Rules for the bad intersection, Edit Rule, save, then Validate
options.D: Change the Account Type of the target account in the Dimension Library, then Validate again

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says to drill down on the bad intersection, right-click View Transformation Rules, investigate each dimension's Target Value, right-click Edit Rule to choose the right target, save, and click Validate again. A is incorrect — Retransform without a rule change produces the same result. B is incorrect — the issue is mapping, not Cube data. D is incorrect — the guide fixes the Transformation Rule, not the metadata.

questions.question: What is the Pre-Process task?

options.A: A Parse step that runs before Import
options.B: The same as the Process task, added as a first step in the Form channel
options.C: A Confirmation Rule run before data entry
options.D: A step that clears Forms data before input

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'The Pre-Process task is the same as the normal Process task. This can be added as a first step in the Form channel process.' A is incorrect — it is not a parse step. C is incorrect — Confirmation Rules run at Confirm. D is incorrect — it processes (calculates); it does not clear data.

questions.subtopic: OnePlace Workflow — Revert Workflow vs Revert Form
questions.question: A user clicked Complete Workflow on Forms and now must change one Form. What must they do?

options.A: Click Revert Workflow only
options.B: Click Revert Form only
options.C: Click Revert Workflow and also Revert Form, edit, then complete the Form/Workflow again
options.D: Ask an administrator to unlock the Workflow period

questions.explanation: C is correct: Revert Workflow re-opens the Workflow, but 'To make changes to the Form, Revert Form must also be clicked,' and then Complete Form/Workflow again. A is incorrect — the Form itself is still completed. B is incorrect — the Workflow is still completed. D is incorrect — completing the Workflow is not the same as locking it.

questions.question: On which Origin members is Cell Detail available?

options.A: Any writeable O#Import or O#Forms member
options.B: Only O#AdjInput
options.C: Any O#Top member
options.D: Any writeable O#Forms or O#BeforeAdj member

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Cell Detail is available on any writeable O#Forms or O#BeforeAdj Member.' A is incorrect — Import is not listed. B is incorrect — AdjInput is where journals post. C is incorrect — Top is a parent and not writeable.

questions.question: Why would a designer use the No Calculate option on the Process step?

options.A: To allow Data Management Sequences to be assigned
options.B: To skip the Confirm step
options.C: To run translation without calculation
options.D: To process only Forms data

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'No Calculate can be used to allow the assignment of Data Management Sequences.' B is incorrect — Confirm still follows Process. C is incorrect — Translate is a separate standard option. D is incorrect — No Calculate is not limited to Forms data.

questions.question: In the Certify step, when does the Set Certification Status icon become enabled?

options.A: As soon as Confirm turns green
options.B: After each question group's status is set to Completed with Set Questionnaire Status
options.C: After every question is answered Yes
options.D: After the parent Workflow is locked

questions.explanation: B is correct: users answer the questions, click Set Questionnaire Status and select Completed; 'After each group of questions is completed, the Set Certification Status icon will be enabled.' A is incorrect — questionnaires must be completed first. C is incorrect — answers do not have to be Yes. D is incorrect — locking the parent is not a prerequisite.

questions.question: Which item does Dependent Status NOT display?

options.A: The Workflow Channel
options.B: The last step completed for each input type
options.C: The Confirmation Rule Failure Messages
options.D: When the last activity took place for each step

questions.explanation: C is correct: Dependent Status shows the Workflow Profile and input types, Workflow Channel, status, last step completed, percentages OK/In Process/Not Started/errors, and last activity time; Failure Messages are shown in the Confirm step. A is incorrect — the Workflow Channel is shown. B is incorrect — the last step completed is shown. D is incorrect — the last activity time is shown.

questions.subtopic: OnePlace Workflow — Multi-Period and Calculation Status
questions.question: Which TWO statements are correct? (1) Multi-Period Processing is opened by clicking the Year in the Navigation Pane. (2) Cube Views | Calculation Status is available on Origin (Import/Forms/Journals) steps.

options.A: Both are correct
options.B: Neither is correct
options.C: Only (2) is correct
options.D: Only (1) is correct

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Click on the Year in the Navigation Pane to enact Multi-Period Processing,' but Calculation Status 'will be available at the total Monthly (not an Origin process) Review, Process, or Certify tasks.' A is incorrect — (2) is false. B is incorrect — (1) is true. C is incorrect — (2) is the false one.

questions.question: In the Intercompany Matching analysis, a cell shows a red triangle. What does it mean?

options.A: The counterparty set the status to Disputed
options.B: The intercompany difference exceeds tolerance
options.C: The data is dynamically derived, usually because the report is translating currency
options.D: An annotation was added to the cell

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'A red triangle indicator displays in the cell when data is dynamically derived. This generally occurs when the intercompany matching report performs currency translations.' A is incorrect — status is set via Set IC Transaction Status, not a triangle. B is incorrect — variance is shown by a red button in the status column. D is incorrect — annotations are not described as a red triangle.

questions.question: Which is NOT an option in Set IC Transaction Status?

options.A: Disputed
options.B: Adjusting
options.C: Finalized
options.D: Reconciled

questions.explanation: D is correct: the options are Not Started, Loaded, Adjusting, Disputed and Finalized; Reconciled is not one of them. A is incorrect — Disputed is listed. B is incorrect — Adjusting is listed. C is incorrect — Finalized is listed.

questions.subtopic: Batch File Loading — Setup and Scheduling
questions.question: An administrator wants batch file loads to run every night from the Windows Task Scheduler. What does the guide describe?

options.A: Schedule the Extender Business Rule directly in Windows Task Scheduler
options.B: Create a PowerShell script that runs the batch processing Data Management Sequence, and call it from the scheduling tool
options.C: Enable the Batch option on the Harvest folder in File Explorer
options.D: Turn on Enforce Global POV so the batch picks up the current period

questions.explanation: B is correct: batch processing can run from Windows Task Scheduler or any scheduler 'by creating a PowerShell Script to execute a batch processing Data Management Sequence.' The sequence uses a Business Rule step that calls the Extender rule. A is incorrect — the Extender rule runs through a DM sequence, not directly from Windows. C is incorrect — there is no such folder option. D is incorrect — Enforce Global POV limits imports to the Global POV; it does not schedule anything.

questions.question: An IT admin will run OneStream Data Management Sequences from PowerShell scripts on a server. Which setup steps does the guide require?

options.A: Install OneStream Web API on the machine, register it with Okta, and run set-executionpolicy remotesigned.
options.B: Run set-executionpolicy remotesigned, configure PowerShell for .NET 4.0, and install OneStream Studio.
options.C: Run set-executionpolicy restricted and install the Excel Add-in.
options.D: Grant the server account the TaskScheduler role.

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists enabling unsigned scripts (set-executionpolicy remotesigned), creating or editing the powershell.exe.config and powershell_ise.exe.config files for .NET 4.0, and installing OneStream Studio on each machine. A is incorrect — Web API is a separate RESTful option needing a web server and identity provider; PowerShell needs the .NET 4.0 config files and OneStream Studio. C is incorrect — the guide uses remotesigned and OneStream Studio. D is incorrect — Task Scheduler roles aren't part of PowerShell setup.

questions.question: In a PowerShell script using OneStreamClientApi, which call runs a Data Management Sequence with substitution variables?

options.A: ExecuteStep(dataMgmtGroupName, stepName, customSubstVarsAsCommaSeparatedPairs)
options.B: GetAdoDataSetForCubeViewCommand(sequenceName)
options.C: ExecuteSequence(sequenceName, customSubstVarsAsCommaSeparatedPairs)
options.D: LogonAndOpenApplication(sequenceName)

questions.explanation: C is correct: DataManagement.ExecuteSequence takes a sequenceName and customSubstVarsAsCommaSeparatedPairs and returns a DataMgmtResult. A is incorrect — ExecuteStep takes dataMgmtGroupName, stepName and custom substitution variables and runs a single Step. B is incorrect — this returns a DataSet for a Cube View. D is incorrect — this logs on and opens an application.

questions.question: A company wants a third-party tool to start Data Management Sequences using OneStream's RESTful Web API. Which statement is true?

options.A: It runs on the application server, accepts and returns XML only, and does not support Postman as a client.
options.B: It authenticates with native OneStream user names and passwords, with no external identity provider needed.
options.C: It must be installed on a web server and uses JSON, but exposes only ExecuteStep, not ExecuteSequence.
options.D: It needs a web server and an OAuth2.0/OpenID Connect provider such as Okta or Azure AD, and it uses JSON.

questions.explanation: D is correct: OneStream Web API must be installed on a web server and configured for external authentication providers using OAuth2.0/OpenID Connect (Okta, Azure AD/Microsoft Entra ID, PingFederate), and it accepts and returns JSON. A is incorrect — it is installed on a web server, uses JSON, and the guide mentions Postman as a widely used client. B is incorrect — it must be configured for an external OAuth2.0/OpenID Connect provider. C is incorrect — there are endpoints for both ExecuteSequence and ExecuteStep.

questions.question: Which OneStream Web API DataProvider endpoint requires the Administrator role?

options.A: GetAdoDataSetForSqlCommand
options.B: GetAdoDataSetForAdapter
options.C: GetAdoDataSetForCubeViewCommand
options.D: ExecuteStep

questions.explanation: A is correct: GetAdoDataSetForSqlCommand returns a DataSet for a SQL query and requires the Administrator role (as does GetAdoDataSetForMethodCommand). B is incorrect — the guide doesn't list an Administrator requirement for the Dashboard Adapter endpoint. C is incorrect — the guide doesn't list an Administrator requirement for the Cube View endpoint. D is incorrect — this is a DataManagement endpoint, not DataProvider, and has no stated Administrator requirement.

questions.question: After upgrading, an administrator looks for the Data Management Groups that were built on the legacy Data Management page. Where are they in Application > Presentation > Workspaces?

options.A: Default workspace > Maintenance Units > Default > Data Management Groups
options.B: A new workspace named Data Management
options.C: Under Data Management Profiles in each workspace
options.D: System > Tools > File Explorer > DataManagement

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says legacy Data Management objects are in the Default folder under Maintenance Units in the Default Workspace. B is incorrect — no such workspace is created. C is incorrect — Data Management Profiles are not displayed in the user interface. D is incorrect — that File Share path holds export files, not DM objects.

questions.question: An application uses Data Management Profiles. What does the guide say about them in the Data Management and Workspaces pages?

options.A: They are converted into Maintenance Units
options.B: They are not shown in either page's user interface, but the DataMgmtProfile and DataMgmtProfileMember tables (with their audit tables) still exist
options.C: They show only in the Default workspace
options.D: They are deleted, along with their tables

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Data Management group profiles will not be displayed in the UI on either page, and lists DataMgmtProfile, DataMgmtProfileMember, AuditDataMgmtGroup and AuditDataMgmtProfileMember. A is incorrect — the guide says nothing about converting them. C is incorrect — they are not displayed in the UI at all. D is incorrect — the guide says the tables still exist.

questions.question: In Workspaces, an administrator copies one Sequence and, separately, copies one Step, then pastes each into another Data Management Group. What gets pasted?

options.A: Both paste alone; Steps must be re-linked by hand
options.B: The Step brings its parent Sequence with it
options.C: The Sequence comes with its associated Steps; the Step comes alone without its Sequence
options.D: Neither works; copy is only on the legacy Data Management page

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says copying a sequence also copies its associated steps, while copying a step copies only that step. A is incorrect — copying a Sequence includes its Steps. B is incorrect — copying a Step copies only the Step. D is incorrect — Workspaces support copy and paste.

questions.question: A Sequence named Load_Actuals is copied (1) into another Group in the same workspace and Maintenance Unit, and (2) into a Group in a different workspace. What names result?

options.A: (1) Load_Actuals; (2) Load_Actuals_Copy
options.B: Both become Load_Actuals_Copy
options.C: Both keep Load_Actuals
options.D: (1) Load_Actuals_Copy; (2) Load_Actuals

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says a copy in the same maintenance unit and workspace gets "_Copy", but in a different workspace the name stays as is. A is incorrect — this reverses the rule. B is incorrect — the different-workspace paste keeps the original name. C is incorrect — the same-workspace paste adds _Copy.

questions.question: In Workspaces, an administrator multi-selects a Sequence and its associated Steps together and tries to copy them. What happens?

options.A: Copy is not available; you can copy several Sequences or several Steps, but not Sequences and Steps in the same selection
options.B: Everything copies, and the Steps are duplicated
options.C: Only the Sequence copies; the Steps are skipped
options.D: The copy works only when pasting into a different workspace

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says if you multi-select a sequence and its steps, you will not be able to use the copy functionality. B is incorrect — copy is not available for this mixed selection. C is incorrect — the guide says copy cannot be used. D is incorrect — target workspace does not matter.

questions.question: In Workspaces, an administrator uses CTRL to select Sequences in Group A and Steps in Group B, then tries to delete them. What happens?

options.A: All selected items are deleted
options.B: Delete is disabled, because items in different Data Management Groups cannot be deleted together
options.C: Only the items in the first Group are deleted
options.D: Sequences are deleted, and their Steps move to the Default Group

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says selecting items in different Data Management Groups disables delete; multi-select delete works within one Group. A is incorrect — delete works only within the same Group. C is incorrect — delete is disabled. D is incorrect — no such behavior is described.

questions.question: An administrator selects a Sequence in Workspaces and clicks Run. The Sequence has no Steps. What happens?

options.A: It runs and finishes with nothing to do
options.B: Run is greyed out for Sequences; only Steps can run from Workspaces
options.C: A confirmation box appears, and running the empty Sequence produces an error message
options.D: It is sent to Task Scheduler as a one-time task

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says you get a confirmation box, and running a sequence without steps produces an error message. A is incorrect — the guide says it errors. B is incorrect — both Sequences and Steps can run. D is incorrect — Run runs it directly.

questions.subtopic: Data Mgmt Export Sequences — Workspace Prefix
questions.question: A Data Mgmt Export Sequence Data Source picks the Export Budget (Version 4) Sequence from the Budget Data Management workspace. How does the Data Export Sequence Name appear?

options.A: With the workspace name before the Sequence name
options.B: Only the Sequence name, as with Default workspace Sequences
options.C: With the Maintenance Unit name added after the Sequence name
options.D: It can't be picked; only Default workspace Sequences are allowed

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the workspace name is put in front of the Sequence name when you choose a sequence outside the Default Workspace. B is incorrect — the prefix is added for non-Default workspaces. C is incorrect — the guide describes a workspace name prefix. D is incorrect — the guide says Sequences from non-Default workspaces can be picked.

questions.question: An administrator clicks the binoculars on the Data Management page to find an object. Which Object types can be chosen in the Select Data Management Object dialog?

options.A: All Items, Sequence, or Step
options.B: Group, Sequence, or Step
options.C: Profile, Group, or Sequence
options.D: All Items, Group, or Profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says to select the Object type from the drop-down: All Items, Sequence, or Step; results can then be shown with View in Hierarchy. B is incorrect — Group is not one of the search Object types. C is incorrect — Profiles and Groups are not search Object types. D is incorrect — only All Items is right; Group and Profile are not listed.

questions.question: An administrator copies a Step and pastes it back into the same Data Management Group on the Data Management page. What does the guide say happens?

options.A: The paste is blocked because Step names must be unique in the Group
options.B: The pasted Step is named "Name_copy"
options.C: The original Step is overwritten after a confirmation dialog
options.D: The Step is pasted into the Data Management Profile instead of the Group

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide notes that pasting a Sequence or Step in the same hierarchy results in "Name_copy". A is incorrect — the guide says the paste succeeds with a _copy name. C is incorrect — nothing is overwritten; the confirmation dialog the guide mentions is for renaming a Sequence. D is incorrect — Steps live in Groups; Groups and Profiles cannot be copied or pasted.

questions.question: An administrator renames a Data Management Sequence from the toolbar. What happens before the new name is applied?

options.A: The Sequence must first be removed from all Task Scheduler tasks
options.B: The rename is only allowed for Steps, not Sequences
options.C: A confirmation dialog appears; OK renames it and Cancel reverts the change
options.D: The Sequence is copied as "Name_copy" and the original is kept

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide notes a confirmation dialog appears when changing the name of a Sequence; click OK to rename or Cancel to revert. A is incorrect — the guide says nothing about this requirement. B is incorrect — both Steps and Sequences can be renamed. D is incorrect — that is the paste behavior, not rename.

questions.question: An administrator wants to reuse an existing Data Management setup. Which statement is true?

options.A: Groups and Profiles can be copied and pasted, but Steps must be re-created by hand in each Group.
options.B: Sequences and Steps can be copied and pasted, but Data Management Groups and Profiles cannot.
options.C: A Data Management Group can belong to only one Data Management Profile.
options.D: Pasting a Step into the same Group overwrites the original Step after a confirmation dialog.

questions.explanation: B is correct: existing Sequences and Steps can be renamed, copied and pasted using the toolbar, but Data Management Groups and Profiles cannot be copied or pasted. A is incorrect — this is backwards: Steps can be copied; Groups cannot. C is incorrect — the guide says a Data Management Group can be assigned to multiple Profiles. D is incorrect — pasting in the same hierarchy creates 'Name_copy'; the confirmation dialog is for renaming a Sequence.

questions.question: A year-end Data Management Sequence runs for hours and should always run on a specific server. What setting fits?

options.A: The Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling property on the Step
options.B: Parameter Substitution 1 with the server name
options.C: The optional Application Server property on the Sequence
options.D: Use Detailed Logging on each Step

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Sequence's Application Server (optional) property lets you specify a particular application server when the Sequence has an unusually long run-time or one server is preferred. A is incorrect — this property belongs to the Sequence's queueing settings and only controls how long the task may wait in the queue. B is incorrect — parameter substitutions pass variable values into the Sequence; they do not pick a server. D is incorrect — detailed logging adds detail to the Task Activity log; it does not pick a server.

questions.question: A Sequence has Enable Email Notification = True and users selected, but no email is ever sent, whether the run succeeds or fails. The email server works. Which setting most likely explains this?

options.A: Notification Event Type is set to On Success or Failure
options.B: Notification Event Type is set to Not Used
options.C: Use Queueing is set to True
options.D: Notification Connection was picked automatically

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Not Used disables the feature even when Enable Email Notification is set to True. A is incorrect — that sends an email whenever the Sequence finishes. C is incorrect — queueing controls CPU-based start, not emails. D is incorrect — the guide says email server connections are automatically identified; that is normal.

questions.question: On a Data Management Sequence, the email notification feature is disabled and cannot be used. According to the guide, what causes this?

options.A: The Sequence has no Application Server specified
options.B: The Sequence has fewer than two Steps
options.C: No email server is available
options.D: Enable Email Notification defaults to True and must be reset

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide notes that if there is no email server available, this feature is disabled. A is incorrect — Application Server is optional and unrelated to notifications. B is incorrect — Step count does not affect notifications. D is incorrect — the default is False; that alone does not disable the feature.
