questions.question: An administrator sets Enable Email Notification to True on a Sequence, picks users, and selects On Failure, but one user never gets emails. Where should the administrator look first?

options.A: Task Activity, which lists every email recipient and delivery status for each Sequence run
options.B: The Notification Event Type, which must be Not Used for individual users
options.C: Logon Activity, because notifications are sent at logon
options.D: The Error Log, which captures users with no, invalid or deactivated email accounts

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide notes the Error Log captures information about users with no, invalid or deactivated email accounts. On Failure sends email only when the Sequence fails. A is incorrect — the guide names the Error Log, not Task Activity, for email account problems. B is incorrect — Not Used disables notifications entirely. C is incorrect — notifications are sent based on Sequence events, not logon.

questions.question: To keep a heavy Sequence from slowing users, an administrator sets Maximum % CPU Utilization To Run = 5. What risk does the guide warn about?

options.A: The value is ignored and 70% is used instead
options.B: The task runs immediately because values under 10 turn queueing off
options.C: The task is canceled at once with no queue time
options.D: The task may never start; the guide says not to set a value less than 10

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide's note says do not set a value less than 10 or the task may never start. A is incorrect — blank uses the default of 70%; a value of 5 is accepted. B is incorrect — nothing says low values disable queueing. C is incorrect — cancellation is driven by Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling, default 20 minutes.

questions.question: A Sequence has Use Queueing = True and Maximum % CPU Utilization To Run left blank. Which statement is true?

options.A: It stays Queued until CPU is below the default 70% or earlier queued tasks finish; don't set it below 10.
options.B: The task runs right away, because a blank Maximum % CPU value turns queueing off for that Sequence.
options.C: It stays Queued until server CPU drops below 10%, which is the default set in the Application Server Configuration.
options.D: It stays Queued indefinitely, because Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling has no default value.

questions.explanation: A is correct: with queueing, the task won't start until CPU is below the specified value or all previously queued tasks are done; blank uses the default of 70% (changeable in Application Server Configuration), and values under 10 may stop the task from ever starting. B is incorrect — blank uses the default value; it does not turn queueing off. Use Queueing defaults to True. C is incorrect — 10 is the minimum the guide recommends, not the default; the default is 70%. D is incorrect — Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling defaults to 20 minutes.

questions.question: A nightly Sequence sometimes disappears from the queue without running when the server is busy. Settings were left at defaults. What is the most likely explanation?

options.A: Queued tasks are canceled after 70 minutes by default.
options.B: It was queued longer than the default 20 minutes and was canceled automatically.
options.C: Use Queueing defaults to False, so busy tasks are dropped.
options.D: The Workflow batch processing queue setting overrode the Sequence and canceled the queued task.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling sets how many minutes a task may stay queued before it is automatically canceled; the default is 20 minutes. A is incorrect — 70 is the default maximum % CPU, not the queue time. C is incorrect — Use Queueing defaults to True. D is incorrect — the guide says the batch processing queue applies to the Batch screen in Workflow, not Data Management Sequences.

questions.question: Where on a Data Management Sequence are Steps assigned and put in run order?

options.A: The Parameter Substitutions section
options.B: The Data Management Profile
options.C: The Notification section
options.D: The Sequence Steps tab

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the Sequence Steps tab is where Steps are assigned and ordered; a Sequence runs its Steps in the order they are organized. A is incorrect — that section holds parameter names and values passed into the Sequence. B is incorrect — Profiles organize Groups; they do not order Steps. C is incorrect — that section controls email notifications.

questions.question: A Data Management Sequence needs to pass named parameter values into its Steps. How many Parameter Substitution name/value slots does the Sequence offer?

options.A: Eight (Parameter Substitutions 1-8)
options.B: Four (Parameter Substitutions 1-4)
options.C: Six, one for each built-in Step type
options.D: Unlimited, entered as a comma-separated list

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists Parameter Substitutions 1-8, each with an optional Parameter Name and a Value. B is incorrect — the guide lists eight, not four. C is incorrect — six is the number of built-in Step types the guide mentions, not parameter slots. D is incorrect — comma-separated name-value lists belong to Step Parameters fields, not the Sequence's Parameter Substitutions.

questions.question: The Data Management queueing note says the batch processing queue overrides other Workflow batch queue settings. To what does the batch processing queue apply?

options.A: Only the Batch screen in the Workflow, not batch script
options.B: Only batch script, not the Batch screen
options.C: Both batch script and the Batch screen
options.D: Only Task Scheduler tasks

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the batch processing queue does not apply to batch script, only the Batch screen in the Workflow. B is incorrect — this reverses the guide's statement. C is incorrect — the guide excludes batch script. D is incorrect — the note is about Workflow batch processing, not Task Scheduler.

questions.question: A user starts a Sequence and the progress dialog stays on "Task Queued." Where does the guide say to watch the queued task and the current server CPU utilization?

options.A: Logon Activity
options.B: Task Activity
options.C: Error Log
options.D: Task Scheduler Grid View

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says to open Task Activity to monitor the queued task and the current server CPU utilization. A is incorrect — Logon Activity shows sessions, such as Client Module = Scheduler. C is incorrect — the Error Log captures errors, such as invalid email addresses, not queue status. D is incorrect — the grid shows scheduled tasks, not live queue and CPU status.

questions.question: A planner needs a step that calculates base Entities and then translates their data, but does NOT roll up the Consolidation dimension. Which Calculation Type is the BEST fit?

options.A: Calculate
options.B: Consolidate
options.C: Translate
options.D: Custom Calculate

questions.explanation: C is correct: Translate runs the Calculate step at the Entity level and then translates data in the Translated member of the Consolidation dimension for each applicable relationship; Consolidate would also roll up the Consolidation dimension. A is incorrect — Calculate runs at the Entity level in the Local member only, without translating or consolidating. B is incorrect — Consolidate runs Calculate and Translate and then completes the calculations all the way up the Consolidation dimension, which isn't wanted. D is incorrect — Custom Calculate runs a Finance Business Rule function on a slice of data; it is a separate step type, not a translation option.

questions.question: A Consolidate step must include a parent in an alternate Entity hierarchy. Which Calculate step filter is meant for this?

options.A: Consolidated Filter
options.B: Entity Filter
options.C: Parent Filter
options.D: Scenario Filter

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says if alternate hierarchies are used, a Parent may be specified in the Parent Filter. A is incorrect — that selects Consolidation dimension members. B is incorrect — that selects Entities or Entity hierarchies, not the alternate parent relationship. D is incorrect — that selects Scenario members.

questions.question: A Calculate step uses Execute Scenario Hybrid Source Data Copy. When does the copy into the target Scenario actually happen?

options.A: Right away when the step is saved, before any calculation
options.B: Only when a Copy Data step runs after it in the same Sequence
options.C: When the source Scenario is consolidated
options.D: When a standard calculation is run on the target Scenario, following the standard calculation sequence by default

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the copy of base-level Cube data from the source Scenario (per its Hybrid Source Data settings) occurs when a standard calculation is run on the target Scenario. A is incorrect — the copy is tied to a calculation run, not to saving. B is incorrect — Hybrid copy is its own option and does not need a Copy Data step. C is incorrect — the calculation runs on the target Scenario.

questions.question: A Clear Data step must also remove journal data and the journals themselves. Which setting does this?

options.A: Clear Adjustment Data and Delete Journals = True
options.B: Clear Forms Data = True
options.C: Clear Imported Data = True
options.D: Use Detailed Logging = True

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says this setting includes the Adjustment members of the Origin dimension in the Clear step. B is incorrect — that covers the Forms member of Origin. C is incorrect — that covers the Import member of Origin. D is incorrect — that only adds detail to the Task Activity log.

questions.question: A Clear Data step must remove only data that users entered in Forms, keeping imported data and journals. How should it be set?

options.A: Clear Imported Data = True; Clear Forms Data and Clear Adjustment Data and Delete Journals = False
options.B: Clear Adjustment Data and Delete Journals = True; Clear Imported Data and Clear Forms Data = False
options.C: Use a Reset Scenario step with Reset All Time Periods = False and Start Year set to the current year
options.D: Clear Forms Data = True; Clear Imported Data and Clear Adjustment Data and Delete Journals = False

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Clear Data step has separate True/False settings for the Import, Forms and Adjustment members of the Origin dimension, so only Clear Forms Data should be True. A is incorrect — this would clear the Import Origin member, not Forms. B is incorrect — this clears Adjustment members and deletes journals, which the user wants to keep. C is incorrect — Reset Scenario clears all data in the range plus audit, Workflow and Calculation Status; it can't target Forms only.

questions.question: Budget data is stored as YTD in the source Scenario, but the target Scenario needs Periodic values. How can a Copy Data step handle this?

options.A: Set Source View to YTD and Destination View to Periodic.
options.B: Leave both View fields blank; the step converts YTD to Periodic automatically.
options.C: Set Copy Imported Data to False so the View is recalculated.
options.D: It can't be done; Copy Data only copies data within the same View.

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Source View selection lets users copy YTD data into a Periodic member and vice versa, with a matching Destination View. B is incorrect — with both blank, data copies to the same View member (YTD to YTD). C is incorrect — Copy Imported Data controls whether O#Import data is copied; it doesn't change View. D is incorrect — the guide says Copy Data can copy YTD into Periodic and vice versa.

questions.question: A Copy Data step must copy imported and form-entered data, but not journal adjustments. How should it be set?

options.A: Copy Imported Data = True only; Forms data always copies
options.B: Copy Imported Data = True, Copy Forms Data = True, Copy Adjustment Data = False
options.C: Leave Source and Destination View blank to skip adjustments
options.D: Copy Adjustment Data = True, the others False

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide maps these to O#Import, O#Forms and O#Adjustments. A is incorrect — each Origin member has its own True/False setting. C is incorrect — blank Views copy to the same View member; they do not filter Origin. D is incorrect — that copies only O#Adjustments.

questions.question: A designer writes the logic for a Custom Calculate Data Management Step. What does the guide say the rule must be?

options.A: An Extender Business Rule run by Execute Business Rule
options.B: A Member Formula on the target Account
options.C: A Finance-type Business Rule and a function inside it, using FinanceFunctionType.CustomCalculate
options.D: A Dashboard Extender rule with a Calculate function type

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Business Rule / Function Name is the Finance-type Business Rule and contained Function, and its example checks api.FunctionType = FinanceFunctionType.CustomCalculate. A is incorrect — Execute Business Rule is a different step type. B is incorrect — Custom Calculate names a Business Rule, not a Member Formula. D is incorrect — the guide calls for a Finance-type rule.

questions.question: A planner wants one Custom Calculate step to run on both the Budget and Forecast Scenarios for several Entities. What does the guide say?

options.A: Possible: list both Scenarios in the Scenario Filter
options.B: Possible: put the second Scenario in the Point of View settings
options.C: Not possible: it can affect only one Entity at a time
options.D: Not possible in one step: it affects a single Cube and Scenario, though multiple Entities, Parents, Consolidation members and Time periods are allowed

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says a single Cube and Scenario can be affected by this Step, and multiple Entities, Parents, Consolidation members and Time periods can be set through filters. A is incorrect — Custom Calculate does not allow multiple Scenarios. B is incorrect — POV settings cover View, Account, Flow, Origin, IC and UD1-UD8, not Scenario. C is incorrect — multiple Entities are allowed.

questions.subtopic: Data Management — Custom Calculate and Calc Status
questions.question: A Custom Calculate step's Data Unit settings include 3 Entities and 12 Time periods for one Cube and Scenario. Which statement is true?

options.A: The rule runs once in total and must loop through the Entities and Time periods itself using API.Pov.
options.B: The rule runs once per Data Unit, and those Data Units' Calculation Status is reset to needing calculation.
options.C: Several Scenarios could be added, because Scenario uses the Member Filter Builder like Entity and Time.
options.D: Calculation Status stays OK, because Custom Calculate writes no audit information for the affected cells.

questions.explanation: B is correct: the related Business Rule runs once for each Data Unit specified, and running the step resets the Calculation Status of the affected Data Units to needing calculation. A single Cube and Scenario can be affected. A is incorrect — the guide says the rule runs once for each Data Unit specified. C is incorrect — a single Cube and Scenario can be affected by this step. D is incorrect — the step creates no cell-level audit information, but it does reset Calculation Status to needing calculation.

questions.question: A designer wants one Finance Business Rule function reused by three Custom Calculate steps, each acting on a different UD1 product. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Add a UD1 Member Filter to each step's Data Units section and read it with api.Pov.Entity.Name.
options.B: Create three Extensibility Business Rules, one per product, and pass each one in the Parameters field.
options.C: Use the Sequence's Application Server property to route each product.
options.D: Set a different UD1 in each step's Point of View and read it in the rule with api.Pov.UD1.Name.

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Custom Calculate POV entries (View, Account, Flow, Origin, IC, UD1-UD8) can be referenced from the rule, for example api.Pov.UD1.Name, so the same rule runs differently based on the step's POV. A is incorrect — the Data Unit settings cover Cube, Scenario, Entity, Parent, Consolidation and Time; UD1 is a POV setting read with api.Pov.UD1.Name. B is incorrect — the step calls a Finance-type Business Rule; the POV is designed to avoid duplicate rules. C is incorrect — the Application Server property picks a server, not a dimension member.

questions.question: The same calculation must run from a Custom Calculate step and also from a Member Formula. What does the guide suggest?

options.A: Have both refer to the same saved Finance Business Rule function by name
options.B: Copy the logic into each object so they run on their own
options.C: Mark the Member Formula as Durable so the step can call it
options.D: Call the Member Formula from an Execute Business Rule step

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide suggests both refer to the same saved Finance Business Rule function by name (see Defining a Reference to a Shared Business Rule). B is incorrect — the guide recommends a shared function rather than copies. C is incorrect — Durable is a storage type, not a way to share logic. D is incorrect — the guide's advice is a shared Finance Business Rule function.

questions.question: Results from a Custom Calculate step disappear after a later Consolidation because they were not saved as Durable. Which step of the standard Calculation Sequence removes them?

options.A: Translation, which rewrites Local data
options.B: ClearCalculatedData, the first step of the standard Calculation Sequence
options.C: Reset Scenario, run automatically before each Consolidation
options.D: The last step of the Calculation Sequence, after Member Formulas

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says ClearCalculatedData is the first step in the standard Calculation Sequence during a Calculation or Consolidation. A is incorrect — translation writes the Translated member; it does not clear calculated data. C is incorrect — Reset Scenario is a Data Management step an administrator runs; it is not part of the calculation sequence. D is incorrect — the guide places ClearCalculatedData first, not last.

questions.question: A Custom Calculate step writes results with api.Data.Calculate(..., True). Later a standard Consolidate runs on the same Data Unit. What happens to those results?

options.A: They are cleared, because ClearCalculatedData runs first in the Calculation Sequence and clears all calculated data.
options.B: They are kept only if a Force Consolidate is used.
options.C: They are kept; Durable data is skipped by ClearCalculatedData unless a ClearCalculated function clears it.
options.D: They are moved to the Forms Origin member.

questions.explanation: C is correct: data saved by the step is cleared by a later Calculate/Consolidate unless saved with Storage Type Durable; ClearCalculatedData is the first step of the Calculation Sequence, and Durable data is ignored even by a Force calculation unless a ClearCalculated function is used. A is incorrect — Durable data is skipped by ClearCalculatedData. B is incorrect — the guide says Durable data is ignored during a calculate or even a Force Calculate or Consolidate; Force is not what keeps it. D is incorrect — Durable storage does not move data between Origin members.

questions.question: A Custom Calculate step's Parameters field contains Name1=Frankfurt, Name3=|!myParam!|. What happens when the step runs?

options.A: Name1 is passed as Frankfurt, and the user is prompted at run time for myParam.
options.B: Both values are prompted at run time.
options.C: The step fails because parameters must be set on the Sequence's Parameter Substitutions.
options.D: |!myParam!| is passed as literal text to the Business Rule.

questions.explanation: A is correct: parameters are listed as name-value pairs, and custom parameters using |!myParam!| syntax result in a prompt to the user at run time. B is incorrect — Name1 has a fixed value; only the |!myParam!| entry prompts. C is incorrect — the step's Parameters field supports name-value pairs and custom parameters directly. D is incorrect — the guide says this syntax prompts the user at run time.

questions.question: A team has a custom application Business Rule (not a Finance calculation) that rebuilds staging tables. They want to run it inside a Data Management Sequence with a few parameters. Which step type fits?

options.A: Custom Calculate
options.B: Export File
options.C: Execute Business Rule
options.D: Calculate

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says this step selects from the available application Business Rules to run custom scripts or procedures, with an optional Parameters field. A is incorrect — that runs a Finance-type Business Rule function against Data Units. B is incorrect — that exports an Extensible Document or Report Book to the File Share. D is incorrect — that runs the built-in calculation, translation or consolidation options.

questions.question: An Export Data step covers 20 Entities and two Scenarios. Each export file must show which Entity and Scenario it holds, and reruns should replace earlier files. Which settings fit?

options.A: Include Cube in File Name = True and Include Member Descriptions = True
options.B: Use a File Name Suffix for each Entity
options.C: Include Object Name in File = True
options.D: Include Entity in File Name = True, Include Scenario in File Name = True, Overwrite Existing Files = True

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide gives a separate Include ... in File Name setting for Cube, Entity, Parent, Cons, Scenario and Time, plus Overwrite Existing Files to replace a previous export. A is incorrect — Member Descriptions adds descriptions to the content, not to the file name. B is incorrect — File Name Suffix is an Export File step setting. C is incorrect — that is an Export Report setting for Dashboard objects.

questions.question: A reviewer complains that the Export Data file has no zero-amount rows and shows only Member names. Which settings fix both?

options.A: Include Zeroes = True and Include Member Descriptions = True
options.B: Include Calculated Data = True and Include Cell Annotations = True
options.C: Include Input Data = True and Overwrite Existing Files = True
options.D: Include Cons in File Name = True and Include Zeroes = True

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says Include Zeroes adds zero amount records and Include Member Descriptions adds Member descriptions. B is incorrect — these add calculated data and annotations. C is incorrect — these add input data and replace earlier files. D is incorrect — Include Cons only changes the file name.

questions.question: An auditor wants a nightly Export Data file with only input values (no calculated data) and the cell annotations attached to them. Which settings fit?

options.A: Include Zeroes = True, Include Member Descriptions = True, Include Calculated Data = False
options.B: Use Detailed Logging = True
options.C: Include Input Data = True, Include Calculated Data = False, Include Cell Annotations = True
options.D: Overwrite Existing Files = False, Include Entity in File Name = True, Include Cons in File Name = True

questions.explanation: C is correct: Export Data has separate True/False properties to include input data, calculated data and cell annotations in the export. A is incorrect — these add zero records and member descriptions, but Include Input Data and Include Cell Annotations are not set, so annotations aren't exported. B is incorrect — this adds detail to the Task Activity log; it doesn't change file content. D is incorrect — these control file naming and overwrite behavior, not content.

questions.question: An Export Data step must export all stored base-level data for every Account, Flow, Origin, IC and UD dimension. What should the Data Filter fields contain?

options.A: Root
options.B: #All
options.C: Leave every filter blank
options.D: Descendants of Top

questions.explanation: B is correct: the 'Combinations of Data Filters' section says to use #All for all stored base-level data. A is incorrect — Root is a top member, not the guide's syntax for all stored base-level data. C is incorrect — the guide specifies #All, not blanks. D is incorrect — Member Filter expressions like .Descendants select members, but the guide's stated method for all stored base-level data is #All.

questions.question: An Export Data step uses Combinations of Data Filters, but the analyst needs only a few exact intersections. Which setting does the guide provide for this?

options.A: Combinations of Data Filters set to #All
options.B: Specific Data Filters
options.C: The Parent Filter
options.D: The Consolidated Filter

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Specific Data Filters use standard Member Filter functionality for fine-grain control and to choose more specific intersections. A is incorrect — #All exports all stored base-level data. C is incorrect — that names a parent for alternate hierarchies. D is incorrect — that selects Consolidation members.

questions.question: An Export File step should save its output in a certain File Share folder and add "_Q3" to the file name. Which two settings fit?

options.A: File Share File Name and Include Time in File Name
options.B: URL or Full File Name and Overwrite Existing Files
options.C: Object Name and Include Object Name in File
options.D: File Share Folder and File Name Suffix

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says File Share Folder is where the file is saved and File Name Suffix adds a suffix to the file name. A is incorrect — these are Export Data settings. B is incorrect — these pick the source file and allow replacing an earlier export. C is incorrect — these are Export Report settings.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a File Source Type in the Export File Data Management Step?

options.A: URL
options.B: Application/System Dashboard File
options.C: Cube View
options.D: File Share File

questions.explanation: C is correct: the File Source Types listed are URL, Application/System Dashboard File, Application/System Database File and File Share File; Cube View is not one of them. A is incorrect — listed: displays a file from an internal or external web page. B is incorrect — listed: a file stored in a Dashboard Maintenance Unit File section. D is incorrect — listed: a file from the File Share.

questions.question: An Export File step must process an Extensible Document. Which file name meets the guide's naming rule?

options.A: Forecast.xfDoc.pptx
options.B: Forecast.pptx.xfDoc
options.C: Forecast_xfDoc.pptx
options.D: Forecast.xfDoc.pdf

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says an Extensible Document is a Text, Word, PowerPoint or Excel file whose name contains .xfDoc before the extension (e.g., StatusReport.xfDoc.docx). B is incorrect — the .xfDoc part must come before the extension, not replace it. C is incorrect — the name needs ".xfDoc" as its own segment before the extension. D is incorrect — Extensible Documents are Text, Word, PowerPoint or Excel files, not PDF.

questions.subtopic: Data Management — Export File Extensible Doc
questions.question: An Export File step points at StatusReport.xfDoc.docx, but the file saved to the File Share still shows raw parameter text instead of values. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The file name must end in .xfDoc with no other extension.
options.B: Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc is set to True.
options.C: The File Source Type must be URL for Word documents.
options.D: Process Extensible Document is set to False.

questions.explanation: D is correct: Process Extensible Document set to True processes the attached Extensible Document; False displays the unprocessed file, mainly for testing. Extensible Documents must have .xfDoc before the extension. A is incorrect — the guide's example is StatusReport.xfDoc.docx; .xfDoc goes before the extension. B is incorrect — this prompts the user for parameters at run time; it doesn't leave the document unprocessed. C is incorrect — URL is for files on web pages; any supported source type can hold the document.

questions.question: A scheduled Export File step for an Extensible Document must run unattended without prompting for parameters. Which setup fits?

options.A: Set Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc to False and list values in the Parameters property.
options.B: Set Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc to True so values are read from the document automatically.
options.C: Set Process Extensible Document to False to skip parameters.
options.D: Set Overwrite Existing Files to True.

questions.explanation: A is correct: if Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc is True, parameters prompt the user when the Sequence runs; if False, they can be specified ahead of time in the Parameters property as comma-separated name-value pairs. B is incorrect — True causes prompts at run time. C is incorrect — False shows the unprocessed file, which defeats the purpose. D is incorrect — this only controls whether a previous file is overwritten.

questions.subtopic: Export Report — Object Name in File
questions.question: An Export Report step exports a Dashboard Profile with several Dashboards. The files must show which Dashboard each came from. Which setting fits?

options.A: Include Entity in File Name = True
options.B: Include Object Name in File = True
options.C: Process Extensible Document = True
options.D: Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc = True

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says this puts the Dashboard object in the file name when exporting. A is incorrect — that is an Export Data setting. C is incorrect — that is an Export File setting. D is incorrect — that is an Export File setting for prompting parameters.

questions.question: A Dashboard needs a parameter value that a user would normally pick when opening it. How is that value given in an Export Report step?

options.A: Parameter Substitutions 1-8 on the Step
options.B: Read Parameter Names from Extensible Doc
options.C: Object Parameters (optional)
options.D: Specific Data Filters

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Object Parameters is for passing parameters or variables used when running the report normally. A is incorrect — Parameter Substitutions belong to the Sequence, not the Export Report step. B is incorrect — that is an Export File setting. D is incorrect — that is an Export Data filter setting.

questions.question: An Export Report step must produce one PDF per dashboard in a Dashboard Profile, delivered as one download. Which setting fits?

options.A: Object Type = Dashboard; Report File Type = Combined PDF File
options.B: Object Type = Dashboard Profile; Report File Type = PDFs in Zip File
options.C: Use an Export File step with File Source Type = Application Dashboard File
options.D: Object Type = Cube View; Report File Type = PDFs in Zip File

questions.explanation: B is correct: Object Type can be a Dashboard or Dashboard Profile, and PDFs in Zip File exports each PDF individually inside a ZIP file. A is incorrect — Combined PDF merges everything into one PDF, not one per dashboard. C is incorrect — Export File exports an Extensible Document or Report Book, not dashboards as reports. D is incorrect — Object Type options are Dashboard or Dashboard Profile only.

questions.subtopic: Data Management — Reset Scenario Best Practice
questions.question: Before running a Reset Scenario step on a Forecast scenario whose Manage Data Group is Nobody, what does the guide recommend?

options.A: Set Manage Data Group to Everyone permanently so the step can run under any scheduled or interactive account.
options.B: Run a Clear Data step first, because Reset Scenario cannot clear data stored as Durable.
options.C: Back up the database, switch Manage Data Group to an exclusive group, run the step, then reset it to Nobody.
options.D: Nothing; members of the Administrators group bypass the Manage Data Group check on Reset Scenario.

questions.explanation: C is correct: the user running Reset Scenario must be in the Scenario's Manage Data Group or the step fails; the guide recommends changing it from Nobody to an exclusive group before running and back to Nobody afterward, and backing up the database first. A is incorrect — the guide warns against unauthorized users launching such steps and recommends an exclusive group. B is incorrect — Reset Scenario clears even Durable data. D is incorrect — the step fails if the user isn't in the Manage Data Group.

questions.subtopic: Data Management — Reset All Time Periods
questions.question: An administrator wants a Reset Scenario step to clear only 2024 onward for a scenario. What must be changed?

options.A: Enter 2024 in the Time Filter; Reset All Time Periods is ignored when a filter exists.
options.B: Choose multiple Scenarios and the step resets only the current year.
options.C: Leave the default; Reset All Time Periods is False by default.
options.D: Set Reset All Time Periods to False, which enables Start Year and End Year.

questions.explanation: D is correct: Reset All Time Periods defaults to True (all periods removed and Workflow Status reset); setting it to False enables the Start Year/End Year and Start Time Period properties. A is incorrect — Reset Scenario has no Time Filter; it uses Start/End Year after Reset All Time Periods is False. B is incorrect — Reset Scenario takes one Scenario, and multiple Scenarios don't limit years. C is incorrect — the default is True.

questions.question: After running a Sequence with an Export Data step, where does the user find the file?

options.A: System > Tools > File Explorer > File Share > Applications > [app] > DataManagement > Export > [Username]
options.B: Application > Tools > Load/Extract > Extract tab > File Type: Data Management > [Username] > latest export folder
options.C: OnePlace > Documents > Public > DataManagement > Export > [Username] > latest folder from the run
options.D: System > Logging > Task Activity > select the Data Management task > drill into the step > Download File

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says to go to System Tab > Tools > File Explorer and then File Share > Applications > the application > DataManagement > Export > Username > the latest folder. B is incorrect — Load/Extract moves application artifacts; it isn't where Data Management export files go. C is incorrect — the guide gives the File Share path under File Explorer. D is incorrect — Task Activity shows job status and logs, not export files.

questions.question: A user moves an Excel model into the Spreadsheet tool. Which feature is listed as a Spreadsheet limitation?

options.A: Cube View Connections
options.B: Retrieve functions like XFGetCell
options.C: Macros
options.D: Quick Views

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide lists macros, Solver and document properties as Spreadsheet limitations. A is incorrect — Spreadsheet supports Cube View Connections. B is incorrect — Spreadsheet supports retrieve functions. D is incorrect — Spreadsheet supports Quick Views.

questions.question: Which statement about Spreadsheet behavior is correct?

options.A: Undo/Redo is supported up to 100 steps, and CTRL+N prompts to save
options.B: Undo/Redo is supported, and CTRL+N opens File Explorer
options.C: Center Across Selection is the default alignment, and Shift+End is supported
options.D: Undo/Redo isn't supported, and CTRL+N can close an open spreadsheet with unsaved edits without saving

questions.explanation: D is correct: Both are listed limitations. A is incorrect — 100-step undo is a Quick Views tab feature. B is incorrect — Undo/Redo isn't supported, and CTRL+N creates a new spreadsheet. C is incorrect — both are listed limitations.

questions.question: A report designer wants to add a chart to a worksheet in the Windows App Spreadsheet feature. Which chart type is incompatible and unavailable there?

options.A: Waterfall
options.B: Pareto
options.C: 3-D Line
options.D: Sunburst

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide states the Excel 3-D Line chart is incompatible and unavailable with the Spreadsheet feature. A, B and D are incorrect — Waterfall, Pareto and Sunburst are among the seven Excel 2016 chart types that were added to the Spreadsheet component.

questions.question: Which chart type was added to Spreadsheet as one of the seven Excel 2016 chart types?

options.A: Waterfall
options.B: Stacked Cylinder
options.C: 3-D Line
options.D: Stacked Horizontal Pyramid

questions.explanation: A is correct: The seven are Box and Whisker, Waterfall, Histogram, Pareto, Funnel, Sunburst and Treemap. B is incorrect — this column chart is unavailable in Spreadsheet. C is incorrect — this line chart is unavailable in Spreadsheet. D is incorrect — this bar chart is unavailable in Spreadsheet.

questions.question: In a Spreadsheet waterfall chart, Net Income floats mid-chart. How is it anchored at zero?

options.A: Change it to a Pareto chart
options.B: Right-click the chart, choose Set as Total, and check Net Income
options.C: Use Shrink to fit on the Net Income cell
options.D: Apply a Selection Style to the Net Income row

questions.explanation: B is correct: This makes a total start at zero and not float. A is incorrect — Pareto charts are sorted histograms with a cumulative line. C is incorrect — Shrink to fit reduces cell text size. D is incorrect — Selection Styles format cells, not chart columns.

questions.question: A designer wants a Spreadsheet chart in which each level of an organization hierarchy is a ring, with the innermost circle as the top of the hierarchy, to show how one ring breaks into its pieces. Which chart type fits?

options.A: Box and Whisker
options.B: Treemap
options.C: Funnel
options.D: Sunburst

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says a sunburst chart represents each level of the hierarchy as one ring or circle with the innermost circle as the top, and is most effective at showing how one ring is broken into its contributing pieces. B is incorrect — a treemap is hierarchical too, but shows categories by color and proximity and is good for comparing proportions, not rings. C is incorrect — a funnel shows values across stages in a process. A is incorrect — box and whisker shows distribution in quartiles with outliers.

questions.question: Which file source is NOT listed in the Spreadsheet File Open dialog?

options.A: Local Folder
options.B: OneStream File System
options.C: Data Management Export Folder
options.D: Application Workspace File

questions.explanation: C is correct: The sources are Local Folder, OneStream File System, Application Workspace File and System Workspace File. A is incorrect — this is listed. B is incorrect — this is listed. D is incorrect — this is listed.

questions.question: A user right-clicks a workbook in OnePlace Documents. Which option opens it in Excel on the local computer?

options.A: Open in Spreadsheet Page
options.B: Open With…
options.C: Save Offline Copy
options.D: Open

questions.explanation: D is correct: Open opens the file directly in Excel if Excel is on the local computer. A is incorrect — this opens it in Spreadsheet. B is incorrect — this lets the user pick a program. C is incorrect — this saves a copy; it doesn't open the file.

questions.question: A Spreadsheet user wants long labels to fit without changing column widths. What should they use?

options.A: Format Cells > Alignment > Shrink to fit
options.B: Format Cells > Alignment > Center Across Selection
options.C: Resize Initial Column Widths Using Cube View Settings
options.D: Retain All Formatting when Saving Offline

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide gives this path to reduce text size. B is incorrect — this isn't supported in Spreadsheet and doesn't shrink text. C is incorrect — this changes column widths. D is incorrect — this is an Excel Add-In Preference for offline copies.

questions.question: How does the Spreadsheet OneStream ribbon differ from the Excel Add-In ribbon?

options.A: It adds a Save to Server button under General, and the task pane must be turned on
options.B: It has no File Operations group, Save Offline Copy is under General, and there's no Display Context Pane option
options.C: It removes Explore, so Quick Views must be built from the task pane
options.D: It has File Operations, but Save Offline Copy is removed

questions.explanation: B is correct: Save to Server and File Explorer are integrated, Save Offline Copy moves to General, and the task pane appears automatically. A is incorrect — Save to Server isn't available in Spreadsheet. C is incorrect — Explore exists in Spreadsheet. D is incorrect — File Operations doesn't exist, and Save Offline Copy moves to General.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Adding the OneStream Ribbon
questions.question: A new analyst installed the Excel Add-In but doesn't see the OneStream ribbon. Per the guide, how is the ribbon turned on?

options.A: File > Options > Add-ins, set Manage to COM Add-ins, click Go, and check OneStreamExcelAddIn
options.B: OneStream > Administration > Preferences, then set Display Context Pane to True
options.C: File > Options > Trust Center, then turn on Enable Macros for OneStream Event Processing
options.D: Run the Client Updater from OnePlace, which adds the ribbon automatically

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide's steps are File > Options, Add-ins, Manage drop-down = COM Add-ins, Go, then check OneStreamExcelAddIn. B is incorrect — Display Context Pane only shows or hides the task pane once the ribbon already exists. C is incorrect — that is an Add-In Preference for macros on OneStream API calls, not how the ribbon is added. D is incorrect — the Client Updater updates the Add-In shipped with the Windows app; the ribbon is still enabled through COM Add-ins.

questions.question: A user installed the Excel Add-In separately (not the one provided with the Windows application). How should it be updated to a new version?

options.A: Run the Client Updater
options.B: Uninstall it, then reinstall it as described in the Installation Guide
options.C: Set Force Add-In Compatibility for Registration to True
options.D: Click Log In and connect to the new server URL so it downloads automatically

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says if you don't use the Add-In provided with the Windows application, update it by uninstalling then reinstalling. A is incorrect — the Client Updater is only for the Add-In provided with the Windows application. C is incorrect — that setting forces re-registration when other add-ins turn the Add-In off at start-up; it doesn't update versions. D is incorrect — logging in only authenticates; the Add-In doesn't self-update.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main components of the Excel Add-In?

options.A: Task Pane
options.B: OneStream Ribbon
options.C: Data Explorer Grid
options.D: Error Logs

questions.explanation: C is correct: The three components are the Task Pane, the OneStream Ribbon and Error Logs; the Data Explorer Grid is a web/OnePlace grid. A is incorrect — it is a main component, used to quickly access POV, Quick Views and Documents. B is incorrect — it is a main component, used to access data from the platform. D is incorrect — it is a main component, used to troubleshoot Add-In related issues.

questions.question: A user wants to open a user-specific document directly from the Excel Add-In task pane. Which task pane tab should they use?

options.A: POV
options.B: Quick Views
options.C: File Operations
options.D: Documents

questions.explanation: D is correct: The Documents tab displays public or user-specific application or system documents. A is incorrect — the POV tab shows the Global, Workflow and Cube POV and lets you update the Cube POV. B is incorrect — the Quick Views tab builds and edits Quick Views. C is incorrect — File Operations is a ribbon category, not a task pane tab; the task pane tabs are POV, Quick Views and Documents.

questions.question: A user enters a rate with 12 decimal places in an Excel cell used by a OneStream function. What does the guide say happens?

options.A: Decimals are automatically truncated after the ninth character
options.B: The value is rounded to six decimal places on submit
options.C: The full precision is stored because Excel passes values as doubles
options.D: The cell shows #REFRESH until the decimals are reduced

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide notes that when working in Excel, decimals are automatically truncated after the ninth character in a cell or a function. B is incorrect — the guide states truncation after the ninth character, not rounding to six. C is incorrect — the guide explicitly says decimals are truncated. D is incorrect — #REFRESH appears after entering a new XF function, not because of decimal length.

questions.question: A workbook has three tabs, each with a Cube View Connection that uses a different parameter. The user is on tab 2 and clicks Refresh Sheet. Which parameters is the user prompted for?

options.A: All parameters used in the workbook
options.B: Only the parameters used on tab 2
options.C: No parameters; refresh never prompts
options.D: Only parameters that changed since the last submit

questions.explanation: B is correct: Refresh Sheet prompts with any parameters used on the selected tab; Refresh Workbook prompts with all parameters in the workbook. A is incorrect — that is the behavior of Refresh Workbook. C is incorrect — refresh does prompt for Cube View parameters; it is Submit that has no prompts. D is incorrect — the guide ties prompts to the tab(s) refreshed, not to changes.

questions.question: A user clicks Submit Workbook on a workbook with parameterized Cube Views on every tab. What parameter prompts appear?

options.A: Prompts for all parameters used in the workbook
options.B: Prompts only for parameters on the active tab
options.C: None; Submit Sheet and Submit Workbook do not prompt for parameters
options.D: Prompts only for unresolved parameters

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide's comparison table lists 'No prompts' for both Submit Sheet and Submit Workbook. A is incorrect — that is Refresh Workbook behavior. B is incorrect — that is Refresh Sheet behavior. D is incorrect — the guide lists no prompts at all for submits.

questions.question: A user selects four cells, the first holding 900, and wants each later cell to equal the previous cell times 1.5. Which Spreading Type does this?

options.A: Accumulate
options.B: Factor
options.C: Proportional Distribution
options.D: Fill

questions.explanation: A is correct: Accumulate multiplies the first cell's value by the rate, places it in the next cell and repeats, so each cell is a factor of the previous cell. B is incorrect — Factor multiplies all selected cells by the rate; it doesn't chain from the previous cell. C is incorrect — Proportional spreads the Amount to Spread by each cell's share of the total. D is incorrect — Fill puts the Amount to Spread into every selected cell.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Spreading: Fill vs. Even
questions.question: A planner selects 12 monthly cells and wants each month to show 1,000. Which Spreading Type and Amount to Spread should be used?

options.A: Even Distribution with an Amount to Spread of 1,000
options.B: Fill with an Amount to Spread of 1,000
options.C: Factor with a Rate of 1,000
options.D: Accumulate with a Rate of 1

questions.explanation: B is correct: Fill fills each selected data cell with the value in Amount to Spread. A is incorrect — Even Distribution divides 1,000 evenly across the 12 cells (about 83.33 each). C is incorrect — Factor multiplies existing cell values by the rate. D is incorrect — Accumulate chains the first cell's value through the rate; it doesn't set a fixed amount.

questions.question: A user wants a quarterly amount spread with weights of 4, 5 and 4 across the three months. Which Spreading Type should be used?

options.A: 454 Distribution
options.B: 445 Distribution
options.C: 544 Distribution
options.D: Even Distribution

questions.explanation: A is correct: 454 gives a weight of 4 to the first cell, 5 to the second and 4 to the third. B is incorrect — 445 gives weights of 4, 4 and 5. C is incorrect — 544 gives weights of 5, 4 and 4. D is incorrect — Even spreads equally across the cells.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Spreading: Proportional with Zeros
questions.question: A user applies Proportional Distribution of 50,000 to selected cells that all currently contain zero. What happens?

options.A: Nothing is spread because each cell's share of the total is zero
options.B: The full 50,000 goes to the first selected cell
options.C: An error is returned for divide by zero
options.D: The Amount to Spread behaves like an Even Distribution

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says if all cells have a zero value, Proportional Distribution behaves like Even Distribution. A is incorrect — the guide specifically says it falls back to Even Distribution. B is incorrect — no spreading type puts everything into the first cell. C is incorrect — the guide describes the fallback to Even Distribution, not an error.

questions.question: The Rate property in Spreading applies to which Spreading Types?

options.A: Factor and Proportional Distribution
options.B: All distribution types (445, 454, 544, Even)
options.C: Factor and Accumulate only
options.D: Accumulate and Fill

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide labels Rate 'Factor and Accumulate Spreading Types Only'. A is incorrect — Proportional Distribution uses the Amount to Spread, not a Rate. B is incorrect — the weighted and even distributions use the Amount to Spread. D is incorrect — Fill uses the Amount to Spread, not a Rate.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Spreading: Amount to Spread Default
questions.question: When a user opens Spreading, what value does the Amount to Spread property default to?

options.A: The sum of all selected cells
options.B: The value of the last cell selected
options.C: The value of the first cell selected
options.D: Zero

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says the Amount to Spread defaults to the last cell selected. A is incorrect — the default comes from the last cell selected, not a total. C is incorrect — the guide says the last cell selected. D is incorrect — the guide gives the last selected cell as the default.

questions.question: A user flagged two months with Flag Selected Cells and wants spreading to skip them. Which property must be True?

options.A: Include Flagged Readonly Cells in Totals
options.B: Clear Flags
options.C: Retain Amount in Flagged Input Cells
options.D: Use Add-In Compatibility Filter

questions.explanation: C is correct: If Retain Amount in Flagged Input Cells is True, spreading won't apply to the flagged cells. A is incorrect — this includes locked base-level cell values in spreading totals; it doesn't protect flagged input cells. B is incorrect — Clear Flags removes the flags, which is the opposite of what's needed. D is incorrect — that Preference controls whether third-party add-ins and macros can change cells.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Spreading: Readonly Cells Default
questions.question: What is the default for Include Flagged Readonly Cells in Totals, and what does it do?

options.A: False; locked cells are excluded unless the user turns it on
options.B: True; flagged cells keep their original amounts during spreading
options.C: False; read-only cells are overwritten by the spread
options.D: True; locked base-level cell values are included when calculating spreading totals

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says set it to True to include locked base-level cell values when calculating totals, and True is the default. A is incorrect — the guide states True is the default. B is incorrect — keeping original amounts is what Flag Selected Cells and Retain Amount in Flagged Input Cells do. C is incorrect — the setting is about including values in totals, and its default is True.

questions.question: In the Excel Add-In File Explorer, which attributes can Edit Selected Folder/Edit Selected File Information change?

options.A: Description, Maintenance Group and Access Group
options.B: Name, Description and Security Role
options.C: Access Group only
options.D: Maintenance Group, Display Member Group and Description

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says it edits the Description, Maintenance Group and Access Group for the selected folder or file. B is incorrect — the guide lists Description, Maintenance Group and Access Group; no security role. C is incorrect — Description and Maintenance Group can also be edited. D is incorrect — Display Member Group is a dimension security property, not a File Explorer attribute.

questions.question: A user opened a workbook from their local C: drive, then clicks Save to Server. What happens?

options.A: It saves back to the local C: drive location
options.B: File Explorer opens so the user can pick a OneStream location their security allows
options.C: It saves to the user's Documents folder in OnePlace by default
options.D: It saves an offline copy without functions

questions.explanation: B is correct: If the file wasn't opened from a OneStream location, File Explorer opens; files opened from OneStream are saved back to that location. A is incorrect — Save to Server saves to the OneStream folder structure, not the local drive. C is incorrect — the guide says File Explorer opens; there's no automatic default folder. D is incorrect — that's Save Offline Copy.

questions.question: A controller needs to send a workbook to an external auditor who doesn't have the Excel Add-In. Which option should be used?

options.A: Save to Server
options.B: Convert to XFGetCells
options.C: Save Offline Copy
options.D: Download Selected File's Content File

questions.explanation: C is correct: Save Offline Copy saves the worksheet without the functions so users without the Add-In can open it and see the saved values. A is incorrect — Save to Server saves to the OneStream folder structure with functions intact. B is incorrect — this replaces a Quick View with XFGetCell formulas, which still need the Add-In. D is incorrect — this downloads a File Explorer file's content file; it doesn't strip functions.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Object Lookup for Extensible Documents
questions.question: While building an Extensible Document in Excel, which items can a designer insert using Object Lookup?

options.A: Cube View Connections, Quick Views or Table Views
options.B: Data Management Sequences, Workspaces or Business Rules
options.C: Selection Styles, Excel Styles or Named Regions
options.D: Parameters, Substitution Variables or Image Content

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says Object Lookup in an Extensible Document can insert Parameters, Substitution Variables or Image Content. A is incorrect — these are inserted from the Explore category, not Object Lookup. B is incorrect — Object Lookup is used to browse for DM sequences in In-Sheet Actions, but these aren't the Extensible Document inserts the guide lists. C is incorrect — these are formatting features, not Object Lookup inserts.

questions.question: An Excel macro must respond to OneStream API events, but nothing fires. Which Preference controls this, and what is its default?

options.A: Enable Macros for OneStream Event Processing; default False
options.B: Use Add-In Compatibility Filter; default True
options.C: Force Add-In Compatibility for Registration; default False
options.D: Enable Macros for OneStream Event Processing; default True

questions.explanation: A is correct: When True this enables Excel macros for OneStream API calls; the default is False. B is incorrect — this blocks third-party add-ins and macros from changing cells when True; it doesn't enable event macros. C is incorrect — this forces re-registration when external add-ins turn the Add-In off. D is incorrect — the setting is correct but its default is False.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Preferences: Invalidate Old Data
questions.question: A team wants every workbook to pull fresh data automatically as soon as it's opened. Which Preference should be True?

options.A: Use Minimal Calculation for Refresh
options.B: Invalidate Old Data When Workbook is Opened
options.C: Disable Interactive User During Refresh
options.D: Use Multithreading for Retain Formulas

questions.explanation: B is correct: When True it forces a data refresh on the opened workbook; the default is False. A is incorrect — this limits calculation to the active sheet during refresh. C is incorrect — this fixes functions not completing on certain touchscreen hardware. D is incorrect — this controls multithreading for Cube Views with Retain Formulas, not refreshing on open.

questions.question: Which statement about Use Minimal Calculation for Refresh is correct?

options.A: It defaults to False and must be turned on to speed up refreshes
options.B: It applies to both the Excel Add-In and Spreadsheet
options.C: It defaults to True, calculates only the active sheet, and applies to the Excel Add-In only, not Spreadsheet
options.D: When True it calculates all open workbooks but skips charts

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says it's Excel Add-In only, defaults to True, and only calculates formulas in the active sheet; False reverts to full calculation of all workbooks and sheets. A is incorrect — the default is True. B is incorrect — the guide says it's for the Excel Add-In only, not Spreadsheet. D is incorrect — True limits calculation to the active sheet; False calculates all workbooks and sheets.

questions.question: A workbook has many worksheets with Retain Formulas enabled on Cube Views, and refresh is slow in Excel. Which Preference speeds this up?

options.A: Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells
options.B: Invalidate Old Data When Workbook is Opened
options.C: Preserve Excel Formatting by Default (Cube Views)
options.D: Use Multithreading for Retain Formulas

questions.explanation: D is correct: When True, collecting and applying formulas for Cube Views with retain formulas runs concurrently across worksheets for faster refreshes (Excel Add-In only). A is incorrect — this is a Cube View Connection option that highlights changed cells without a refresh; it doesn't speed up refresh. B is incorrect — this forces a refresh on open, which adds work. C is incorrect — this only sets the default for preserving formatting.

questions.question: On a touchscreen laptop, a user clicks Refresh Sheet but cells with functions never finish calculating. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Set Disable Interactive User During Refresh to True, noting it may cause incompatibility with other Excel add-ins
options.B: Set Use Minimal Calculation for Refresh to False
options.C: Set Force Add-In Compatibility for Registration to True
options.D: Set Excel calculation to Automatic

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide ties this setting to a known Excel situation on certain touchscreen hardware, with a note about possible add-in incompatibility. B is incorrect — this reverts to full calculation; it isn't the touchscreen fix. C is incorrect — this is for when external add-ins turn the Add-In off at start-up. D is incorrect — the guide recommends Manual calculation with OneStream workbooks, and this isn't the touchscreen fix.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Preferences: Retain All Formatting
questions.question: What is the default for Retain All Formatting when Saving Offline, and why?

options.A: True, so offline copies match the original exactly
options.B: False, because offline copies can't hold any formatting
options.C: False, which keeps basic formatting for better performance
options.D: True, but only for Spreadsheet

questions.explanation: C is correct: The default is False to derive basic formatting and better performance; True keeps all character-by-character formatting. A is incorrect — the default is False. B is incorrect — False still keeps basic formatting. D is incorrect — this setting is for the Excel Add-In only, not Spreadsheet, and its default is False.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Preferences: Hidden Rows Offline
questions.question: A user wants hidden rows to stay hidden in offline copies, but the Preserve Hidden Rows and Columns setting is unavailable. Why?

options.A: Preserve Excel Format must be enabled on the Cube View Connection
options.B: Retain All Formatting when Saving Offline must be True first
options.C: The workbook must be opened from the OneStream File System
options.D: Use Add-In Compatibility Filter must be False

questions.explanation: B is correct: Preserve Hidden Rows and Columns only becomes active when Retain All Formatting when Saving Offline is True. A is incorrect — that is a connection-level option, not what activates this Preference. C is incorrect — the guide ties it to Retain All Formatting, not where the file came from. D is incorrect — that controls third-party cell changes, not this setting.

questions.question: A third-party Excel add-in is unexpectedly changing values in OneStream-linked cells. Which Preference stops this?

options.A: Set Force Add-In Compatibility for Registration to True
options.B: Set Enable Macros for OneStream Event Processing to False
options.C: Set Disable Interactive User During Refresh to True
options.D: Set Use Add-In Compatibility Filter to True

questions.explanation: D is correct: When True, only cell selection change events like keystrokes or mouse clicks are allowed; third-party add-ins and macros can't change cells. A is incorrect — this forces re-registration of the OneStream Add-In; it doesn't block other add-ins' edits. B is incorrect — this controls macros for OneStream API calls, not other add-ins changing cells. C is incorrect — this addresses touchscreen refresh issues and may itself cause add-in incompatibility.

questions.question: Each time Excel starts, the OneStream ribbon is gone because another vendor's add-in turns it off. Which Preference addresses this?

options.A: Force Add-In Compatibility for Registration
options.B: Use Add-In Compatibility Filter
options.C: Display Context Pane
options.D: Invalidate Old Data When Workbook is Opened

questions.explanation: A is correct: When True this forces a re-registration of the OneStream Add-In and should be used when external add-ins turn it off on start-up. B is incorrect — this stops third-party add-ins from changing cells, not from disabling the Add-In. C is incorrect — this shows or hides the task pane. D is incorrect — this forces a data refresh when a workbook opens.

questions.question: A user wants to double-click an expanded Quick View row header to collapse it again. Which Default Expansion setting is required?

options.A: TreeDescendants
options.B: NextLevel
options.C: TreeDescendantsR
options.D: ChildrenInclusive

questions.explanation: B is correct: The double-click-to-collapse feature only works with the NextLevel setting, which is also the default. A is incorrect — the guide says collapse on double-click only works with NextLevel. C is incorrect — this reverses member display order; it doesn't enable collapsing. D is incorrect — only NextLevel supports collapsing on double-click.

questions.question: What is the default for the Preserve Excel Formatting by Default settings for Quick Views, Cube Views and Table Views?

options.A: True for all three
options.B: True for Cube Views, False for Quick Views and Table Views
options.C: True for Quick Views only
options.D: False for all three

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide lists the default as False for Quick Views, Cube Views and Table Views. A is incorrect — each default is False. B is incorrect — all three are False. C is incorrect — all three are False.

questions.question: What does the guide recommend for Excel's calculation setting when working with OneStream spreadsheets, and is it enforced?

options.A: Manual is recommended but not forced, because some users prefer Automatic with small amounts of data
options.B: Automatic is required so XF functions recalculate
options.C: Manual is forced by the Add-In when a user logs in
options.D: Automatic Except for Data Tables is recommended and enforced

questions.explanation: A is correct: Automatic recalculates every time a OneStream workbook changes data (such as navigating a Quick View), so Manual is recommended; it isn't forced. B is incorrect — the guide recommends Manual. C is incorrect — the guide says it is not forced. D is incorrect — the guide recommends Manual and doesn't force any mode.

questions.question: Support asks a user for Excel Add-In error logs from five months ago. Where are logs stored, and are they still there?

options.A: In the application's Error Log on the System tab; yes, they're kept indefinitely
options.B: In the AppData folder on the local drive; no, logs are deleted automatically after 60 days
options.C: In the AppData folder; yes, they're kept for one year
options.D: In File Explorer under the user's Documents folder; no, they're deleted after 30 days

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Add-In stores error logs locally in AppData, and logs are deleted automatically after 60 days. A is incorrect — Add-In error logs are stored locally, not in the server Error Log. C is incorrect — logs are deleted after 60 days. D is incorrect — logs are stored in local AppData and kept 60 days.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Cube View Connection Name
questions.question: A user types 'Q1 P&L' in the Name field of a new Cube View Connection, then selects a Cube View. What name does the connection get?

options.A: The Cube View's name, overwriting the typed name
options.B: The Refers To cell address
options.C: Q1 P&L, because a name typed first is kept
options.D: A blank name that must be re-entered after clicking OK

questions.explanation: C is correct: The name is generated if the Cube View is selected first; if a name is typed first and then the Cube View is selected, the typed name is kept. A is incorrect — the typed name is kept when typed first. B is incorrect — Refers To is the starting cell or range, not the name. D is incorrect — the guide says the typed name is retained.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells
questions.question: A designer can't select Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells in the Cube View Connection dialog. What must be selected first?

options.A: Retain Formulas in Cube View Content
options.B: Preserve Excel Format
options.C: Include Cube View Header
options.D: Add Parameter Selectors to Sheet

questions.explanation: A is correct: Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells is only available if Retain Formulas in Cube View Content is selected. B is incorrect — that keeps native Excel formatting; it doesn't unlock this option. C is incorrect — that adds header rows. D is incorrect — that generates parameter selectors.

questions.question: A designer created a Cube View Connection last week without parameter selectors and now wants to use Add Parameter Selectors to Sheet. What does the guide say?

options.A: Edit the connection and check the option; selectors appear on next refresh
options.B: It must be selected during creation and can't be added retroactively; parameters can be added via OneStream > General > Parameters
options.C: Enable Retain Formulas in Cube View Content to unlock the option
options.D: Run Refresh Workbook, which adds selectors for all parameters

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says this option must be selected during creation and can't be added later; parameters are managed from General > Parameters. A is incorrect — the guide says it can't be added retroactively. C is incorrect — Retain Formulas unlocks Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells, not parameter selectors. D is incorrect — Refresh Workbook prompts for parameters; it doesn't add selectors to the sheet.

questions.question: A designer deletes a Cube View Connection that was created with Add Parameter Selectors to Sheet. What happens to its parameter selectors?

options.A: They're deleted automatically with the connection
options.B: They become In-Sheet Action buttons
options.C: They're orphaned and must be deleted manually from the Parameters ribbon
options.D: They move to the next Cube View Connection on the sheet

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says deleting the connection alone orphans the parameters; they must be deleted manually. A is incorrect — the guide says they remain and are orphaned. B is incorrect — nothing converts parameters into In-Sheet Actions. D is incorrect — the guide says they're orphaned.

questions.question: A user turned off Resize Initial Column Widths Using Cube View Settings, adjusted columns and saved. Later they open the same Cube View Connection to change another setting. What must they watch for?

options.A: Nothing; the choice is saved permanently with the connection
options.B: Preserve Excel Format turns off automatically
options.C: The connection must be deleted and recreated to change any setting
options.D: The check box will be enabled again, so they must turn it off again to keep their column widths

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says if you go back into the connection, the box is enabled again and must be disabled again. A is incorrect — the guide says the box is re-enabled when you go back into the connection. B is incorrect — the guide doesn't say that; the issue is the column-width box. C is incorrect — connections can be edited from the Cube View Connections dialog.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas and External Workbooks
questions.question: A Cube View Connection has Retain Formulas on but Dynamically Highlight Evaluated Cells off. Its formulas reference an external workbook that was just updated. What must the user do so OneStream gets the new values?

options.A: Just Submit Sheet; the changes are detected automatically
options.B: Convert the connection to XFGetCells, then submit
options.C: Use Save Offline Copy, then Save to Server
options.D: Refresh Sheet to see the dirty cells, then Submit Sheet

questions.explanation: D is correct: With external workbooks or referenced-sheet updates, you must Refresh Sheet to see dirty cells and then Submit Sheet unless Dynamically Highlight Evaluated Cells is on. A is incorrect — without dynamic highlighting, a refresh is needed first to see the dirty cells. B is incorrect — Convert to XFGetCells applies to Quick Views and isn't part of this process. C is incorrect — those save files; they don't submit data.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas: Well-Formed Grid
questions.question: To make sure relative (=C2) and absolute (=$C$2) formulas are kept in a Cube View with Retain Formulas, what row definition does the guide suggest?

options.A: A member expansion such as A#Root.Descendants
options.B: A Well-Formed Grid using Root.List or a comma-separated list
options.C: A dynamic row using TreeDescendantsInclusive
options.D: Any row definition, as long as Include Cube View Header is on

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide suggests a 'Well-Formed Grid' (Root.List or Comma Separated List) so relative and absolute formulas are retained. A is incorrect — with member expansion functions, references must be adjusted or referenced as text. C is incorrect — dynamic expansions break cell-reference formulas when members move. D is incorrect — the header option doesn't affect formula retention.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas: Excel vs. Spreadsheet
questions.question: A planner wants a writeable Cube View cell to keep a formula pointing to a cell in a separate saved workbook. Where does this work?

options.A: Only in the Excel Add-In, not in Spreadsheet
options.B: Only in Spreadsheet
options.C: In both the Excel Add-In and Spreadsheet
options.D: In neither; Retain Formulas only supports references on the same sheet

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says linking a writeable cell to a cell in a different workbook works ONLY in Excel and NOT in Spreadsheet. B is incorrect — Spreadsheet can't point cell references to external workbooks. C is incorrect — Spreadsheet doesn't support external workbook references. D is incorrect — the guide's use cases include other sheets and, in Excel, other workbooks.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas: Member Expansion
questions.question: A Cube View uses a member expansion function in rows, and a retained formula is =VLOOKUP(D30,Sheet1!A:B,2,FALSE). Members shift when metadata changes. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Keep D30, because Retain Formulas re-points cell references automatically
options.B: Change D30 to $D$30
options.C: Reference the member as text, such as =VLOOKUP("52000 - Promotions",Sheet1!A:B,2,FALSE)
options.D: Turn on Dynamically Evaluate Highlighted Cells

questions.explanation: C is correct: With member expansion functions, the cell ref D30 won't work when members move, so the lookup should use text. A is incorrect — the guide says D30 will NOT work in a dynamic grid or when a member moves. B is incorrect — an absolute reference still points to a fixed cell that may hold a different member. D is incorrect — this highlights changed cells; it doesn't fix moved references.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas: What Keeps Formulas
questions.question: With Retain Formulas in Cube View Content enabled, which action keeps the existing formulas in place?

options.A: Pivoting the Cube View's dimensions
options.B: Changing row order from Account, Entity, UD3 to UD3, Entity, Account
options.C: Clearing the Retain Formulas in Cube View Content check box
options.D: Changing the POV to select a different member

questions.explanation: D is correct: Changing the POV changes results but keeps existing formulas; the user can use, change or delete them. A is incorrect — the guide says pivoting breaks formulas. B is incorrect — changing the grid structure breaks formulas. C is incorrect — clearing it removes all formulas on the grid.

questions.question: A retained formula in a writeable Cube View cell is an INDEX/MATCH that returns #N/A. What happens on refresh?

options.A: The formula isn't kept, and the cell goes back to its original Cube View value
options.B: The formula is kept and #N/A is submitted as zero
options.C: The cell turns yellow as a dirty cell and blocks submission
options.D: The sheet refresh fails with an error naming the first bad member

questions.explanation: A is correct: Formulas that return errors or non-numeric data can't be converted to a number, so the formula isn't kept and the cell returns to its original value. B is incorrect — error results don't retain the formula. C is incorrect — the guide says it returns to its original value. D is incorrect — that error behavior is for misspelled members in XF functions.

questions.subtopic: Excel Add-In — Retain Formulas: Renamed Files
questions.question: A user does Save As on an external workbook that a Cube View's retained formulas reference. When must the links be updated?

options.A: After the next submit, so the old values post first
options.B: Before doing a refresh or submit
options.C: Never; OneStream updates external links automatically
options.D: Only if Dynamically Highlight Evaluated Cells is turned off

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says when the referenced file is renamed or saved as, update the links BEFORE a refresh or submit. A is incorrect — links should be updated before refresh or submit. C is incorrect — the user must update the links. D is incorrect — the guide gives no such exception.

questions.question: Bringing a Cube View into Excel creates Named Regions for which areas?

options.A: Only the data section
options.B: Each Workflow Profile and Scenario in the POV
options.C: The Cube View, column headers, row headers and data sections
options.D: XFTV_ ranges for each column

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says Named Regions are created for the Cube View, column headers, row headers and data sections. A is incorrect — named regions also cover the Cube View and its headers. B is incorrect — named regions are tied to the grid, not to POV members. D is incorrect — XFTV_* named ranges manage Table View data cells.

questions.subtopic: Cube Views in Excel — Named Regions
questions.question: A designer wants a Total row formatted differently from detail rows in a Cube View brought into Excel. What does the guide suggest?

options.A: Use XFGetCell for the total
options.B: Intersection-based Named Regions with different Styles
options.C: Turn on Include Cube View Header and bold the header rows
options.D: Use Shrink to fit on the total row

questions.explanation: B is correct: bringing a Cube View into Excel creates Named Regions for the Cube View, column headers, row headers and data; the guide says to use intersection-based Named Regions with different Styles to separate sections like a Total row. A is incorrect — that's not the suggested approach. C is incorrect — that adds header rows. D is incorrect — that changes text size, not section formatting.

questions.question: A user can't find a Cube View in the Object Lookup when adding a Cube View Connection in Excel, although it works in OnePlace. What should the administrator check?

options.A: That Preserve Excel Formatting by Default (Cube Views) is True
options.B: That the workspace is set to Is Sharable Workspace = True
options.C: That the Cube View has Include Cube View Header turned on
options.D: That the Cube View is in a group within a Cube View Profile whose visibility is set for Excel

questions.explanation: D is correct: Before defining Cube View Connections, the Cube View must be in a group within a profile that has visibility set for Excel. A is incorrect — that setting only controls formatting. B is incorrect — sharability is needed for dependent parameters to refresh, not Cube View visibility. C is incorrect — that's a connection option, not what makes the Cube View visible.

questions.question: How does a Cube View Connection differ from exporting a Cube View to Excel?

options.A: The connection stays live, so data can be refreshed and submitted
options.B: The connection is read-only, while an export can be submitted
options.C: The connection keeps Excel formulas, while an export doesn't
options.D: The connection only works in Spreadsheet

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says Cube View Connections differ from exporting because the connection remains live. B is incorrect — it's the reverse; the live connection supports submit. C is incorrect — formula retention is an optional connection setting, not the defining difference. D is incorrect — Cube View Connections work in both Excel and Spreadsheet.

questions.question: How many changes can be undone using the Quick Views tab Undo button?

options.A: Up to 10
options.B: Up to 100
options.C: Up to 25
options.D: Only the last change
