questions.explanation: B is correct: The Quick Views tab Undo button undoes up to 100 changes. A is incorrect — the guide says 100. C is incorrect — the guide says 100. D is incorrect — the guide says up to 100.

questions.question: A user creates a Quick View without selecting members for several dimensions. What do those dimensions use?

options.A: The top member of each dimension
options.B: The None member of each dimension
options.C: The user's default POV settings
options.D: The Workflow POV of the Cube View last opened

questions.explanation: C is correct: If you don't select a member, the Quick View POV reflects your default POV settings. A is incorrect — the guide says default POV settings are used. B is incorrect — the guide says default POV settings are used. D is incorrect — the Quick View uses default POV settings, not a Cube View's.

questions.subtopic: Quick Views — Preserve Format and Drill Down
questions.question: A Quick View has Preserve Excel Format on. The user drills down to add rows. What happens to formatting?

options.A: Formatting isn't adjusted automatically; manual reformatting may be needed
options.B: The new rows inherit formatting from the row above
options.C: Preserve Excel Format turns off until the next refresh
options.D: The Quick View is converted to XFGetCells to keep formatting

questions.explanation: A is correct: With Preserve Excel Format on Quick Views, structural changes like drill down don't adjust formatting automatically. B is incorrect — the guide says formatting doesn't adjust automatically. C is incorrect — the setting stays on; formatting just isn't adjusted. D is incorrect — drill down doesn't convert the Quick View.

questions.question: A user copies a Quick View in the Spreadsheet tool and wants to paste it into a different workbook. What happens?

options.A: It pastes normally, as it does in Excel
options.B: It pastes as XFGetCell formulas
options.C: It pastes only if Preserve Excel Format is enabled
options.D: They can't; in Spreadsheet, copied Quick Views can only be pasted in the same workbook

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says copied Quick Views can only be pasted within the same workbook when using Spreadsheet. A is incorrect — Excel allows another workbook; Spreadsheet doesn't. B is incorrect — pasting doesn't convert to XFGetCells. C is incorrect — the restriction doesn't depend on formatting.

questions.subtopic: Quick Views — Adding a New Dimension
questions.question: A user wants to add the Scenario dimension to an existing Quick View that doesn't use Scenario. How should the member be typed before clicking Rebuild Quick View?

options.A: With the dimension token, such as S#Actual
options.B: Just Actual, because the Quick View finds the dimension
options.C: [Actual] in brackets
options.D: =XFGetMemberInfo("Scenario","Actual")

questions.explanation: A is correct: To add a dimension or member, enter # before the dimension or member; if the dimension is already used, # isn't required. B is incorrect — the token is needed because the dimension isn't used yet. C is incorrect — brackets are used for parameter values with spaces in In-Sheet Actions, not here. D is incorrect — Quick Views use dimension tokens, not XF functions.

questions.question: A user types comma-separated account names 60999,43000,61000 in one cell to add to a Quick View. What does the guide require?

options.A: Enclose the list in square brackets
options.B: Insert a space after each comma, because the names are numeric
options.C: Use semicolons instead of commas
options.D: Add a leading apostrophe to the whole cell

questions.explanation: B is correct: If names are numeric or start with an apostrophe, insert a space after each comma. A is incorrect — the guide calls for a space after each comma. C is incorrect — the guide uses commas with a space after each. D is incorrect — names starting with an apostrophe also need spaces after commas.

questions.question: A user wants to clear a Quick View down to three accounts without losing those selections. Which option fits?

options.A: Clear only a selected item
options.B: Convert to XFGetCells
options.C: Keep Only
options.D: Apply User POV

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Keep Only keeps the selected rows and columns unchanged, letting you clear a Quick View without losing selected data. A is incorrect — that clears one item. B is incorrect — that deletes the Quick View definition. D is incorrect — that passes a POV between Quick Views.

questions.question: A user wants double-clicking a Quick View row to show members in reverse display order. What should Default Expansion for Rows be set to?

options.A: NextLevel
options.B: DescendantsInclusive
options.C: TreeDescendantsR
options.D: Ancestors

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says set Default Expansion for Rows to TreeDescendantsR in Administration > Preferences. A is incorrect — NextLevel is the default and shows the next level, not reversed order. B is incorrect — this returns the member and all members under it in a list, not reversed. D is incorrect — this returns all members up the chain.

questions.question: A Quick View has a Zero Suppression Threshold of 499.99. Which value is suppressed?

options.D: 499.99 and every value above it

questions.explanation: C is correct: The threshold suppresses values less than the number specified, such as 499.19 when the threshold is 499.99. A is incorrect — 500.00 is above the threshold. B is incorrect — this is above the threshold. D is incorrect — the threshold suppresses values below it, not above.

questions.subtopic: Quick Views — Suppress Repeating Member Names
questions.question: In Quick View options, what happens when Suppress Repeating Member Names is False?

options.A: Repeating names show only once per group
options.B: Rows with invalid data are hidden
options.C: Values under the threshold are hidden
options.D: The repeating name displays in each row

questions.explanation: D is correct: If False, the repeating name displays in each row. A is incorrect — that is the True behavior. B is incorrect — that is Suppress Invalid Rows/Columns. C is incorrect — that is Zero Suppression Threshold.

questions.question: Which parameter type is NOT supported when using Parameters in the Excel Add-In or Spreadsheet?

options.A: Member Dialog
options.B: Bound List
options.C: Delimited List
options.D: Literal Value

questions.explanation: A is correct: The member dialog parameter is not supported. B is incorrect — Bound is supported. C is incorrect — Delimited is supported. D is incorrect — Literal is supported.

questions.question: A parameter has Display Items MI, OH and Value Items Michigan, OH. In the Parameter Selector Definition, Use Display Value is cleared. What appears in the drop-down?

options.A: MI and OH
options.B: Michigan and OH
options.C: MI, OH, Michigan and OH
options.D: Nothing until On Change Refresh is set

questions.explanation: B is correct: When Use Display Value is cleared, the Value Items appear; when selected, the Display Items (MI and OH) appear. A is incorrect — that's what appears when Use Display Value is selected. C is incorrect — only one set of items appears. D is incorrect — On Change Refresh controls what refreshes after a change.

questions.question: A designer adds nested and input parameters to a sheet but doesn't use them in any Cube View or Table View. What does the guide warn?

options.A: They work normally as standalone filters
options.B: They are automatically converted to Literal parameters
options.C: They're supported only in Spreadsheet
options.D: Nested and input parameters must be consumed by a Cube View or Table View; standalone ones may give undesirable results

questions.explanation: D is correct: The best practice says nested and input parameters need to be consumed by a Cube View or Table View. A is incorrect — the guide warns of undesirable results. B is incorrect — there's no such conversion. C is incorrect — the guidance applies to both Excel and Spreadsheet.

questions.subtopic: Excel Parameters — Dependent Order and Sharing
questions.question: Dependent Year and Month parameters were added manually to a sheet, but Month doesn't refresh when Year changes. Which TWO items does the guide call for?

options.A: Add Month before Year, and set On Change Refresh to Nothing
options.B: Add Year before Month, and turn on Use Display Value
options.C: Add Year before Month, and set Is Sharable Workspace to True for the workspace holding the Cube View or dependent parameter
options.D: Use a Member Dialog parameter for Month, and enable Retain Formulas

questions.explanation: C is correct: Manually added dependent parameters must be added in resolution order, and the workspace must be sharable for them to refresh correctly. A is incorrect — Year must come before Month; Nothing keeps the sheet as is. B is incorrect — Use Display Value only picks display vs. value items. D is incorrect — Member Dialog isn't supported, and Retain Formulas is unrelated.

questions.question: Which task can an In-Sheet Action button NOT perform?

options.A: Consolidate the selected cell
options.B: Refresh a worksheet or workbook
options.C: Submit a worksheet or workbook
options.D: Run a Data Management sequence

questions.explanation: A is correct: In-Sheet Actions refresh, submit, or run a Data Management sequence; consolidation from Excel uses the Calculation ribbon or right-click. B is incorrect — this is a listed in-sheet action. C is incorrect — this is a listed in-sheet action. D is incorrect — this is a listed in-sheet action.

questions.question: A designer makes an In-Sheet Action button span four cells in Excel. What happens when the workbook opens in Spreadsheet?

options.A: The button keeps all four cells
options.B: The button reverts to a single cell
options.C: The button is removed because In-Sheet Actions are Excel-only
options.D: The button turns into a parameter drop-down

questions.explanation: B is correct: If a button spans more than one cell, it reverts to a single cell when opened in Spreadsheet. A is incorrect — the guide says it reverts to a single cell. C is incorrect — In-Sheet Actions work in Excel and Spreadsheet. D is incorrect — nothing converts buttons into parameters.

questions.question: An In-Sheet Action runs a Data Management sequence that needs MyEntity set to South Houston and MyYear set to 2024. What is the correct syntax?

options.A: MyEntity="South Houston"; MyYear=2024
options.B: |!MyEntity!|=South Houston, |!MyYear!|=2024
options.C: MyEntity=[South Houston], MyYear=2024
options.D: MyEntity=South Houston, MyYear=2024

questions.explanation: C is correct: Separate parameters with a comma and use brackets when a value has a space. A is incorrect — the guide uses brackets and commas, not quotes and semicolons. B is incorrect — the guide's syntax is name=value, with brackets for values with spaces. D is incorrect — a value with a space must be in brackets.

questions.question: An In-Sheet Action's DM sequence needs a parameter that no Cube View on the sheet uses. What happens, and how can it be fixed?

options.A: The user is prompted at run time, so no fix is needed
options.B: Set Do not wait for task to finish so the parameter resolves on the server
options.C: Use Add Parameter Selectors to Sheet on the existing connection
options.D: No prompt appears; add the parameter somewhere in a Cube View, such as the page caption, or for Table Views, in GetCustomSubsVars

questions.explanation: D is correct: Parameters must be resolved in an existing Cube View or Table View; in-sheet actions don't prompt for unresolved parameters. A is incorrect — in-sheet actions don't prompt for unresolved parameters. B is incorrect — this setting only lets the sequence run in the background. C is incorrect — this can only be chosen during connection creation, and it doesn't make In-Sheet Actions prompt.

questions.subtopic: In-Sheet Actions — Background Run and Format
questions.question: Which statement about In-Sheet Action buttons is correct?

options.A: Do not wait for task to finish lets the user keep working while the DM sequence runs, and buttons default to black with white text
options.B: Buttons default to white with black text and accept six-character hex color codes
options.C: The Refresh field must be set for the Submit field to work
options.D: Workspace Name must be typed before choosing a DM sequence

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide describes both settings. B is incorrect — the default is black with white text, and colors use eight-character hex codes. C is incorrect — Submit and Refresh are separate drop-downs, each with a Nothing option. D is incorrect — Workspace Name fills in after the sequence is selected.

questions.question: Using right-click Create Quick View Using POV from Selected Cell, which cell types' POV can be used?

options.A: Only Quick View cells
options.B: Only Table View cells
options.C: Any cell, including blank cells, using the Global POV
options.D: A Quick View cell, a Cube View cell or an XFGetCell

questions.explanation: D is correct: The right-click version can use a Quick View cell's, a Cube View cell's or an XFGetCell's POV. A is incorrect — Cube View cells and XFGetCells also work. B is incorrect — Table View cells aren't listed. C is incorrect — the option uses the selected cell's POV from a Quick View, Cube View or XFGetCell.

questions.subtopic: Quick Views — Expand Options: List vs. Hierarchy
questions.question: A user right-clicks a parent member in a Quick View and wants every member below it shown as an indented hierarchy that includes the selected member. Which Expand option should be used?

options.A: DescendantsInclusive
options.B: TreeDescendantsInclusive
options.C: TreeDescendants
options.D: ChildrenInclusive

questions.explanation: B is correct: TreeDescendantsInclusive returns the selected member and every member under it in a hierarchy. A is incorrect — this returns the same members as a list, not a hierarchy. C is incorrect — this returns members under the selected member in a hierarchy but excludes the selected member. D is incorrect — this returns only the selected member and its first level of children.

questions.subtopic: Quick Views — Expand Options: Parents vs. Ancestors
questions.question: An entity belongs to three alternate hierarchies. Which Expand option returns only its direct parents across all of those hierarchies?

options.A: Ancestors
options.B: AllTops
options.C: Parents
options.D: AllBase

questions.explanation: C is correct: Parents returns the direct parents of the selected member regardless of how many hierarchies it belongs to. A is incorrect — Ancestors returns all members up the chain, not just direct parents. B is incorrect — AllTops returns the top of the dimension. D is incorrect — AllBase returns all base members of the dimension.

questions.question: A user needs to run a Force Consolidate with additional logging on a cell from Excel. Where should they launch it?

options.A: The Calculation group on the OneStream ribbon
options.B: General > In-Sheet Actions with a Data Management Sequence
options.C: Tasks > Task Activity
options.D: Right-click > OneStream > Consolidate

questions.explanation: D is correct: Right-click Calculate/Translate/Consolidate work like the ribbon icons but add the choice of Force operations and additional Logging. A is incorrect — the ribbon icons run the calculation on the selected cell but don't offer Force or Logging choices. B is incorrect — in-sheet buttons run DM sequences, refresh or submit; that's not the direct Force/Logging option the guide describes. C is incorrect — Task Activity only views running, scheduled and completed tasks.

questions.question: A user wants a long list of properties about a cell, such as whether it is read-only. Which right-click option?

options.A: Cell Status
options.B: Cell Detail
options.C: Data Attachments
options.D: Navigate

questions.explanation: A is correct: Cell Status returns a long list of properties about a cell. B is incorrect — Cell Detail is for entering detail. C is incorrect — that shows comments and attachments. D is incorrect — Navigate launches linked Cube Views or dashboards.

questions.question: Where does a user find OneStream retrieve functions in Insert Function, in Excel versus Spreadsheet?

options.A: Both use the category OneStreamExcelAddIn.XFFunctions
options.B: Excel: category OneStreamExcelAddIn.XFFunctions; Spreadsheet: category User Defined
options.C: Excel: User Defined; Spreadsheet: OneStreamExcelAddIn.XFFunctions
options.D: Both are found only through Object Lookup

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Excel guide says to select OneStreamExcelAddIn.XFFunctions, and Spreadsheet says User Defined. A is incorrect — Spreadsheet uses User Defined. C is incorrect — the categories are reversed. D is incorrect — the guide points to Insert Function categories.

questions.subtopic: Retrieve Functions — XFGetCell vs. Member Script
questions.question: How does XFGetCell take dimension members compared with XFGetCellUsingScript?

options.A: XFGetCell requires the full member script in one parameter
options.B: Both need member script syntax in every parameter
options.C: XFGetCell takes each member as a separate parameter (CT, Sales); UsingScript functions combine member script parts like E#CT:A#Sales
options.D: XFGetCell only accepts five UD dimensions

questions.explanation: C is correct: XFGetCell uses one parameter per dimension without member script syntax, while UsingScript combines member script pieces. A is incorrect — that describes UsingScript functions. B is incorrect — XFGetCell doesn't use member script syntax. D is incorrect — limiting UDs to five is XFGetCell5.

questions.question: From Excel, a user wants to launch a linked dashboard from a Cube View cell. Which option?

options.A: Drill Down
options.B: Apply User POV
options.C: Paste POV
options.D: Navigate

questions.explanation: D is correct: Navigate launches a Cube View or dashboard from Excel when configured (Linked Cube Views and Linked Dashboards). A is incorrect — Drill Down shows more detail on a cell. B and C are incorrect — they pass POVs between Quick Views.

questions.question: How does XFGetCell5 differ from XFGetCell?

options.A: It returns values for five time periods at once
options.B: It's the volatile version for Excel charts
options.C: It always uses Local consolidation and Forms origin
options.D: It limits the User Defined dimensions to five instead of eight

questions.explanation: D is correct: XFGetCell5 works like XFGetCell but limits UDs to five. A is incorrect — the 5 refers to UD dimensions. B is incorrect — volatile versions end in Volatile. C is incorrect — that describes functions like XFGetCellLocalForms5.

questions.question: A workbook needs the EUR-to-USD rate, but only the USD-to-EUR rate is stored. Which function returns it directly?

options.A: XFGetCalculatedFxRate
options.B: XFGetFXRate
options.C: XFSetFXRate
options.D: XFGetMemberProperty

questions.explanation: A is correct: It retrieves an exchange rate even if only the inverse rate exists. B is incorrect — XFGetFXRate retrieves stored rates; the guide names XFGetCalculatedFxRate for inverse rates. C is incorrect — this saves rates. D is incorrect — this returns member properties, not FX rates.

questions.question: A user needs the Currency property of the Houston entity in a cell. Which formula follows the guide?

options.A: XFGetRelationshipProperty("Entity","Houston","Currency","","")
options.B: XFGetMemberProperty("Entity","Houston","Currency","","","")
options.C: XFGetMemberInfo("Currency","Entity","Houston","","")
options.D: XFGetHierarchyProperty("Entity","Houston","Currency")

questions.explanation: B is correct: XFGetMemberProperty gets Member Properties tab values; unused vary-by fields use double quotes, and property names have no spaces. A is incorrect — XFGetRelationshipProperty gets relationship properties and needs parent and child. C is incorrect — XFGetMemberInfo retrieves descriptions. D is incorrect — XFGetHierarchyProperty answers hierarchy questions like HasChildren.

questions.question: A report needs TRUE or FALSE for whether Houston Heights has children. Which function is used?

options.A: XFGetMemberProperty with property HasChildren
options.B: XFInternalGetDataFromServer
options.C: XFGetHierarchyProperty with property HasChildren
options.D: XFGetRelationshipProperty with property PercentConsolidation

questions.explanation: C is correct: This function determines whether a dimension member has children and returns True or False. A is incorrect — XFGetMemberProperty reads Member Properties tab values. B is incorrect — it returns True or False but is internal-only and takes no arguments. D is incorrect — this returns a relationship property value.

questions.subtopic: Retrieve Functions — Dashboard Parameter in Spreadsheet
questions.question: A Spreadsheet embedded in a dashboard needs XFGetCell formulas to use the dashboard's ParamEntity value. What practice does the guide describe?

options.A: Type |!ParamEntity!| directly as the XFGetCell entity argument
options.B: Use Add Parameter Selectors to Sheet on the XFGetCell
options.C: Use XFGetMemberInfo to look up the parameter name
options.D: Use XFGetDashboardParameterValue to put the parameter value in a cell (such as B1), then point XFGetCell at B1

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says fetch the value or its default into a cell, then reference that cell. A is incorrect — the guide's practice is XFGetDashboardParameterValue into a cell. B is incorrect — that option is for Cube View Connections only. C is incorrect — XFGetMemberInfo retrieves member descriptions.

questions.question: How do the first arguments of XFSetCell differ from XFGetCell?

options.A: XFSetCell starts with CellValue and StoreZeroAsNoData; XFGetCell starts with NoDataAsZero
options.B: Both start with NoDataAsZero, then Cube
options.C: XFSetCell starts with Cube and ends with CellValue
options.D: XFSetCell starts with StoreZeroAsNoData, then FXRateType

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide lists XFSetCell(CellValue, StoreZeroAsNoData, Cube, …) and XFGetCell(NoDataAsZero, Cube, …). B is incorrect — XFSetCell starts with CellValue and StoreZeroAsNoData. C is incorrect — CellValue is first. D is incorrect — FXRateType is in XFSetFXRate.

questions.question: An Excel chart that references calculated cells isn't updating with XFGetCell values. Which functions does the guide suggest?

options.A: …Ex versions, such as XFGetCellUsingScriptEx
options.B: Volatile versions, such as XFGetCellVolatile
options.C: XFInternal functions, such as XFInternalPrepareCalculationStep
options.D: 5 versions, such as XFGetCell5

questions.explanation: B is correct: Excel sometimes needs a volatile function to refresh properly, for example charts that reference calculated cells. A is incorrect — Ex versions add parameters for combining member scripts. C is incorrect — XFInternal functions only work for internal processes. D is incorrect — 5 versions limit UDs to five.

questions.question: What does XFSetCellLocalForms do?

options.A: Saves data only to Workflow Forms
options.B: Saves data in local currency and translates it
options.C: Saves data using the Local Consolidation member and the Forms Origin member
options.D: Retrieves data from AdjInput using five UDs

questions.explanation: C is correct: These functions use Consolidation and Origin; XFSetCellLocalForms uses Local and Forms. A is incorrect — it fixes Consolidation and Origin members. B is incorrect — it uses the Local Consolidation member; it doesn't translate. D is incorrect — that describes XFGetCellLocalAdjInput5.

questions.question: Before converting a large Quick View to XFGetCells, what should a designer know?

options.A: Use Undo on the Quick Views tab to reverse it
options.B: It can't be converted back to a Quick View, so save the Quick View content as a template first
options.C: Formulas reference the Quick View POV, so members stay dynamic
options.D: Use Create Quick View Using POV from Selected Cell to rebuild it

questions.explanation: B is correct: Converted data can't go back into a Quick View, but the content can be saved as a template first. A is incorrect — the definition is deleted, and the guide says it can't be converted back. C is incorrect — conversion hardcodes all dimension members. D is incorrect — that makes a new Quick View from one cell's POV, not the original layout.

questions.question: A user manually inserts an XFGetCell, leaves the UD8 argument as "", and clicks OK. What happens?

options.A: UD8 defaults to None, and the value appears right away
options.B: UD8 defaults to Top, and the cell shows #VALUE!
options.C: The function is rejected because each parameter must be filled
options.D: UD8 uses the Cube POV, and the cell shows #REFRESH until the sheet is refreshed

questions.explanation: D is correct: A "" argument defaults to the Cube POV, and the cell changes to #REFRESH after OK. A is incorrect — "" defaults to the Cube POV. B is incorrect — "" defaults to the Cube POV, and the cell shows #REFRESH. C is incorrect — "" is allowed.

questions.question: An XFGetCell has two misspelled member names. What does the cell return after refresh?

options.A: An error naming the first misspelled member
options.B: Zero, because NoDataAsZero is True
options.C: An error listing every misspelled member
options.D: #REFRESH until the names are fixed

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says the cell returns an error calling out the first misspelled member. B is incorrect — a misspelled member gives an error, not a zero. C is incorrect — only the first is called out. D is incorrect — #REFRESH appears before refresh; misspellings return an error.

questions.question: A VBA macro must log on to a OneStream IdentityServer (OIS) environment. Which approach?

options.A: LogonAndOpenApplicationWithToken with a Personal Access Token
options.B: ProcessSSOAuthenticationAndCreateToken with user and password
options.C: LogonAndOpenApplication with user and password
options.D: XFInternaSetConnectionInfo

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide shows OIS supports Personal Access Tokens via LogonAndOpenApplicationWithToken(url, PAT, application). B is incorrect — ROPC isn't supported and that method is deprecated. C is incorrect — that is Native Authentication (self-hosted). D is incorrect — XFInternal functions are internal only.

questions.question: In VBA, how do the guide's examples get the object used to call procedures like RefreshXFFunctions?

options.A: Application.Run "XFFunctions.RefreshXFFunctions"
options.B: CreateObject("OneStream.XFFunctions").Refresh
options.C: Workbooks("OneStreamExcelAddIn").RefreshXFFunctions
options.D: Set xfAddIn = Application.COMAddIns("OneStreamExcelAddIn"), then call xfAddIn.Object.RefreshXFFunctions

questions.explanation: D is correct: Each example gets the COM add-in OneStreamExcelAddIn and calls procedures on .Object. A is incorrect — the guide uses the COMAddIns object. B is incorrect — the guide uses Application.COMAddIns. C is incorrect — the Add-In is a COM add-in, not a workbook.

questions.question: For a self-hosted environment with native authentication, which VBA procedure logs on with a user name and password?

options.A: LogonAndOpenApplication(url, user, password, application)
options.B: LogonAndOpenApplicationWithToken(url, PAT, application)
options.C: ProcessSSOAuthenticationAndCreateToken
options.D: ShowParametersDlg()

questions.explanation: A is correct: Native authentication uses LogonAndOpenApplication with a user ID and password. B is incorrect — this is for token-based logons such as OIS PATs. C is incorrect — this is deprecated because ROPC is no longer supported. D is incorrect — this shows the parameters dialog.

questions.question: A finance team wants a VBA routine to submit many workbooks linked to other files without opening each one. Which procedure applies, and what does it submit?

options.A: SubmitXFFunctions, which submits all Cube Views, Quick Views and XFSetCells
options.B: RefreshXFFunctions, which refreshes and then submits
options.C: SubmitXFFunctions, which submits XFSetCells only
options.D: RefreshCubeViewsForActiveWorkSheet

questions.explanation: C is correct: SubmitXFFunctions automates loading for files with XFSET functions and calls only XFSetCells. A is incorrect — the procedure calls only XFSetCells. B is incorrect — RefreshXFFunctions only refreshes. D is incorrect — this refreshes Cube Views on the active sheet.

questions.question: When enabling Preserve Excel Format on Cube Views or Table Views, what does the guide recommend, and what extra requirement applies to Table Views?

options.A: Turn on Insert or Delete Rows/Columns; Table Views need XFTV_ named ranges
options.B: Turn off Insert or Delete Rows/Columns When Resizing; Table View DataType columns must be numeric
options.C: Turn off Include Cube View Header; Table Views must use a Spreadsheet-type rule
options.D: Turn on Retain Formulas; Table Views must have fewer than 8000 rows

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide recommends disabling insert/delete when preserving formatting, and Table Views need a numeric DataType column. A is incorrect — the guide recommends disabling insert/delete, and the Table View requirement is DataType. C is incorrect — neither is the guide's Preserve Format guidance. D is incorrect — neither is the guide's Preserve Format guidance.

questions.question: A user copies a Quick View that has Preserve Excel Format on and custom formatting. What happens to the formatting?

options.A: It's removed; copies always use Default Cube View Format
options.B: It's kept only if the copy is pasted in the same workbook
options.C: It carries to the copy because Preserve Excel Format is on in the source
options.D: It's kept only after the copy is converted to XFGetCells

questions.explanation: C is correct: Formatting stays on the copy when Preserve Excel Format is on in the source view. A is incorrect — formatting is kept when the source preserves it. B is incorrect — the guide doesn't limit formatting retention by workbook. D is incorrect — conversion isn't required.

questions.subtopic: Formatting — Custom Styles for Quick Views
questions.question: A user creates an Excel cell style with format #,, to show millions. How is it applied to a Quick View?

options.A: Through Cube Views > Selection Styles
options.B: Through Preferences > Default Display Settings
options.C: Through In-Sheet Actions > Button Theme
options.D: Through Edit Quick View Options on the Quick Views tab, using the Data Style

questions.explanation: D is correct: After creating the style, it's assigned through Edit Quick View Options. A is incorrect — Selection Styles format Cube View Connections. B is incorrect — that sets defaults for new Quick Views, not this style. C is incorrect — Button Theme only formats buttons.

questions.question: A Cube View range has Cube View styles, a Selection Style and an Excel conditional rule (Greater Than 6000). A cell is above 6000. Which formatting shows?

options.A: The conditional formatting, which overrides Cube View styles and Selection Styles
options.B: The Selection Style, which always overrides conditional formatting
options.C: The Cube View style, because server formatting takes priority
options.D: Pale yellow, because conditional cells are dirty cells

questions.explanation: A is correct: Conditional formatting overrides styles from the Cube View and selection styles on that range. B is incorrect — conditional formatting wins when the condition is met. C is incorrect — conditional formatting overrides it. D is incorrect — pale yellow marks changed values, not met conditions.

questions.question: A cell had a Selection Style and a Greater Than 6000 rule. The user changes it to 4000 and submits. What formatting shows?

options.A: The conditional format until the workbook is saved
options.B: The Selection Style, because the condition is no longer met
options.C: Pale yellow until the next Refresh Workbook
options.D: Default Cube View Format, removing the Selection Style

questions.explanation: B is correct: After submit, it converts back to the selection style. A is incorrect — it reverts once the condition isn't met. C is incorrect — pale yellow shows before refresh or submit. D is incorrect — the guide says it goes back to the Selection Style.

questions.question: What is a prerequisite to creating a Selection Style?

options.A: A Quick View on the sheet
options.B: A Cube View Connection on the sheet
options.C: Preserve Excel Format enabled on the sheet
options.D: A Table View on the sheet

questions.explanation: B is correct: the steps for creating a Selection Style start with logging in and adding a Cube View via Cube Views > Cube View Connections; Selection Styles are for Cube Views. A and D are incorrect — Selection Styles are for Cube Views. C is incorrect — not required.

questions.question: When creating a Selection Style, which ranges can it apply to?

options.A: Data Section, Row Header or Column Header
options.B: Sheet, Workbook or Cube View
options.C: Current Selection, Entire Row or Entire Column
options.D: Current Selection only

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide lists those three options. A is incorrect — those are Named Regions, not the range choices. B is incorrect — the options are Selection, Entire Row or Entire Column. D is incorrect — Entire Row and Entire Column are also choices.

questions.question: A user opens Selection Styles but doesn't pick an Excel Style. What formatting is used?

options.A: Excel's Normal style
options.B: The last Selection Style used in the workbook
options.C: No formatting
options.D: Default Cube View Format

questions.explanation: D is correct: If a style isn't selected, the Default Cube View Format is used. A is incorrect — the guide names Default Cube View Format. B is incorrect — the guide names Default Cube View Format. C is incorrect — the Default Cube View Format applies.

questions.question: A designer applies a Selection Style to a Cube View Connection. What must they do so the formatting persists?

options.A: Submit Sheet
options.B: Save the file
options.C: Save Offline Copy
options.D: Run Refresh Workbook

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says to save the file to save formatting to the Cube View. A is incorrect — Submit sends data, not formatting. C is incorrect — this saves a copy without functions. D is incorrect — refresh doesn't save formatting.

questions.question: In Manage Selection Styles, a designer deletes a style from a Cube View. What happens to it?

options.A: It's removed from the Cube View but stays in the workbook
options.B: It's deleted from the workbook and all Cube Views
options.C: It becomes inactive and is reactivated on refresh
options.D: It's sent to the server as a Cube View style

questions.explanation: A is correct: A deleted style is still available in the current workbook. B is incorrect — the guide says it stays in the workbook. C is incorrect — inactive styles are reactivated with Activate. D is incorrect — Selection Styles are stored in the workbook.

questions.question: An administrator in the Administrators group tries to mass delete metadata and data from the Database page and is refused. Which explanation matches the guide?

options.A: The AdministerApplication role must be assigned to the Administrators group first
options.B: The ManageMetadata role overrides Administrator rights on the Database page
options.C: Mass deletes are only available through a Data Management Reset Scenario step
options.D: The Administrator Database role is unlike most roles: Administrators are not automatically given access to operations that require it

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the Administrator Database role is for a few people allowed to mass delete metadata and data, primarily on the Database page, and that Administrators are not automatically given access to operations requiring it. A is incorrect — Administer Application allows administering the application and loading zip files; it is not the role for mass deletes. B is incorrect — Manage Metadata only allows editing metadata in the Dimension Library; it does not override anything. C is incorrect — the guide ties mass deletes to the Administrator Database role and the Database page, not only to a Data Management step.

questions.question: An environment hosts three applications, each supported by a different group of administrators. Which application security role lets each group administer only its own application and load zip files into it?

options.A: Administer Application
options.B: Manage Application Properties
options.C: Open Application
options.D: Administrator Database

questions.explanation: A is correct: Administer Application allows a user to administer the application and load zip files, and the guide calls it useful when multiple applications in one environment are administered by different groups. B is incorrect — Manage Application Properties only allows updating the application's properties. C is incorrect — Open Application only lets a user see and open the application. D is incorrect — Administrator Database is for mass deleting metadata and data on the Database page.

questions.question: A user can open the application and run Cube Views but cannot save any data anywhere in the application. Which role is the user most likely missing?

options.A: View All Data
options.B: Manage Data
options.C: Modify Data
options.D: Unlock Workflow Unit

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says without Modify Data the user is basically a read-only user throughout the application. A is incorrect — View All Data lets a group view all data; it does not grant write access. B is incorrect — Manage Data covers administrative data tasks such as exporting and clearing data through Data Management, not ordinary data saving. D is incorrect — Unlock Workflow Unit only allows unlocking a Workflow Unit.

questions.subtopic: Application Security Roles — Unlock Workflow Unit
questions.question: A user is in the Unlock Workflow Unit role. What else does the guide say the user needs in order to lock a Workflow Unit?

options.A: The Certify and Lock Descendants role
options.B: Workflow Execution access
options.C: The Manage Workflow Profiles role
options.D: The Preserve Import Data role

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide states Unlock Workflow Unit allows unlocking, but the user must also have Workflow Execution access in order to lock a Workflow Unit. A is incorrect — Certify and Lock Descendants certifies and locks descendants from the Workflow; it is not the stated requirement. C is incorrect — Manage Workflow Profiles allows creating Workflow Profiles, not locking units. D is incorrect — Preserve Import Data is used to preserve imported data while Workflows are locked.

questions.subtopic: Application Security Roles — Preserve vs Restore Import Data
questions.question: After an administrator preserved imported data and then unlocked the Workflow so changes could be made, the business wants the imported data put back to its original state. Which role allows this?

options.A: Preserve Import Data
options.B: Unlock and UnCertify Ancestors
options.C: Manage Data
options.D: Restore Import Data

questions.explanation: D is correct: Restore Import Data allows the administrator to restore imported data to the original state from the Preserve Import process. A is incorrect — Preserve Import Data is the earlier step that saves the imported data; it does not restore it. B is incorrect — Unlock and UnCertify Ancestors unlocks and uncertifies ancestors from the Workflow. C is incorrect — Manage Data covers exporting and clearing data through Data Management.

questions.subtopic: Application Security Roles — View Source Data Audit
questions.question: Auditors need to see the Source Data Audit Report from within the Import Workflow. Which role grants this?

options.A: View All Data
options.B: Open Application
options.C: Create Audit Attachments
options.D: View Source Data Audit

questions.explanation: D is correct: View Source Data Audit allows a user to view the Source Data Audit Report within the Import Workflow. A is incorrect — View All Data lets a group view all data in the application, not the audit report specifically. B is incorrect — Open Application only allows seeing and opening the application. C is incorrect — Create Audit Attachments allows creating data attachments for supporting documentation.

questions.subtopic: Security Roles — Certify and Lock Descendants
questions.question: At month-end, a controller wants to certify and lock all child Workflow Profiles below a parent in one action. Which Application Security Role allows this?

options.A: Certify and Lock Descendants
options.B: Unlock and UnCertify Ancestors
options.C: Unlock Workflow Unit
options.D: Manage Workflow Profiles

questions.explanation: A is correct: Certify and Lock Descendants allows the user to certify and lock descendants from the Workflow, which is typically an administrator function. B is incorrect — this role does the opposite direction: it uncertifies and unlocks ancestors. C is incorrect — this role unlocks a Workflow Unit; it does not certify descendants. D is incorrect — this role allows creating new Workflow Profiles, not certifying them.

questions.question: Which application security role does the guide describe as allowing users to manage data 'in all aspects', including exporting data and clearing data completed through Data Management?

options.A: Modify Data
options.B: Administrator Database
options.C: Manage Data
options.D: Manage Data Sources

questions.explanation: C is correct: Manage Data allows users to manage data in all aspects, including but not limited to exporting data and clearing data completed through Data Management; it is typically an administrator function. A is incorrect — Modify Data allows modifying data; without it a user is read-only. B is incorrect — Administrator Database is for mass deleting metadata and data on the Database page. D is incorrect — Manage Data Sources allows creating new Data Sources.

questions.question: A consultant needs to encrypt a proprietary Finance Business Rule so other administrators cannot read its code. Which Application Security Role controls this?

options.A: Encrypt Business Rules
options.B: Business Rules Page
options.C: Manage Application Properties
options.D: Administrator Database

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Encrypt Business Rules role allows a user to Encrypt and Decrypt a rule from the Business Rule screen in the Application tab. B is incorrect — this is a User Interface role that only gives access to the Business Rules screen. C is incorrect — this role lets a user update the application's properties, not encrypt rules. D is incorrect — this role is for mass deleting metadata and data from the database page.

questions.subtopic: Application Security Roles — Manage Application Database Files
questions.question: A manager wants to edit the security on another user's personal folder in the Application Database file system. What does the guide say?

options.A: Security cannot be edited for a user folder; user folders are private to the user and managers
options.B: Assign the folder's Maintenance Group to the manager
options.C: Grant the manager ManageSystemDatabaseFiles, which overrides user folder security
options.D: Use the folder's individual security settings, which apply to User folders and sub-folders

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says user folders are private to the user and managers, and security cannot be edited for a user folder; folder-level security settings exclude User folders and sub-folders. B is incorrect — folder security settings can grant access to specific folders, but the guide excludes User folders from this. C is incorrect — ManageSystemDatabaseFiles gives full access to the user's own folders in the System database file system; it does not change user folder security. D is incorrect — the guide explicitly says individual folder security excludes access to User folders and sub-folders.

questions.subtopic: Application UI Roles — Application Load Extract Page
questions.question: Which application user interface role gives access to the Load/Extract screen under Application | Tools?

options.A: SystemLoadExtractPage
options.B: Application Load Extract Page
options.C: Data Management Admin Page
options.D: Application Properties Page

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Application Load Extract Page role gives access to the Load/Extract screen located in Application | Tools and is typically restricted to administrators. A is incorrect — SystemLoadExtractPage is a system-level role for System | Tools | Load/Extract. C is incorrect — Data Management Admin Page opens the Data Management Admin screen. D is incorrect — Application Properties Page opens the Application Properties screen.

questions.question: Which pairing of application user interface role and screen location is INCORRECT according to the guide?

options.A: Business Rules Page — Application | Tools
options.B: Data Management Admin Page — Application | Tools
options.C: BookAdminPage — Application | Presentation
options.D: Dimension Library Page — Application | Tools

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Dimension Library Page gives access to the Dimension Library screen located in Application | Cube, not Tools. A is incorrect — Business Rules Page is correctly located in Application | Tools. B is incorrect — Data Management Admin Page is correctly located in Application | Tools. C is incorrect — BookAdminPage gives access to Book Designer in Application | Presentation.

questions.question: Which role controls who can use OneStream connectors to pull data into external systems, and becomes available when access to the Power BI Connector is granted?

options.A: AnalyticsApi
options.B: View All Data
options.C: Manage Data Sources
options.D: Open Application

questions.explanation: A is correct: the AnalyticsApi role allows a user to access OneStream connectors to pull data into external systems and becomes available when access to the Power BI Connector is granted. B is incorrect — View All Data controls viewing all data in the application, not connector access. C is incorrect — Manage Data Sources allows creating Data Sources for imports. D is incorrect — Open Application only allows seeing and opening the application.

questions.subtopic: Application Properties — Global POV Initial Value
questions.question: A team does not plan to enforce Global Scenario and Global Time through the Transformation settings. What does the guide recommend for the Global Point of View?

options.A: Leave Global Scenario and Global Time blank
options.B: Set Enforce Global POV to True anyway
options.C: Configure an initial value even though the Transformation setting is not being used
options.D: Define the Global POV on each Workflow Profile instead

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the Global POV is enabled when forcing Global Scenario and Time through Transformation settings, and an initial value should be configured even if that setting is not used. A is incorrect — the guide recommends configuring an initial value rather than leaving it blank. B is incorrect — Enforce Global POV locks users' Workflow View; that is not needed if the team does not want enforcement. D is incorrect — Global Scenario and Global Time are Application Properties, not Workflow Profile settings.

questions.question: What file format and size does the guide specify for the Company Information logo that appears on Cube Views and Reports?

options.A: JPG, about 105 pixels high
options.B: PNG, about 50 pixels high
options.C: BMP, about 50 pixels wide
options.D: PNG, about 300 pixels wide

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Logo File property calls for a PNG image approximately 50 pixels high. A is incorrect — 105 pixels is the guide's example for the Standard Reports logo Height setting, and JPG is not the required format. C is incorrect — BMP is not the stated format, and the guide gives a height, not a width. D is incorrect — PNG is right, but the guide gives about 50 pixels high, not 300 wide.

questions.subtopic: Application Properties — UD Dimension Type for Workflow Channels
questions.question: A company plans by Entity by Product, and five people own different products within one Entity. They want each product's data locked on its own instead of locking the whole Entity. Which Application Properties setting supports this?

options.A: Lock after Certify
options.B: Enforce Global POV
options.C: User Defined Dimensions (Descriptions)
options.D: UD Dimension Type for Workflow Channels

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide uses this exact example: the Origin dimension controls data load, but a UD dimension can be designated for Workflow Channels so each channel can be locked separately instead of locking the entire Entity. A is incorrect — Lock after Certify auto-locks the Workflow after certification; it does not add a locking layer by UD. B is incorrect — Enforce Global POV stops users from changing their Workflow View. C is incorrect — UD descriptions only change the labels users see for the UD dimension types.

questions.question: The application Number Format is N0, but one report needs two decimals. According to the guide, where can the application setting be overridden?

options.A: Standard Reports settings in Application Properties
options.B: The Entity member's properties
options.C: Cube View formatting
options.D: The Currencies list

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the application Number Format setting can be overridden through Cube View formatting. A is incorrect — Standard Reports settings control logos, titles, headers and footers of auto-generated reports. B is incorrect — Entity properties do not control display number formats. D is incorrect — the Currencies list defines which currencies the application can use.

questions.question: In the Number Format #,###,0;(#,###,0);0, what do the three sections separated by semicolons represent?

options.A: Positive numbers; negative numbers; zeros
options.B: Thousands; millions; billions
options.C: Data cells; header cells; total cells
options.D: Decimal places; separator; currency symbol

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the three sections, separated by semicolons, represent the format for positive numbers, negative numbers and zeros. B is incorrect — the sections are not scaling levels. C is incorrect — the sections do not apply to different cell types. D is incorrect — the sections are not separate pieces of one number's format.

questions.question: In reports that show negative values in parentheses, positive and negative numbers are not lining up vertically. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Switch the format to N2
options.B: Override the format in the Standard Reports Header Labels
options.C: Add a percent sign to the zero section
options.D: Add a trailing space in the positive number format, e.g. #,###,0.00 ;(#,###,0.00);0.00

questions.explanation: D is correct: to align positives and negatives where parentheses are used, the guide says to include trailing spaces in the positive format to account for the trailing parenthesis, e.g. #,###,0.00 ;(#,###,0.00);0.00. A is incorrect — N2 only sets two decimals; it does not fix alignment. B is incorrect — Header Labels settings control label fonts and margins, not number formats. C is incorrect — a percent sign changes the display to a percentage and does not address alignment.

questions.question: An application needs a currency that is no longer in use for historical data, and it does not appear in the Application Properties Currencies list. What does the guide say to do?

options.A: Add it as a new member in the Dimension Library
options.B: Call OneStream Support
options.C: Create it as a new FX Rate Type
options.D: Load it through Application Load/Extract with the FX Rate CSV

questions.explanation: B is correct: the list already includes pre-Euro and phased-out currencies for historical loads, and if a defunct or new currency is not listed, the guide says to call OneStream Support. A is incorrect — currencies are not Dimension Library members that administrators add. C is incorrect — an FX Rate Type (e.g. Average, Closing) is not a currency. D is incorrect — the FX Rate CSV extracts rates; it does not add currencies.

questions.subtopic: Application Properties — Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year
questions.question: Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year is set to False, and the Workflow year is 2026. A user tries to import a file that has 2025 periods. What happens?

options.A: The 2025 data loads but is flagged on the Validate task
options.B: The data loads only if Enforce Global POV is also False
options.C: The data is redirected to the first period of 2026
options.D: Data cannot be imported to periods before the current Workflow year, and an indicator shows on the Import task

questions.explanation: D is correct: when this setting is False, data cannot be imported to time periods prior to the current Workflow year, and an icon displays on the Import task. A is incorrect — the guide says the data cannot be imported at all. B is incorrect — Enforce Global POV is a separate setting about locking the Workflow View; it does not override this restriction. C is incorrect — nothing in the guide redirects data to another period.

questions.question: Which Application Properties setting automatically locks the Workflow once it is certified?

options.A: Lock after Certify
options.B: Certify and Lock Descendants
options.C: Enforce Global POV
options.D: Unlock Workflow Unit

questions.explanation: A is correct: under Certification, Lock after Certify set to True auto-locks after certification in the Workflow. B is incorrect — Certify and Lock Descendants is a security role, not an application property. C is incorrect — Enforce Global POV locks users' Workflow View, not Workflow status. D is incorrect — Unlock Workflow Unit is a security role for unlocking.

questions.question: Which two Dimension Properties in Application Properties set the range of years the application covers?

options.A: Global Scenario and Global Time
options.B: Start Year and End Year
options.C: Allow Loads Before and Allow Loads After Workflow View Year
options.D: Vary Settings By Year and Use Weeks

questions.explanation: B is correct: under Dimension Properties, Time Dimension, Start Year is the application's starting year and End Year is its ending year. A is incorrect — Global Scenario and Global Time set the default Workflow POV. C is incorrect — these Transformation settings control whether loads are allowed outside the Workflow year. D is incorrect — these are settings for building a custom Time Dimension Type in System Tools.

questions.question: An administrator enters 'Product' as the UD2 Description in Application Properties. What is true about this description?

options.A: It renames the UD2 dimension in every cube
options.B: It applies only to the dimension that is assigned to UD2 in the default cube
options.C: It applies to the dimension type and appears in places like the POV, Dimension Library, Cube View Member Filters, Excel Add-in and Journals
options.D: It only appears on reports generated automatically from Cube Views

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the description applies to the dimension type, not to each dimension, and shows in hover tips and other interfaces including the POV, Dimension Library, Cube View Member Filters, drill-down headers, Excel Add-in/Spreadsheet and Journals. A is incorrect — it is a description shown to users, not a rename of any dimension. B is incorrect — the guide says it applies to the dimension type, not to each dimension. D is incorrect — it shows in many interfaces, not only on generated reports.

questions.question: When are the Standard Reports settings in Application Properties (Logo, Title, Header Labels, Header Bar, Footer) applied?

options.A: When a Report Book is exported to PDF
options.B: When a report is generated automatically from a Cube View
options.C: When a Dashboard Report component is rendered
options.D: When a Cube View is opened in the Excel Add-in

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says these settings are applied when auto-generating a report from a Cube View. A is incorrect — the guide does not tie these settings to Report Book exports. C is incorrect — Dashboard report components are not the stated scope. D is incorrect — Excel Add-in output is not a generated report.

questions.question: Which setting is NOT one of the Footer options in the Standard Reports section of Application Properties?

options.A: Show Line
options.B: Show Date
options.C: Show Page Numbers
options.D: Show Logo

questions.explanation: D is correct: the footer options listed are Text, Font Family, Font Size, Show Line, Show Date, Show Page Numbers, Line Color and Text Color; the logo has its own Logo section (Height, Bottom Margin). A is incorrect — Show Line is a footer option. B is incorrect — Show Date is a footer option. C is incorrect — Show Page Numbers is a footer option.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Three Ways to Write Logic
questions.question: A developer writes logic directly in a Data Source and wants to reuse it later in other Data Sources. What does the guide say about this choice?

options.A: A Complex Expression can be shared across artifacts after it is saved
options.B: A Member Formula is the only form that can be shared
options.C: Complex Expressions use different syntax than Business Rules
options.D: A Complex Expression stays with its artifact; to share the logic across artifacts it should be a Business Rule

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says the syntax is the same, but a Business Rule can be shared across many artifacts while a Complex Expression is contained within its artifact. A is incorrect — Complex Expressions are contained within the artifact; they are not shared. B is incorrect — Member Formula logic stays with the member and cannot be shared. C is incorrect — the guide says the syntax is the same.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — BRAPI, API and ARGS
questions.question: A Parser Business Rule is assigned to the Account dimension of a Data Source. Which utility group supplies the Account value being parsed and functions to use on it?

options.A: ARGS
options.B: BRAPI
options.C: API
options.D: XFBR

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide's example says that if a Parser rule is assigned to the Account dimension, args supplies the Account dimension data and a set of functions to use against it. B is incorrect — BRAPI provides common functions available in all areas of the product where a rule can be used. C is incorrect — API is the type-specific parameter (e.g. finance calculation functions), not the value passed in. D is incorrect — XFBR is the syntax for calling a Dashboard XFBR String rule, not a utility group.

questions.question: A developer encrypted a Business Rule and has lost the password. What does the guide say?

options.A: Any administrator can decrypt it from the Business Rules page
options.B: Compile All Business Rules and Formulas will decrypt it
options.C: It cannot be decrypted for further changes without the help of OneStream Support
options.D: Set the Is Encrypted property to False

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide warns to record the password, or the rule cannot be decrypted for further changes without the assistance of OneStream Support. A is incorrect — decrypting requires the password, even for an authorized user. B is incorrect — compiling checks syntax; it does not decrypt. D is incorrect — Is Encrypted is a read-only indicator that shows whether the rule is encrypted.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Enabling the Encrypt Button
questions.question: An administrator just added a user to the Encrypt Business Rules role, but the user does not see the Encrypt Business Rule button. What step from the guide is missing?

options.A: Go to Application > Tools > Business Rules and refresh the screen
options.B: Restart IIS on the application server
options.C: Set Contains Global Functions for Formulas to True
options.D: Assign the user to the rule's Maintenance group

questions.explanation: A is correct: after setting the role, the guide says to go to the Business Rules section and refresh the screen, and the Encrypt Business Rule button will appear in the menu. B is incorrect — restarting IIS is needed for server config changes such as whitelists, not for this. C is incorrect — Contains Global Functions for Formulas has nothing to do with encryption. D is incorrect — the Maintenance group lets users maintain the rule; the button depends on the Encrypt Business Rules role and a refresh.

questions.question: Right after a Business Rule is encrypted, what does the user see?

options.A: The rule is hidden from the Business Rules list
options.B: A 'Business Rule Is Encrypted' message in a read-only editor, and the Decrypt button in the menu bar
options.C: The editor stays read/write until the rule is compiled
options.D: A prompt to set the Access and Maintenance groups

questions.explanation: B is correct: the system shows 'Business Rule Is Encrypted' in the editor, puts the editor in read-only mode and shows the Decrypt Business Rule button in the menu bar. A is incorrect — the rule stays listed; only its text is protected. C is incorrect — the editor goes to read-only right away. D is incorrect — no security prompt appears; the dialog only asks for the password.

questions.question: When a user clicks Business Rule Search on the Business Rules page, what opens?

options.A: The Find Modified Items dialog
options.B: The Object Lookup dialog box
options.C: The Business Rule Editor's IntelliSense list
options.D: The Task Activity grid

questions.explanation: B is correct: clicking Business Rule Search opens the Object Lookup dialog box, where typing the start of a name filters the matching rules. A is incorrect — Find Modified Items is used in dimension extracts. C is incorrect — IntelliSense is an editor feature, not the search. D is incorrect — Task Activity is a system log.

questions.question: After a software upgrade, an administrator wants to check whether any rule or formula syntax has broken. Which toolbar action fits, and who can use it?

options.A: Compile Business Rule to Check Syntax — any user with the Business Rules Page role
options.B: Execute Extender — users in the Maintenance group
options.C: Ctrl+M — any user
options.D: Compile All Business Rules and Formulas to Check Syntax — only application administrators

questions.explanation: D is correct: Compile All Business Rules and Formulas is most commonly used after an upgrade where syntax may have changed, and is only available for application administrators. A is incorrect — this compiles only the selected rule. B is incorrect — Execute Extender runs the selected Extender rule. C is incorrect — Ctrl+M expands or collapses all regions and methods.

questions.question: In the Business Rule editor, what does Ctrl+M do?

options.A: Compiles the selected rule
options.B: Opens Business Rule Search
options.C: Expands/collapses all regions and methods
options.D: Encrypts the rule

questions.explanation: C is correct: Ctrl+M expands or collapses all regions and methods; you click in the script after selecting the rule to use it. A is incorrect — compiling uses the Compile toolbar button. B is incorrect — search uses the Business Rule Search button. D is incorrect — encryption uses the Encrypt Business Rule button.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Contains Global Functions for Formulas
questions.question: Why does the guide say to set Contains Global Functions for Formulas to True only on Business Rules that are referenced from Member Formulas?

options.A: It encrypts the rule automatically
options.B: It makes the rule run on every Formula Pass
options.C: It adds overhead when the system compiles Member Formulas
options.D: It stops the rule from being called by other Business Rules

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says to use this setting only for rules referenced from Member Formulas because it adds some overhead when the system compiles Member Formulas. A is incorrect — encryption is separate. B is incorrect — the setting does not change when the rule runs. D is incorrect — the setting exists so functions can be called from Member Formulas or other Business Rules.

questions.question: In a Business Rule's Referenced Assemblies property, how do you reference another Business Rule and a DLL stored in the File Share's Business Rule Assembly Folder?

options.A: BR\RuleName for the rule; XF\FileName.dll for the DLL
options.B: XF\RuleName for the rule; BR\FileName.dll for the DLL
options.C: BR\RuleName for the rule; the full path for the DLL
options.D: No prefix for either

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says to enter BR\ followed by the rule name to reference another Business Rule, and XF\ followed by the DLL name (e.g. XF\ThirdPartyFunctions.dll); use no prefix and the full path only for DLLs on the application server's file system. B is incorrect — the prefixes are reversed. C is incorrect — the full path with no prefix is for DLLs elsewhere on the application server, not the File Share assembly folder. D is incorrect — both of these references use a prefix.

questions.question: On a Business Rule's Security properties, what is the difference between the Access and Maintenance groups?

options.A: Access lets members run the rule; Maintenance lets members encrypt it
options.B: Access is for Finance rules; Maintenance is for Extensibility rules
options.C: Access gives members access to the rule; Maintenance gives members authority to maintain the rule
options.D: Access controls the Business Rules Page; Maintenance controls the Encrypt Business Rules role

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Access group members have access to the Business Rule, and Maintenance group members have authority to maintain it. A is incorrect — encryption is controlled by the Encrypt Business Rules role. B is incorrect — both groups apply to any rule type. D is incorrect — page access and encryption are separate roles, not these properties.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Finance Rules on a Cube
questions.question: How many Finance Business Rules can be assigned to run at the Cube level during consolidations?

options.A: Four
options.B: Six
options.C: Eight
options.D: Nine

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says eight Finance Business Rules can be assigned to run at the Cube level during consolidations. A is incorrect — the guide says eight, not four. B is incorrect — the guide says eight, not six. D is incorrect — nine is the number of Business Rule types, not the number of cube rule slots.

questions.question: A Finance Business Rule needs custom logic to decide the foreign exchange rate for any intersection. Which Finance Function Type is used?

options.A: Translate
options.B: Consolidate Share
options.C: Calculate
options.D: FXRate

questions.explanation: D is correct: the FXRate function type is custom logic used to determine Foreign Exchange rates for any intersection. A is incorrect — Translate is additional logic for custom translation, not rate lookup. B is incorrect — Consolidate Share is logic for calculating the Share member. C is incorrect — Calculate sets values for a qualified POV during calculation.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Conditional Input Result Types
questions.question: A Conditional Input Finance rule must make cells read-only for data entry but still let users add cell detail. Which result should it return?

options.A: ConditionalInputResultType.NoInput
options.B: ConditionalInputResultType.NoInputAllowCellDetail
options.C: ConditionalInputResultType.NoCellDetailAllowInput
options.D: ConditionalInputResultType.Default

questions.explanation: B is correct: the listed return values include NoInputAllowCellDetail, which blocks input while still allowing cell detail. A is incorrect — NoInput makes the cell fully read-only with no exception for cell detail. C is incorrect — NoCellDetailAllowInput is the opposite: it allows input but blocks cell detail. D is incorrect — Default leaves the cube's normal input behavior.

questions.question: Which Connector action type runs a query against the source system to provide more detail than was originally imported?

options.A: GetDrillBack
options.B: GetData
options.C: GetFieldList
options.D: GetDrillBackTypes

questions.explanation: A is correct: ConnectorActionTypes.GetDrillBack runs the needed SQL query against the source system and provides greater detail than what was originally imported. B is incorrect — GetData retrieves the source data and returns it to Stage. C is incorrect — GetFieldList returns the field list to the Data Source for dimension assignment. D is incorrect — GetDrillBackTypes only returns the list of drill-back types (e.g. File or Data Grid).

questions.question: A Conditional (mapping) Business Rule can be applied to Transformation Rules of which types?

options.A: One-to-One and Composite only
options.B: Derivative only
options.C: Composite, Range, List, or Mask
options.D: Any type, including One-to-One

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Conditional Rules apply only to Transformation Rules of type Composite, Range, List, or Mask, as a Business Rule or Complex Expression. A is incorrect — One-to-One is not in the list. B is incorrect — Derivative is where Derivative Rules apply. D is incorrect — only the four listed types are supported.

questions.question: In a Conditional mapping rule, what does args.OutputValue return, and what happens if the rule never calls it?

options.A: The source value; the source is used as the target
options.B: The parsed Data Source line; the record is bypassed
options.C: The Cube value at the target intersection; the rule fails
options.D: The originally mapped target value from the Transformation Rules; if not called, the target field can be empty and is not considered

questions.explanation: D is correct: args.OutputValue returns the originally mapped target value from the Transformation Rules, and if the rule does not call it, the target field can be empty and will not be considered. A is incorrect — args.GetSource returns the source value. B is incorrect — args.Line in a Parser rule returns the whole record. C is incorrect — args.OutputValue does not return cube data, and the guide does not say the rule fails.

questions.question: Which is NOT listed as a common use of a Derivative Business Rule?

options.A: Calculating mathematical expressions
options.B: Looking up a value from the Cube for calculations
options.C: Source system check rule logic (validation rules on source data)
options.D: Concatenating field values while the Stage Parser reads the file

questions.explanation: D is correct: field value concatenation is listed as a common use of Parser rules; the Derivative list is math expressions, transformation cache lookups, Cube lookups and source system check rules. A is incorrect — this is a listed Derivative use. B is incorrect — this is a listed Derivative use. C is incorrect — this is a listed Derivative use.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Cube View Extender Scope
questions.question: A Cube View Extender rule changes header logos and colors in a Cube View. A user opens the same Cube View in the Data Explorer Grid view and sees none of the formatting. Why?

options.A: The Cube View is missing the Can Modify Data setting
options.B: Extender rules only run in the Excel Add-in
options.C: The rule must be set to Contains Global Functions for Formulas
options.D: Cube View Extender rules apply in Report view and do not apply to the Data Explorer Grid view

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Cube View Extender rules format a Cube View in Report view and do not apply to how it looks in the Data Explorer Grid view. A is incorrect — data entry settings do not control extender formatting. B is incorrect — the rules apply to Report view, not the Excel Add-in. C is incorrect — that setting is for functions called from Member Formulas.

questions.question: A developer with the Business Rules Page role and Maintenance group access cannot edit an Extensibility Rule. What does the guide require?

options.A: Full Administrator rights
options.B: The Encrypt Business Rules role
options.C: The Manage Data role
options.D: The AdministerApplication role only

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide states that full Administrator rights are required to edit Extensibility Rules. B is incorrect — Encrypt Business Rules only allows encrypting and decrypting rules. C is incorrect — Manage Data is for data tasks such as exporting and clearing. D is incorrect — the guide specifically says full Administrator rights.

questions.question: An auditor must receive an e-mail about every metadata change as it happens. Which event handler does the guide give as an example of this?

options.A: WCF Event Handler
options.B: Data Quality Event Handler
options.C: Save Data Event Handler
options.D: Transformation Event Handler

questions.explanation: A is correct: the WCF Event Handler listens to communication between the client and web server and can run logic when criteria are met; the guide's example is e-mailing an auditor about every metadata change as it happens. B is incorrect — Data Quality Event Handler runs around process cube, confirmation and certification events. C is incorrect — Save Data Event Handler tracks save events in an application. D is incorrect — Transformation Event Handler runs at points from Import through Load.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Data Quality Event Handler
questions.question: Custom logic must run right after an Intercompany Matching process ends. Which event handler type has an EndICMatch operation?

options.A: Data Quality Event Handler
options.B: Transformation Event Handler
options.C: Data Management Event Handler
options.D: Journals Event Handler

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Data Quality Event Handler's operations include PrepareICMatch, StartICMatch, PrepareICMatchData and EndICMatch, along with process cube, confirm and certify events. B is incorrect — Transformation operations cover parsing, mapping, validation and loading. C is incorrect — Data Management operations are StartSequence, ExecuteStep and EndSequence. D is incorrect — Journals operations cover submit, approve, reject, post and unpost.

questions.subtopic: Business Rules — Data Management Event Handler
questions.question: Which operations are available to a Data Management Event Handler?

options.A: StartProcessCube, Calculate, EndProcessCube
options.B: StartSequence, ExecuteStep, EndSequence
options.C: UpdateWorkflowStatus, WorkflowLock, WorkflowUnlock
options.D: SubmitJournal, PostJournal, UnpostJournal

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Data Management Event Handler can run before or after a sequence or step, with operations StartSequence, ExecuteStep and EndSequence. A is incorrect — these are Data Quality Event Handler operations. C is incorrect — these are Workflow Event Handler operations. D is incorrect — these are Journals Event Handler operations.

questions.question: A user's Excel Add-In version does not match the server, and the Client Updater fails because the user cannot write to the installation folder. What does the guide offer on the Client Updater page?

options.A: A link to download the add-in from MarketPlace
options.B: A Restart OneStream as Windows Administrator button to restart with elevated privileges
options.C: An option to roll back the server version
options.D: A Compile All option to rebuild the add-in

questions.explanation: B is correct: the user must be able to write to the installation folder; from the page they can save work and restart with elevated Windows privileges using the Restart OneStream as Windows Administrator button. A is incorrect — the updater gets software from the OneStream server, not MarketPlace. C is incorrect — it updates the client to match the server; it does not change the server. D is incorrect — Compile All is a Business Rules toolbar action.

questions.question: Which statement about the Client Updater is correct according to the guide?

options.A: Excel must stay open during the update
options.B: Outdated versions are deleted with no backup
options.C: A backup folder with the outdated version's files is created automatically, in the same location as the updated version folder
options.D: If disabled, it silently skips the update

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says a backup folder with the outdated version's files is created automatically as part of the update and can be found where the newly updated version folder is. A is incorrect — the guide says to close any open Excel sessions before clicking OK. B is incorrect — a backup is created automatically. D is incorrect — if disabled, a message says the System Administrator disabled the Client Updater and to use the full client installation program.

questions.question: An IT team wants a PowerShell script that calls OneStream Data Management to run every night. Which scheduler does the guide mention for automating PowerShell script runs?

options.A: Windows Task Scheduler
options.B: OneStream Task Scheduler
options.C: Workflow Batch screen
options.D: Data Management Sequence queueing

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says you can use Windows Task Scheduler to automate PowerShell script execution. B is incorrect — it schedules Data Management Sequences inside OneStream, not PowerShell scripts. C is incorrect — that processes Workflow batches. D is incorrect — queueing controls CPU-based starts, not script schedules.

questions.question: A script writer needs to create and edit a OneStream automation script saved as a .ps1 file. Which program does the guide say supports this?

options.A: Windows PowerShell (command line)
options.B: OneStream Task Scheduler
options.C: Windows PowerShell ISE
options.D: The Text Editor in the OneStream Windows App

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says ISE is an integrated script editor for typing commands and editing and running .ps1 files, while the Windows PowerShell console can run scripts but cannot create or modify them. A is incorrect — it can run commands or scripts but cannot create or modify scripts. B is incorrect — that schedules Data Management Sequences, not scripts. D is incorrect — that is for text documents, not PowerShell scripts.

questions.question: To use OneStreamClientApi, PowerShell must run on .NET Framework v4.0. Which files does the guide say to create or change?

options.A: web.config on the OneStream web server
options.B: XFAppServerConfig.xml through the Server Configuration Utility
options.C: A profile.ps1 file that runs set-executionpolicy unrestricted
options.D: powershell.exe.config and powershell_ise.exe.config in C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0, with supportedRuntime v4.0.30319
