questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide names these two files in that folder and gives startup content that includes supportedRuntime version v4.0.30319. A is incorrect — the change is made on the machine running PowerShell. B is incorrect — PowerShell setup does not use server configuration. C is incorrect — the guide uses set-executionpolicy remotesigned, and .NET is set in the .config files.

questions.question: Which statement about OneStreamClientApi for PowerShell is true?

options.A: It is a RESTful service that exchanges JSON with Postman
options.B: It is installed with the Client API Installer and lets scripts connect, authenticate, run Data Management Sequences and do basic data retrieval
options.C: It is installed on the application server and needs Okta or PingFederate
options.D: It can only run single Steps, not Sequences

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the Client API is installed with the Client API Installer and offers functions to connect, authenticate, execute Data Management Sequences and do basic data retrieval. A is incorrect — that describes the OneStream Web API. C is incorrect — external identity providers are a Web API requirement. D is incorrect — it has both ExecuteSequence and ExecuteStep.

questions.question: A script writer wants a PowerShell script that doesn't store a plain-text password. Which OneStreamClientApi Authentication function takes a clear-text password and authentication type and returns a string?

options.A: Logon
options.B: OpenApplication
options.C: EncryptPassword
options.D: LogonAndReturnCookie

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide lists EncryptPassword(string clearTextPassword, XFClientAuthenticationType clientAuthenticationType), which returns a string. A is incorrect — Logon takes webServerUrl, userName, password and authentication type and returns LogonInfo. B is incorrect — OpenApplication takes an application name and returns LogonInfo. D is incorrect — that is a Web API endpoint, not a Client API function.

questions.question: Which OneStreamClientApi function signs in and opens a named application in one call?

options.A: Logon
options.B: OpenApplication
options.C: ExecuteSequence
options.D: LogonAndOpenApplication

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide lists LogonAndOpenApplication with webServerUrl, userName, password, application and clientAuthenticationType. A is incorrect — Logon authenticates but has no application parameter; OpenApplication is a separate call. B is incorrect — it takes only the application name and expects an existing logon. C is incorrect — it runs a Data Management Sequence.

questions.question: A PowerShell script must run one Data Management Step instead of a whole Sequence. Besides the substitution-variable string, what does ExecuteStep need?

options.A: The Data Management Group name and the Step name
options.B: The Sequence name and the Step name
options.C: The Data Management Profile name and the Step name
options.D: Only the Step name, since Step names are unique

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists ExecuteStep(dataMgmtGroupName, stepName, customSubstVarsAsCommaSeparatedPairs). B is incorrect — ExecuteStep names the Group, not the Sequence. C is incorrect — Profiles are not a parameter. D is incorrect — the Group name is also needed.

questions.question: A PowerShell script must pull data from a Cube View into a DataSet. Which OneStreamClientApi DataProvider function does this?

options.A: GetAdoDataSetForMethodCommand
options.B: GetAdoDataSetForCubeViewCommand
options.C: ExecuteSequence
options.D: GetAdoDataSetForAdapter

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists it under DataProvider with CubeViewName and table options, returning a DataSet. A is incorrect — that runs an XFCommandMethodType method query. C is incorrect — that runs a Data Management Sequence and returns DataMgmtResult. D is incorrect — in the guide, that is a Web API endpoint for Dashboard Adapters, not a Client API function.

questions.question: A developer setting up Postman to call the OneStream Web API needs its documentation. Where does the guide point?

options.A: The autogenerated documentation at http(s)://[servername]:[port]/onestreamapi
options.B: System > Tools > File Explorer > Documentation
options.C: The OneStreamClientApi object hierarchy in the PowerShell section
options.D: The Application Server Configuration Utility

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide refers to autogenerated documentation at that address. B is incorrect — no such File Explorer location is given. C is incorrect — that documents the Client API, not the Web API. D is incorrect — that configures servers, not Web API documentation.

questions.question: What is the POST api/Authentication/LogonAndReturnCookie endpoint mainly used for, per the guide?

options.A: Running a Data Management Sequence after logon
options.B: Returning a Cube View as JSON
options.C: Checking that the Web API installation finished successfully; it returns a one-time cookie holding authentication state
options.D: Encrypting a password for PowerShell scripts

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the Enablement Team mainly uses it to verify the Web API installation, and it returns a one-time cookie value or a failure message. A is incorrect — that is api/DataManagement/ExecuteSequence. B is incorrect — that is api/DataProvider/GetAdoDataSetForCubeViewCommand. D is incorrect — that is the Client API EncryptPassword function.

questions.question: A third-party reporting tool needs the results of a Dashboard Adapter as JSON through the OneStream Web API. Which endpoint fits?

options.A: POST api/DataProvider/GetAdoDataSetForSqlCommand
options.B: POST api/DataManagement/ExecuteStep
options.C: POST api/DataProvider/GetAdoDataSetForCubeViewCommand
options.D: POST api/DataProvider/GetAdoDataSetForAdapter

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says it returns a JSON representation of a DataSet for a given Dashboard Adapter. A is incorrect — that runs a SQL query and requires the Administrator role. B is incorrect — that runs a Data Management Step. C is incorrect — that returns data for a Cube View.

questions.question: A third-party tool calls the Web API to run a Data Management Sequence stored in a non-Default workspace. What does the guide say about the request?

options.A: The Workspace Name is required for every call
options.B: Workspace Sequences cannot be run through the Web API
options.C: The Maintenance Unit name must be put before the Sequence name
options.D: The REST API accepts an optional Workspace Name for the Sequence (REST API 7.2.0 and 5.2.0)

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide's IMPORTANT note says REST API 7.2.0 and 5.2.0 accept an optional Workspace Name for a Data Management Sequence. A is incorrect — the guide says it is optional. B is incorrect — they can, with the optional Workspace Name. C is incorrect — the guide mentions a Workspace Name parameter, not a Maintenance Unit prefix.

questions.question: When creating a task, a user can't find a workspace in the Sequences list. Which explanation fits the guide?

options.A: Task Scheduler can only run Default workspace Sequences
options.B: The workspace has no Sequences or is not set to shareable
options.C: The user lacks ManageTaskScheduler
options.D: Workspace Sequences must first be extracted with Load/Extract

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says workspaces, Groups or Maintenance Units with no sequences are not shown, and a workspace not set to shareable cannot be selected. A is incorrect — Sequences under workspace names and paths can be picked. C is incorrect — the guide does not tie the list to that role. D is incorrect — there is no such requirement.

questions.question: In the Task Scheduler Grid View, what does the Count column show?

options.A: How many retries are left (up to three)
options.B: How many Steps are in the task's Sequence
options.C: How many users can see the task
options.D: How many times the task has run

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide defines Count as the amount of times the task has run. A is incorrect — retries are set on the Advanced tab. B is incorrect — the grid does not count Steps. C is incorrect — visibility depends on roles and Show Tasks for All Users.

questions.question: An administrator turned on the setting that requires tasks to be validated. In the grid, a task shows an Invalidate Date/Time. What does that mean?

options.A: It is the date and time the task last ran successfully, shown for audit of the schedule.
options.B: It is when the task is deleted permanently.
options.C: It is when the task stops running permanently, the same behavior as Expire Date/Time.
options.D: On that date and time the task will be suspended and won't run until it is validated.

questions.explanation: D is correct: when enabled by an administrator, Invalidate Date/Time is when the task will be suspended and not run until validated, and Validate Task keeps it active. A is incorrect — that is Last Start Time. B is incorrect — the task is suspended until validated, not deleted. C is incorrect — Expire Date/Time is when the task stops for good; Invalidate suspends it until validated.

questions.subtopic: Task Scheduler — Grid Filter and Group
questions.question: An administrator wants the Task Scheduler grid grouped by User Name and then by Sequence, and filtered to two users. What does the guide say?

options.A: Drag column headers into the header bar to group by more than one column, and filter on several selections in fields with the filter icon
options.B: Only one grouping column is allowed at a time
options.C: Filtering is available only in Calendar View
options.D: Grouping needs the ManageTaskScheduler role

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says you can filter on multiple selections and group by more than one column by dragging and dropping into the header bar. B is incorrect — the guide says you can group by more than one column. C is incorrect — the grid fields with the filter icon can be filtered. D is incorrect — the guide does not tie grouping to a role.

questions.question: A user with the TaskScheduler role edits their own task but the 'Enabled by Manager' check box is grayed out. Why?

options.A: The task has already passed its Expire Date/Time and can no longer be enabled.
options.B: The Sequence has no Steps.
options.C: Only an administrator can change the Enabled by Manager check box.
options.D: The task must first be validated through Invalidate Date/Time.

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says that if you are not the Administrator, you will not have the rights to change the Enabled by Manager check box. A is incorrect — expiry stops the task from running; it isn't why the check box is locked. B is incorrect — a Sequence without Steps makes the job fail; it doesn't lock the check box. D is incorrect — validation keeps a task active; the check box is limited to administrators.

questions.question: In Task Scheduler Calendar View, when are tasks color coded?

options.A: Always, by State (Enabled or Disabled)
options.B: When Show Tasks for All Users is selected and more than one user's tasks are showing
options.C: Only when grouping by Date
options.D: Only for tasks that failed their last run

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says tasks are color coded when more than one user is showing and Show Tasks for All Users is selected. A is incorrect — the guide links color to users, not State. C is incorrect — the guide does not tie colors to grouping. D is incorrect — run status is seen in Task Activity.

questions.question: Which is NOT a grouping option in Task Scheduler Calendar View?

options.A: User name
options.B: Date
options.C: Sequence
options.D: No group

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Calendar View can group by user name, date or no group; Sequence is not listed. A is incorrect — listed as a grouping option. B is incorrect — listed as a grouping option. D is incorrect — listed as a grouping option.

questions.question: A user hovers over a task in Calendar View. Which item is NOT in the hover information the guide lists?

options.A: Sequence Name
options.B: Expire Date/Time
options.C: State
options.D: Count (number of runs)

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide lists User Name, Task Name, Sequence Name, Schedule, State, Expire Date/Time and, if enabled, Invalidate Date/Time; Count is not included. A is incorrect — listed in the hover information. B is incorrect — listed in the hover information. C is incorrect — listed in the hover information.

questions.question: Which statement about Task Scheduler Calendar View is true?

options.A: New Task, Edit Task and Delete Task are available there, and a task can be double-clicked or right-clicked to edit or delete
options.B: It is read-only; changes must be made in Grid View
options.C: It shows only your own tasks; other users' tasks never show
options.D: It offers only Month and Agenda views

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says you can create, edit or delete tasks from the calendar view, and double-click or right-click a task. B is incorrect — the guide allows changes from the calendar. C is incorrect — you can view all users' tasks if the option is checked. D is incorrect — the guide lists today, work week, month, timeline and agenda.

questions.question: The setting that requires task validation is on. A user with only the TaskScheduler application security role must keep their own task active. What can they do?

options.A: Nothing; only ManageTaskScheduler can validate tasks
options.B: Extract and reload the task with Load/Extract
options.C: Validate the task themselves; TaskScheduler lets users create tasks, edit their own and validate tasks when the setting is on
options.D: Rename the task to reset its Invalidate Date/Time

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says TaskScheduler allows you to create new tasks, edit your tasks and validate tasks if the setting is on. A is incorrect — the guide lists validation for TaskScheduler. B is incorrect — TaskScheduler has no access to load and extract. D is incorrect — neither role can change the task name.

questions.question: Which restriction applies to BOTH the TaskScheduler and ManageTaskScheduler roles?

options.A: Neither can view other users' tasks
options.B: Neither can use Load/Extract for tasks
options.C: Neither can edit other users' tasks
options.D: Neither can change a task's name

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says "You cannot change the task name" for both roles. A is incorrect — both can view all user tasks. B is incorrect — ManageTaskScheduler can load and extract. C is incorrect — ManageTaskScheduler can edit other users' tasks.

questions.question: After upgrading to platform release 8.4, how are existing scheduled tasks updated to use the new time zone logic?

options.A: Open each existing task and click OK; tasks don't have to be recreated.
options.B: Delete and recreate each task so the time zone logic is applied to it.
options.C: Extract all tasks through Load/Extract and reload them into the upgraded application.
options.D: Nothing; tasks convert automatically during the upgrade.

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide notes that on upgrading to 8.4, existing tasks must be edited by opening the task and clicking OK, which applies the time zone logic without recreating tasks. B is incorrect — the guide says opening and clicking OK applies the logic without recreating. C is incorrect — the stated method is to open each task and click OK. D is incorrect — the guide says existing tasks must be edited.

questions.subtopic: Task Scheduler — Start Date and Parameters
questions.question: A user creates a task without entering a Start Date/Time and adds a parameter value that isn't valid for the Sequence. What happens?

options.A: The task can't be saved until a Start Date/Time is entered, and invalid parameters are dropped.
options.B: It defaults to the current date and time, and the job fails because of the invalid parameter.
options.C: It defaults to the current date and time, and the task runs while ignoring the invalid parameter.
options.D: It defaults to midnight UTC the next day, and the job fails because of the invalid parameter.

questions.explanation: B is correct: if no time is specified, Start Date/Time defaults to the current date and time; additional parameters must be valid, or the job will fail. A is incorrect — the field defaults to now if left empty. C is incorrect — the start time part is right, but the guide says invalid parameters cause the job to fail. D is incorrect — Start Date/Time defaults to the current date and time, not midnight UTC.

questions.subtopic: Task Scheduler — Weekly Time Zone Storage
questions.question: A user in Eastern Time creates a new Weekly recurring task. How is its time stored?

options.A: It's created and saved in the application server's time zone, regardless of the user.
options.B: It's created and saved in Eastern Time, and shifts to the editor's time zone if another user edits it.
options.C: The user must enter the time in UTC, and it is saved without any time zone conversion.
options.D: It's created in the user's local time zone and saved in UTC.

questions.explanation: D is correct: new Weekly and Monthly recurring tasks are created in the inputting user's local time zone and saved in UTC, with 'Save using the current user's Time Zone' as the default selection. A is incorrect — the guide says UTC. B is incorrect — it is saved in UTC. C is incorrect — the user enters local time; conversion happens on save.

questions.question: Which is NOT a schedule type on the Schedule tab of a new Task Scheduler task?

options.A: One Time
options.B: Hourly
options.C: Minutes
options.D: Monthly

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists One Time, Minutes (5-180), Daily, Weekly and Monthly; there is no Hourly type, and hourly runs use Minutes. A is incorrect — listed: runs once at the Start Date/Time on the Task tab. C is incorrect — listed: recurring from 5-180 minutes. D is incorrect — listed: choose how often it recurs and the days it runs.

questions.question: A user wants a task to run every 30 minutes, but only between 2:30pm and 5:30pm. Which statement is true?

options.A: Use Minutes recurrence (1–60) with Time From/To; the first run is at 3:00pm, one interval after 2:30pm.
options.B: Use Minutes recurrence (5–180) with Time From/To; first run 2:30pm, though the Calendar may show entries all day.
options.C: Use Daily recurrence with Recur Every 30 and Time From/To; Minutes recurrence can't be limited to a window.
options.D: Use Minutes recurrence; Time From is checked by default, and the Calendar shows only runs within the window.

questions.explanation: B is correct: Minutes recurs from 5 to 180 minutes, and Time From/To limit the window (Time From is unchecked by default); the guide notes Calendar entries may display outside the run window. A is incorrect — the guide gives a 5–180 minute range and says the first run occurs at 2:30pm. C is incorrect — Daily controls how many times it recurs by day; the Minutes recurrence is the one with Time From/To. D is incorrect — Time From is unchecked by default, and the Calendar may show entries outside the run window.

questions.question: A scheduled task sometimes fails due to a temporary database lock. How can it retry automatically, and what is the limit?

options.A: On the Schedule tab, set Recur Every; the maximum is five.
options.B: Set Maximum Queued Time Before Canceling on the Sequence; there is no limit.
options.C: On the Advanced tab, set the retry count; the maximum is three.
options.D: On the Advanced tab, set the retry count; the maximum is ten.

questions.explanation: C is correct: clicking Advanced lets you set the number of times to retry a failed task, with a maximum of three. A is incorrect — Recur Every sets the schedule, not retries. B is incorrect — that setting controls queue time; retries are on the Advanced tab. D is incorrect — the maximum is three.

questions.question: A task has Start Date/Time Wednesday 5/7, Recur Every 2 Weeks on Sunday, Monday and Friday, expiring 5/28. Which runs match the guide's expected result?

options.A: Fri 5/9, Sun 5/11, Mon 5/12, then skip the next week, then Fri 5/23, Sun 5/25, Mon 5/26
options.B: Sun 5/11, Mon 5/12, Fri 5/16, then skip a week, then Sun 5/25, Mon 5/26 (Friday 5/9 is skipped)
options.C: Wed 5/7, Wed 5/21 only
options.D: Every Sunday, Monday and Friday from Fri 5/9 through Mon 5/26, with no weeks skipped

questions.explanation: A is correct: run logic begins with the Start Date and then the recurring days; the guide's example runs 5/9, 5/11, 5/12, skips 5/16–5/19, then runs 5/23, 5/25, 5/26. B is incorrect — the guide's example runs Friday 5/9 first and skips Friday 5/16. C is incorrect — the task runs on the selected days (Sunday, Monday, Friday), not the start weekday. D is incorrect — the two-week recurrence skips the week of 5/16–5/19.

questions.question: An application extract will be larger than 2 GB. What does the guide say about the format?

options.A: Split the XML into multiple files under 2 GB
options.B: Use the Extract and Edit option
options.C: Extract as an XML file and compress it manually
options.D: Use a zip file

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says applications can be extracted as XML or zip, and if the file is larger than 2 GB you must use a zip file. A is incorrect — the guide does not mention splitting files. B is incorrect — Extract and Edit lets you edit the XML; it does not get around the size limit. C is incorrect — the guide says a zip extract is required to load it successfully.

questions.subtopic: Dimension Extract — Find Modified Items User Filter
questions.question: In Find Modified Items, an administrator wants dimension changes made by everyone during the last two weeks. What should the User field be set to?

options.A: Leave it empty
options.B: Enter Administrator
options.C: Enter * as a wildcard
options.D: Enter the security group name

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says to leave the User field empty to find changes by all users. B is incorrect — that would return only the Administrator user's changes. C is incorrect — the guide does not use a wildcard; it says to leave the field empty. D is incorrect — the filter is by user name, not security group.

questions.subtopic: Dimension Extract — Extract Members for Each Selected Relationship
questions.question: An administrator selected new relationships to migrate and wants the members used in those relationships included too. What should be checked?

options.A: Include in XML on the Members to Delete tab
options.B: Extract Unique IDs
options.C: Extract Members for Each Selected Relationship
options.D: Select All Descendants on the Members to Delete tab

questions.explanation: C is correct: checking Extract Members for Each Selected Relationship includes the members used in the selected relationships. A is incorrect — this checkbox adds deletions to the XML. B is incorrect — Extract Unique IDs is a System Security extract option. D is incorrect — Select All Descendants is a right-click option on a Relationships parent member, not on the delete tab.

questions.subtopic: Dimension Extract — Include in XML Default
questions.question: Members deleted in the source app appear on the Members to Delete tab. The administrator extracts and loads the XML into the target without changing anything. What happens to those members in the target?

options.A: They are deleted because Action=Delete is written by default
options.B: They are moved under a NotUsed parent
options.C: They are deleted only if they have no stored data
options.D: They are not deleted, because Include in XML is not checked by default

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says Include in XML is not checked by default; only when checked do Members to Delete get Action=Delete in the XML and get deleted on load. A is incorrect — Action=Delete is written only if Include in XML is checked. B is incorrect — nothing in the guide moves members to another parent. C is incorrect — the stored data rule applies only when deletes are included, and here they are not.

questions.question: An XML has ten member changes, three deleted members and one new relationship. Loading it errors when deleting the first member. What is the result?

options.A: Nothing is applied; the load is rolled back
options.B: The ten member changes are applied; the deletes from the error onward and the new relationship are not
options.C: Only the new relationship is applied
options.D: All changes except the failed delete are applied

questions.explanation: B is correct: the XML processes new/changed members, then deleted members, then new relationships, then deleted relationships; OneStream applies as many changes as it can up to the error, so the ten member changes take effect and anything after the error does not. A is incorrect — the guide says changes before the error do occur; there is no full rollback. C is incorrect — new relationships come after deleted members, so they are not processed. D is incorrect — changes after the error are not applied.

questions.subtopic: Dimension Load — Deleting a Member with Data
questions.question: A member without data was deleted in Dev, but the same member has data in Prod. Loading the dimension XML into Prod gives an error. Which is NOT one of the guide's resolutions?

options.A: Clear the member's data in Prod and reload the XML
options.B: Create a new XML extract that excludes the member
options.C: Edit the XML to remove the member and the action
options.D: Load the XML with the Replace load method to force the delete

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide lists clearing the data in the destination and reloading, creating a new extract without that member, or editing the XML; a Replace option is not a resolution, and members with stored data cannot be deleted. A is incorrect — this is a listed resolution. B is incorrect — this is a listed resolution. C is incorrect — this is a listed resolution.

questions.question: Loading a dimension XML into Prod fails because a Scenario member in the source references an FX Rate Type that does not exist in Prod. Which fix does the guide list?

options.A: Create the FX Rate Type in the destination application and reload the file
options.B: Load the FX Rate CSV first
options.C: Add the currency in Application Properties
options.D: Check Extract Unique IDs and re-extract

questions.explanation: A is correct: for an undefined FX Rate Type, the guide says to create it in the destination and reload, create a new extract excluding the member, or edit the XML to exclude the member and action. B is incorrect — the FX Rate CSV holds rate amounts; it does not create rate types for this error. C is incorrect — currencies are not the missing object. D is incorrect — Extract Unique IDs applies to System Security extracts.

questions.question: Before deleting an Entity member that has no data of its own, what extra check does the guide recommend?

options.A: Confirm it has no FX Rate Type
options.B: Confirm it is not used as an Intercompany Partner on any records
options.C: Confirm it is not in a Cube View Profile
options.D: Confirm it has no UD description

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide warns that an Entity with no data may still be used as an Intercompany Partner, so make sure it is not used on any data records or as an IC Partner. A is incorrect — FX Rate Types are assigned to Scenarios, not Entities. C is incorrect — Cube View Profiles are not mentioned. D is incorrect — UD descriptions are application properties for dimension types.

questions.question: A solution designer wants to export Business Rules, Cube Views and Dashboard Maintenance Units as one package that works with Git. What must be created first?

options.A: An Application Zip File extract
options.B: A Data Management sequence that exports each object
options.C: A manually defined XML project file saved with the .xfProj extension
options.D: A Report Book listing the objects

questions.explanation: C is correct: the designer must first manually define an XML file and save it with the .xfProj extension to a local project folder that can also support version control. A is incorrect — an Application Zip File extracts everything except data and FX; it is not a defined project. B is incorrect — Data Management is not used to define project contents. D is incorrect — Report Books are for reports, not for packaging objects.

questions.question: Which two attributes are on the xfProject root node of an .xfProj file?

options.A: ProjectItemType and Name
options.B: FolderPath and IncludeDescendants
options.C: TopFolderPath and DefaultZipFileName
options.D: Workspace and Name

questions.explanation: C is correct: the xfProject root node has TopFolderPath (the starting folder where files are extracted) and DefaultZipFileName (the default name for zip extracts). A is incorrect — these are projectItem attributes. B is incorrect — these are projectItem attributes. D is incorrect — Workspace is not an xfProject root attribute.

questions.question: In an .xfProj file, the projectItem attribute IncludeDescendants defaults to True. Which project item type does it NOT affect?

options.A: CubeViewGroup
options.B: DashboardMaintenanceUnit
options.C: DataManagementGroup
options.D: BusinessRule

questions.explanation: D is correct: IncludeDescendants affects only group-type items such as CubeViewGroup, DashboardGroup, DashboardMaintenanceUnit and DataManagementGroup (plus DashboardWorkspace in the workspace version); BusinessRule is not one of them. A is incorrect — CubeViewGroup is affected. B is incorrect — DashboardMaintenanceUnit is affected. C is incorrect — DataManagementGroup is affected.

questions.question: On the Application Load/Extract Extract tab with an .xfProj file selected, what happens if Extract to Zip is NOT checked?

options.A: Nothing is extracted until a zip name is given
options.B: All objects are exported to one XML in the TopFolderPath
options.C: Only Business Rules are exported
options.D: All defined objects are exported as files to the FolderPath locations in the .xfProj

questions.explanation: D is correct: the standard File option exports all objects in the .xfProj to the folder paths it defines; the .zip option collects them into a zip file at the .xfProj file's location. A is incorrect — Extract to Zip is optional. B is incorrect — objects go to their defined folder paths, not one combined XML. C is incorrect — all defined objects are exported.

questions.question: A developer loads an .xfProj file with the Replace method. The project contains Business Rules and a DataManagementGroup. How is each handled?

options.A: Both are fully replaced
options.B: Files that differ are removed for the DataManagementGroup; for the Business Rules, Replace acts as a Merge
options.C: Business Rules are replaced; the DataManagementGroup is merged
options.D: Replace is not allowed when Business Rules are present

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Replace only removes files that differ for CubeViewGroups, DataManagementGroups, DashboardMaintenanceUnits and DashboardGroups; for other items such as business rules or extensibility rules, Replace acts as a Merge. A is incorrect — Business Rules are merged, not replaced. C is incorrect — this reverses the guide. D is incorrect — nothing in the guide blocks Replace.

questions.question: An administrator loads a project zip file and looks for the Merge/Replace choice. What does the guide say?

options.A: The contents are merged into the application; zip load does not support the Merge or Replace options
options.B: Zip load always replaces the target objects
options.C: The Merge/Replace prompt appears after selecting the zip
options.D: Zip loads must be done through System Load/Extract

questions.explanation: A is correct: zip file load works like any other application file load: the contents are merged into the application, and zip load does not support the alternative Merge or Replace options. B is incorrect — zip contents are merged, not replaced. C is incorrect — the Merge/Replace prompt applies to .xfProj file loads. D is incorrect — project files are loaded under Application > Tools > Load/Extract.

questions.question: An older extract file has <applicationDashboardsRoot> on its third line. What happens when it is loaded with Application Workspaces as the file type?

options.A: The load fails and must be re-extracted
options.B: It is converted into a Data Management XML
options.C: The system still loads it for backward compatibility; new extracts use <applicationWorkspacesRoot>
options.D: Only its Cube Views load

questions.explanation: C is correct: for XML extract, the Application Workspaces type writes <applicationWorkspacesRoot>; on load, the system still accepts files with <applicationDashboardsRoot> for backward compatibility. A is incorrect — the guide says the older version still loads. B is incorrect — nothing converts it to a Data Management file. D is incorrect — the guide does not say only some content loads.

questions.question: An administrator cannot delete a Data Management sequence from the Workspaces page. What is the most likely reason the guide gives?

options.A: The sequence is assigned to a Task Scheduler item
options.B: The sequence has a Data Management Event Handler
options.C: The sequence is in the default workspace
options.D: The sequence was never extracted

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says you cannot delete a sequence on the Workspaces or Data Management pages if it is assigned to a Task Scheduler item. B is incorrect — event handlers do not block deletion. C is incorrect — the default workspace does not block deletion. D is incorrect — extracts have nothing to do with deletion.

questions.question: An administrator wants to extract Data Management Profiles from Application Load/Extract. What does the guide say?

options.A: Profiles extract automatically with their groups
options.B: Profiles can't be extracted; you can extract specific Data Management Groups or all of them
options.C: Profiles extract only with the Application Workspaces file type
options.D: Profiles extract only through System Load/Extract

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says you cannot extract data management profiles, since they no longer show in the interface, but you can extract specific Data Management Groups or all of them; the tree shows All and Groups. A is incorrect — profiles are not extracted. C is incorrect — Application Workspaces is not described as a way to extract DM profiles. D is incorrect — System Load/Extract covers system artifacts, not DM profiles.

questions.question: Three Task Scheduler items use sequences in (1) the Default workspace/default MU, (2) the Default workspace/non-default MU, and (3) a non-default workspace. Which items have the workspace name prefixed to <DataMgmtSequenceName> in the extract?

options.A: All three
options.B: Only (1)
options.C: Only (3)

questions.explanation: C is correct: the workspace name is prefixed only when the Task Scheduler item uses a sequence in a non-default workspace (e.g. NonDefaultWorkspace.SequenceName); for the Default workspace, with either MU, there is no prefix. A is incorrect — items using the Default workspace are not prefixed. B is incorrect — (1) uses the Default workspace, so it has no prefix. D is incorrect — (2) is still in the Default workspace, so it has no prefix.

questions.question: Which statement about Application Load/Extract matches the guide's description of Load/Extract Application Artifacts?

options.A: Any user in Open Application can extract all artifacts
options.B: It imports and exports application sections in XML format, only Administrators have access, and Extract and Edit is available for all extracts
options.C: It only supports CSV files
options.D: Extract and Edit is only available for the Application Zip File

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says you import and export sections of the application in XML, only Administrators have access, and Extract and Edit is available for all extracts so the XML can be edited. A is incorrect — only Administrators have access. C is incorrect — it uses XML (FX Rate CSV is the one CSV option). D is incorrect — Extract and Edit is available for all extracts.

questions.question: Which set of sections is part of the Metadata file type in Application Load/Extract?

options.A: Groups, Profiles and Cube Views
options.B: Business Rules, Time Dimension Profiles, Dimensions and Cubes
options.C: Workflow Profiles and Workflow Profile Templates
options.D: FX Rate Types and Time Periods

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says Metadata has sections such as Business Rules, Time Dimension Profiles, Dimensions and Cubes, and supports Find Modified Items by user and timestamp. A is incorrect — these describe the Cube Views file type. C is incorrect — these describe the Workflow Profiles file type. D is incorrect — these describe the FX Rates file type.

questions.question: An administrator uses Application > Tools > Load/Extract with the Metadata item. What does the guide say about it?

options.A: It includes data and FX rates for each Cube
options.B: It has sections such as Business Rules, Time Dimension Profiles, Dimensions and Cubes, and Find Modified Items can search Member and Relationship changes by username and time stamp
options.C: It is extracted with System Load/Extract
options.D: It includes Workflow Profiles and Workflow Profile Templates

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide lists those sections and says OneStream can search for Dimension Member and Relationship changes by username and time stamp. A is incorrect — data and FX rates are not part of Metadata; FX Rates are their own extract. C is incorrect — Metadata is in Application Load/Extract. D is incorrect — those are a separate Workflow Profiles extract.

questions.question: An administrator needs to move just one Data Management Group, with its Sequences and Steps, to another application. Which Application Load/Extract approach fits?

options.A: Extract the Application Zip File, the only way to include Data Management
options.B: Use System Load/Extract with File Type Data Management
options.C: Extract the Data Management item, which defaults to All; pick the specific items or turn sections on or off
options.D: Use the Task Scheduler extract, which includes the Sequences

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the Data Management item has sections such as Groups and Profiles, the default is All, and you can pick specific items or turn sections on or off. A is incorrect — Data Management has its own extract item. B is incorrect — Data Management is an Application Load/Extract item. D is incorrect — the Task Scheduler file type extracts scheduled tasks.

questions.question: A Workflow Profile XML extracted earlier is edited to drop several property settings and then reloaded. What happens to those properties in the application?

options.A: They keep their current values
options.B: They are set from the Workflow Profile Template
options.C: The load fails validation
options.D: The load clears old property settings that are not specified in the XML

questions.explanation: D is correct: when loading Workflow Profiles from an XML, the load clears old property settings that are not in the file, so edits made to the extract are honored on reload. A is incorrect — missing properties are cleared, not kept. B is incorrect — templates are not used to fill in missing properties. C is incorrect — the guide does not describe a validation failure.

questions.question: An administrator uses the Extensibility Rules file type to extract all Business Rules, but a Parser rule attached to a Data Source is missing. Why?

options.A: Parser rules must be decrypted first
options.B: The Extensibility Rules type only exports Extensibility Rules; other rule types are exported with the object they belong to, such as the Data Source
options.C: Parser rules are only exported with Metadata
options.D: Parser rules can only move through an .xfProj file

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says this type only exports Extensibility Rules; all others are exported with the object they are tied to (for example, a Parser rule goes with its Data Source). A is incorrect — encryption is not why it is missing. C is incorrect — the guide's example says Parser rules go with the Data Source. D is incorrect — .xfProj is one option, not the only one.

questions.question: Which columns does the FX Rate CSV extract contain?

options.A: FxRateType, Time, SourceCurrency, DestCurrency, Amount, HasData
options.B: Entity, Currency, RateType, Period, Rate
options.C: Cube, Scenario, Time, Account, Amount
options.D: FxRateType, Scenario, Currency, Amount

questions.explanation: A is correct: the FX Rate CSV is a CSV extract of the application FX rates with FxRateType, Time, SourceCurrency, DestCurrency, Amount and HasData. B is incorrect — these are not the listed columns. C is incorrect — these are cube data dimensions, not FX rate columns. D is incorrect — FX rates are not stored by Scenario, and this list is incomplete.

questions.question: Loading a Security extract into another environment fails because some user records already exist there. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: Use the Replace load method
options.B: Uncheck Extract Unique IDs and extract again
options.C: Extract with All selected
options.D: Use Application Load/Extract with Application Security Roles

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says loading security with unique IDs can fail if some records already exist; in that case uncheck Extract Unique IDs and extract without them. A is incorrect — Merge/Replace applies to .xfProj loads, not System Security. C is incorrect — All is already the default and does not address the ID conflict. D is incorrect — Application Security Roles do not contain users or groups.

questions.question: Which items are covered by the Security file type in System Load/Extract?

options.A: Application Security Roles and Application UI Roles
options.B: Users and Workflow Profiles only
options.C: Logon Activity and Error Log
options.D: System Roles, Users, Security Groups and Exclusion Groups

questions.explanation: D is correct: Security covers System Roles, Users, Security Groups and Exclusion Groups, found under System | Administration | Security. A is incorrect — these are application artifacts extracted from Application Load/Extract. B is incorrect — Workflow Profiles are application artifacts. C is incorrect — these are separate System Load/Extract types.

questions.question: An administrator wants to extract only one week of Logon Activity. What does the guide describe?

options.A: Uncheck Extract All Items and set a Start Time and End Time
options.B: Filter Logon Activity on screen and export to Excel
options.C: Use Find Modified Items with a date range
options.D: Logon Activity can't be filtered by date

questions.explanation: A is correct: for Error Log, Task Activity and Logon Activity, the screen shows Extract All Items with Start Time and End Time; if it is not checked, you pick the start and end times. B is incorrect — the guide describes the System Load/Extract option, not a grid export. C is incorrect — Find Modified Items is for dimension changes. D is incorrect — date filtering is supported.

questions.question: A new application database is created with no Time Dimension Type assigned. Which type is used?

options.A: Custom
options.B: StandardUsingBinaryData
options.C: Standard

questions.explanation: C is correct: if a Time Dimension Type is not assigned to a new application database, the default Standard type is used. A is incorrect — Custom must be chosen and is only for new applications. B is incorrect — StandardUsingBinaryData must be chosen; it is not the default. D is incorrect — this weekly 445 type is not the default.

questions.question: A new application is monthly for now, but the business may later convert it to a weekly Time Dimension. Which type does the guide recommend?

options.A: Standard
options.B: StandardUsingBinaryData
options.D: Custom with Use Weeks = False

questions.explanation: B is correct: StandardUsingBinaryData creates a monthly Time Dimension and stores data in a binary data table; the guide says to use it if you may later convert to weekly. A is incorrect — Standard stores data by month in the data tables and is the type used by applications created before 4.1.0. C is incorrect — this is a weekly 53-week 544 calendar, not monthly now. D is incorrect — this makes a custom monthly dimension; the guide does not name it for later conversion.

questions.question: With a Custom Time Dimension Type, a designer needs a different number of weeks per month in 2027 than in 2026. Which settings are needed?

options.A: Use Weeks = False and Vary Settings By Year = True
options.B: Use Weeks = True and Vary Settings By Year = False
options.C: Use Weeks = True and Vary Settings By Year = True

questions.explanation: C is correct: Use Weeks = True defines a custom weekly dimension, and Vary Settings By Year = True lets you set the weeks per month for each year; then you set M1–M16 Number of Weeks for the chosen year. A is incorrect — Use Weeks = False creates a custom monthly dimension with no weeks. B is incorrect — Vary Settings By Year = False applies the same weeks per month to every year. D is incorrect — a predefined type cannot be assigned per year.

questions.question: An administrator wants to switch a live production application to a Custom Time Dimension Type. What does the guide say?

options.A: Custom can be applied anytime from Application Properties
options.B: Custom is only available for new applications
options.C: Custom requires a System Load/Extract of the Time Dimension XML
options.D: Custom only works with StandardUsingBinaryData

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the Custom type is only available for new applications; pre-4.1.0 monthly applications can be converted to weekly through the Database Configuration Utility with Support's help. A is incorrect — Application Properties only sets Start and End Year. C is incorrect — the generated Time Dimension XML is used by new applications, not to convert existing ones. D is incorrect — no such dependency is stated.

questions.question: A team needs to store a 1.5 GB file in OneStream. Which folder fits, and what secures it?

options.A: Internal folder, secured by Maintenance groups
options.B: Incoming folder, secured by the Workflow Profile
options.C: Contents folder, secured by System Security Roles (Administrator and ManageFileShare have full rights)
options.D: Outgoing folder, secured by Application Security Roles

questions.explanation: C is correct: both Application and System folders have an auto-generated Contents folder for files over 300 MB, managed and secured by System Security Roles; Administrator and ManageFileShare have full rights. A is incorrect — Internal holds Application or System Database file contents and is not the large-file area. B is incorrect — Incoming is for source files to import into Stage. D is incorrect — Outgoing is for custom processes that need a fixed folder location.

questions.question: Which statement about the Harvest folder in File Share is correct?

options.A: Any user with FileExplorerPage can add files
options.B: Loaded files stay in the folder until an administrator deletes them
options.C: Adding or deleting files needs Administrator rights or ManageFileShare; loaded files are cleared and copied to an archive folder
options.D: It stores files over 300 MB

questions.explanation: C is correct: Harvest and Batch automate Connector data loads; when Harvest loads a file it is cleared and an archive copy is made, and adding or deleting files requires Administrator rights or the ManageFileShare role. A is incorrect — FileExplorerPage alone does not allow adding Harvest files. B is incorrect — the file is cleared automatically after loading. D is incorrect — the Contents folder is meant for files over 300 MB.

questions.question: The Harvest archive folder is growing. What does the guide say can clear the archive folder and its files?

options.A: Data Import Schedule Manager
options.B: A Reset Scenario step
options.C: The Uploads flag
options.D: System Load/Extract

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide notes the archive folder and its files can be cleared using Data Import Schedule Manager. B is incorrect — Reset Scenario clears scenario data. C is incorrect — the Uploads flag controls upload and edit access through File Explorer. D is incorrect — System Load/Extract moves system artifacts.

questions.question: Where do Data Management export steps write files by default?

options.A: The Data Management folder in File Share
options.B: The Harvest folder
options.C: The user's folder in the Application Database
options.D: The Internal folder

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the Data Management folder is the default folder for the data management export process. B is incorrect — Harvest is for automated Connector loads. C is incorrect — Application Database user folders are private document storage. D is incorrect — Internal stores Application or System Database file contents.

questions.subtopic: File Share — Incoming and Groups Folders
questions.question: A File Viewer component must show a document only to members of a specific user group. Where should the file go?

options.A: The Incoming folder for the Workflow Profile
options.B: The Outgoing folder
options.C: The Data Management folder
options.D: A folder named after the user group under the application's Groups folder

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Groups folder supports security for File Viewer: put the file in a folder with the same name as a User Group under Applications\<App>\Groups, and the user must have permission to that group. A is incorrect — Incoming holds source files for import into Stage, available through that Workflow Profile. B is incorrect — Outgoing is for custom processes that need a fixed location. C is incorrect — Data Management is the default folder for DM exports.

questions.subtopic: File Share — Internal Folder Export Rights
questions.question: A non-administrator needs the toolbar icons that export Application Database content to File Share from the Internal folder. Which roles does the guide require?

options.A: ManageFileShare and ManageApplicationDatabaseFiles
options.B: SystemPane and FileExplorerPage
options.C: SystemLoadExtractPage and ManageFileShare
options.D: AdministerApplication and FileExplorerPage

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the user must be granted the SystemPane role and the FileExplorerPage role; the icons then show in System > Tools > File Explorer. A is incorrect — these are not the roles the guide names for these icons. C is incorrect — SystemLoadExtractPage is for System Load/Extract. D is incorrect — AdministerApplication is not the stated requirement.

questions.question: In the Windows application, what is the maximum upload size to the Application or System folders, compared with the Content folder?

options.A: 300 MB for Application/System; 2 GB for Content
options.B: 2 GB for both
options.C: 300 MB for both
options.D: 1 GB for Application/System; 5 GB for Content

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists uploads up to 300 MB for Applications and System and up to 2 GB for Content; downloads are up to 2 GB for both. B is incorrect — Application/System uploads are limited to 300 MB. C is incorrect — Content uploads go up to 2 GB. D is incorrect — these numbers are not in the guide.

questions.question: The File Share Uploads flag is set to False. What is the effect?

options.A: Only Administrators can upload
options.B: No users can upload, edit files or edit folders through File Explorer, but normal browsing still works
options.C: File Explorer is hidden from all users
options.D: Uploads go to the Harvest folder only

questions.explanation: B is correct: when False, no users have upload, edit file or edit folder access through File Explorer, but normal access rules still apply to browsing; API or non-File Explorer write attempts get a security error. A is incorrect — the guide says no users, without an administrator exception. C is incorrect — browsing still works. D is incorrect — the flag does not redirect uploads.

questions.question: Which three file storage root folders does File Explorer show?

options.A: Public, Users, Internal
options.B: Application Database, System Database, File Share
options.C: Incoming, Outgoing, Harvest
options.D: Contents, Groups, Batch

questions.explanation: B is correct: documents are stored in one of three root folders: Application Database (current application only), System Database (whole system) and File Share (self-service directory). A is incorrect — these are folders inside the database document stores. C is incorrect — these are folders within File Share. D is incorrect — these are folders within File Share.

questions.question: Where can a named Cube POV be saved in File Explorer?

options.A: Only the File Share Outgoing folder
options.B: Any of the three root folders, including File Share
options.C: The application or system folders
options.D: Only the user's Excel Add-in preferences

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says a spreadsheet can be saved to any of the three root folders, but a Cube POV can be saved only to the application or system folders. A is incorrect — a Cube POV is not saved to File Share. B is incorrect — this applies to spreadsheets, not Cube POVs. D is incorrect — Cube POVs are saved in File Explorer folders.

questions.question: An on-premises administrator wants to allow only .xlsx, .pdf and .txt uploads into File Explorer. Where is this set, and what is needed afterward?

options.A: Application Properties > Formatting; log off and on
options.B: System Configuration > General; nothing
options.C: Whitelist File Extensions in the Application Server Configuration File (via the Server Configuration Utility); restart IIS
options.D: File Share Uploads flag; restart the scheduler

questions.explanation: C is correct: whitelisted extensions are set in the Application Server Configuration file through the OneStream Server Configuration Utility (Whitelist File Extensions), saved, and then IIS is restarted; cloud customers ask Support. A is incorrect — Application Properties has no whitelist. B is incorrect — the guide puts the whitelist in the Application Server Configuration file. D is incorrect — the Uploads flag turns all File Explorer uploads on or off; it does not filter by extension.

questions.question: An administrator types .txt into the Whitelist File Extensions dialog. What is stored?

options.A: txt, because the period is removed automatically
options.B: .txt exactly as typed
options.C: An error, because periods are invalid
options.D: *.txt

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says certain characters, including the period, are removed automatically, so .txt becomes txt. B is incorrect — the period is removed. C is incorrect — the period is removed, not rejected. D is incorrect — asterisks are also removed; nothing adds a wildcard.

questions.question: After a whitelist is set, a user uploads a file whose extension is not on the list. What happens?

options.A: It uploads to a quarantine folder
options.B: It uploads with a warning
options.C: It uploads only to the Contents folder
options.D: It is blocked and the user gets an error message

questions.explanation: D is correct: if the extension is whitelisted the file uploads; if not, the user gets an error, and new files with non-whitelisted extensions are restricted from uploading. A is incorrect — there is no quarantine folder. B is incorrect — the upload is blocked, not warned. C is incorrect — the whitelist applies to File Explorer uploads generally.

questions.question: In the Application Database documents area, a user is in a folder's Maintenance group but not its Access group. What can the user do?

options.A: Nothing until added to the Access group
options.B: Read only
options.C: Create, modify and delete objects only in the Users folder
options.D: View the folder and create, modify and delete objects; Access group membership is not required

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Maintenance group lets a user view and create, modify and delete objects, and a Maintenance group member does not need to be in the Access group. A is incorrect — the Access group is not required. B is incorrect — Maintenance gives more than read access. C is incorrect — the Users folder holds private documents for named users.

questions.question: In the Application Database or System Database document folders, what is the Internal folder?

options.A: Files available to everyone with access
options.B: Private documents for named users
options.C: Files used internally that cannot be modified
options.D: The default Data Management export location

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says Internal holds files used internally that cannot be modified. A is incorrect — this describes Public. B is incorrect — this describes Users. D is incorrect — this is the File Share Data Management folder.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity in Excel Add-In — Location
questions.question: Where is the Task Activity icon found in the Excel Add-In?

options.A: In the Analysis section of the OneStream ribbon
options.B: In the Tasks section of the OneStream ribbon
options.C: Only in the Windows Application; Excel users must switch clients to cancel
options.D: Under File > Options in Excel

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'You can access the Task Activity icon in the Excel Add-In in the Tasks section in the OneStream ribbon'. A is incorrect — the guide places Task Activity in the Tasks section. C is incorrect — the guide says you do not have to be logged into the Windows application to cancel from Excel. D is incorrect — Task Activity is on the OneStream ribbon, not in Excel options.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity in Excel Add-In — Cancel Rights
questions.question: A user working only in the Excel Add-In (not logged into the Windows application) starts a long-running cube view. Which statement about cancelling is correct?

options.A: The user must log into the Windows application to cancel
options.B: Only an Administrator can cancel tasks from Excel
options.C: Cancelling from Excel requires an IIS reset
options.D: The user can cancel their own task from Excel's Task Activity, and an Administrator can cancel another user's running task

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide states you do not have to be logged into the Windows application, Task Activity in the Excel Add-In lets you cancel your task, and an Administrator can cancel another user's running task. A is incorrect — the guide explicitly says you do not have to be logged into the Windows application. B is incorrect — regular users can cancel their own tasks. C is incorrect — cancelling through Task Activity is the alternative to resetting IIS.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity — Cube View Connection Dialog
questions.question: A user adds a Cube View connection in Excel and the connection takes a very long time to establish. What lets them cancel before the cube view finishes connecting?

options.A: The Task Activity icon in the Cube View connection dialog box
options.B: The Refresh Sheet button
options.C: The Close button in the Cube View Connections dialog
options.D: Convert to XFGetCells

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Task Activity icon is also in the Cube View connection dialog box, letting you cancel 'while in the process of establishing a connection'; the note adds it is also in the Windows Application. B is incorrect — Refresh Sheet re-runs the content; it does not cancel. C is incorrect — Close only closes the dialog. D is incorrect — this converts the cube view to formulas; it does not cancel a connection.

questions.question: A user converts a cube view to XFGetCells, clicks Refresh Sheet, then opens Task Activity to cancel it. Which task type appears for this refresh?

options.A: Cube View
options.B: Get Excel Data
options.C: Quick View
options.D: Process Cube

questions.explanation: B is correct: after Refresh Sheet on converted XFGetCells, 'a Get Excel Data task type displays in the Task Activity dialog box'. A is incorrect — Cube View is the task type for running a cube view, not an XFGetCell refresh. C is incorrect — Quick View is the task type for quick views. D is incorrect — Process Cube is a data/calculation task, not a spreadsheet refresh.

questions.question: How does the Task Progress dialog for cancelling an XFGetCell refresh differ from the one for cancelling a cube view or quick view?

options.A: XFGetCell refreshes cannot be cancelled
options.B: Both show the same indeterminate bar
options.C: XFGetCell cancels show a progress bar with a percentage; cube views and quick views show an indeterminate bar
options.D: XFGetCell cancels require Administrator rights

questions.explanation: C is correct: the note says 'a progress bar with a percentage load will display for XFGetCell canceled tasks', while cube and quick view cancels show the indeterminate load bar. A is incorrect — the guide gives steps to cancel an XFGetCell refresh. B is incorrect — XFGetCell shows a percentage progress bar. D is incorrect — the guide says the task status will show if the user or administrator cancelled.

questions.question: In the Excel Add-In, what is the benefit of cancelling a paged cube view through Task Activity?

options.A: A single page can be cancelled without waiting for the entire cube view to load and process
options.B: It converts the remaining pages to XFGetCells
options.C: It saves all loaded pages to the File System
options.D: It stops paging and loads every row on one sheet

questions.explanation: A is correct: this 'allows you to cancel a single page using Task Activity instead of waiting for the entire cube view to load and process'. B is incorrect — cancelling does not convert pages. C is incorrect — no save behavior is described. D is incorrect — cancelling stops loading; it does not remove paging.

questions.question: In the Excel Add-In, what does each page show alongside the paging controls for a paged cube view?

options.A: The page number and elapsed seconds
options.B: The total row count and the server name
options.C: The page number and the percentage of data loaded
options.D: The percentage of CPU in use on the app server

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Each page will display the page number and data loaded in a percentage below the tabs in the right-hand corner'. A is incorrect — elapsed time is not described. B is incorrect — row counts are in the tool tip; the server is not shown. D is incorrect — CPU percentages are Task Activity columns (Queued CPU, Start CPU).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT shown in the paging tool tip for a paged cube view or quick view in Excel?

options.A: Number of total rows
options.B: Number of suppressed columns
options.C: Rows processed
options.D: Unsuppressed rows on a page

questions.explanation: B is correct: the paging tool tip shows 'the number of total rows, rows processed, and unsuppressed rows on a page'; columns are not mentioned. A is incorrect — this is shown. C is incorrect — this is shown. D is incorrect — this is shown.

questions.question: What security role is needed to use cube view paging in the Excel Add-In or Spreadsheet?

options.A: No special role is needed; any user can use cube view paging
options.B: Administrator
options.C: ManageCubeViews
options.D: TaskActivityPage

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Any user can use cube view paging in Excel Add-In or Spreadsheet'. B is incorrect — paging is not limited to Administrators. C is incorrect — no role is required for paging. D is incorrect — no role is required for paging.

questions.question: A user opens a saved Excel file that has a paged Cube View on one sheet, and another file that has a Quick View with paging. Which ribbon button does the guide say to use to refresh each so the paging controls appear?

options.A: Cube View file: Refresh Workbook; Quick View file: Refresh Sheet
options.B: Cube View file: Refresh Sheet; Quick View file: Refresh Workbook
options.C: Both: Refresh Sheet
options.D: Both: Submit Sheet

questions.explanation: B is correct: for the cube view file the steps say 'Click the Refresh Sheet button', and for the quick view file 'Click the Refresh Workbook button'. A is incorrect — this reverses the guide's steps. C is incorrect — the Quick View steps use Refresh Workbook. D is incorrect — Submit sends data; it does not refresh to show paging.

questions.subtopic: Cube View Paging — Next Page Dialog
questions.question: While paging through a cube view in Excel, when does the cancel dialog appear after clicking Next Page?

options.A: Every time Next Page is clicked
options.B: Only after the first page
options.C: Only when Use Detailed Logging is True
options.D: When that page takes more than 10 seconds to load

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'If you click on the paging controls to go to the next page and the load time takes more than 10 seconds, the dialog box will appear allowing you to cancel the Cube View'. A is incorrect — it appears only when the load takes more than 10 seconds. B is incorrect — the trigger is load time, not page number. C is incorrect — detailed logging does not trigger the dialog.

questions.subtopic: Cube View Paging — Next Page Cancel Result
questions.question: A user clicks Next Page on a paged cube view in Excel, then cancels that page load in Task Activity. What do they see in the data cells?

options.A: A blank page
options.B: The previous page's data
options.C: #REFRESH text in the data cells
options.D: #CANCELED text

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Canceling the Next Page load for a Cube View/Quick View will display the #REFRESH text in the data cells, rather than the page blank for the Initial Load'. A is incorrect — a blank page is the result of cancelling the initial load, not a Next Page load. B is incorrect — the guide describes #REFRESH, not the prior page's data. D is incorrect — the guide describes #REFRESH.

questions.question: Where are Quick View paging controls now located in the Excel Add-In/Spreadsheet?

options.A: Inside the Quick Views tab only
options.B: Below all three tabs
options.C: In the Tasks section of the OneStream ribbon
options.D: In the Create Quick View dialog

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Previously, Quick View paging controls appeared in the Quick Views tab. It is now located below all three tabs'. A is incorrect — that was the previous location. C is incorrect — the Tasks section holds Task Activity. D is incorrect — that dialog names the quick view; it does not hold paging controls.

questions.question: Which object does NOT have the usual Access and Maintenance security groups?

options.A: Cube Views
options.B: Transformation Rules
options.C: Task Scheduler
options.D: Workflow Profiles

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says every object has access and maintenance security rights, with the exception of Task Scheduler. A is incorrect — Cube Views use Access and Maintenance groups. B is incorrect — Transformation Rule Groups and Profiles use Access and Maintenance. D is incorrect — Workflow Profiles have Access and Maintenance groups.

questions.question: A regional team must create, edit and delete rules in one Entity Transformation Rule Group only, without becoming administrators of all transformation rules. What is the BEST setup?

options.A: Grant their group the ManageTransformationRules application role for the application
options.B: Assign their group as the Access Group
options.C: Give them Workflow Execution access on the Import profile
options.D: Assign their group as the Maintenance Group of that Transformation Rule Group

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says a Maintenance Group is the middle level of power and, when assigned to a specific Entity Transformation Rule Group, lets assigned users create, edit and delete rules within that group. A is incorrect — an application role makes them pseudo administrators over all rules of that type. B is incorrect — Access is the lowest level; the object can be used but not edited. C is incorrect — execution access lets users run Workflow, not maintain rules.

questions.question: What does the guide call the best way to control Data Sources?

options.A: Use the ManageDataSources application role, with no security settings at the object level
options.B: Set Access = Everyone and Maintenance = Administrators on each Data Source object
options.C: Set each Data Source's Access Group to the Workflow Execution Group of its Workflow Profile
options.D: Lock Data Sources with Data Cell Conditional Input

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says the best way to control Data Sources is the ManageDataSources application role and no security settings at the object level; run-time access comes from Workflow execution. B is incorrect — that is the pattern for Confirmation Rules, Certification Questions and Form/Journal templates. C is incorrect — Data Source access at run time comes from the Workflow Profile; the guide recommends no object-level security. D is incorrect — Conditional Input controls cell input, not Data Source objects.

questions.question: A location-specific Account Transformation Rule Group should be reviewed and edited by that location's data loaders. Why does the guide say user groups should be assigned to Access and Maintenance here?

options.A: Without Access to the rule group, the location's users cannot run the Import step of their Workflow Profile
options.B: Users can right-click an Import Workflow Profile to view/edit its rules, so include that Workflow's executors
options.C: Maintenance on the rule group is required for users to run Validate in Stage for their Workflow
options.D: Every Transformation Rule Group, including corporate ones, should be assigned to each location's data loaders

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says an appropriate group needs Access and Maintenance because users can right-click an Import Workflow Profile and view/edit their rules; groups should include users who execute those Workflow Profiles, while core/corporate groups stay Access Everyone, Maintenance Administrators. A is incorrect — the guide says users do not need Access or Maintenance to Transformation Rules to run the Import. C is incorrect — validation runs under Workflow execution. D is incorrect — core, shared or corporate groups should be Access Everyone, Maintenance Administrators.

questions.question: Which Cube View setting does OneStream recommend for most report Cube Views, and how can it be preset for new ones?

options.A: Set Can Modify Data, Can Calculate, Can Translate and Can Consolidate to True so users can process from reports
options.B: Set the four Can properties to False once in Application Properties so every Cube View inherits it
options.C: Set Can Modify Data, Can Calculate, Can Translate, Can Consolidate to False; preset via a template Cube View
options.D: Set Access to Nobody on every Cube View Group, and Maintenance to Administrators

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide recommends setting these properties to False and says this can be preset for new Cube Views by creating an example or template Cube View to copy. A is incorrect — the recommendation is False, except for data-entry forms or admin-only Cube Views. B is incorrect — the guide uses a template Cube View, not an application-wide setting. D is incorrect — access groups do not replace these properties.

questions.question: A user has access to a Dashboard Group but not to the Dashboard Profile that contains it. What happens in OnePlace?

options.A: The user sees the Dashboards because group access overrides profile access
options.B: The user sees the Dashboards with NoAccess in every cell
options.C: The user sees the Dashboards but cannot run the Parameters
options.D: The user cannot see the Dashboards in OnePlace

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says if a user has access to the Dashboard Groups but not the Profiles, they will not be able to see the Dashboards in OnePlace. A is incorrect — profile access is also required. B is incorrect — NoAccess appears when the user lacks data access, not profile access. C is incorrect — the guide says security has no bearing on Parameters.

questions.question: Which statement about Dashboard Parameters is TRUE according to the security best practices?

options.A: They can be used across all Dashboards without copying per Maintenance Unit, and security has no bearing on them
options.B: Each Parameter has its own Access Group and Maintenance Group, and the user must be in the Access Group to use it
options.C: Parameters must be copied into every Dashboard Maintenance Unit that uses them, with matching names
options.D: Parameters inherit the Maintenance Group of the Dashboard Profile that contains the Dashboard using them

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says Dashboard Parameters can be used across all Dashboards, do not need to be copied across Maintenance Units, and security has no bearing on their use. B is incorrect — security has no bearing on Parameters. C is incorrect — the guide says they do not need to be copied. D is incorrect — no such inheritance is described.

questions.question: A user has the ManageWorkflowProfiles role but sees no Workflow Profiles under a Cube Root. What is missing?

options.A: Workflow Execution Group membership on every child profile
options.B: At least Access Group privileges to the Cube Root Workflow Profile
options.C: The ManageApplicationProperties role
options.D: Certification SignOff Group membership on the Cube Root Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says users need at least Access Group privileges on the Cube Root Workflow Profile to edit Workflow Profiles with ManageWorkflowProfiles; otherwise they will not see any Workflow Profiles under it. A is incorrect — execution is about running Workflow, not seeing profiles to edit. C is incorrect — that role is not related. D is incorrect — sign-off is not required to see profiles.

questions.question: A Workflow user with execution access needs to post a journal from an approved template. Does she need the ManageJournalTemplates role?

options.A: Yes; creating or posting any journal requires the ManageJournalTemplates application role
options.B: Yes, unless she is also in the Workflow Profile's Maintenance Group, which substitutes for the application role
options.C: No; Workflow execution and the template Access Groups govern this. The Manage role is for maintaining templates
options.D: No; ModifyData alone is enough, and Workflow Execution access is not needed for journals

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the Manage roles relate to creating, reading, updating and deleting Journal/Form templates (metadata); most Workflow users have no Application Roles, their access comes from the template Access Groups, and they need Workflow Execution access, not a Manage role, to create a journal. A is incorrect — the guide says the user does not need the Manage role to create a journal. B is incorrect — Maintenance is not the documented path. D is incorrect — Workflow Execution Group access is required for import, forms and journal actions.

questions.question: In what order does the guide say to assign access to Workflow Profiles and data?

options.A: Workflow Profile Access, Data and Approver groups first, then assign those groups as the Entities' Read and Read/Write groups
options.B: Application Security Roles first, then Entity Read/Write groups, then Workflow Profile groups last
options.C: Cube Data Access slice filters first, then Entity groups, then Workflow Profile Access and Approver groups
options.D: Entity Read and Read/Write groups first, then Access, Data and Approver groups per Workflow Profile that include them

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says first assign Read and Read/Write Groups to the Entities, next create an Access Group, Data Group and Approver Group for each Workflow Profile and include the appropriate Entity groups. A is incorrect — the Entity groups come first. B is incorrect — the guide's order starts with Entity groups. C is incorrect — slice filters only work after cube, scenario and entity access are given.

questions.question: A regional controller must see the Parent Entity and all Entities below it. Each child has its own View group. What does the guide say must be done?

options.A: Assign all the child Entities' View Groups to the Parent-level Entity View Group
options.B: Assign the Parent's View group to each child's Read/Write Data Group
options.C: Turn on Use Parent Security for Relationship Consolidation Dimension Members on the cube
options.D: Give the controller the ViewAllData role

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says all the Entities' View Groups below the Parent must be assigned to the Parent Level Entity View Group to gain access to data at the Parent and View Entities below it, and to minimize the number of View groups. B is incorrect — Read/Write groups are for loading, not viewing. C is incorrect — that changes access to relationship consolidation members, not entity viewing. D is incorrect — that grants view of all data, beyond the region.

questions.question: What does the Display Member Group on a dimension member control?

options.A: Read access to the member's data, with Read/Write still controlled by the data groups
options.B: Whether slice filters apply to the member
options.C: Only whether the member can be displayed; it does not control data access
options.D: Who can maintain the member in the Dimension Library

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the display member group only refers to the member display access level, not the data access level. A is incorrect — data access is from Read and Read/Write Data Groups. B is incorrect — that is Use Cube Data Access. D is incorrect — the guide describes the Display Member Group only as the member display access level, not maintenance rights.

questions.question: After creating a new security group in System > Administration > Security, an administrator cannot find it in the OpenApplication drop-down in Application > Tools > Security Roles. What should be done?

options.A: Reset IIS so the new group is loaded into the Application Security Roles lists
options.B: Assign the group to SystemAdministrationLogon
options.C: Recreate the group as an exclusion group
options.D: Refresh the application so the new group appears in the drop-down menus

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide's steps say to refresh the application for the new security group to appear in all drop-down menus before selecting it for OpenApplication (which defaults to Everyone when an application is created).
