A is incorrect — the guide says refresh the application. B is incorrect — that controls the System Administration application, not OpenApplication's list. C is incorrect — exclusion groups are not required.

questions.subtopic: Data Cell Conditional Input — Omit for Scenario
questions.question: Many Data Cell Conditional Input rules make intersections read-only in Actual. A Preserve scenario must still accept copies of historical data in those intersections. What does the guide recommend?

options.A: A top-positioned rule for the Preserve scenario with behavior Increase Access And Stop
options.B: A rule for the Preserve scenario with behavior Decrease Access And Stop placed at the bottom
options.C: Delete the existing rules and rebuild them with Scenario filters
options.D: Grant the ViewAllData role to the copy job

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says to create a rule for the entire scenario with behavior Increase Access And Stop, position it at the top, so access increases and the subsequent rules are ignored for that scenario. B is incorrect — decreasing access would block the copy, and rules below are already skipped by the top rule. C is incorrect — the guide offers the top rule as a simple alternative. D is incorrect — ViewAllData is for viewing, not bypassing conditional input.

questions.question: Which platform engine does the guide call the controlling engine, or puppeteer, which tracks the status of business processes in Workflow hierarchies?

options.A: Data Management Engine
options.B: Workflow Engine
options.C: Finance Engine
options.D: Presentation Engine

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide describes the Workflow Engine as the controlling engine or puppeteer that controls and tracks Workflow process status. A is incorrect — it provides task automation through sequences and steps. C is incorrect — it enriches and aggregates data into consolidated information. D is incorrect — it provides data visualization services.

questions.question: Which engine is described as an in-memory, multi-threaded engine that parses source data, maps it to valid Members and runs Derivative Check Rules?

options.A: Finance Engine
options.B: Stage Engine
options.C: Data Quality Engine
options.D: Workflow Engine

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Stage Engine reads and parses source data, transforms or maps it, and validates by running Derivative Check Rules. A is incorrect — it is the in-memory financial analytic engine for calculations and aggregation. C is incorrect — it controls confirmation and certification. D is incorrect — it controls and tracks Workflow status.

questions.question: Which pair of engines works together to run Confirmation Rules that validate analytic data values?

options.A: Finance Engine and Data Quality Engine
options.B: Stage Engine and Data Quality Engine
options.C: Workflow Engine and Presentation Engine
options.D: Data Management Engine and Finance Engine

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says the Finance Engine works with the Data Quality Engine to run Confirmation Rules. B is incorrect — the Stage Engine works with the Finance Engine to validate incoming intersections and runs Derivative Check Rules. C is incorrect — these are not the engines named for Confirmation Rules. D is incorrect — Data Management steps can use Finance Engine services, but Confirmation Rules involve the Data Quality Engine.

questions.question: The Data Quality Engine has two parts. Which part manages user certifications and decides the completion status of Workflow dependents?

options.A: Confirmation Engine
options.B: Workflow Engine
options.C: Parameter Engine
options.D: Certification Engine

questions.explanation: D is correct: The Certification Engine manages user certifications and determines Workflow dependents' completion status. A is incorrect — it defines and controls the sequence of data value checks. B is incorrect — it tracks Workflow status but is separate from the Data Quality Engine. C is incorrect — it is part of the Presentation Engine.

questions.question: How does the guide describe the Data Management Engine?

options.A: It parses source files into tabular format for mapping
options.B: It manages certifications and Workflow dependents
options.C: It runs batches of commands organized into sequences of steps, which can include Business Rule steps
options.D: It is made of the Cube View, Dashboard, Parameter and Book engines

questions.explanation: C is correct: The Data Management Engine runs batches of commands organized into sequences with steps, including Business Rule steps that run custom rules. A is incorrect — this is the Stage Engine. B is incorrect — this is the Data Quality (Certification) Engine. D is incorrect — this is the Presentation Engine.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the component engines of the Presentation Engine?

options.A: Parameter Engine
options.B: Book Engine
options.C: Confirmation Engine
options.D: Extensible Document Engine

questions.explanation: C is correct: The Presentation Engine is made up of the Cube View, Dashboard, Parameter, Book and Extensible Document engines; the Confirmation Engine is part of the Data Quality Engine. A is incorrect — it is a listed component. B is incorrect — it is a listed component. D is incorrect — it is a listed component.

questions.question: An Azure-hosted environment sets Scaling Type to use System Business Rules. What decides whether scaling happens?

options.A: A user-defined System Extender Business Rule that implements the scaling function and returns the proper scaling object
options.B: A Finance Business Rule attached to the cube
options.C: The Maximum Average CPU Utilization setting in Task Load Balancing
options.D: A Data Management sequence scheduled in Task Scheduler

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'If System Business Rules is selected as a Scaling Type, then a user-defined System Extender Business Rule determines if scaling is needed. You must implement the scaling function and return the proper scaling object'. B is incorrect — Finance rules are not used for server/eDTU scaling. C is incorrect — that setting decides whether a server can take a task, not scaling. D is incorrect — scaling decisions come from the System Extender rule.

questions.question: Which metrics are passed to the System Extender Business Rule for DATABASE scaling?

options.A: Environment metrics and Scale Set metrics
options.B: Scale Set metrics and SQL Server Elastic Pool metrics
options.C: Environment metrics and SQL Server Elastic Pool metrics
options.D: Only SQL Server Elastic Pool metrics

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'For server scaling, Environment metrics and Scale Set metrics are passed. For database scaling, Environment metrics and SQL Server Elastic Pool metrics are passed'. A is incorrect — these are passed for server scaling. B is incorrect — Environment metrics are passed in both cases; Scale Set metrics are for server scaling. D is incorrect — Environment metrics are also passed.

questions.subtopic: System Security — Role vs Maintenance vs Access Group
questions.question: A user has ManageSystemDashboards but is not in the Maintenance Group or Access Group of a System Dashboard Group. What can they do with that group's dashboards?

options.A: Create, edit and delete them; the system role gives higher privilege than group membership
options.B: Only view them, because they are not in the Maintenance Group
options.C: Nothing, because they are not in the Access Group
options.D: Edit them, but not delete them, unless they are in the Maintenance Group

questions.explanation: A is correct: A user with ManageSystemDashboards does not need to be in any Maintenance or Access Group and can create, edit and delete any System Dashboard, Dashboard Group or Profile. B is incorrect — the system role overrides the need for group membership. C is incorrect — the system role gives full rights without the Access Group. D is incorrect — the role gives create, edit and delete.

questions.subtopic: System Security — Maintenance vs Access Group
questions.question: Which statement about Maintenance Groups and Access Groups is correct?

options.A: A Maintenance Group member can create, edit and delete objects without also being in the Access Group
options.B: A Maintenance Group member must also be in the Access Group to see the object
options.C: An Access Group member can edit an object's contents but not delete it
options.D: Only the Access Group can control the contents of Profiles

questions.explanation: A is correct: Maintenance Group members can see, create, edit and delete objects and do not need the Access Group; the Access Group only lets users see and read. B is incorrect — the guide says Access Group membership is not needed. C is incorrect — the Access Group only allows seeing and reading. D is incorrect — the guide says the Maintenance Group can control Profile contents.

questions.question: Which change management approach does the guide recommend?

options.A: Apply small Business Rule changes directly in production during business hours when users can verify them, then extract to development
options.B: Test in production using copies of the affected Workflow Profiles, then delete the copies afterward
options.C: Make changes in test, then restore the test application database over production during a slow period
options.D: Test in development (ideally a renamed copy of production), then assess extracted changes in a separate test environment

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide recommends deploying and testing changes in development first, noting benefits of using a renamed recent copy of production, and extracting changes to assess in a separate test environment before production. A is incorrect — Business Rules should not be changed in production during heavy activity. B is incorrect — the guide calls for dev and test environments. C is incorrect — the guide says extract changes and deploy them, not overwrite production.

questions.question: A user who has not logged in for months gets a message that they are disabled. In System > Security > Users, their Remaining Allowed Inactivity shows 0 Days. How does the administrator restore access?

options.A: Raise the Logon Inactivity Threshold and reset IIS
options.B: Add the user to the Administrators group
options.C: Select the user, set Is Enabled to True and Save; Remaining Allowed Inactivity then updates
options.D: Delete the user and reload them through System Load/Extract

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says to set Is Enabled to True and Save, after which the Remaining Allowed Inactivity field updates so the user can log back in within the threshold. A is incorrect — this changes the policy for everyone and is not the documented fix for one user. B is incorrect — the threshold still applies to members of the Administrator group. D is incorrect — this is unnecessary; setting Is Enabled to True restores access.

questions.question: The disable-inactive-users feature adds the business rules GetStatusByID, GetStatusByName and LogonInactivityThresholdForAdmin. Where are they found?

options.A: Application > Business Rules > Dashboard Extender
options.B: Application > Business Rules > Extensibility Rules
options.C: Application > Business Rules > Connector
options.D: System > Administration > System Configuration

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says to click Application > Business Rules > Extensibility Rules to find the three new business rules. A is incorrect — they are listed under Extensibility Rules. C is incorrect — Connector rules connect to source systems; these rules are under Extensibility Rules. D is incorrect — System Configuration holds settings, not business rules.

questions.question: A self-hosted customer wants to keep native OneStream logins for a few service accounts while most users sign in through their corporate identity provider. Which configuration does the guide say is supported in a self-hosted environment?

options.A: Native authentication together with one external identity provider
options.B: Native authentication together with two OIDC providers, such as Okta and Azure AD
options.C: Two SAML 2.0 providers side by side, with native authentication disabled
options.D: MSAD and LDAP together, plus native authentication

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says a self-hosted environment can use native authentication, one external identity provider, or both native authentication and one external identity provider. B is incorrect — only one external identity provider is supported at a time. C is incorrect — two external providers are not supported; the limit is one. D is incorrect — this is two external providers; only one external IdP can be configured.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers the guide lists as supported?

options.A: Okta
options.B: PingFederate
options.C: Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID)
options.D: Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS)

questions.explanation: D is correct: ADFS is listed only as an example of a SAML 2.0 identity provider; the three OIDC providers are Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID), Okta and PingFederate. A is incorrect — Okta is one of the three listed OIDC providers. B is incorrect — PingFederate is one of the three listed OIDC providers. C is incorrect — Azure AD is one of the three listed OIDC providers.

questions.question: A non-administrator on the IT team must assign groups to system security roles but must not create users or groups. Which role should their group get?

options.A: ManageSystemSecurityUsers
options.B: ManageSystemSecurityRoles
options.C: ManageSystemSecurityGroups
options.D: SecurityAdminPage

questions.explanation: B is correct: ManageSystemSecurityRoles assignees manage role assignment to provide group-based access to artifacts and tools. A is incorrect — this lets them create, modify and manage users. C is incorrect — this lets them define and manage groups and group membership. D is incorrect — this UI role lets them view, but not modify, security artifacts.

questions.question: During a security cleanup, an administrator removes the Administrators group from several system security roles. What happens to the Administrator's access?

options.A: The Administrator loses access to those roles until the group is reassigned
options.B: The Administrator keeps access only until the next IIS reset
options.C: Nothing; the Administrator keeps complete access to all roles
options.D: The Administrator account is disabled until an inactivity review is done

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says the Administrator is assigned to all system security roles, and removing or reassigning the Administrator group, or assigning other groups to roles, does not revoke the Administrator's access. A is incorrect — the guide says this does not revoke the Administrator's access. B is incorrect — access is not tied to an IIS reset. D is incorrect — the Administrator cannot be disabled.

questions.question: A company buys licenses for executives who will only look at data, reports and dashboards in production and must never load, calculate, consolidate or certify. Which User Type fits?

options.A: Restricted
options.B: View
options.C: Third Party Access
options.D: Financial Close

questions.explanation: B is correct: View users can access data, reports and dashboards in production but cannot load, calculate, consolidate, certify or change data. A is incorrect — Restricted users are limited from certain OneStream Solutions (such as Lease and Account Reconciliation) by contract, not limited to view-only. C is incorrect — Third Party Access is for logging in through a third-party application with a named account and cannot use the Windows or browser application. D is incorrect — Financial Close is for Account Reconciliation and Transaction Matching.

questions.question: Which User Type is described as being unable to use some OneStream Solution features, such as Lease and Account Reconciliation, because of contractual limitations?

options.A: Restricted
options.B: View
options.C: Financial Close
options.D: Interactive

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide defines Restricted users as unable to use some OneStream Solution features such as Lease and Account Reconciliation due to contractual limitations. B is incorrect — View users cannot load, calculate, consolidate, certify or change data; the definition is not about specific Solutions. C is incorrect — Financial Close users can use Account Reconciliation, the opposite of this restriction. D is incorrect — Interactive users can use all features and tools.

questions.subtopic: Users — User Type: Third Party Access
questions.question: An external reporting tool must reach OneStream through a named account. The account must never change data or modify artifacts and must not open the Windows or browser application. Which User Type matches?

options.A: View
options.B: Restricted
options.C: Interactive
options.D: Third Party Access

questions.explanation: D is correct: Third Party Access users access applications through a third-party application with a named account and cannot change data, modify artifacts, or access the Windows or browser-based application. A is incorrect — View users still use the OneStream application to see data, reports and dashboards. B is incorrect — Restricted is about contractual limits on certain Solutions. C is incorrect — Interactive users can use all features, including changing data.

questions.question: Which User Type does the guide define specifically as allowing use of the Account Reconciliation and Transaction Matching OneStream Solutions?

options.A: Restricted
options.B: View
options.C: Financial Close
options.D: Third Party Access

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says Financial Close users can use the Account Reconciliation and Transaction Matching Solutions. A is incorrect — Restricted users are the ones who cannot use some Solutions, such as Account Reconciliation. B is incorrect — View is the read-only license type. D is incorrect — Third Party Access is for named-account access through a third-party application.

questions.question: An administrator is creating a native (non-SSO) user in System > Security. How should the authentication fields be set?

options.A: Select the native provider in External Authentication Provider and enter the OneStream user name in External Provider User Name
options.B: Set External Authentication Provider to (Not Used) and enter the password in External Provider User Name
options.C: Set External Authentication Provider to (Not Used), leave External Provider User Name blank, and enter the password in Internal Provider Password
options.D: Leave External Authentication Provider blank and set Is Enabled to False until the user resets the password

questions.explanation: C is correct: For native authentication the guide says to select Not Used, leave External Provider User Name blank, and enter the password in Internal Provider Password; the user can change it at first login. A is incorrect — there is no native provider to select; native users use (Not Used) and a blank External Provider User Name. B is incorrect — External Provider User Name is left blank for native users; the password goes in Internal Provider Password. D is incorrect — Is Enabled controls activation, not authentication; the provider must be set to (Not Used).

questions.question: A user's OneStream name is LHall. In Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) the user's name is Azure_LHall@azure.com. What must be entered in External Provider User Name?

options.A: LHall, because it must match the OneStream user name
options.B: Azure_LHall@azure.com
options.C: Nothing; the provider matches users on the Email property
options.D: The name of the Azure AD group the user belongs to

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says to enter the user name in the IdP (its example is exactly Azure_LHall@azure.com) and that it must be unique and match the user name in the IdP. A is incorrect — the field must match the name in the identity provider, not the OneStream name. C is incorrect — the field is required for external users and must match the IdP user name. D is incorrect — groups cannot be externally authenticated, and the field holds the user's IdP name.

questions.question: A remote user with a slow connection and a small screen wants grids to show fewer rows before a page break. Which setting does the guide point to?

options.A: Max Number of Unsuppressed Row Per Cube View Page
options.B: Grid Rows Per Page on the user's profile
options.C: Max Number of Expanded Cube View Rows
options.D: Custom Text

questions.explanation: B is correct: Grid Rows Per Page sets how many rows show on grids before a page break, and the guide says to consider connectivity and screen resolution. A is incorrect — this System Configuration setting applies to Cube Views across the whole environment, not one user. C is incorrect — this environment-wide setting caps rows on expanded Cube Views. D is incorrect — Custom Text personalizes functionality, such as tagging or filtering; it does not control paging.

questions.question: A designer wants to tag users so a business rule can filter a distribution list and open a controller- or executive-specific view of the workspace. Which user property does the guide suggest?

options.A: Custom Text (Text 1–8)
options.B: Culture
options.C: Grid Rows Per Page
options.D: External Provider User Name

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says Custom Text can act as a metadata tag, filter a distribution list, or launch a functionally tailored view. B is incorrect — Culture sets the user's locale for formatting. C is incorrect — this controls grid paging only. D is incorrect — this must match the user's name in the identity provider and is used for authentication.

questions.question: An administrator copies user JSmith with Copy References made by parent groups selected. JSmith belongs to three groups and one exclusion group. What group membership does the new user get?

options.A: All four, including the exclusion group
options.B: Only the exclusion group, so access is denied by default
options.C: None; group references copy only when Copy child user and group references is also selected
options.D: The three groups, but not the exclusion group

questions.explanation: D is correct: The option adds the new user to the original user's groups except exclusion groups. A is incorrect — exclusion groups are excluded from the copy. B is incorrect — it works the other way: the regular groups are copied and the exclusion group is not. C is incorrect — Copy child user and group references is the option for copying a group, not a user.

questions.question: An auditor asks what a specific user can access. From System > Security > Users, which action does the guide suggest for identifying the user's access?

options.A: Show All Users
options.B: Show All Groups
options.C: View All Logon Activity
options.D: Show all parent groups for user

questions.explanation: D is correct: Since group assignment to system security roles and user interface roles determines what a user can do, the guide says to use this option to identify their access. A is incorrect — Show All Users is a group action that lists a group's users. B is incorrect — Show All Groups is a group action that lists the groups nested in a group. C is incorrect — this is a system security role for seeing logon activity, not a user action for reviewing access.

questions.question: Which statement about the logon inactivity threshold is correct?

options.A: It applies only to native users; external users are governed by the identity provider
options.B: It applies to native and external users, including members of the Administrators group, but not to the Administrator
options.C: It exempts every member of the Administrators group
options.D: It disables users automatically as soon as the threshold passes, even if they never try to log in

questions.explanation: B is correct: The threshold deactivates all users, native and external, and applies to users in the Administrator group but not to the Administrator. A is incorrect — the guide says it applies to both native and external users. C is incorrect — only the Administrator is exempt; members of the Administrator group are subject to it. D is incorrect — the guide describes users who try to log in after the threshold receiving an error.

questions.question: Using the Server Configuration Utility, where does an administrator set the Logon Inactivity Threshold?

options.A: In the Application Server Configuration file (XFAppServerConfig.xml), under Authentication > Security
options.B: In the Web Server Configuration file, under Security
options.C: In the Database Server Connections section of the Application Server Configuration file
options.D: In Application > Tools > Application Properties

questions.explanation: A is correct: The steps are File > Open Application Server Configuration File, then in Authentication click Security and enter Logon Inactivity Threshold. B is incorrect — the setting is in the Application Server Configuration file. C is incorrect — database connections do not hold the inactivity threshold. D is incorrect — the threshold is a server and system setting, not an application property.

questions.question: An implementation team will bulk-load 400 users and their groups. Which way of building the XML load file does the guide recommend?

options.A: Extract security from the GolfStream sample application and edit the XML
options.B: Use the Application Load/Extract tool with File Type Security
options.C: Build it in a Table View and save it through the Excel add-in
options.D: Generate it with SecurityTemplate.xlsx from the Sample Templates OneStream Solution

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide recommends using SecurityTemplate.xlsx from the SampleTemplates solution to generate the XML load file. A is incorrect — this is the other listed method, but not the recommended one. B is incorrect — security is loaded through System > Tools > Load/Extract, and this does not build the file. C is incorrect — the guide does not describe this method for security loads.

questions.question: When extracting users through System > Tools > Load/Extract with File Type Security, which option also exports each user's ID?

options.A: Extract and Edit
options.B: Copy References made by parent groups
options.C: Export Unique IDs
options.D: Show all parent groups for user

questions.explanation: C is correct: After selecting Users in Items to Extract, choose Export Unique IDs to also extract each user's ID. A is incorrect — Extract and Edit opens the extract in an XML Editor. B is incorrect — this is an option when copying a user. D is incorrect — this is a user-management action, not an extract option.

questions.subtopic: Groups — External Authentication and Role Assignment
questions.question: Which statement about groups and access is correct?

options.A: Group membership can be synchronized from Azure AD when the group's External Authentication Provider is set
options.B: Groups cannot be externally authenticated, and access to tools and artifacts comes from assigning groups, not individual users, to roles
options.C: Individual users can be assigned directly to a system security role when only one user needs it
options.D: Child groups inherit a parent's access only when inheritance is turned on for the child

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says you cannot assign individual users access to tools and artifacts, that roles assigned to groups determine access, and that groups cannot be externally authenticated. A is incorrect — groups cannot be externally authenticated. C is incorrect — you cannot assign individual users to roles; use a group. D is incorrect — child groups always inherit the parent group's access.

questions.question: The group Frankfurt is a child of Europe_Controllers, which is assigned to a system security role. An administrator removes Frankfurt from Europe_Controllers. What happens to Frankfurt's members?

options.A: They keep the access until they log off and back on
options.B: They lose the access that Europe_Controllers provided through its role assignments
options.C: They keep the access because it was copied to Frankfurt when it was nested
options.D: Nothing, because inheritance flows upward from child to parent

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says removing child groups from parent groups revokes access to the tools and artifacts the parent provides through its role assignments. A is incorrect — the guide says removal revokes access, with no grace period. C is incorrect — access is inherited from the parent, not copied. D is incorrect — inheritance flows downward from parent to child.

questions.question: After a reorganization, a few users must lose access that several roles grant through a deep nested-group hierarchy. What does the guide suggest?

options.A: Remove the users from every nested group in the hierarchy
options.B: Set Is Enabled to False for the affected users
options.C: Lower the Logon Inactivity Threshold for those users
options.D: Create an exclusion group with the affected users and apply it to the roles they no longer need

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says removing a few users from a group hierarchy is time-consuming, so create an exclusion group with those users and apply it to the roles. A is incorrect — the guide calls this time-consuming and recommends an exclusion group. B is incorrect — this blocks login entirely instead of removing specific access. C is incorrect — the threshold disables inactive users; it does not control role access.

questions.question: Amelia and Bob are members of the Frankfurt Controller group. An exclusion group lists Amelia (Deny Access) and Bob (Deny Access) first, then Frankfurt Controller (Allow Access). What happens, and how should it be fixed?

options.A: Amelia and Bob still have access; put Frankfurt Controller first set to Allow Access, then Amelia and Bob below it set to Deny Access
options.B: Amelia and Bob are denied, because Deny Access always wins over Allow Access
options.C: Amelia and Bob are denied, because users listed first are always evaluated first
options.D: Everyone in Frankfurt Controller is denied, so the group should be removed

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says this order does not restrict them because they are in the Frankfurt Controller group; to deny them, list the group first (Allow) and the users below it (Deny). B is incorrect — access follows the order you set, regardless of group membership, so Deny does not always win. C is incorrect — the guide's example shows this order does not restrict them. D is incorrect — the issue is only that Amelia and Bob are not restricted; the group should stay, listed first.

questions.question: An administrator copies an existing group and wants the new group to have the same users and child groups. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Copy References made by parent groups
options.B: Show All Groups
options.C: Copy child user and group references
options.D: Export Unique IDs

questions.explanation: C is correct: When copying a group, selecting Copy child user and group references adds the same users or groups to the new group. A is incorrect — this option is for copying a user. B is incorrect — this shows nested groups; it does not copy anything. D is incorrect — this is an option for extracting security.

questions.question: A user needs read and write access to every folder in the System (Framework) database file system through File Explorer. Which pair of roles is needed?

options.A: ManageApplicationDatabaseFiles and FileExplorerPage
options.B: ManageSystemDatabaseFiles and FileExplorerPage
options.C: ManageFileShare and DatabasePage
options.D: ManageSystemDatabaseFiles and DatabasePage

questions.explanation: B is correct: ManageSystemDatabaseFiles grants read and write to all folders and files in the Framework database file system and is tied to the FileExplorerPage UI role. A is incorrect — this covers the Application database file system, not the System one. C is incorrect — ManageFileShare covers the Windows File Share, and DatabasePage opens the Database page. D is incorrect — the role is tied to FileExplorerPage, not DatabasePage.

questions.question: Where is the location of the File Share configured?

options.A: In XFAppServerConfig.xml, using the FileShareRootFolder setting
options.B: In System Configuration > Database Server Connections
options.C: In Application > Tools > Application Properties
options.D: In the properties of the Contents folder in File Explorer

questions.explanation: A is correct: The File Share is a Windows folder that application servers can read and write, configured in XFAppServerConfig.xml with FileShareRootFolder. B is incorrect — database connections do not set the File Share. C is incorrect — the File Share is server-side, not an application property. D is incorrect — File Explorer shows the File Share but does not set its root location.

questions.subtopic: System Configuration — Cube View Time Limit
questions.question: What are the default and maximum values for Max Number Seconds To Process Cube View?

options.A: Default 180 seconds; maximum 1,800 seconds
options.B: Default 2000 seconds; maximum 100,000 seconds
options.C: Default 20 seconds; maximum 600 seconds
options.D: Default 30 seconds; maximum 120 seconds

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the default of 20 comes from the OneStream Server Configuration Utility and the maximum is 600 seconds; this setting affects paging. A is incorrect — 180 is the Get Data Cells logging default. B is incorrect — 2000 and 100,000 are the unsuppressed row default and maximum. D is incorrect — 30 is the recycle Max Pause Time default in minutes.

questions.subtopic: Manage System Security — UI Roles Granted
questions.question: Users with Manage System Security roles get access to which System User Interface Roles?

options.A: SecurityAdminPage and SystemLoadExtractPage
options.B: ApplicationAdminPage and DatabasePage
options.C: SystemConfigurationPage and ApplicationServersPage
options.D: SystemAdministrationLogon and SystemPane

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says users with Manage System Security roles can access the System User Interface Roles SystemAdministrationLogon and SystemPane. A is incorrect — these are not the ones the guide names. B is incorrect — these are not the ones the guide names. C is incorrect — these are not the ones the guide names.

questions.question: An accountant who reports to the Controller must create exclusion groups and manage group membership, with no other security rights. Which role fits?

options.A: ManageSystemSecurityGroups
options.B: ManageSystemSecurityUsers
options.C: ManageSystemSecurityRoles
options.D: ManageSystemDashboards

questions.explanation: A is correct: It grants permission to manage groups, exclusion groups and group membership. B is incorrect — this manages user accounts and properties. C is incorrect — this manages system security role assignment. D is incorrect — this manages System Dashboards.

questions.question: With only ManageSystemSecurityUsers, which user setting area can the role holder NOT manage?

options.A: General
options.B: Authentication
options.C: Custom Text
options.D: Group Membership

questions.explanation: D is correct: The role lets you set General, Authentication, Preferences and Custom Text; managing group membership or copying users requires ManageSystemSecurityGroup. A is incorrect — General is one of the property areas the role can set. B is incorrect — Authentication is one of the property areas the role can set. C is incorrect — Custom Text is one of the property areas the role can set.

questions.question: A help-desk analyst has ManageSystemSecurityUsers. Which action will succeed?

options.A: Deleting their own account
options.B: Updating the email address of an Administrators group member
options.C: Disabling an inactive non-administrator user
options.D: Giving a colleague ManageSystemSecurityUsers

questions.explanation: C is correct: The role can create, modify, delete and disable users. A is incorrect — role holders cannot delete themselves. B is incorrect — role holders cannot create, modify or delete administrators, directly or indirectly. D is incorrect — role holders cannot add other users to Manage System Security privileges.

questions.question: A user with ManageSystemSecurityGroups tries the actions below. Which one is allowed?

options.A: Adding themselves to the Finance Reviewers group
options.B: Copying the Administrators group to make a backup admin group
options.C: Copying a non-administrative group
options.D: Changing the parent group of a group they belong to

questions.explanation: C is correct: The role can copy groups except groups with Administrator privileges, and can add or remove members. A is incorrect — role holders cannot change their own membership in other groups. B is incorrect — groups with Administrator privileges cannot be copied. D is incorrect — role holders cannot change the parent group of a group they are a member of.

questions.question: A user with ManageSystemSecurityRoles belongs only to the group IT_Support. Which change can they make?

options.A: Assign the Everyone group to ErrorLogPage
options.B: Assign the Treasury group to ManageSystemDashboards
options.C: Change which group is assigned to ManageSystemSecurityRoles
options.D: Add IT_Support to ManageFileShare

questions.explanation: B is correct: They can manage system security roles as long as they do not touch ManageSystemSecurityRole, the Everyone or Nobody groups, or roles involving their own groups. A is incorrect — assigning Everyone or Nobody requires Administrator-level privileges. C is incorrect — the ManageSystemSecurityRole itself requires Administrator-level privileges. D is incorrect — they cannot add a group they are a member of to a role.

questions.question: How does OneStream enforce Manage System Security limits when a non-administrator loads a security XML file?

options.A: It compares the current security in the target environment to the changed state produced by processing the source file
options.B: It checks the user's role assignments in the source environment the file came from
options.C: It loads the file and then rolls back any rows that break the limits
options.D: It does not enforce the limits during XML loads; they apply only in the UI

questions.explanation: A is correct: Validation compares the current security state in the target with the changed state from the source file, so security must already exist. B is incorrect — validation uses the target environment's current state. C is incorrect — validation is done by comparing states during the load; the guide describes no rollback. D is incorrect — the guide says the limits are enforced during Load and Extract.

questions.question: A non-administrator must be able to copy users. Which role assignment does the guide require?

options.A: ManageSystemSecurityUsers alone
options.B: ManageSystemSecurityRoles alone
options.C: ManageSystemSecurityUsers together with SystemLoadExtractPage
options.D: ManageSystemSecurityUsers together with ManageSystemSecurityGroups

questions.explanation: D is correct: Copying users or managing group membership requires ManageSystemSecurityGroup, and the guide's combined-roles example says users-plus-groups lets you copy a user. A is incorrect — the Users role alone cannot copy users. B is incorrect — this role manages role assignment only. C is incorrect — SystemLoadExtractPage is for the Load/Extract page; copying needs the Groups role.

questions.question: A dashboard button runs a BRApi function that inserts a new user. When a user clicks it, what does the system check?

options.A: That the user is in the dashboard's Maintenance Group
options.B: That the user has ManageSystemDashboards
options.C: That the user clicking is in the Administrators group or has ManageSystemSecurityUsers
options.D: Nothing; business rules run with the rule author's rights

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says the system validates that the user clicking the button is in the Administrators Group or has the ManageSystemSecurityUsers role. A is incorrect — the Maintenance Group controls editing the dashboard, not BRApi security actions. B is incorrect — this role manages System Dashboards, not users. D is incorrect — BRApi security functions are controlled by the caller's Manage System Security role.

questions.question: Dashboards and business rules must read files from the File Share Contents folder, but users must not see the Contents folder in File Explorer. Which role fits?

options.A: AccessFileShareContents
options.B: ManageFileShareContents
options.C: ManageSystemDatabaseFiles
options.D: RetrieveFileShareContents

questions.explanation: D is correct: With this role the Contents folder is not shown in File Explorer, but files are reachable through the application, such as Dashboards and Business Rules. A is incorrect — this shows the Contents folder and allows viewing and download. B is incorrect — this shows the folder and grants full create, upload, download and delete rights. C is incorrect — this covers the database file system, not the File Share.

questions.question: A group must see the File Share Contents folder and download files, but must not create, upload or delete. Which role fits?

options.A: ManageFileShareContents
options.B: RetrieveFileShareContents
options.C: ManageFileShare
options.D: AccessFileShareContents

questions.explanation: D is correct: It shows the Contents folder and allows only seeing the folder and its files and downloading. A is incorrect — this grants full rights to create, upload, download and delete. B is incorrect — this hides the Contents folder in File Explorer. C is incorrect — this role lets users edit File Share folders and files.

questions.subtopic: System Roles — Encrypt System Business Rules
questions.question: A developer must hide the contents of a business rule on the System tab Business Rules screen from all users. Which role allows this?

options.A: Encrypt Business Rules (application security role)
options.B: ManageSystemConfiguration
options.C: Encrypt System Business Rules
options.D: ManageSystemDashboards

questions.explanation: C is correct: This role lets a user encrypt or decrypt a rule from the System tab Business Rule screen to hide its contents from all users. A is incorrect — this is the application-level role for application business rules, not System tab rules. B is incorrect — this manages server configurations. D is incorrect — this manages System Dashboards.

questions.subtopic: System Roles — View All Error Log
questions.question: A support analyst can open System > Logging > Error Log but needs to see errors for all users in the environment. Which role should be added?

options.A: View All Logon Activity
options.B: View All Error Log
options.C: View All Task Activity
options.D: ManageSystemConfiguration

questions.explanation: B is correct: With access to the System tab and the Error Log page, members of this role can see the Error Log for all users. A is incorrect — this covers logon activity, not errors. C is incorrect — this covers tasks and their child steps. D is incorrect — this manages server configurations.

questions.subtopic: System Roles — View All Task Activity
questions.question: A finance manager without System tab access must see all users' tasks and their child steps. Which role meets this, and where will they see the information?

options.A: View All Task Activity, through the Task Activity icon in the toolbar
options.B: TaskActivityPage, through System > Logging > Task Activity
options.C: SystemPane, through System > Logging
options.D: View All Logon Activity, through the toolbar

questions.explanation: A is correct: Members can view tasks and child steps through the Task Activity icon in the toolbar; System tab access is needed only to see them on System > Logging > Task Activity. B is incorrect — this UI role opens the page on the System tab, which the manager cannot reach. C is incorrect — SystemPane only opens the System tab. D is incorrect — this role covers logon activity, not tasks.

questions.question: When a security group is assigned to SystemAdministrationLogon, what changes for its members?

options.A: The System Administration application appears in their Application list at logon
options.B: They can see the System tab at the bottom left of the screen
options.C: They can see the Application tab
options.D: They can change server configurations under System Configuration

questions.explanation: A is correct: When a group is assigned, the System Administration application becomes available in the Application list during logon. B is incorrect — this is SystemPane. C is incorrect — this is ApplicationAdminPage. D is incorrect — this needs ManageSystemConfiguration.

questions.question: A user has ManageSystemDashboards but cannot reach System > Administration > Dashboards. Which System User Interface Role does the guide tie to ManageSystemDashboards?

options.A: ApplicationAdminPage
options.B: SecurityAdminPage
options.C: SystemDashboardAdminPage
options.D: FileExplorerPage

questions.explanation: C is correct: SystemDashboardAdminPage gives access to the Dashboard section under System > Administration > Dashboards and ties to ManageSystemDashboards. A is incorrect — this gives access to the Application tab. B is incorrect — this gives view-only access to security artifacts. D is incorrect — this ties to ManageSystemDatabaseFiles and ManageFileShare.

questions.question: An internal auditor must review security artifacts and settings on System > Administration without changing anything except their own password. Which role fits?

options.A: ManageSystemSecurityRoles
options.B: SystemPane
options.C: ApplicationAdminPage
options.D: SecurityAdminPage

questions.explanation: D is correct: This role lets you view, but not modify, security artifacts and settings other than your password. A is incorrect — this allows changing role assignments. B is incorrect — this only opens the System tab. C is incorrect — this opens the Application tab.

questions.question: Which System User Interface Role gives access to System > Tools > Application Servers?

options.A: DatabasePage
options.B: SystemConfigurationPage
options.C: ApplicationServersPage
options.D: TimeDimensionPage

questions.explanation: C is correct: It gives access to the Application Servers section under System Tab > Tools > Application Servers. A is incorrect — this opens the Database page on System > Tools. B is incorrect — this opens System Configuration. D is incorrect — this opens the Time Dimension on System > Tools.

questions.question: An administrator defines a group in System > Administration > Security while in Application A. Which statement is true?

options.A: The group exists only in Application A until it is extracted and loaded elsewhere
options.B: Users, groups and roles are not application-specific
options.C: Groups are application-specific, but users are system-wide
options.D: Groups must be recreated in each application database

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says users, groups and system security roles are not application-specific. A is incorrect — groups are system-wide. C is incorrect — both users and groups are system-wide. D is incorrect — they are stored at the system (Framework) level.

questions.question: Which BRApi function returns both regular groups and exclusion groups in one call?

options.A: BRApi.Security.Admin.GetGroupsAndExclusionGroups
options.B: BRApi.Security.Admin.GetGroups
options.C: BRApi.Security.Admin.GetExclusionGroups
options.D: BRApi.Security.Admin.GetGroupInfoEx

questions.explanation: A is correct: This function is listed for getting groups and exclusion groups together. B is incorrect — this returns groups only. C is incorrect — this returns exclusion groups only. D is incorrect — this returns extended information for a group.

questions.question: In the guide's example of changing a user's Description, which BRApi call saves the change after GetUser returns the UserInfo object?

options.A: BRApi.Security.Admin.RenameUser
options.B: BRApi.Security.Admin.SaveUser
options.C: BRApi.Security.Admin.CopyUser
options.D: BRApi.Security.Admin.GetUser

questions.explanation: B is correct: The example sets objUserInfo.User.Description and then calls BRApi.Security.Admin.SaveUser. A is incorrect — RenameUser changes the user's name, not other properties. C is incorrect — CopyUser creates a new user from an existing one. D is incorrect — GetUser only retrieves the UserInfo object.

questions.subtopic: BRApi — Adding a User to a Group
questions.question: In the guide's example of adding a user to a group with BRApi, how is the membership added?

options.A: By adding the group's UniqueID to the user's ParentGroups key list and calling SaveUser with that list
options.B: By calling CopyGroup to copy the user into the group
options.C: By calling GetGroupInfoEx, which adds the user automatically
options.D: By calling SaveExclusionGroup with the user set to Allow Access

questions.explanation: A is correct: The example gets the GroupInfo and UserInfo, adds objGroupInfo.Group.UniqueID to the parent group ID list, and calls SaveUser with True and the list. B is incorrect — CopyGroup copies a group; it does not add members. C is incorrect — GetGroupInfoEx is a retrieval function. D is incorrect — this works on exclusion groups and is not the guide's example.

questions.question: A user in Germany sees German number formatting in the web client but US formatting in Excel. What controls number and text formatting in Excel?

options.A: The user's Culture setting in System > Security
options.B: The Culture Codes setting in General System Configurations
options.C: The application's default Culture in Application Properties
options.D: The Windows Regional settings of the client operating system

questions.explanation: D is correct: Excel formatting is controlled by the client OS's Windows Regional settings, while the web client and server use the user's Culture in Security; the guide recommends keeping them matched. A is incorrect — Culture applies to the web client and server components. B is incorrect — this defines available cultures on the server. C is incorrect — the guide ties Excel formatting to Windows Regional settings.

questions.question: An administrator wants to set a user's Culture to de-DE, but de-DE does not appear in the Culture list on the user's profile. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The user's Windows Regional settings are not set to German
options.B: The user's User Type is Restricted
options.C: The de-DE culture code has not been defined in the Application Server Configuration
options.D: The user lacks the SecurityAdminPage role

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says the necessary culture codes must first be defined in the Application Server Configuration file (the Culture Codes setting) before they can be set on user profiles. A is incorrect — Windows Regional settings control Excel formatting on the client; they do not fill the Culture list in Security. B is incorrect — User Type governs license access, not available cultures. D is incorrect — the Culture list is the same for every user; it depends on the configured culture codes.

questions.question: What does the guide say is required to link an application to an existing database with Create Application Reference?

options.A: The database must first be extracted as an Application Zip File
options.B: A new Time Dimension XML file must be selected
options.C: The application must have no users or groups
options.D: The application and database must be from the same release version

questions.explanation: D is correct: Create Application Reference links an application and an existing database if they are from the same release version. A is incorrect — a reference links an existing database directly. B is incorrect — the Time Dimension Definition is chosen when creating a new database. C is incorrect — users and groups are system-level and unrelated to this.

questions.subtopic: System Applications — Delete Reference and Status
questions.question: Which statement about System > Administration > Applications is correct?

options.A: Delete Selected Application Reference drops the SQL database
options.B: A Database Status of Error means the database is being upgraded and will show in the Application list later
options.C: Delete Selected Application Reference removes only the application's link, not the database files
options.D: Test Database Connection creates a new database if none is attached

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says Delete Selected Application Reference removes the database link and does not delete database files. A is incorrect — it does not delete database files. B is incorrect — Error means the database was deleted or detached and will not be in the Application list. D is incorrect — it only checks for an active connection.

questions.question: What is the main difference between System Dashboards and Application Dashboards?

options.A: System Dashboards cannot use parameters or business rules
options.B: System Dashboards can use Framework database objects such as security and users; Application Dashboards use application data stored in Cubes
options.C: System Dashboards are visible only to the Administrator user
options.D: Application Dashboards can read security tables but not Cube data

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says System Dashboards use OneStream Framework database objects such as security and users, while Application Dashboards use application-level data in Cubes. A is incorrect — the guide describes no such limit. C is incorrect — access is controlled by roles such as ManageSystemDashboards and SystemDashboardAdminPage. D is incorrect — this reverses the difference.

questions.question: A System Administrator wants to look at application database tables while debugging, without changing data. What does the guide say about System > Tools > Database?

options.A: It allows direct SQL edits to table rows
options.B: It shows only System Database tables
options.C: It is found under Application > Tools > Database
options.D: It provides read-only access to Application Database and System Database tables

questions.explanation: D is correct: Application Database > Tables or System Database > Tables give 'read-only access to the data tables that can be used for debugging tasks that do not affect the database or system logs'. A is incorrect — access is read-only. B is incorrect — both Application Database and System Database tables are shown. C is incorrect — the path is System > Tools > Database.

questions.question: In System > Tools > Database, how are tables imported through MarketPlace Solutions named?

options.A: Their schema name replaces dbo at the start of the table name (for example, rcm.AccessGroup)
options.B: They keep the dbo prefix and add the solution name as a suffix
options.C: They are stored only in the System Database
options.D: They are hidden from the Database screen

questions.explanation: A is correct: MarketPlace tables 'have their schema name added to the beginning of the database table name and replace dbo (for example, rcm.AccessGroup and txm.AccessGroup)'. B is incorrect — the schema name replaces dbo. C is incorrect — the guide does not describe this; the naming rule is the schema prefix. D is incorrect — they are listed with their schema prefix.

questions.question: Where in the Database screen does an administrator view data records and filter them with a member filter?

options.A: System Database > Tables > Data Records
options.B: Application Database > Tools > Data Records
options.C: System > Tools > Environment > Database Servers > Diagnostics
options.D: Application > Tools > Data Management

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Go to Application Database > Tools > Data Records to view data for the entire system. Filter the data using the member filter'. A is incorrect — Data Records is under Application Database > Tools. C is incorrect — Diagnostics runs SQL diagnostic commands. D is incorrect — Data Management runs sequences and steps.

questions.subtopic: Saved Cube POV — Public vs User
questions.question: An administrator wants to save a Cube POV that many users can reuse. Where should it be saved?

options.A: In the User directory
options.B: In the Public area
options.C: In the File Share Incoming folder
options.D: In the File Share Outgoing folder

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says a POV 'can be stored for all users in the Public area or for the specific user in the User directory'. A is incorrect — it is for one specific user. C is incorrect — Incoming is for source files for Stage import. D is incorrect — the guide says a Cube POV can be saved only to the application or system folders.

questions.question: Source files placed in a Workflow Profile's Incoming folder in the File Share can be accessed how?

options.A: By any Workflow Profile in the application
options.B: Only through the System Database Documents folder
options.C: Only through that Workflow Profile
options.D: Only by users in the ManageFileShare role

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide states 'Files stored in an Incoming folder are accessible only through that Workflow Profile'. A is incorrect — access is limited to that Workflow Profile. B is incorrect — Incoming is part of the File Share, not the System Database. D is incorrect — the guide limits access by Workflow Profile, not that role.

questions.question: Which statement about OneStream's three file storage root folders is true?

options.A: A Cube POV can be saved to any of the three root folders
options.B: The System Database shows documents only for the current application
options.C: File Share holds files temporarily before database import
options.D: The Application Database shows documents for all applications

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide calls File Share 'a self-service directory that temporarily stores files before they are imported into the Application or System Database'. A is incorrect — the guide says a Cube POV can be saved to the application or system folders only. B is incorrect — that describes the Application Database; the System Database covers the entire system. D is incorrect — it shows documents for the current application only.

questions.question: A OneStream Cloud customer wants to change the Whitelist File Extensions. What should they do?

options.A: Contact OneStream Support to make the change
options.B: Edit it in Application Properties
options.C: Edit XFAppServerConfig.xml themselves and restart IIS
options.D: Load it with System Load/Extract

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide notes 'Cloud customers should contact support to have this configuration change made for them'. B is incorrect — it is a server configuration setting. C is incorrect — this is the on-premises process. D is incorrect — Load/Extract moves system artifacts and does not set server configuration.

questions.question: An application created before version 4.1.0 needs to move from monthly to weekly. What does the guide say?

options.A: Rebuild it as a new application that uses a Custom weekly Time Dimension
options.B: Change the Time Dimension Type in Application Properties and reprocess
options.C: Load a new Time Dimension XML with System Load/Extract
options.D: Convert it with the Database Configuration Utility, with Support's help

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide notes 'Applications created prior to 4.1.0 can convert a monthly application to weekly application using the Database Configuration Utility. Contact Support for assistance'. A is incorrect — the guide describes converting it. B is incorrect — the guide names the Database Configuration Utility. C is incorrect — Time Dimension is not one of the System Load/Extract items.

questions.subtopic: Managing the Environment — IIS Idle Time-Out
questions.question: What does the guide recommend for the IIS Idle Time-Out on the OneStreamAppAppPool?

options.A: Set it to 20 minutes to match User Inactivity Timeout
options.B: Set it to 1440 minutes so the pool recycles daily
options.C: Leave the IIS default so idle servers free memory
options.D: Set it to 0, because OneStream has its own settings to recycle IIS

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says this setting should be 0 since OneStream has other settings to recycle IIS. A is incorrect — the guide says 0. B is incorrect — daily recycling is handled by OneStream's recycling settings; Idle Time-Out should be 0. C is incorrect — the guide says 0.

questions.question: A large environment needs to apply maintenance without shutting down the whole application. Current tasks should finish while new requests wait. Which tool does the guide name?

options.A: Auto Recycle Max Pause Time
options.B: Setting all users' Is Enabled to False
options.C: The Process Blocker OneStream Solution
options.D: Setting Logon Inactivity Threshold to -1

questions.explanation: C is correct: Process Blocker pauses critical processes for maintenance without shutting down the application, letting current tasks finish while new requests are queued. A is incorrect — this controls pause before an automatic recycle, not maintenance windows. B is incorrect — this blocks logins and does not queue requests. D is incorrect — this only disables the inactivity threshold.

questions.question: An administrator wants to check user logon status data behind the inactivity feature in the System database. Which table does the guide point to?

options.A: SystemConfig
options.B: TaskActivity
options.C: ErrorLog
options.D: UserLogonStatus

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says to go to System > Database > System Database > Tables, where there is a table named UserLogonStatus. A is incorrect — SystemConfig is where System Database Table audits of configuration are viewed. B is incorrect — Task Activity logs tasks, not logon inactivity status. C is incorrect — the Error Log holds errors, not logon status.

questions.question: A custom business rule writes a message that includes sensitive information to the error log. What does the guide say OneStream does?

options.A: It tries to filter sensitive information, replacing it with [Redacted]
options.B: It blocks the write and raises an exception
options.C: It writes the text as-is; only Use Detailed Error Logging = False hides it
options.D: It encrypts the entry so only Administrators can read it

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says when writing to the error log, OneStream attempts to filter sensitive information and redact it, replacing it with [Redacted], and advises against sensitive information in business rules. B is incorrect — it filters and redacts, it does not block. C is incorrect — the guide describes automatic redaction; Detailed Error Logging controls stack traces. D is incorrect — encryption is not what is described.

questions.question: Which platform engine controls data confirmation and certification processes?

options.A: Workflow Engine
options.B: Data Quality Engine
options.C: Finance Engine
options.D: Data Management Engine

questions.explanation: B is correct: the guide says the Data Quality Engine controls data confirmation and certification; its Certification Engine manages user certifications and Workflow dependents' status. A is incorrect — the Workflow Engine controls and tracks business process status. C is incorrect — the Finance Engine works with the Data Quality Engine to run Confirmation Rules but does not control the process. D is incorrect — the Data Management Engine provides task automation through sequences and steps.

questions.question: An administrator opens System > Administration > System Configuration but cannot change any setting. Why?

options.A: SystemConfigurationPage defaults to Nobody, so administrators see the page only through ApplicationServersPage
options.B: ManageSystemConfiguration defaults to Nobody and is not automatically granted to Administrator; SystemConfigurationPage only gives read-only access
options.C: System Configuration is always read-only; changes must be made in the Server Configuration Utility
options.D: The Administrators group must also be given ManageSystemSecurityRoles

questions.explanation: B is correct: The guide says ManageSystemConfiguration defaults to Nobody and is not granted automatically, while SystemConfigurationPage defaults to the Administrator group with read-only rights. A is incorrect — SystemConfigurationPage defaults to the Administrator group. C is incorrect — users with ManageSystemConfiguration can change settings in the app. D is incorrect — the role needed to edit is ManageSystemConfiguration.

questions.question: Which statement about application server configurations made in the application is correct?

options.A: Customer Support can disable full features, sections and property changes through XML/App config
options.B: They are disabled by default on install and must be turned on by an administrator
options.C: They need an IIS restart before they take effect
options.D: They are not audited because the configuration file keeps the history

questions.explanation: A is correct: To prevent misuse, the guide says Customer Support can disable full features, sections and property changes through XML/App config. B is incorrect — they are enabled by default on install. C is incorrect — changes are applied automatically every two minutes. D is incorrect — the application keeps an audit trail of changes.

questions.question: An administrator changes the Logon Inactivity Threshold once through the Server Configuration Utility and later through System > Administration > System Configuration. What is needed for each change to take effect?

options.A: The configuration-file change needs an IIS reset; the System Configuration change is applied automatically within about two minutes
options.B: Both changes need an IIS reset
options.C: Neither change needs anything; both apply immediately on Save
options.D: The System Configuration change needs an IIS reset; the file change applies within two minutes

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide says to reset IIS after saving the configuration file, while System Configuration changes are applied automatically every two minutes with no IIS restart. B is incorrect — System Configuration changes do not need an IIS restart. C is incorrect — the file change needs an IIS reset, and System Configuration changes apply on a two-minute cycle. D is incorrect — this reverses the two behaviors.

questions.question: Which two System Configuration categories must be enabled by OneStream Support before customers can use them?

options.A: Recycling and Database Server Connections
options.B: General and Environment
options.C: Environment and Recycling
options.D: Memory and Multithreading

questions.explanation: D is correct: The note says Memory and Multithreading must be enabled, and customers should contact support for this. A is incorrect — these are available categories with no support-enable note. B is incorrect — these are available categories with no support-enable note. C is incorrect — these are available categories with no support-enable note.

questions.subtopic: System Configuration — Overriding the Config File
questions.question: On General System Configurations, a property's box is selected and the value is greyed out. What does that mean, and how is a custom value set?

options.A: The property is locked by Customer Support and cannot be changed
options.B: The property needs an IIS restart before it can be changed
options.C: The value comes from the configuration file; clear the box, enter the custom value and save to override it
options.D: The value is a custom override; select the box again to edit it

questions.explanation: C is correct: When the box and setting are greyed out the value comes from the configuration file; clearing the box lets you override it, and selecting it again goes back to the file. A is incorrect — greyed out means the file value is used; clearing the box allows an override. B is incorrect — System Configuration changes need no IIS restart. D is incorrect — this reverses the meaning: a selected box means the configuration file value.

questions.question: What does Use Detailed Error Logging control?

options.A: Whether slow formulas are written to the error log
options.B: Whether GetDataCells calls are logged
options.C: Whether stack trace information is shown
options.D: Whether Cube View openings are written to Task Activity

questions.explanation: C is correct: When True, stack trace information is shown; when False, it is not. A is incorrect — this is Num Seconds Before Logging Slow Formulas. B is incorrect — this is Log Get Data Cells Threshold. D is incorrect — this is Log Cube Views.

questions.question: An administrator wants idle sessions to time out after 45 minutes. Which setting should be changed?

options.A: Logon Inactivity Threshold (days)
options.B: User Inactivity Timeout (minutes)
options.C: Task Inactivity Timeout (minutes)
options.D: Auto Recycle Max Pause Time (minutes)

questions.explanation: B is correct: This sets the number of minutes after which a user is timed out for inactivity. A is incorrect — this is the number of days without logging in before a user is disabled. C is incorrect — this times out tasks, not user sessions. D is incorrect — this controls how long a server waits for tasks before recycling.

questions.question: In General System Configurations, what value turns off the Logon Inactivity Threshold (days)?

options.B: Blank

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says to set Logon Inactivity Threshold (days) to -1 to disable the setting. A is incorrect — 0 does not disable it; a Remaining Allowed Inactivity of 0 days means a user no longer has access. B is incorrect — the guide names -1, not an empty value. C is incorrect — a large number only lengthens the threshold; it does not disable it.

questions.subtopic: General Configuration — White List File Extensions
questions.question: White List File Extensions is blank in General System Configurations. What is the effect?

options.A: Any file type can be saved to a root folder and uploaded
options.B: No files can be uploaded to File Explorer until types are added
options.C: Only default Office and PDF types can be uploaded
options.D: Only administrators can upload files

questions.explanation: A is correct: When blank, any file type can be saved to a root folder and uploaded; adding types restricts what File Explorer supports. B is incorrect — blank means no restriction. C is incorrect — blank means any type. D is incorrect — the setting controls file types, not who can upload.

questions.question: What does the guide warn about Num Seconds Before Logging Slow Formulas?

options.A: It works only on servers that have Multithreading enabled
options.B: It writes to Task Activity instead of the Error Log, so it has no performance cost
options.C: Its default of 180 seconds should be raised only for debugging
options.D: It turns on formula logging and affects consolidation performance, so disable it when no longer needed

questions.explanation: D is correct: The guide says the setting enables logging of formulas, affects consolidation performance, and should be disabled when no longer required. A is incorrect — no such dependency is stated. B is incorrect — the guide warns about a consolidation performance impact. C is incorrect — the 180-second default applies to Number Seconds Before Logging Get Data Cells.

questions.subtopic: General Configuration — Get Data Cells Default
questions.question: What is the default for Number Seconds Before Logging Get Data Cells, and when should it be raised?

options.A: 20; raise it when Cube Views page too often
options.B: 30; raise it during month-end close
options.C: 2000; raise it for large Excel retrieves
options.D: 180; raise it only for debugging

questions.explanation: D is correct: The default is 180 and it should only be increased for debugging. A is incorrect — 20 is the default for Max Number Seconds To Process Cube View. B is incorrect — 30 is the default for Auto Recycle Max Pause Time. C is incorrect — 2000 is the default for Max Number of Unsuppressed Row Per Cube View Page.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity Configuration — Defaults and Triggers
questions.question: Which Task Activity setting is True by default?

options.A: Log Cube Views
options.B: Log Books
options.C: Log Quick Views
options.D: Use Detailed Error Logging

questions.explanation: B is correct: Log Books is set to True by default. A is incorrect — the guide does not say this defaults to True; it logs Cube View opens, report runs and Excel exports in the data explorer. C is incorrect — the guide does not say this defaults to True; it logs Quick View creation and row/column moves. D is incorrect — this is a General Menu setting for stack traces, not a Task Activity setting.

questions.question: To study analysis performance, an administrator wants Task Activity entries when users create Quick Views or move rows and columns. Which setting should be True?

options.A: Log Quick Views
options.B: Log Cube Views
options.C: Log Books
options.D: Log Get Data Cells Threshold

questions.explanation: A is correct: It logs to Task Activity when a Quick View is created or rows and columns are moved. B is incorrect — this logs Cube View opens, report runs and Excel exports in the data explorer. C is incorrect — this logs Book items included as Task Activity steps. D is incorrect — this logs large GetDataCells calls.

questions.question: An administrator wants a Task Activity entry each time a Cube View is opened, a report is run, or it is exported to Excel from the Data Explorer, to analyze performance. Which setting should be True?

options.A: Log Quick Views
options.B: Log Books
options.C: Use Detailed Error Logging
options.D: Log Cube Views

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide says when Log Cube Views is True, a log is created in Task Activity when a Cube View is opened, a report is run or an export to Excel is completed in the Data Explorer, to analyze performance. A is incorrect — Log Quick Views logs Quick View creation and row/column moves. B is incorrect — Log Books (default True) logs book items as Task Activity steps. C is incorrect — that controls stack traces in errors.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity Configuration — Get Data Cells Threshold
questions.question: An administrator sets Log Get Data Cells Threshold to 50,000. What is logged?

options.A: Any Get Data Cells call that runs longer than 50,000 milliseconds
options.B: Cube Views that return more than 50,000 unsuppressed rows
options.C: Calls to GetDataCells and GetDataCellsUsingScript requesting 50,000 or more cells, with context such as the Excel file or Cube View name
options.D: Calls requesting fewer than 50,000 cells, to find many small calls

questions.explanation: C is correct: The setting logs GetDataCells and GetDataCellsUsingScript calls with context such as the Excel file or Cube View name, only when the number of cells requested is equal to or greater than the value. A is incorrect — the threshold counts data cells, not time. B is incorrect — this is the cell count of GetDataCells calls, not Cube View rows. D is incorrect — logging happens when the count is equal to or greater than the value.

questions.subtopic: Cube Views Configuration — Limits and Override
questions.question: Which statement about the Cube Views menu in System Configuration is correct?

options.A: Max Number of Unsuppressed Row Per Cube View Page defaults to 2000 with a maximum of 100,000, and one Cube View can override it in its General Settings/Common/Paging properties
options.B: Max Number Seconds To Process Cube View defaults to 20 with a maximum of 6000 seconds
options.C: The settings apply only to Cube Views created after the change
options.D: Individual Cube Views cannot override these settings

questions.explanation: A is correct: The guide gives a default of 2000 and maximum of 100,000, and says these settings can be overridden through each Cube View's General Settings/Common/Paging properties. B is incorrect — the maximum is 600 seconds. C is incorrect — they affect all Cube Views in the environment. D is incorrect — they can be overridden with each Cube View's paging properties.

questions.question: An administrator wants the production environment clearly labeled and a planned-outage notice that users can dismiss. Which settings are used?

options.A: Environment Name for the label, and Logon Agreement Message for the notice
options.B: Environment Name and Environment Color for the label, and Full Width Banner Message with Can Close Full Banner set to True
options.C: Environment Color for the label, and Full Width Banner Message with Can Close Full Banner set to False
options.D: Full Banner Display Type for the label, and Environment Name for the notice

questions.explanation: B is correct: Environment Name (up to 150 characters) and Environment Color set the label; Can Close Full Banner set to True lets the banner be dismissed after logon. A is incorrect — Logon Agreement Message is for a logon agreement, not a dismissible banner. C is incorrect — False means the banner cannot be dismissed. D is incorrect — this mixes up what the settings do.

questions.question: Compliance wants every user to see an acceptable-use message after logging on. Which setup does the guide describe?

options.A: Enter the text in Full Width Banner Message and set Can Close Full Banner to False
options.B: Enter the text in Environment Name, which allows up to 150 characters
options.C: Set Full Banner Display Type to Critical
options.D: Set Logon Agreement Type to Custom and enter the text in Logon Agreement Message

questions.explanation: D is correct: To show a message after logon, select Custom for Logon Agreement Type and enter the text. A is incorrect — this is a banner across the top, not a logon agreement. B is incorrect — Environment Name is the label shown for the environment. C is incorrect — this sets the banner's severity, not a logon agreement.

questions.question: Which is NOT an option for Full Banner Display Type?

options.A: Informational
options.B: Warning
options.C: Error
options.D: Critical

questions.explanation: C is correct: The options are Informational, Warning, Successful and Critical; Error is not one of them. A is incorrect — Informational is a listed option. B is incorrect — Warning is a listed option. D is incorrect — Critical is a listed option.

questions.question: With default Recycling settings, when may an application server recycle automatically?

options.A: Once every 24 running hours, between 05:00 and 07:00 server local time
options.B: Once every 24 running hours, between 05:00 and 07:00 UTC
options.C: Every 12 running hours, at any time
options.D: Only when an administrator recycles it from System > Tools > Environment
