questions.explanation: B is correct: Auto Recycle Num Running Hours defaults to 24, Start Hour UTC to 5 and End Hour UTC to 7. A is incorrect — the start and end hours are in UTC. C is incorrect — the default is 24 hours within a set window. D is incorrect — automatic recycling is on by default.

questions.question: Auto Recycle Max Pause Time is at its default. A server reaches its recycle time while two long consolidations are running. What happens?

options.A: The server stops accepting new tasks and lets running tasks continue for up to 30 minutes before recycling
options.B: The server waits for the consolidations to finish no matter how long they take
options.C: The server recycles at once and the consolidations are re-queued
options.D: The recycle is skipped until the next day's window

questions.explanation: A is correct: With the default of 30, the server pauses new tasks and lets current tasks run for 30 minutes before recycling; with no active tasks it recycles right away. B is incorrect — the wait is capped by Max Pause Time. C is incorrect — it first pauses and allows up to 30 minutes. D is incorrect — the server pauses and recycles after the pause time.

questions.question: Under Database Server Connections, which menu configures Connection, Security and Timeouts but NOT Database settings?

options.A: External
options.B: Custom
options.C: Environment
options.D: Internal

questions.explanation: D is correct: The Internal menu configures Connection, Security and Timeouts, while External and Custom also include Database. A is incorrect — External includes Database settings. B is incorrect — Custom includes Database settings. C is incorrect — Environment is a separate System Configuration category, not a Database Server Connections menu.

questions.question: An administrator edits a Custom connection string whose password shows as ? and saves without retyping it. What happens to the password?

options.A: The password is replaced with a literal ?
options.B: The save fails until the password is entered again
options.C: The original password is kept; saving with ? does not overwrite it
options.D: The password is cleared and the connection falls back to Windows authentication

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says a connection string can be changed without changing the password and saved with ? without overriding the original. A is incorrect — saving with ? does not override the original password. B is incorrect — saving without changing the password is allowed. D is incorrect — the original password is kept.

questions.subtopic: Database Server Connections — Moving External Connections
questions.question: Existing External database connections are being moved to Custom connections. What does the guide advise?

options.A: Give them new names so the audit trail can tell them apart
options.B: Delete the External connection first and reset IIS before creating the Custom one
options.C: Keep the previous connection name so Task Scheduler jobs, business rules and other references keep working
options.D: Move them to the Internal menu, which also supports Database settings

questions.explanation: C is correct: The guide says pre-existing External connections moved to Custom connections should use the previous name to avoid breaking connections with Task Scheduler, Business Rules and so on. A is incorrect — renaming would break references. B is incorrect — the guide does not say this, and changes apply without an IIS restart. D is incorrect — the Internal menu does not include Database settings.

questions.question: Where does the guide say System Database Table audits for configuration are viewed?

options.A: System > Tools > Database > SystemConfig
options.B: System > System Configuration > Audit
options.C: System > Tools > Environment > Application Server Sets
options.D: System > Logging > Error Log

questions.explanation: A is correct: System Database Tables audits are viewed at System > Tools > Database > SystemConfig. B is incorrect — this shows configuration setting changes in the Audit tab. C is incorrect — this shows the settings servers are using. D is incorrect — the Error Log records errors.

questions.question: An administrator wants to see the settings an application server is actually using, with a Last Updated column. Where is this?

options.A: System > System Configuration > Audit
options.B: System > Tools > Environment > Application Server Sets
options.C: System > Tools > Database > SystemConfig
options.D: System > Logging > Task Activity

questions.explanation: B is correct: Environment audits under Environment > Application Server Sets show the settings the server is using, updated every 2 minutes, with a Last Updated column. A is incorrect — this tracks configuration changes, not the values the server is using. C is incorrect — this is where System Database Table audits are viewed. D is incorrect — Task Activity tracks tasks, not server configuration values.

questions.question: An auditor asks for a file of the current Logon Activity grid. How does an administrator export the grid contents?

options.A: Right-click in the grid, select Export, then choose an export file type
options.B: Use System > Tools > Load/Extract and extract the Logon Activity item
options.C: Click the filter icon and select Export to Excel
options.D: Use the paging buttons at the bottom left of the grid and select Save

questions.explanation: A is correct: every logging grid can be exported by right-clicking, selecting Export and then an export file type. B is incorrect — the guide describes exporting directly from the logging grid by right-click; Load/Extract is not the described method for this grid. C is incorrect — the filter icon filters by criteria; it does not export. D is incorrect — the bottom-left buttons navigate pages; they do not export.

questions.question: A security reviewer wants to know which logged-on sessions came from the Excel Add-In versus another client. Which Logon Activity column answers this?

options.A: Client Version
options.B: Client Module
options.C: Application
options.D: Primary App Server

questions.explanation: B is correct: Client Module 'will display items such as Excel'. A is incorrect — Client Version shows the version of the application being used, not the client type. C is incorrect — Application shows which OneStream application the user is logged into. D is incorrect — Primary App Server shows the application server the user is utilizing.

questions.question: An administrator wants to find users who logged on hours ago but have not done anything since, before deciding whose sessions to log off. Which Logon Activity column is most useful?

options.A: Logon Time
options.B: Logoff Time
options.C: Last Activity Time
options.D: Logon Status

questions.explanation: C is correct: Last Activity Time is 'a time stamp of the user's last activity'. A is incorrect — Logon Time only records when the user logged in, not later activity. B is incorrect — Logoff Time records when the user logged off, which an idle open session will not have. D is incorrect — Logon Status shows when users logged on and off, not their most recent activity.

questions.question: In System > Logging > Logon Activity, what does the Clear Logon Activity button do?

options.A: Clears logon activity for the current user only
options.B: Logs off every active session
options.C: Clears only sessions with a Logoff Time
options.D: Clears all logon activity

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide states Clear Logon Activity 'clears all logon activity'. A is incorrect — unlike Task Activity and Error Logs, Logon Activity has a single clear button that clears all logon activity. B is incorrect — logging off is done with Logoff Selected Session, one session at a time. C is incorrect — the guide does not limit the clear to logged-off sessions; it clears all logon activity.

questions.question: During an incident, an administrator suspects one application server is unhealthy and wants to see which logged-on users are being served by it. Which logging grid and column show this?

options.A: Error Log — Tier
options.B: Logon Activity — Primary App Server
options.C: Logon Activity — Client IP Address
options.D: Task Activity — Description

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Logon Activity grid includes Primary App Server, which 'shows the application server the end user is utilizing'. A is incorrect — Tier shows App Server, Web Server or Client for an error, not which server a logged-on user uses. C is incorrect — Client IP Address shows the end user's IP address, not the application server. D is incorrect — Description shows task details such as the POV, not user-to-server assignment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way described in the guide to open Task Activity in the web/Windows client?

options.A: The Task Activity icon at the top right of the client
options.B: System > Logging > Task Activity
options.C: Application > Tools > Task Activity
options.D: The Task Activity icon in the Cube View connection dialog box

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide lists only two ways: click Task Activity at the top right of the client, or select System > Logging > Task Activity; there is no Application > Tools > Task Activity path. A is incorrect — this is one of the two documented access points. B is incorrect — this is one of the two documented access points. D is incorrect — the guide states this icon is featured in the Cube View connection dialog in both the Excel Add-In and the Windows Application.

questions.question: An administrator clicks 'Clear task activity for all users' in Task Activity. What is the result?

options.A: Only completed tasks are cleared for all users; running tasks are kept
options.B: Only the administrator's own task activity is cleared
options.C: Task activity is archived to the Error Log
options.D: All task activity is cleared for ALL users

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide states this button 'clears all activity for ALL users'. A is incorrect — the guide does not limit the clear to completed tasks. B is incorrect — that is 'Clear task activity for current user'. C is incorrect — clearing removes activity; nothing is described as moving to the Error Log.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity — Task Type vs Description
questions.question: In the Task Activity grid, which column would show values such as Consolidate, Process Cube, Load and Transform, or Clear Stage Data?

options.A: Task Type
options.B: Description
options.C: Task Status
options.D: Server

questions.explanation: A is correct: Task Type 'shows the user's activity (e.g., Consolidate, Process Cube, Load and Transform, Clear Stage Data, etc.)'. B is incorrect — Description shows details of the activity, such as the POV or Multiple Data Units. C is incorrect — Task Status shows Completed, Failed, Canceling, Canceled, Running and so on. D is incorrect — Server shows the application server used.

questions.question: A user wants to confirm which POV a consolidation in Task Activity was run for. Which column shows this?

options.A: Task Type
options.B: Application
options.C: Description
options.D: Start CPU

questions.explanation: C is correct: Description 'shows the details of the activity (e.g., the POV, Multiple Data Units, etc.)'. A is incorrect — Task Type shows the kind of activity, such as Consolidate. B is incorrect — Application shows which application the task was processed against. D is incorrect — Start CPU shows % CPU utilization when the job began from the queue.

questions.question: A user cancels a long-running task. Which sequence of Task Status values does the guide describe?

options.A: Running, then Failed
options.B: Stopping, then Stopped
options.C: Paused, then Canceled
options.D: Canceling, then Canceled

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Canceling the task will transition it from Canceling to Canceled'. A is incorrect — a canceled task is not shown as Failed. B is incorrect — these are not the Task Status values the guide uses for cancellation. C is incorrect — Paused is not a Task Status value; Pause is an application server action on the Environment page.

questions.question: A Task Activity row has two highlighted icons on its left side. What does the SECOND icon open?

options.A: Detailed information about the error, when one is present
options.B: The child steps within the task
options.C: The Running Task Progress dialog
options.D: The Logon Activity record for the user who ran the task

questions.explanation: A is correct: the first icon shows child steps within the task; 'the second shows detailed information of the error when present'. B is incorrect — child steps are the first icon. C is incorrect — Running Task Progress is a separate button, not one of the two left-side drill-down icons. D is incorrect — the icons do not link to Logon Activity.

questions.subtopic: Task Progress Dialog — Close vs Cancel Task
questions.question: A user opens Running Task Progress for a long cube view and clicks Close in the Task Progress dialog. What happens?

options.A: The task is cancelled and shows Canceled
options.B: Only the Task Progress dialog closes; the task keeps running
options.C: The task is paused until the dialog is reopened
options.D: The task moves to Canceling and the report opens empty

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'The Close button does not cancel or close the actual task; it only closes the Task Progress dialog box for that specific task'. A is incorrect — only Cancel Task cancels the task. C is incorrect — tasks are not paused by closing the dialog. D is incorrect — Close does not start a cancellation.

questions.subtopic: Task Activity — Admin vs Non-Admin Filters
questions.question: Which Task Activity option is available to Administrators but NOT to non-admin users?

options.A: Show running tasks only
options.B: Running Task Progress to cancel their own task
options.C: Show tasks for all users
options.D: Refresh

questions.explanation: C is correct: Administrators can show tasks for all users and show running tasks only; 'Non-admins have the option to show running tasks only'. A is incorrect — non-admins also have this option. B is incorrect — users can cancel their own tasks. D is incorrect — Refresh is a general Task Activity button, not admin-only.

questions.question: After a cube view is cancelled, a manager wants to know whether the user or an administrator cancelled it. Where is this shown?

options.A: The Task Status column in Task Activity
options.B: The Error Level column in the Error Log
options.C: The Logon Status column in Logon Activity
options.D: The Description column in Task Activity

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'the Task Status column will display whether the task was canceled by a User or Administrator'. B is incorrect — Error Level shows error types such as Fatal or Warning. C is incorrect — Logon Status shows logon/logoff times. D is incorrect — Description shows details such as POV, not who cancelled.

questions.question: Before this enhancement, a runaway cube view often required an IIS reset. What does the guide say users and administrators can now do instead?

options.A: Recycle the App Pool from the Environment page
options.B: Pause the Web To App Server connection
options.C: Clear the error log for the current user
options.D: Track the cube view's progress and cancel it in Task Activity

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'a User or Administrator can track cube view progress and cancel a long-running cube view instead of resetting IIS'. A is incorrect — Recycle App Pool resets IIS, which is what this feature avoids. B is incorrect — pausing a connection stops requests to a server; it does not cancel one cube view. C is incorrect — clearing logs does not stop running work.

questions.question: A user starts a consolidation (a non-UI task). What does the guide say the Task Activity icon will do?

options.A: Show a pop-up progress dialog after 10 seconds
options.B: Start blinking within a few minutes
options.C: Blink only if Use Detailed Logging is True
options.D: Not change; consolidations appear only in System > Logging

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'For all non-UI tasks, such as consolidation or other long-running tasks, the task activity icon will start blinking within a few minutes'. A is incorrect — the 10-second pop-up applies to UI tasks such as running a cube view, Show Report or Export to Excel. C is incorrect — blinking is not tied to detailed logging. D is incorrect — the icon blinks for long-running non-UI tasks.

questions.question: When a user runs a cube view in Data Explorer, how long must it run before a dialog with an indeterminate progress bar and Cancel Task/Close buttons appears?

options.A: Longer than 30 seconds
options.B: Longer than 60 seconds
options.C: Longer than 10 seconds
options.D: Longer than a few minutes

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'if it takes longer than 10 seconds in the OneStream application, a dialog box will display an indeterminate progress bar'. A is incorrect — the threshold is 10 seconds. B is incorrect — the threshold is 10 seconds. D is incorrect — a few minutes is when the icon blinks for non-UI tasks such as consolidation.

questions.question: A cube view runs past the threshold and the progress dialog appears. The user clicks Close. What happens?

options.A: A canceling message displays and the report does not run
options.B: The cube view is cancelled and must be re-run
options.C: The dialog closes and the report is discarded; results must be viewed in Task Activity
options.D: The dialog closes, Task Activity blinks to show a background task, and the report opens when complete

questions.explanation: D is correct: if you click Close, 'the dialog box will close, the Task Activity will blink ... and the report will open when completed'. A is incorrect — that is the Cancel Task button. B is incorrect — Close does not cancel. C is incorrect — the report still opens when complete.

questions.question: A cube view has been running for 30 seconds but the Task Activity icon is not blinking. According to the guide, which is a valid reason?

options.A: A Task Activity dialog box is already open
options.B: Use Detailed Logging is set to False
options.C: The user is not an Administrator
options.D: The cube view uses paging

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'The Task Activity icon will not blink if a task activity dialog box is open'. B is incorrect — blinking is not controlled by Use Detailed Logging. C is incorrect — blinking is not role-dependent. D is incorrect — paging is not a reason for the icon not blinking.

questions.question: A user runs Export to Excel on a large cube view, waits past 10 seconds, and clicks Cancel Task in the dialog. What is the result?

options.A: Excel launches with a partial export
options.B: Excel launches with #REFRESH in the cells
options.C: A canceling message displays and Excel does not launch
options.D: The export continues in the background and Task Activity blinks

questions.explanation: C is correct: for Export to Excel, 'If you select Cancel Task, a canceling message displays and Excel will not launch'. A is incorrect — Excel does not launch. B is incorrect — #REFRESH appears when cancelling a Next Page load in cube view/quick view paging. D is incorrect — that is the Close button.

questions.subtopic: Dashboard with Cube View Components — Cancel
questions.question: A dashboard with several cube view components takes over a minute to load. How does a user cancel one of the cube views?

options.A: Use the 10-second pop-up dialog's Cancel Task button
options.B: Close the dashboard; that cancels all cube view components
options.C: Only an Administrator can cancel dashboard cube views
options.D: No pop-up appears; the user opens Task Activity and uses Running Task Progress to cancel each cube view

questions.explanation: D is correct: for dashboards 'you will not see a pop-up dialog box. You must click Task Activity to review all cube views' and cancel each with Running Task Progress. A is incorrect — dashboards with cube view components do not show the pop-up. B is incorrect — the guide does not describe closing the dashboard as cancelling. C is incorrect — users can cancel through Running Task Progress.

questions.subtopic: Dashboard with Cube View Components — Verify Cancel
questions.question: After cancelling a cube view component on a dashboard, how can the user confirm the cancellation worked?

options.A: A message displays that it cannot open the cube view
options.B: The cube view cells show #REFRESH
options.C: The component shows the Error Level Warning
options.D: The dashboard reloads with the last cached data

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'To verify if a cube view has been canceled, a message displays that it cannot open the cube view'. B is incorrect — #REFRESH applies to cancelling a Next Page load in paging. C is incorrect — no such indicator is described. D is incorrect — no cached reload is described.

questions.subtopic: Cube View — Use Detailed Logging Location
questions.question: An administrator wants richer Task Activity information (individual steps, data cells) for one slow cube view. Where is this turned on?

options.A: TALogCubeViews in the Task Activity section of the Application Server Configuration file
options.B: Use Detailed Logging on the cube view itself (Designer or Advanced tab, General Settings > Common)
options.C: Detailed Logging in the Task Load Balancing section of the Environment settings
options.D: Detailed Logging in Environment Monitoring

questions.explanation: B is correct: Use Detailed Logging was removed from the App Server Config file (TALogCubeViews in the Task Activity section) and added to individual cube views, on both the Designer and Advanced tabs. A is incorrect — the guide says this was removed and moved to individual cube views. C is incorrect — that setting logs entering/exiting the Task Load Balancing function, not cube view details. D is incorrect — that setting logs entering/exiting metric collection and the Active System check.

questions.subtopic: Cube View — Use Detailed Logging Default
questions.question: What is the default value of Use Detailed Logging on a cube view, and what does setting it True provide?

options.A: True; when False, the cube view is excluded from Task Activity
options.B: False; when True, errors are written to the Error Log with Tier = Client
options.C: True; it can only be turned off in the Application Server Configuration file
options.D: False; when True, Task Activity shows individual steps and additional information about the cube view

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'For Use Detailed Logging, the default is set to False' and 'When set to True, detailed logging will provide information in Task Activity, such as individual steps and additional information about the cube view'. A is incorrect — the default is False and cube views still appear in Task Activity. B is incorrect — the benefit is more detail in Task Activity, not Error Log entries. C is incorrect — the default is False and the setting is on the cube view.

questions.question: Which pair of clear buttons is available in the Error Log?

options.A: Clear error log by Tier, and Clear error log by Error Level
options.B: Clear errors older than 30 days, and Clear all errors
options.C: A single Clear Error Log button that clears all users
options.D: Clear error log for current user, and Clear error log for all users

questions.explanation: D is correct: the guide lists 'Clear error log for current user' and 'Clear error log for all users'. A is incorrect — no such buttons are described. B is incorrect — no age-based clear is described. C is incorrect — a single all-users clear describes Logon Activity, not Error Logs.

questions.question: A user reports intermittent errors. In System > Logging > Error Logs, which column shows which application server the user was connected to when the error occurred?

options.A: Tier
options.B: Application
options.C: App Server
options.D: Error Level

questions.explanation: C is correct: App Server 'identifies the application server to which a user was connected when they encountered an error'. A is incorrect — Tier shows App Server, Web Server or Client, not the specific server name. B is incorrect — Application identifies the application the user was logged onto. D is incorrect — Error Level shows the error type, such as Unknown, Fatal or Warning.

questions.question: A consultant tries to open System > Tools > Environment from a browser session and cannot find it. Why?

options.A: The Environment page requires the Excel Add-In
options.B: The Environment page is only on the application server console
options.C: The Environment page is only available in Azure-hosted environments
options.D: The Environment page is only accessible from the OneStream Windows App

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'The Environment page is only accessible via the OneStream Windows App'. A is incorrect — it is a Windows App page. B is incorrect — it is in the Windows App under System > Tools. C is incorrect — it is in all environments, with some settings applying only to Azure.

questions.question: The Environment page checks connection status and configuration for several component types. Which is NOT one of them?

options.A: File Share servers
options.B: Mobile Web Servers
options.C: Application Server Sets
options.D: Database Servers

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide lists Web Servers, Mobile Web Servers, Application Server Sets and Database Servers. B is incorrect — this is listed. C is incorrect — this is listed. D is incorrect — this is listed.

questions.question: Which task can be done on the Environment page?

options.A: Edit users, security groups and system role assignments
options.B: Turn on Use Detailed Logging for all cube views at once
options.C: Monitor servers, isolate bottlenecks and replay performance data
options.D: Define the Time Dimension Type and calendar for a new application

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says users can 'monitor the environment, isolate bottlenecks… save collection metrics files, and replay collected performance data'. A is incorrect — this is done under System > Security. B is incorrect — this is set on each individual cube view. D is incorrect — this is done under Time Dimensions.

questions.question: In System > Tools > Environment > Monitoring > Settings, which is NOT one of the KPI metric types you can choose to monitor?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Web Servers
options.C: Database Servers
options.D: Server Sets

questions.explanation: B is correct: the KPI metric types listed are Environment, Application Servers, Database Servers and Server Sets; Web Servers is not listed. A is incorrect — this is listed. C is incorrect — this is listed. D is incorrect — this is listed.

questions.question: A support analyst wants to save collected performance metrics and replay them later. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Metrics can only be exported as a CSV from the grid
options.B: Metrics can only be saved to the application server's local disk
options.C: Save As stores metrics and configurations locally or in the File System, and Open reloads them from either
options.D: Saved metrics files can be opened only on the same server

questions.explanation: C is correct: Open accesses 'a metrics and configuration setting file from the File System or a local folder' and Save As saves 'locally or in the File System'. A is incorrect — the Monitoring page has Open and Save As. B is incorrect — they can be saved locally or in the File System. D is incorrect — no such restriction is described.

questions.question: An administrator turns on 'Refresh Automatically Using a Timer' on the Monitoring page. Which setting controls how often the charts update?

options.A: General Play Update Frequency (seconds)
options.B: Metric Update Interval (seconds)
options.C: Server Heartbeat Update Interval (seconds)
options.D: Metric and Task Time Range

questions.explanation: A is correct: the timer retrieves metrics 'based on the Play Update Frequency interval setting', which sets how often Performance charts update. B is incorrect — that is in the Application Server Configuration and controls how often metrics are collected. C is incorrect — that controls how often a server records that it is alive. D is incorrect — that sets how much history to retrieve, not refresh frequency.

questions.subtopic: Environment Monitoring — Time Range and Y-Axis
questions.question: On the Monitoring Performance chart, one series is in the thousands and another is a percentage. Which General setting is meant for this?

options.A: Y-Axis Auto Range
options.B: Secondary Y-Axis
options.C: Metric and Task Time Range
options.D: Source Filter

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Secondary Y-Axis 'can be used when the numbers in a chart vary widely from data series to data series, or when there are mixed types of data'. A is incorrect — Auto Range lets the system set Min/Max on the single Y-axis. C is incorrect — that controls how much historical data is retrieved. D is incorrect — Source Filter filters the server Source List.

questions.question: An administrator is looking into a server problem that happened yesterday afternoon and wants the Performance chart to show that period. Which setting should be changed?

options.A: Metric and Task Time Range
options.B: General Play Update Frequency
options.C: Secondary Y-Axis
options.D: Source Filter

questions.explanation: A is correct: the guide says it shows 'how much historical data to retrieve and depict on the Performance Chart' and 'can help identify the cause of a server event or issue'. B is incorrect — it controls how often the charts update. C is incorrect — it is used to show series with very different value ranges. D is incorrect — it filters the list of servers.

questions.question: Where is the interval that drives how often environment metrics are COLLECTED set?

options.A: General Play Update Frequency on the Monitoring page
options.B: Server Heartbeat Update Interval in the web configuration file
options.C: Metric Update Interval (seconds) in the Application Server Configuration utility
options.D: Maximum Queued Processing Interval in Task Load Balancing

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Metrics are collected based on the Metric Update Interval (seconds) setting in the Application Server Configuration utility'; some metrics skip iterations based on their count settings. A is incorrect — that controls chart refresh, not collection. B is incorrect — heartbeat records that a server is alive. D is incorrect — that controls how often the queuing thread checks for tasks.

questions.question: What does the Server Heartbeat Update Interval (seconds) setting control?

options.A: How often web servers retry a failed WCF connection
options.B: How often app servers are automatically recycled
options.C: How long offline servers stay in the heartbeat table
options.D: How often each server updates its record that it is alive and responding

questions.explanation: D is correct: it specifies 'how often each server updates its record that it is alive and responding to user input'. A is incorrect — no retry interval is described. B is incorrect — that is Number of Running Hours Before Automatic Recycle. C is incorrect — that is Number Hours To Retain Offline Servers.

questions.question: On the Environment page, a web server shows 'Used for Stage Load = True'. What is this value based on?

options.A: The Process Queued Stage Tasks setting on the Server Set
options.B: The web configuration file, which configures this server as a Stage server
options.C: Whether a Stage task is currently running on the server
options.D: The Tier column in the Error Log

questions.explanation: B is correct: Used for Stage Load 'examines the web configuration file to see if this server is configured as a Stage server'. A is incorrect — that is an application server queuing setting, not the web server's Used For value. C is incorrect — it reflects configuration, not current activity. D is incorrect — Tier is an Error Log column.

questions.question: On a Web Server's Audit tab, which column shows the name of the person who made a change?

options.A: User From
options.B: Property Name
options.C: User To
options.D: Description To

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'User To — Displays the user name of the person that made the change if available'. A is incorrect — User From shows the original user name. B is incorrect — Property Name is the name of the property that changed. D is incorrect — Description To shows the new description of the setting.

questions.question: Where does the Mobile Web Servers section of the Environment page pull its information from?

options.A: The XFAppServerConfig.xml file
options.B: The Logon Activity grid
options.C: The application database Data Records
options.D: The ServerHeartBeat table in the Framework database

questions.explanation: D is correct: mobile web servers 'pulls the information from the ServerHeartBeat table in the Framework database'. A is incorrect — that is the application server configuration file whose changes show on the Server Sets Audit tab. B is incorrect — Logon Activity tracks user sessions. C is incorrect — Data Records holds application data.

questions.subtopic: Web To App Server Connections — Pause
questions.question: An administrator wants to temporarily stop a web server sending requests to a load balancer that fronts several application servers. Where is this done?

options.A: Environment > Web To App Server Connections > Pause on that WCF Address connection
options.B: Application Server Sets > Behavior > Recycle App Pool
options.C: Logon Activity > Logoff Selected Session
options.D: Database Servers > Behavior

questions.explanation: A is correct: this section lists connections from web server configuration files to application servers, and 'the user can pause and then resume a specific connection to an application server or a load balancer'. B is incorrect — recycling resets IIS on one app server. C is incorrect — this logs off one user session. D is incorrect — this scales an Azure Elastic Pool.

questions.question: On the Environment page under Application Server Sets, how is an offline server indicated?

options.A: Yellow highlighting
options.B: A blinking icon
options.C: A red X
options.D: WCF Connection = Failed

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'A red "X" indicates offline servers'. A is incorrect — yellow marks changed properties on the Server Sets Audit tab. B is incorrect — blinking describes the Task Activity icon. D is incorrect — WCF Connection is shown for web servers; the guide uses a red X for offline app servers.

questions.subtopic: Server Set Behavior — Manual Scaling Prerequisite
questions.question: On the Server Sets Behavior tab, manual Scale Out/Scale In is available only when Scaling Type in the Server Configuration Utility is set to which values?

options.A: Manual or ManualAndBusinessRule
options.B: BusinessRule only
options.C: Not Used
options.D: Standard

questions.explanation: A is correct: you can scale 'if the Scaling Type setting is set to Manual or ManualAndBusinessRule in the Server Configuration Utility file'. B is incorrect — BusinessRule alone is automatic scaling by rule, not one of the listed values for manual scaling. C is incorrect — Not Used turns scaling off. D is incorrect — Standard is a server set type, not a Scaling Type value.

questions.question: Queuing settings such as Process Queued Consolidation Tasks are defined for a Server Set in the Server Configuration Utility. Can they differ for one server in that set?

options.A: No; all servers in a set must share the same settings
options.B: Yes, but only in Azure Scale Sets
options.C: Yes, but only from the web configuration file
options.D: Yes; they can be overridden at the individual Application Server level

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'You can specify the following settings at the Server Set level using the Server Configuration Utility, but can override them at the individual Application Server level'. A is incorrect — the guide says they can be overridden. B is incorrect — the override is not limited to Azure. C is incorrect — the guide refers to the Server Configuration Utility and individual Application Server level.

questions.question: A dedicated application server should only run tasks specifically assigned to it, not general queued work. Which setting does this?

options.A: Queued Tasks Require Named Application Server = True
options.B: Process Queued Data Management Tasks = False
options.C: Can Change Queuing Options On Servers = True
options.D: Task Logging Only = True

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Queued Tasks Require Named Application Server: If true, the server only runs assigned tasks'. B is incorrect — this only stops the server from picking up Data Management tasks. C is incorrect — this lets administrators change queuing behavior; it does not restrict tasks. D is incorrect — this only logs picked-up tasks.

questions.subtopic: Server Sets — Can Change Queuing Options
questions.question: An administrator wants to change stage, consolidation and data management queuing behavior for specific servers from the Environment page. Which Server Set setting must be True?

options.A: Can Pause or Resume Servers
options.B: Can Change Queuing Options On Servers
options.C: Can Stop or Start Servers
options.D: Queued Tasks Require Named Application Server

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Can Change Queuing Options On Servers: If true, Administrators can change the queuing behavior - impacting stage, consolidation and data management tasks - of specific servers'. A is incorrect — this controls Pause/Resume buttons. C is incorrect — this is Azure Scale Set only and controls stop/restart. D is incorrect — this restricts a server to assigned tasks.

questions.subtopic: Server Sets — Can Pause or Resume
questions.question: The Pause and Resume buttons are missing for application servers on the Environment page. Which Server Set setting controls whether they appear?

options.A: Can Stop or Start Servers
options.B: Can Change Queuing Options On Servers
options.C: Server Set Provider Type
options.D: Can Pause or Resume Servers

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Can Pause or Resume Servers: If set to true, then the user can pause and/or resume the server from the Environment page via the Pause and Resume buttons'. A is incorrect — this is Azure Scale Set only and controls stop/restart. B is incorrect — this controls changing queuing behavior. C is incorrect — this names the external provider, such as Azure.

questions.question: A standard (non-Azure) Server Set should include all servers named OSAPP01 through OSAPP09. What does the guide say about the Server Names setting?

options.A: Server Names for Standard Server Sets supports * and ? wildcards
options.B: Each server must be listed by full WCF address
options.C: Standard Server Sets require Azure Scale Set Name
options.D: Only one server name per set is allowed

questions.explanation: A is correct: the setting is 'Server Names for Standard Server Sets (Supports *? Wildcards)'. B is incorrect — names with wildcards are supported. C is incorrect — Azure Scale Set Name is Azure Scale Set only. D is incorrect — wildcards allow matching several servers.

questions.question: Which Server Set configuration setting applies to BOTH standard and Azure server sets (it is NOT marked Azure Scale Set Only)?

options.A: Maximum | Minimum Capacity
options.B: Can Pause or Resume Servers
options.C: Can Stop or Start Servers
options.D: System Business Rule Name

questions.explanation: B is correct: Can Pause or Resume Servers is not marked Azure-only, while Maximum/Minimum Capacity, Can Stop or Start Servers and System Business Rule Name are all marked '(Azure Scale Set Only)'. A is incorrect — marked Azure Scale Set Only. C is incorrect — marked Azure Scale Set Only. D is incorrect — marked Azure Scale Set Only.

questions.question: On the Server Sets Audit tab, what is tracked and how are changes highlighted?

options.A: Property changes in the web configuration file, shown in red
options.B: Logons by administrators, shown in bold
options.C: Property changes made in XFAppServerConfig.xml, shown in yellow
options.D: Property changes in XFAppServerConfig.xml, shown with a red X

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'The Audit tab identifies all property changes made in XFAppServerConfig.xml. Changes display in yellow'. A is incorrect — the file is XFAppServerConfig.xml and changes are yellow. B is incorrect — the tab tracks configuration property changes. D is incorrect — a red X marks offline servers.

questions.question: During close, an administrator clicks Pause on one application server. What happens to tasks?

options.A: The server stops taking new tasks from the queue, but tasks already started finish
options.B: All running tasks on the server are cancelled immediately
options.C: The server's IIS application pool is recycled
options.D: User sessions on the server are logged off

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'Pause will stop the server from seeking more tasks to run from the queue but will let tasks that have already started, finish'. B is incorrect — running tasks are allowed to finish. C is incorrect — that is Recycle App Pool. D is incorrect — Pause affects queued tasks, not sessions.

questions.question: An Azure Scale Set server will be idle over a holiday. The goal is to avoid VM compute charges, and losing its IP addresses is acceptable. Which action fits?

options.A: Stop
options.B: Stop (Deallocate)
options.C: Pause
options.D: Recycle App Pool

questions.explanation: B is correct: with Stop (Deallocate) 'the cost of virtual machine will not be charged, but the public and internal IP will be deleted'. A is incorrect — Stop keeps the IPs but 'will continue to incur Azure compute charges'. C is incorrect — Pause only stops the server taking new queued tasks; the VM keeps running. D is incorrect — this resets IIS and does not stop the VM.

questions.question: On the Environment page, which application server tab shows machine information such as hardware, based on Server Configuration Utility settings?

options.A: Configurations
options.B: Audit
options.C: Hardware
options.D: Performance

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Application Server Hardware tab 'will show the machine hardware information based on settings in the OneStream Server Configuration Utility'. A is incorrect — this shows server configuration values from the Server Configuration Utility. B is incorrect — this tracks hardware and configuration changes. D is incorrect — this shows metric values for the server and Environment.

questions.question: An administrator rescales Azure Elastic Pool DTUs from the Database Servers Behavior tab during business hours. What should users expect?

options.A: No effect; elastic pool rescaling is always online
options.B: All application servers are recycled
options.C: The Behavior tab is unavailable during business hours
options.D: Database connections are briefly dropped

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'When rescaling Elastic Pool DTUs, database connections are briefly dropped', the same as rescaling a single database. A is incorrect — connections are briefly dropped. B is incorrect — rescaling DTUs does not recycle app servers. C is incorrect — no such restriction is described.

questions.question: An on-premises SQL Server customer does not see a Behavior tab for their database connection. Why?

options.A: The user lacks the Administrator role
options.B: The Behavior tab appears only when SQL Server Azure and Elastic Pool are configured and used
options.C: Can Pause or Resume Servers is False
options.D: The database connection is paused in Web To App Server Connections

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'The behavior will show up if SQL Server Azure and Elastic Pool are configured and used'. A is incorrect — availability depends on Azure/Elastic Pool configuration. C is incorrect — that setting controls app server Pause/Resume buttons. D is incorrect — that section is about web-to-app connections.

questions.question: On the database server Diagnostics tab, Top SQL Commands can be ordered by several measures. Which is NOT one of them?

options.A: Total Logical Reads
options.B: Total Logical Writes
options.C: Total Elapsed Time
options.D: Total Worker Time

questions.explanation: C is correct: Top SQL Commands lists the top SQL by the order the user selects: Total Logical Reads, Total Logical Writes or Total Worker Time. A is incorrect — this is listed. B is incorrect — this is listed. D is incorrect — this is listed.

questions.question: A DBA thinks SQL deadlocks and expensive queries are slowing OneStream. Which Environment tool helps?

options.A: Diagnostic tab of the OneStream Database schema item
options.B: Hardware tab of the Database Server connection item
options.C: Diagnostics tab of the Database Server connection item
options.D: System > Tools > Database > Application Database Tables

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide says the Diagnostics tab runs SQL diagnostic commands, including deadlock information and Top SQL Commands ordered by Total Logical Reads, Writes or Worker Time. A is incorrect — it shows a table fragmentation report. B is incorrect — it shows SQL Server hardware information. D is incorrect — it gives read-only table views, not SQL diagnostics.

questions.question: Under OneStream Database Servers (Schema Items), what does the Diagnostic tab report?

options.A: SQL deadlocks on the instance
options.B: Top SQL Commands by Total Worker Time
options.C: Elastic Pool DTU usage
options.D: Current schema table fragmentation

questions.explanation: D is correct: 'Diagnostics tab will show a report of current schema table fragmentation'. A is incorrect — deadlocks are on the database server (connection) Diagnostics tab. B is incorrect — this is also the database server Diagnostics tab. C is incorrect — DTU scaling is on the Behavior tab.

questions.question: When must the Azure Subscription Settings in the Environment configuration be filled in?

options.A: When using Azure Elastic Pool (or Scale Sets), because they are used to log in and retrieve Azure settings and data
options.B: For every on-premises environment
options.C: Only when Single Sign-On uses an Identity Provider
options.D: Only when Use Detailed Logging is True on a cube view

questions.explanation: A is correct: they 'must be filled in, as they are used to login and retrieve Azure settings and data' and should be filled in when using Azure Elastic Pool or Scale Sets. B is incorrect — they apply when Azure Elastic Pool or Scale Sets are used. C is incorrect — Identity Provider is a web server setting. D is incorrect — unrelated cube view setting.

questions.question: What are the default and the 'turn off' values for Number of Running Hours Before Automatic Recycle?

options.A: Default 12.0; set -1 to turn off
options.B: Default 24.0; whole numbers only, blank turns it off
options.C: Default 24.0; set 0.0 to turn off auto recycling (fractional values allowed)
options.D: Default 48.0; set 0.0 to turn off

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'The default is 24.0. Use 0.0 to turn off auto recycling. Fractional numbers may be used'. A is incorrect — the default is 24.0 and 0.0 turns it off. B is incorrect — fractional numbers are allowed and 0.0 turns it off. D is incorrect — the default is 24.0.

questions.question: In the URL for the Automatic Recycle Service, what is the default port and what does the asterisk do?

options.A: Port 50001; the asterisk makes it recycle all servers
options.B: Port 443; the asterisk turns off HTTPS
options.C: Port 50002; the asterisk makes it use the load balancer address
options.D: Port 50002; the asterisk makes the service use the executing server's fully qualified domain name

questions.explanation: D is correct: the port 'default is 50002' and 'The asterisk will force the service to use the fully qualified domain name of the executing server'. A is incorrect — the default is 50002 and the asterisk is about FQDN. B is incorrect — the protocol is set to match how the service is deployed. C is incorrect — the asterisk uses the executing server's FQDN.

questions.question: An administrator leaves the recycle settings at their defaults. During which UTC window do application servers recycle, and when does the window apply?

options.A: Between 5:00 and 7:00 UTC, only when Number of Running Hours Before Automatic Recycle is 24.0
options.B: Between 0:00 and 2:00 UTC, always
options.C: Between 5:00 and 7:00 local server time, for any running-hours value
options.D: Between 7:00 and 9:00 UTC, only when running hours is 0.0

questions.explanation: A is correct: Start Hour defaults to 5 and End Hour to 7, and both are 'only used if Number of Running Hours Before Automatic Recycle is set to 24.0'. B is incorrect — the defaults are 5 and 7 and the window only applies at 24.0 hours. C is incorrect — the window is in UTC and only applies at 24.0. D is incorrect — 0.0 turns off auto recycling; defaults are 5 and 7.

questions.question: Maximum Number of Minutes to Pause Before Automatic Recycle is at its default. An app server is due to recycle and has no running tasks. What happens?

options.A: The server waits the full 30 minutes
options.B: The setting (default 30) is ignored and the server recycles without waiting
options.C: The server waits the default 60 minutes
options.D: The recycle is skipped until a task runs

questions.explanation: B is correct: the default is 30 minutes, used to let previously started tasks finish; 'If there are no previously running tasks on the application server, the setting is ignored'. A is incorrect — the setting is ignored when nothing is running. C is incorrect — the default is 30, and it is ignored here. D is incorrect — no such behavior is described.

questions.question: Which Environment Monitoring setting controls how often the system runs its monitoring checks for issues such as deadlocks?

options.A: Metric Update Interval (seconds)
options.B: Server Heartbeat Update Interval (seconds)
options.C: Number Past Metric Readings for SQL Blocking
options.D: Active Check Update Interval (seconds)

questions.explanation: D is correct: Active Check Update Interval is 'how often system checks for system monitoring (i.e.; deadlocks ...)'. A is incorrect — this is how often the system checks for metric updates. B is incorrect — this is how often the system records that the server is alive. C is incorrect — this sets how many past values are used for blocking analysis.

questions.question: A DBA wants Page Life Expectancy tracked on the Environment page. Which collection setting covers it?

options.A: Collect Server Memory Metrics
options.B: Collect SQL Page Metrics
options.C: Collect SQL Query Metrics
options.D: Collect SQL File Metrics

questions.explanation: B is correct: Collect SQL Page Metrics is 'how often to collect SQL server Page caching metrics (i.e.; Page Life Expectancy…)'. A is incorrect — this covers server memory such as Available MBytes. C is incorrect — this covers deletes/inserts. D is incorrect — this covers file growth.

questions.question: With ActiveCheckUpdateIntervalInSec set to 60, the guide says the fragmentation check runs about every 10 hours. Which setting drives this?

options.A: Fragmentation Iteration Count
options.B: Fragmentation Percent Threshold
options.C: Collect SQL File Metrics
options.D: Number Past Metric Reading For Analysis

questions.explanation: A is correct: Fragmentation Iteration Count is 'used for fragmentation check, every 10 hours if the ActiveCheckUpdateIntervalInSec is set to 60'. B is incorrect — this sets the fragmentation percent threshold, not frequency. C is incorrect — this collects SQL file growth metrics. D is incorrect — this is a Task Load Balancing setting for analyzing server demand.

questions.question: Old servers that were decommissioned still appear as offline in the environment. Which setting removes offline servers from the heartbeat table after a number of hours?

options.A: Server Heartbeat Update Interval (seconds)
options.B: Number of Running Hours Before Automatic Recycle
options.C: Number Hours To Retain Offline Servers
options.D: Maximum Queued Time (minutes)

questions.explanation: C is correct: it will 'remove offline servers from the heartbeat table after certain number of hours'. A is incorrect — this is how often a live server updates its heartbeat. B is incorrect — this controls auto recycle. D is incorrect — this cancels tasks that wait too long in the queue.

questions.subtopic: Task Load Balancing — Maximum Queued Time
questions.question: Queued Data Management jobs are being cancelled after waiting too long for a free server. Which Task Load Balancing setting controls this?

options.A: Maximum Queued Time (minutes)
options.B: Maximum Queued Processing Interval (seconds)
options.C: Maximum Number of Minutes to Pause Before Automatic Recycle
options.D: Maximum Average CPU Utilization

questions.explanation: A is correct: Maximum Queued Time is the 'maximum time to wait for a task to run before it is cancelled'. B is incorrect — this is how often the queuing thread checks for new tasks. C is incorrect — this is the grace period before an automatic recycle. D is incorrect — this decides whether a server can take a task.

questions.question: Which Task Load Balancing setting decides that a server is too busy to accept another queued task?

options.A: Number Past Metric Reading For Analysis
options.B: Maximum Average CPU Utilization
options.C: Collect Server Set CPU Metrics
options.D: Queued CPU

questions.explanation: B is correct: it is the 'maximum average CPU utilization before we determine that a server can't take a task'. A is incorrect — this sets how many readings are used for analysis, not the threshold. C is incorrect — this sets how often CPU metrics are collected. D is incorrect — Queued CPU is a Task Activity column showing CPU when the task was started.

questions.subtopic: Task Load Balancing — Processing Interval and Logging
questions.question: Which two-part description of Task Load Balancing settings is correct?

options.A: Maximum Queued Processing Interval sets how long a task may wait before cancelling; Task Logging Only = True turns off all task logging
options.B: Maximum Queued Processing Interval sets how often metrics are collected; Detailed Logging = True logs only picked-up tasks
options.C: Maximum Queued Processing Interval sets how often the queuing thread checks for new tasks; Task Logging Only = True logs only picked-up tasks
options.D: Maximum Queued Processing Interval sets heartbeat frequency; Task Logging Only = True logs every queue check

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide defines Maximum Queued Processing Interval as 'how often the queuing thread checks for new tasks to be run' and Task Logging Only as 'If true will only logs picked up tasks'. A is incorrect — wait-before-cancel is Maximum Queued Time, and Task Logging Only logs picked-up tasks. B is incorrect — metrics collection is Metric Update Interval, and Detailed Logging logs entering/exiting the function and what was run. D is incorrect — heartbeat is a separate setting, and Task Logging Only logs only picked-up tasks.

questions.subtopic: Task Load Balancing — Past Metric Readings
questions.question: Which Task Load Balancing setting sets how many metric readings are retrieved to analyze server demand?

options.A: Number Past Metric Readings for SQL Blocking
options.B: Fragmentation Iteration Count
options.C: Metric Update Interval (seconds)
options.D: Number Past Metric Reading For Analysis

questions.explanation: D is correct: it is 'how many metric readings to retrieve for analyzing server demand'. A is incorrect — this is for SQL blocking analysis in Environment Monitoring. B is incorrect — this controls fragmentation check frequency. C is incorrect — this sets how often metrics are checked, not how many are analyzed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Azure Elastic Pool Max DTU and Min DTU settings in the Database Server Connection?

options.A: They set the starting DTUs when the database is created
options.B: They are fail-safes so the user cannot set DTUs above the max or below the min
options.C: They set the CPU threshold for task load balancing
options.D: They set the server count for the Azure Scale Set

questions.explanation: B is correct: Max DTU is 'a fail-safe setting that the user can't set the DTU setting above this point' and Min DTU is the same for below. A is incorrect — they are limits, not starting values. C is incorrect — that is Maximum Average CPU Utilization. D is incorrect — server counts are Maximum/Minimum Capacity on the Server Set.

questions.subtopic: Azure Database Connection — SQL Scaling Type
questions.question: An Azure customer sets Azure SQL Scaling Type to BusinessRule. What else must be configured?

options.A: Server Set Provider Type set to Azure
options.B: Can Stop or Start Servers set to True
options.C: Azure SQL System Business Rule Name, pointing to the rule that scales eDTUs using Environment and database metrics
options.D: Azure Service Level Objective set to BusinessRule

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'If SQL Scaling Type is set to BusinessRule, this setting must be set to a business rule that is used to scale in/out. The Environment metrics and the database metrics are passed to this rule'. A is incorrect — this is a Server Set setting, not database eDTU scaling. B is incorrect — this controls app server stop/restart in Scale Sets. D is incorrect — Service Level Objective is the service level used to create applications on Azure.

questions.subtopic: Azure Database Connection — Scaling Type Default
questions.question: Which value does the guide say the Azure SQL Scaling Type should default to?

options.A: Manual
options.B: BusinessRule
options.C: ManualAndBusinessRule
options.D: Not Used

questions.explanation: D is correct: the options are Manual, Business Rule or ManualAndBusinessRule, and 'The default setting should be set to Not Used'. A is incorrect — Manual is an option but not the default. B is incorrect — BusinessRule is an option but not the default. C is incorrect — ManualAndBusinessRule is an option but not the default.
